Also not absorbed: SIMOPS conflict reconciliation, suspension on general alarm, lockout/tagout multi-holder locks. Agent-to-agent transfer is AD-1161; there is no `transfer_permit`.

### BF-690 (2026-07-27) - the browser offer advertised actions the guard refuses (#1091)

AD-1153 armed a read-only guard inside `DispatchToolExecutor.invoke` but left the *offer* untouched. `tool_registration_to_llm_definition` passes `reg.tool.input_schema` verbatim, so a restricted agent was shown all eleven actions and then refused five by a rule it had never been given — failed attempts burning loop iterations, not absent ones. The description was the sharper half: it ends "then click/type by index", so a read-only agent was *actively instructed* to use the two actions the guard would refuse. Narrowing the enum alone would have left that intact.

The arming condition now produces both consequences. `_narrow_browser_offer` rewrites the enum **and** generates a matching description from the same frozenset that arms the guard. The narrowed enum is the **intersection** of the schema's declared actions with the armed set, in schema order — fail-safe in the same direction as `_BROWSER_LOOP_ACTIONS` itself, so an action named in the restriction but absent from the schema is never advertised. New dicts at every level leave `BrowserTool.input_schema` intact for the AD-745 DM path. An unexpected shape or empty intersection logs and returns the definition unchanged: the invoke-time guard still refuses, so that path degrades to AD-1153 behaviour rather than opening an authority hole. Unarmed paths are byte-identical — a Captain-granted agent keeps the full surface (DD-2 grant-UP semantics).

**Why AD-1153's suite missed it:** its capture harness (`_ToolIdCapturingLLM`) records only `function.name`. The defect lived in `function.parameters` and `function.description`, which nothing inspected. A capture double that discards most of the payload cannot regress the payload.

The description had been a *third* hand-written copy of the action list, beside the enum and `_BROWSER_READ_ONLY_REFUSAL`; it is generated now, and a drift guard asserts the refusal string still lists exactly `_BROWSER_LOOP_ACTIONS`. **Not fixed here:** `verify` is in the enum but absent from the description's own "10-action vocabulary" count — same defect class, left out so the unrestricted path stays byte-identical.

### AD-1158 (2026-07-27) - bind a browser call to the workstation session the Captain is watching

An agent invoking `browser` without a `session_id` created a *fresh* session, so the Captain could be watching one browser while the agent acted in another. The obvious fix — telling the agent the id in its prompt — makes correctness depend on the model copying a UUID accurately, which is not a property worth resting a governance surface on.

`BrowserTool.invoke` now reads `context["browser_session_id"]` when `params["session_id"]` is absent. Precedence is deliberate: an **explicit param always wins**, because an agent that names a session has stated an intent the ambient binding must not override; a non-`str` binding degrades to prior behaviour rather than raising. The binding travels through the call context, so no prompt text and no model accuracy is involved.

### BF-688 / BF-688a (2026-07-27) - four sub-task handlers dropped the priority the scheduler needed (#1089)

Every sub-task handler called `complete(request)` with no priority, so Captain DMs competed on equal footing with proactive background work. Observed: Anvil taking 88 s against a 60 s TTL, timing out a Captain-facing reply behind speculative work. The priority parameter existed and was honoured — nothing passed it. Fixed with `CHAIN_PRIORITY_KEY = "_priority"` and `resolve_chain_priority(context)` so the chain carries its own urgency.

**BF-688a** is the CI repair and the more durable lesson: 28 test files' LLM doubles did not accept `priority`, so a name-filtered test run went green while the full suite failed. **Changing a signature on an interface that test doubles implement requires the full suite — a filtered run cannot prove blast radius.**

### BF-686 (2026-07-27) - 2,025 ERROR lines for 19 breaker events (#1086)

Endpoint-failure logging keyed severity to *attribution* (an upstream fault is an error) rather than to *outcome* (the system compensated and continued). A ~107:1 amplification buried genuine faults and made the log unreadable during exactly the incidents it existed to explain. Now one WARNING per `_EndpointFailureState.epoch`: the transition is logged, not every request that observes it. Log level should describe what happened to the *work*, not whose fault it was.

### BF-685 (2026-07-27) - a stale JetStream handle failed every pool (#1085)

`BadSubscriptionError` / `ConnectionClosedError` were treated as fatal on one path while `_recover_jetstream` already handled them correctly on another — two paths disagreeing about whether the same exception is recoverable. One stale handle therefore failed pools that were otherwise healthy. The recovery logic was never wrong; the classification was, in one of two places.

### BF-684 (2026-07-27) - three compounding defects hid a records backfill that never ran (#1084)

Warm boot's `if already_indexed: return` meant the records backfill ran exactly once, ever — so any record added afterwards was never indexed. `entries[:limit]` then re-walked the same prefix on each pass, so even a forced re-run made no progress past the first 500. Finally `if semantic_results:` short-circuited the keyword index into dead code, with the perverse consequence that **enabling AD-1138 reduced recall**. Each defect alone was survivable; together they presented as "search is a bit weak" rather than as three bugs. Resumability now comes from `_indexed_record_paths()` and the keyword index is consulted unconditionally.

### AD-1157 / AD-1157a (2026-07-27) - notebook classification: honour the ontology, and let the author choose scope (#1088)

The ontology declared notebooks `private`; the code defaulted them to `department`; and the `[NOTEBOOK]` tag carried neither, because its regex had a single capture group with nowhere to put a classification. The result was unanimous: **2,453 of 2,453 records took the default.** A classification field existed, was validated, and was never once supplied by a caller.

The tag now carries the classification, and the crew agent selects scope contextually against a stated policy rather than inheriting a constant — notebooks default `private` (honouring the ontology), findings published through `publish_finding` default `ship`. Verified live end-to-end, including the first cross-department retrieval in the system's history: Anvil (engineering) recalled a finding Ezri (bridge) had published.

**AD-1157a** is the follow-on the first fix exposed: update-in-place re-stamped classification on every write, so three records silently drifted scope in production. `classification=None` now means *no preference stated* — preserve on update, apply the default only on create. Absent and default are different facts, and a field that cannot distinguish them will overwrite deliberate choices with defaults.

### AD-1154 (2026-07-26) - the approval inbox: park an unattended ask instead of acting, and let a standing rule answer it once (#1081)

An unattended agent reaching a consequential action had two outcomes: perform it, or receive the tier-3 gate's `ToolResult(output={"intervention_required": True, ...})` with **`error=None`** — a success-shaped no-op that `ToolCallResult.from_tool_result` renders as `is_error=False` and the model reads as completion. This AD adds the third: file a durable, reviewable record; tell the agent honestly that the step did not happen; carry on. A standing, TTL-bounded rule answers the same ask on the next run without asking again. Two flags, both default-OFF (`approval_inbox.enabled`, `.standing_rules_enabled`); off ⇒ `DispatchToolExecutor.invoke` is byte-identical to AD-1153.

**Three findings a future AD would otherwise rediscover expensively, all read off the live tree rather than assumed.**

**(1) The approval inbox already existed, so this is a fourth `kind`, not a fifth store.** #1081's central premise — that "a durable pending-ask record" is something ProbOS needs to build — was false at HEAD. AD-853's `CapabilityRequestStore` is a complete `ConnectionFactory`-backed approval queue; AD-857 ships the `GET /api/capability-requests?status=pending` + `POST /{id}/decide` surface **and** the Captain-DM notifier on `CAPABILITY_REQUEST_FILED`; AD-855 ships the resume driver on `capability_request_decided`. Decisively, `CapabilityRequestPanel.tsx` types `kind: string`, renders `{req.kind}` / `{req.target}` verbatim and falls through to a neutral colour for an unrecognised key — **a fourth kind renders with no UI change.** A parallel store would have put the ask on a surface nobody polls. So: `RequestKind` gains `"action"`, plus **one** nullable `payload TEXT` column carrying the six-key action shape (`target` is a bare string and cannot hold `params`). `payload` is appended **last** in the schema, the dataclass, the SELECT column list and the positional INSERT — all four move together or `row[N]` shifts silently — and a guarded `ALTER TABLE` runs in `start()` because `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op against an operator's existing 11-column table. The payload is exact-key validated on write **and** re-validated on read (a hand-edited DB is an untrusted input), a corrupt row degrades to `payload=None` with a WARNING rather than blocking startup, `confirmation_token` is stripped before serialisation, and `action="fill_credential"` is never parked at all — converting a per-call human gate into a durable record plus a standing rule would make it a stored credential-access grant.

**(2) `NotificationQueue` is IN-MEMORY, so #1081's prescribed resolution surface could not carry a durable ask.** `notifications.py` backs it with `self._notifications: dict[str, AgentNotification]` — no DB, no `ConnectionFactory`, no `start()`/`stop()` — despite a class docstring that has said "Persistent notification queue" since AD-323. Every unacknowledged ask dies at restart, which is precisely the outlives-the-run property the whole design rests on, and `_prune_acknowledged` only reaps *acknowledged* entries so unacked asks grow without bound in RAM until the process takes them with it. The **AD-1053 invariant is preserved and its surface is not used**: the invariant is *the producer authors the action, the client only references an id*, and the AD-853 decide endpoint has exactly that property (`{approve, reason}` and nothing else) while being backed by SQLite. Resolution therefore goes through `POST /api/capability-requests/{id}/decide`. This is a correction to the issue, not a deviation from its intent. `notifications.py` and `routers/system.py` are untouched.

**(3) Approval cannot replay the parked action, and saying so is the point.** `BrowserToolConfig.session_max_duration_seconds` is **1800 s**; a human decision takes minutes to days. The `session_id` in a parked ask almost certainly names a session already reaped, and creating a *fresh* session to replay a page-relative `click` selector against whatever that page looks like now is **a different act from the one the Captain approved**. So the recorded `session_id` is forensic only and is never passed to any browser API — asserted directly, because it is the property a future refactor is most likely to "improve" away. Work-item re-dispatch is rejected for a second reason: the child already completed with an honest partial result and a persisted `crew_execution` record, and re-running the agentic loop from a REST handler would put an unbudgeted LLM run behind a button. What approval buys is a durable record, a trust signal (existing `decide()` behaviour) and — optionally — a rule that lets the *next* run proceed. This limitation is stated in the config description, in `file_action_request`'s docstring and here, because an AD that quietly implied otherwise would be exactly the "looks like progress" failure this AD exists to prevent.

**Why a fourth store for the standing rule, checked rather than assumed.** #1081 suggested `ToolPermissionStore` / `IntentGrantStore`. The instinct is right; the fit is not. `ToolPermissionStore` keys on `(agent_id, tool_id, permission)` and `IntentGrantStore` on `(agent_id, intent_name)` — **neither has an action column or a scope column**, so granting `browser` would grant every browser verb including `eval_js` and `fill_credential`, and `browser` is not a mesh intent at all. Both are *capability* grants (*may this agent hold this tool*); a standing approval is an *action* grant (*may this agent perform this shape of act, in this scope, until this time*). Widening `ToolPermissionStore` would change the meaning of every existing row and of `check_permission`, which is on the hot path of every tool call in the system. `ActionApprovalStore` therefore mirrors `IntentGrantStore` line for line so it is the fourth instance of one pattern rather than a fourth pattern — and `intent_grants.py`'s own note that a unified `CapabilityGrantStore` is the eventual consolidation still stands, still undone. Two properties differ deliberately: **`expires_at REAL NOT NULL` in the schema**, not merely in the signature (`issue_approval` takes `ttl_seconds: float`, never `expires_at: float | None`), because a standing rule with no TTL is a permanent privilege escalation nobody remembers granting; and **no wildcard** — all four of `(agent_id, tool_id, action, scope_key)` match exactly, and a rule with `scope_key=""` matches only an ask whose scope is `""`. A `""`-means-any convenience would read as ergonomics and behave as "approve every click on every site forever-until-TTL", one typo away. `scope_key` is producer-computed (the wrapper parses the host; the store never parses a URL), so a browser rule is *always* domain-scoped.

**The wrapper fails CLOSED, and that is the one property whose inversion the feature cannot survive.** `DispatchToolExecutor._park_or_admit` sits **above** the tool at the same seam as AD-1153's allowlist — `BrowserTool.invoke` is unchanged, because that method also serves the AD-745 DM dispatch path where a human *is* present and the Captain-ACK reissue flow is the intended mechanism. Six ordered steps: not armed ⇒ admit; not tier 3 ⇒ admit; credential ⇒ refuse without filing; standing rule ⇒ admit; cap reached ⇒ refuse without filing; else file (or dedup onto) the ask and refuse with the request id. **Every step absorbs its own exceptions toward refusal** — a raising `is_approved_sync`, a raising `file_action_request`, a raising pending count and a `None` store each produce a refusal, never an admission. Step 2 carries a deliberate **asymmetry**: classifying needs a session, and `_get_or_create_session` has a side effect, so the wrapper resolves an *existing* session through the public non-creating `BrowserTool.get_session` and, when there is none, treats only the always-tier-3 verbs as tier 3 — `click`/`type` fall through to `BrowserTool`, whose own gate then runs as it does today. A gate must be able to say "I cannot classify this" without allocating resources to answer a policy question. Dedup on `sha256(agent_id | tool_id | action | scope_key | work_item_id | canonical_params)` means a model that retries a refused call three times files **one** ask; the key is recomputed from the payload on cache load, so no twelfth column and no second index. The inbox is bounded per agent and a full inbox degrades to an honest refusal with a WARNING naming the agent and the count — 400 pending asks is indistinguishable from 0 to a human, and an unbounded queue is a memory leak wearing a governance costume. A stale ask is excluded from the *count* only: never auto-approved (walking away would become the approval mechanism) and never auto-denied.

**Consensus is not routable around this, asserted directly rather than inferred.** Arming is `frozenset` membership (`_APPROVAL_INBOX_TOOL_IDS == {"browser"}`) in the same fail-safe direction as `_BROWSER_LOOP_ACTIONS` and `PARALLEL_SAFE_TOOL_IDS`: anything new, renamed or unrecognised is not parked and takes its existing path, so `_MeshIntentTool.invoke` and `_McpTool`'s `CONSENSUS` branch are structurally excluded — and both are tested with the inbox armed, requiring zero requests filed. `decide()` dispatches nothing, so there is no second dispatch path to gate, and a source grep asserts `is_approved_sync` appears in no module under `src/probos/consensus/`.

**Deliberately not built:** re-execution or work-item re-dispatch; heuristic auto-approval (DD-5 — `evaluate_grant_fast_path`'s `peer_precedent` has no referent for an action shape and its `non_destructive` is undecidable for a browser click whose destructiveness is a property of the page); any widening of `_BROWSER_LOOP_ACTIONS`, which is byte-identical and asserted so, because shipping the gate and the actions it gates together would mean the gate's first exercise is in production; any HXI affordance (`grant_standing` is API-only); `HookBus.ask` wiring (`AggregateDecision.asked` remains consumerless); and unification of the four grant stores.

**BF-682 closes here.** The `TOOL_INTERVENTION_REQUIRED` payload carried the raw `confirmation_token`, which `_consume_confirmation_token` will honour — possession of the log line was possession of the approval. The middle link was broken (no `emit_event`-sourced tool event reaches the queryable `EventLog` — measured, zero such rows in the live 402 483-row `events.db`), so it was hardening rather than a live exploit; but this AD is what makes a tier-3 gate reachable from an unattended loop, so the token stops being theoretically exposed and starts being routinely emitted. The payload now carries `confirmation_id = token[:8]`: it correlates a log line to a pending confirmation without being redeemable, since the consumer matches the full key. Both directions are asserted.

### AD-1155 (2026-07-26) - loop-until-done: an outer completion evaluator over the crew child's agentic run (#1082)

A crew child that stops mid-work is now re-invoked with a fresh, independently governed run, bounded by its own cap, stopping early when an iteration achieves nothing. Default-OFF.

**Two of #1082's load-bearing premises were false at HEAD, and both are recorded here because a future AD will otherwise rediscover them the hard way.**

**C-1 — an outer loop already exists, and it is live.** `SubtaskVerifier.converge_for_session` (`crew_verifier.py:1301`) is a complete, governed, bounded loop over `WorkItemAgenticExecutor.run`, called from `crew_finalizer.py:1329` and `:2106` on the live crew-session path. It already re-invokes with a critique (`critiqued_task`), caps at `min(max_convergence_rounds, 8)`, builds a fresh run per round, never persists the enriched text, and records per-round provenance. So the gap was never "there is no outer loop" — it is that the only predicate is an LLM judge, and `_classify_correction_terminal` returns `None` (continue) **only** for `complete` with non-empty text, routing `max_iterations` into `else: correction_execution_defect`. A child cut off mid-work *by a counter* was therefore recorded as a defect rather than as unfinished work. This AD adds a cheap deterministic predicate and a `max_iterations` continuation at the fan-out seam, and touches neither the judge nor the finalizer. A second AI-judge predicate was considered and rejected: it would double the per-round LLM cost for a strictly weaker signal (no `expected_output`, no independence requirement); the correct future move is to fix that `max_iterations` branch, not to build a parallel judge.

**C-2 — `todos_remaining` is not a valid crew-child predicate, and shipping the literal would have re-invoked every crew child, always.** `workforce._all_steps_done` is `bool(steps) and all(...)`, so `_all_steps_done([])` is **`False`** and the proposed `not _all_steps_done(child.steps)` is **`True` for an empty checklist**. The crew fan-out never writes `WorkItem.steps` — `grep '\bsteps\b'` across `crew_executor.py` and `crew_session.py` returns nothing, because steps move through the `[TODOS]`/`[TODO_DONE n]`/`[TODO_CONFIRM n]` tags of `reply_pipeline.step_4l_extract_todos`, a stage of the **DM reply pipeline** that a child running through `AgenticLoop` never enters. That tag path is itself default-OFF (`communications.room_todos_enabled`). So every crew child has an empty list, and the naive predicate would have re-run all of them to the cap. `open_todos` therefore ships **opt-in**, with `_actionable_step_labels` returning `None` — *inapplicable ⇒ stop* — for a non-list, an empty list, a non-dict member or an unknown status, never "not all done ⇒ continue". `_all_steps_done` is deliberately not imported or extended: its empty-list semantics are correct for its own single caller and wrong here. **`submitted` is excluded from actionable**: `_apply_room_todos` gates `submitted → done` on `is_senior or actor == facilitator`, needing rank ≥ `room_todos_min_rank` (default `commander` ⇒ trust ≥ 0.7) while built-ins seed at Beta(2,2) = 0.50 ⇒ **lieutenant**, so the modal crew agent is structurally incapable of closing its own submitted step and re-invoking it is guaranteed-futile work. The default predicate is `stopped_reason`.

**The wrap is `CrewTaskExecutor._run_child`, not `WorkItemAgenticExecutor.run`.** That method has six call sites; wrapping it would have nested this loop *inside* `converge_for_session`'s correction rounds — a four-way multiplication — and would have changed the AD-839 conversational and AD-1072 delegation paths, which is exactly the trap AD-1141/DD-1 and AD-1142/DD-2 caught. Wrapping at the fan-out seam makes the five other callers byte-identical **by construction rather than by flag**, which is the strongest available form of that guarantee. The honest cost: the conversational and delegation paths get nothing from this AD — correct scoping, because both have a human present who can say "keep going" and an unattended crew child does not.

**Re-invokability is decided per stop reason, fail-safe.** `_REINVOKABLE_STOPPED_REASONS = frozenset({"max_iterations"})`, consulted by every predicate as a precondition and asserted against the live `_STOPPED_REASONS` so a future reason cannot be silently admitted — the same admit-don't-exclude direction as `PARALLEL_SAFE_TOOL_IDS` and `_BROWSER_LOOP_ACTIONS`. `token_budget` is **not** re-invoked: it is a spend ceiling the operator set, and `crew_executor` deliberately maps it to `status="failed"` so dependents stay blocked — overriding it here would have silently reversed an AD-1142 decision. `error` is not re-invoked: it is most often provider-window exhaustion, and the continuation block makes `task_text` *longer*, so looping is strictly counterproductive where compaction is the mechanism. `complete` is not re-invoked under any predicate — the model chose to stop.

**Budget is shared and carried forward as a remainder, never reset.** `AgenticLoop` measures its budget against a counter local to one `AgenticResult` and the executor builds a new loop per call, so passing the full figure each iteration would multiply the operator's ceiling by the cap; nobody setting `crew_token_budget=50000` expects 250 000. Iterations 2+ therefore run with *less* room than the first — a ceiling, not an allowance, and both config descriptions say so. Below `_MIN_CREW_TOKEN_BUDGET` the loop stops rather than buying one call that immediately hits the ceiling. The worst case is stated verbatim in the config description rather than softened: 5 × 25 × 16 = **2000 tool invocations for one child**, before `max_parallel_subtasks` multiplies it across siblings and `converge_for_session` adds 8 correction rounds. No cross-field validator — the AD-1142 precedent is that the relation is documented and asserted in tests, because a parse-time raise turns an unrelated `POST /config` into a 422.

**The continuation is composed at runtime into `task_text` and never persisted** — `description` is inside the plan-identity projection, so `plan_seed_hash` and `_final_plan_hash` are asserted byte-identical across a three-iteration run. It is rebuilt from the base text each time so blocks cannot stack, bounded at 3000 chars with the prior output head-truncated at 2000 behind a counted elision marker, and composed **outside** the try that persists `execution_exception`: a composition failure degrades to "stop the loop", never to a failed child. Every authored string is asserted clean against the **imported** `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE` — the natural English for "you didn't finish" is a minefield there, since "you were unable to complete" trips it twice and `lack` is a bare substring.

**No-progress detection is a backstop, and the docstring says so rather than overstating it.** Two *consecutive* iterations with no artifacts, an identical `final_text` hash and no todo movement stop the loop; one is not enough, because a pass can be spent on an investigation whose payoff lands next. Byte-identical text across two LLM calls at non-zero temperature is rare, so the artifact clause carries almost all the weight and a prose-output task will rarely trip it — the cap is the real bound. A semantic-similarity check was rejected as the same LLM-per-iteration cost as the judge.

**Every iteration is an independently governed run**, which falls out of the seam for free: a fresh `DispatchToolExecutor`, `department`/`rank` re-resolved through live `trust_network.get_score`, every `check_permission` offer gate re-run, the AD-1153 browser guard re-armed, its own AD-1151 trace. Asserted rather than merely allowed, with a **real** `ToolRegistry` and `ToolPermissionStore` (BF-287): trust falling 0.55 → 0.30 crosses `TRUST_LIEUTENANT` and the `browser` offer (`ensign: none`) disappears on iteration 2 — Minimal Authority working correctly, and the cheapest proof that these are genuine re-runs rather than a resumed session. Only the **final** `tool_trace_ref` reaches the frozen 14-key `crew_execution` record; intermediate refs are logged at INFO with their iteration index and are *not* durably linked, because inventing a companion key is the "one extra breaks recovery" hazard.

**BF-683 filed, not fixed:** `converge_for_session`'s correction re-runs pass no `compactor`, no `compaction_threshold` and no `token_budget`, so up to 8 rounds per child run entirely outside the AD-1142 ceilings the first pass respects. Pre-existing; this AD's budget arithmetic deliberately does not depend on those rounds being budgeted. 105 tests; 303 passed across the eight-file gate with `crew_verifier`, `crew_finalizer`, `agentic_loop`, `workforce` and `reply_pipeline` untouched.

### AD-1153 (2026-07-26) - the browser offered to the agentic loop, read-only (#1080)

A crew agent can now *read* a live page from inside `AgenticLoop` — navigate, enumerate, extract text — instead of degrading to `http_fetch` or confabulating a verb. Default-OFF (`agentic_tools.browser_enabled`), gated on that flag AND `registry.get("browser")`, which already carries `browser_tool.enabled` plus the Playwright import check, so availability is not re-derived.

**v1 is read-only because the six offered actions provably cannot reach the tier-3 gate — not because the gate protects us.** `_BROWSER_LOOP_ACTIONS = {goto, state, extract_text, back, forward, wait}`: five are tier 1 and `goto` is tier 2, and escalation is reachable only through `click`/`type`/`drag`/`mouse_button` and the always-tier-3 verbs. That matters because **the tier-3 gate returns a success-shaped no-op**: `ToolResult(output={"intervention_required": True, …})` with `error=None`, so `from_tool_result` sets `is_error=False` and an unattended model reads it as completion — likely narrating success or retrying, each retry minting a fresh token into `_pending_confirmations`. This AD ships the subset for which that flow is never consulted; `click`/`type`/`scroll` wait on AD-1154 (#1081) and its approval inbox. A test enumerates the six against the real `classify_action` and requires `max(tier) <= 2`, plus `_pending_confirmations == {}` after a full sequence.

**Three facts contradicted #1080 and are corrected here.** (1) **`goto` is unconditionally tier 2** — `classify_action` returns 2 before any URL inspection, so navigating to `https://shop.example/payment` is **ungated**, not auto-approved; the mechanism the Captain feared is *absence* of a gate. Pinned by test. (2) **`destructive_url_patterns` is not a `BrowserTool` guardrail** — its only reader in `src/` is the AD-745 DM dispatch stage, which this path does not use; a negative-guard test executes `goto` to `/checkout` and asserts tier 2, so a future AD that moves the check into the tool goes red and forces this DD to be revisited. An agentic-loop caller gets domain allow/denylist, `classify_action` tiering, per-domain rate limiting and the session duration cap — and nothing else. (3) **A per-action permission split is not expressible through `check_permission`** — it is keyed by `(agent_id, tool_id, required)` with no action dimension, and `AgenticLoop._run_one_tool_call` invokes without `required=`, so every call defaults to READ regardless of rank; a `commander` and a `lieutenant` receive an identical action surface.

**The enforcement seam is therefore `DispatchToolExecutor`, the only choke point that sees `params`.** Zero edits under `src/probos/tools/browser/`, so the DM path is byte-identical. It is a fail-safe partition in the exact shape of `PARALLEL_SAFE_TOOL_IDS` (AD-1147/DD-1) — membership is the only way through, so an unknown, renamed or newly added action is refused by default; `eval_js` / `fill_credential` / a fabricated verb are all refused *before* the tool. Module constant, not a config field: a safety property, not a tuning knob. The refusal is an **error** `ToolResult`, never a success-shaped no-op — the exact defect it routes around.

**The restriction arms only when the tool arrived through the new offer AND `"browser" not in granted_ids`.** An agent can hold `browser` by both routes; narrowing the grant path would silently revoke a working capability and invert Layer 4's grant-**up** semantics. `browser` is deliberately **not** added to `_GATED_TOOL_IDS` — the siblings are gated because they carry `allowed_departments`, `browser` does not, so the gate would protect nothing and would only remove the Captain's escape hatch for probationary agents. Both directions are tested.

**`ensign: none` is retained, and AD-1140/DD-1's reasoning does not transfer.** That AD chose `write` at every rank because a publish is additive and reversible; driving a live browser is neither — the page is somebody else's system. Rank is trust-derived (`Rank.from_trust`, `TRUST_LIEUTENANT = 0.5`), so `ensign` is not a caste but trust < 0.5, denying the browser precisely to agents that are new, self-designed (Beta(1,3) = 0.25) or currently failing. It is not dead on arrival: built-ins seed at Beta(2,2) = 0.50 and are already lieutenant, and the Captain grant-up path already works — proven by a test that grants `read` to an **ensign** and still sees the tool.

**Bounds and framing are applied in the same guard.** `tool_result_max_chars` ships at 0, so AD-1148 is a no-op on defaults while one `extract_text` returns `inner_text("body")` verbatim; the inner caps are 8000 chars and 100 elements, both elided **visibly** with a counted marker. 8000 sits between AD-1148's head+tail (4000+2000) and `TOOL_TRACE_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS` (8192) so a bounded read survives the AD-1151 durable trace intact — the bound is applied to the value *returned from* `DispatchToolExecutor.invoke`, which is what both the transcript and the trace consume (AD-448 post-hooks fire inside `super().invoke()` and see the raw output; none consumes `browser`). Framing rides inline in the `_ORACLE_DISPOSITION` shape, since `AgenticLoop` has no consumer-side wrapper: a page read is a live observation with a timestamp, not a durable fact. Every authored string is asserted clean against the **imported** `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE` — `lack` is a bare substring there, and the refusal is the dangerous one because the natural English for it is "cannot".

**`PARALLEL_SAFE_TOOL_IDS` is deliberately not extended** — read-only is not parallel-safe: all six actions share one `BrowserSession`, `state()` writes the index map a later call resolves against, and two concurrent `goto`s race. A no-op, pinned by assertion because "it is read-only, add it to the allowlist" is the obvious wrong next move. **Egress is warned about, not forced**: `domain_allowlist` defaults to `None` = allow-all, and requiring one would make the feature useless for the research tasks that motivate it, so a one-shot WARNING fires at first offer (instance-scoped, so once-only is assertable). 64 tests; 353 adjacent passed with `test_ad706_browser_tool.py` and `test_ad745_pipeline_dispatch.py` untouched.

### BF-682 (2026-07-26) - FILED, NOT FIXED - confirmation token in the `TOOL_INTERVENTION_REQUIRED` payload (AD-1153/DD-8)

`browser/tool.py:284-292` emits the event with the raw `confirmation_token` in the payload; `event_log_query`'s `_wire_json` recurses dicts without redaction and `event` is a free-text filter with no event-type allowlist; `_consume_confirmation_token` accepts the token straight from `params`. The theoretical chain is: trigger a tier-3 gate → query your own event log → read the token → replay it.

**The middle link is broken, so this is a hardening note rather than a live exploit.** Probed at build: `_safe_emit` → `runtime.emit_event` → `_emit_event` routes to type-filtered in-memory listeners and NATS, never to `EventLog.log`. Every `add_event_listener` call site in `src/` is type-filtered and none subscribes to `tool_intervention_required`, and the live 82 MB `events.db` (397k rows) holds **zero** rows for `tool_intervention_required`, `tool_invoked`, `browser_session_started` or `browser_session_closed` — no `emit_event`-sourced tool event is persisted at all. So `event_log_query` cannot return the token today.

**Unreachable in AD-1153 v1 by construction** — no action in `_BROWSER_LOOP_ACTIONS` can classify as tier 3, so no token is minted on this path. It becomes load-bearing the moment AD-1154 admits `click`/`type`, and would become exploitable if any future AD bridges `emit_event` into the queryable EventLog. The fix is to emit a non-secret `confirmation_id` and keep the token only in `_pending_confirmations`; blast radius is known — `tests/test_ad706_browser_tool.py:279` asserts the token **is** in the payload.

### AD-1145 (2026-07-25) - W3C PROV-O provenance projection; OTel half deferred (#1070)

Pure-stdlib PROV-O projection so a third party can consume ProbOS provenance without reimplementing its internal shapes. Sibling of AD-1144; same pattern — zero dependencies (`pyproject.toml` diff empty), read-only, default-inert behind a default-OFF `?format=` on the existing records endpoint with no new route. **Built over a different surface than #1070 specified:** `ProvenanceTag` has no agent and no activity (`query_with_provenance()` accepts `agent_id` and discards it; `compute_content_hash` returns 32 bits, unusable as an IRI), so a projection from it would say nothing about who or how. The real mapping is `crew_execution`'s 14 keys plus records frontmatter — `work_item_id`→Activity, `assigned_to`→Agent, `parent_id`→`wasInformedBy`, `artifact_refs`→`wasGeneratedBy`, `tool_trace_ref`→`used`. `tokens_used`/`token_source` deliberately excluded: post-BF-680 a count may be measured or estimated and the frozen contract carries the int without the source, so emitting it would present an estimate as a measurement. Unidentifiable agents omit the triple rather than synthesising one; an unusable `revision` projects an empty graph rather than guessing version 1. **OTel half deferred to AD-1152 (#1079)** — spans are not constructible: `AGENTIC_TOOL_CALL_STARTED` discards `use.tool_call.id` so AD-1147's 16 parallel calls cannot be paired, there is no run/trace id, and `token_source` is dropped at the frozen boundary. The OSS half of an exporter is empty anyway — `runtime.add_event_listener` is already the seam and already consumed by the commercial Airlock. 77 tests; 627 passed.

### BF-680 (2026-07-25) - client-side token estimate when the provider reports none (#1078)

The Copilot proxy returns `{'prompt_tokens': 0, 'completion_tokens': 0, 'total_tokens': 0}` for a completion that produced real output, and all tiers resolve to it. `result.total_tokens` was therefore permanently zero, so `token_budget` (a hard stop with an immediate return) **could never fire** and `crew_execution` recorded `tokens_used: 0` for every child. ProbOS does not own the proxy; the defect was treating an **absent** measurement as a measurement of **zero**. Falls back to AD-1142's `_estimate_context_tokens`. `LLMResponse` has no usage-present flag, so the rule is a named predicate: a zero accompanying a completion that **produced output** is absent. Tool-call-only turns count as output deliberately — they carry no text but are the turns the loop exists for. Byte-identical when the provider reports real usage, proven by monkeypatching the estimator to **raise** and running a full measured multi-turn run to completion. Provenance rides `AgenticResult.token_source` / `WorkItemAgenticOutcome.token_source` / harness metadata; the frozen 14-key set is untouched, so the persisted record still cannot say which — an operator must correlate to logs. Also repaired the CI failure AD-1142 left on main (see BF-678 note). 31 tests; 428 passed.

### AD-1143 (2026-07-25) - Nooplex §8.3 with/without-Σ ablation harness (#1064)

Captures the §8.3 control arm before AD-1141 could change it. Zero production change — 17 files, none under `src/`. `tests/ablation/` is excluded from the default gate by a directory-local `collect_ignore_glob`, **not** `pytestmark=skipif`: the runner imports the whole crew stack, so a skipif module would still be imported and an import failure would break CI for everyone. Verified 20,849 items collected, zero from `tests/ablation/`. An AST-only `compile()` guard keeps never-collected code from rotting. `sigma_flags.py` is the single source of truth for arm flag sets, with a guard asserting both arms carry identical key sets and every dotted path resolves to a `bool` — so a renamed field goes red instead of silently degrading the treatment arm into a second control arm. **Honest scope, stated in the docstrings, artifact and report: a directional signal, not a publishable effect size.** n=12 paired is ~70% powered for d_z 0.8 (100 goals would be 9k–24k live calls); the judge shares a model family with the system under test; crew calls are not temperature-pinned, so three trials measure the noise and a `VARIANCE_DOMINATES` veto forces `inconclusive` when between-trial spread exceeds between-arm delta. The harness is forbidden from printing `significant`/`p=`/`p-value`, asserted in a test. Judge failures use `judge_failed` + exclusion, never a 0 score — a zero is indistinguishable from a genuinely bad artifact. The committed baseline is a **structural** capture that proves the harness, not a result; the live Σ-off baseline is still uncaptured.

### AD-1139 (2026-07-25) - governed `oracle_query` tool: Σ reachable from the agentic loop (#1060)

Crew agents can consult the shared commons mid-task instead of only receiving Oracle context passively during perceive. Σ tiers only, never the sovereign episodic shard. **Framing is carried inline** — disposition preamble plus a per-item `ProvenanceEnvelope` — because `AgenticLoop` has no consumer-side wrapper and a bare result would regress the deliberate work that made Oracle context feel grounded rather than arriving unexplained. All six departments, ensign read upward, permission-checked; a denied agent simply does not see the tool. Also generalised `_GATED_TOOL_IDS` so a Captain grant cannot route around the department gate. Default-OFF. 23 tests, 100% coverage.

### AD-1138 (2026-07-25) - semantic index over Ship's Records: Σ discoverable (#1059)

`RecordsStore.search` was keyword-only (`sum(1 for w in query_words if w in raw_lower)`) while ChromaDB was already wired in five other places. Records now join `SemanticKnowledgeLayer.COLLECTIONS` with classification carried in metadata and enforced **at query time** via a `where` clause, so semantic retrieval cannot become a bypass around scope enforcement — post-filtering would return an empty page while matching records exist further down. Records **fail closed** unless a scope is supplied. `build_records_scope_filter` composes two layers: scope level always applies, reader identity is additive and strictly stricter. Keyword fallback retained; default-OFF. Empirically established that ChromaDB `$and`/`$or` require **≥2** expressions, so a lone predicate must be emitted flat — the count is data-dependent, so this fires at runtime rather than review. 55 tests.

### BF-679 (2026-07-25) - Oracle records queries honour reader identity (#1077)

`oracle_query` returned records classified `private` and `department` to **any** calling agent regardless of author: `build_records_scope_filter("ship")` produced `{'classification': {'$in': ['private','department','ship']}}`. The identity layer existed and was correct — it was never called with a reader. Not a regression from AD-1138/1139: `RecordsStore.search` has always been level-only and AD-1138 mirrored it for parity. What changed is reach and intent — AD-1139 turned a passive injection into an agent-invokable pull, and AD-1140 offers agents a `classification` parameter, so an agent-facing `private` that does not bind on the read path is a governance lie. `make_reader_identity_resolver` reconciles `agent_id` (what the Oracle holds) with callsign (what records are authored by). **Both paths fixed at parity, asserted directly** — leaving one stricter than the other is how this survived the first review. Absent reader is **anonymous** (commons only), not privileged; an unresolvable agent, a raising resolver and a malformed resolver result all degrade to anonymous. Deliberate departure from `read_entry`: a `department` record with no `department` frontmatter is author-only rather than readable by everyone who also lacks one — fail closed. 50+ tests.

### BF-675 (2026-07-25) - Oracle Tier 5 sovereign-shard bypass (#1058)

Tier 5 passed `types=None` into `SemanticKnowledgeLayer.search()`, recalling episodes globally and surfacing them labelled `source_tier="semantic"` — bypassing the AD-607e shard filter entirely. Episodes are now excluded **at the source** via a keyword-only `include_episodes` flag (default `True`, so every existing caller stays byte-identical); any episode-typed row that still arrives is relabelled `episodic` so AD-607e can act on it. `/search` requests the episodic tier explicitly so the Captain loses nothing. **Relabelling alone was proven insufficient** — the policy short-circuits on the default `permissive` setting, so the fix had to be at the retrieval source.

### BF-678 (2026-07-25) - AD-1007 capture-loop stub broken by the AD-1146 loop kwargs

CI went red on `ac7bbf54` with one failure in 20,745: `test_ad1007_capability_gate` monkeypatches `AgenticLoop` with a local `_CaptureLoop` whose `__init__` pinned the exact three kwargs of the day, and AD-1146/1147/1148 added behaviour kwargs to that construction site. The test asserts on the tool set handed to `run()`; how the loop is *constructed* is incidental, so the stub now accepts and ignores construction kwargs rather than re-breaking on the next option. Grep-verified as the only `AgenticLoop` monkeypatch in the suite. Missed locally because the wave's targeted gate did not include the AD-1007 file — the same full-gate-only obsolete-contract class as AD-1056 and AD-C-031. **Reusable rule: before adding a kwarg to any class instantiation, grep tests for monkeypatches/stubs of that class and check their `__init__` signatures.**

### AD-1148 (2026-07-25) - tool-result bounds with head+tail preservation (#1073)

Bounds each tool result before it enters the message history. A head slice **and** a tail slice are preserved — many tools print their header first and their summary last, so truncating either end alone destroys the useful part — with an explicit marker reporting how many characters were elided. `max_chars <= 0` disables bounding (default), returning the text by identity so the OFF path is byte-identical. The elision marker is deliberately worded to avoid `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE`, asserted against the real regex, so the runtime never mistakes a bounded result for the model reporting a capability gap. 41 tests.

### AD-1147 (2026-07-25) - bounded parallel tool execution, order-preserving (#1072)

Fans the read-only allowlisted tool calls of one response out concurrently, bounded by `max_parallel_tool_calls`. Mutating and unrecognised tools stay sequential — tools are not uniformly side-effect-free, and an unknown tool is assumed unsafe. Results are returned in **request order** regardless of completion order, so the assistant turn's `tool_calls` array stays aligned with its replies. Default-OFF; the sequential AD-545 path runs verbatim until an operator opts in. 55 tests.

### AD-1146 (2026-07-25) - AgenticLoop multi-turn message fidelity (#1071)

`LLMRequest.messages` and the OpenAI-compatible client already supported a real messages array; the loop was still flattening the whole transcript into one prompt string and returning tool results as untagged user text. The loop now emits `assistant.tool_calls` followed by `role:"tool"` entries keyed by `tool_call_id`. `SessionCompactor` became group-aware (`align_to_group_start`) so a tail slice never orphans a correlation. Default-OFF — with the flag off the AD-545 flattened prompt is built verbatim. 25 tests. Architect review caught a repair: re-compaction could duplicate the summary when neither a system nor a user message survived; guarded.

### AD-1144 (2026-07-25) - RFC 8785 JCS + RFC 7515 JWS for ARD signatures (#1069)

AD-1095 signed trust manifests with hand-rolled canonical JSON and a bare base64 detached signature. That is *near* RFC 8785 but not it: Python sorts keys by Unicode code point where JCS sorts by UTF-16 code unit, and Python float repr differs from ECMAScript. For ASCII keys with no floats the two agree, so it looked interoperable while a third-party harness could not verify a ProbOS manifest without reimplementing ProbOS quirks. New `federation/ard/jcs.py` is a pure-stdlib RFC 8785 canonicalizer with **zero probos imports** (preserving the ARD purity invariant), rejecting NaN/Inf and out-of-range integers rather than losing precision at a signature boundary. Detached-JWS verification pins `alg` to EdDSA rather than reading it from the header, rejects any `crit` per RFC 7515 §4.1.11, refuses a non-empty payload segment, and alphabet-validates base64url before decode (`urlsafe_b64decode` silently discards out-of-alphabet characters). Dual-verify dispatches on signature shape, so existing signatures and the commercial issuer keep verifying with no `specVersion` bump. No new dependency. 74 tests; RFC 8785 vectors pass byte-exact including the non-BMP key case that proves divergence from `sort_keys=True`.

### AD-1142 (2026-07-25) - Crew-child context compaction + token budget (#1063)

**Context.** Crew children ran the `AgenticLoop` with **no compactor, no token budget and no byte bound of any kind**. `max_iterations = 25` bounds *turns*, not bytes; `agentic_loop.tool_result_max_chars` ships at `0`, so each tool result is unbounded; and AD-1147 lets one turn append up to `max_parallel_tool_calls` results. Enough turns of unbounded `read_page` / `http_fetch` output exhaust any provider window, at which point `llm_client.complete()` raises and the loop returns `stopped_reason="error"` — the child fails, its dependents stay blocked, and the failure reads as an LLM error rather than as a design gap. Default-OFF.

**The justification is context-window economics. It is NOT §3.3 Transparency, and that claim does not survive this AD.** Issue #1063's DD asserted that `_persist_tool_trace` already keeps the durable trace, so compaction may safely discard working context. **That is false**, it had propagated three times, and AD-1151 already superseded one instance of it. The honest retention table — written into the `crew_executor` module block, the three config field descriptions, and here:

| What compaction can drop from `messages` | Recorded durably? | By what |
|---|---|---|
| `role:"tool"` content (tool outputs) | **Partially** | AD-1151 `_persist_tool_trace`, bounded by `tool_trace_output_max_chars = 8192` and `tool_trace_max_bytes = 262_144` |
| Assistant reasoning text | **No** | nothing |
| `assistant.tool_calls` as the model saw it | id / name / arguments only | `ToolCallRequest` fields |
| The flattened prompt actually sent | **No** | nothing |
| The compaction summary itself | **No** | nothing |
| The original user task after a second pass | **No** — see Defect A, fixed here | nothing |

The durable trace is not even a superset of the transcript: `tool_result_max_chars` ships at `0` (unbounded) and `resolve_tool_trace_bounds` clamps the durable cap up only to a **non-zero** context cap, so on shipped defaults the trace records **less** than the model saw. This AD claims exactly one thing: **the crew child's working context becomes bounded.** It claims nothing about what survives durably, because for everything except bounded tool outputs, nothing does.

**Two of issue #1063's own acceptance criteria were wrong and are corrected.** (1) *"A long-running child that previously stopped at `max_iterations` completes."* — **false.** Compaction shrinks `messages`; it grants no additional iterations, so a child needing 30 turns still stops at 25 either way. Window exhaustion (`stopped_reason="error"`) and iteration exhaustion (`max_iterations`) are distinct paths and only the first is addressed. The headline test therefore asserts **`error` → `complete`** on the gate alone, with both arms in one test so the delta is attributable; a companion test pins that a `max_iterations` stop is *unchanged* by compaction. (2) *"Overflows the budget and shows the run completing"* — self-contradicting. `token_budget` is a **hard stop** with an immediate return, and `crew_executor` maps it to `status="failed"`. A run that overflows the budget **fails**; it cannot complete. The two knobs are different mechanisms: `crew_compaction_threshold_tokens` is a working-context ceiling (cross it ⇒ shrink and continue), `crew_token_budget` is a cumulative-spend ceiling (cross it ⇒ stop and fail). They are tested separately.

**Defect B — the compaction trigger latched ON permanently (fixed, DD-3).** `agentic_loop.py` compared `result.total_tokens` against `self._compaction_threshold`. `total_tokens` is **cumulative spend across every call and is never reset**, so once it crossed the threshold it was crossed forever and compaction ran on **every remaining iteration** — one extra fast-tier LLM call per turn for the rest of the run, each summarising an already-summarised list. It was also the wrong quantity: `NativeSWEHarnessConfig.compaction_threshold_pct = 0.8` is wired as `int(0.8 × 100_000) = 80_000`, plainly meaning *"80% of a 100K window"*, i.e. **occupancy**. It had been compared against spend since AD-547. Measured on a synthetic 10-iteration loop with high spend and a tiny history: **10 `compact()` calls before the fix, 0 after.** The trigger now reads a new module-local `_estimate_context_tokens(messages)`, which uses the same `len/4` approximation as `session_compactor.estimate_tokens` but **also counts the serialised `tool_calls` payload** an AD-1146 assistant turn carries — `estimate_messages_tokens` reads `content` only and undercounts a structured history by the whole tool-call array (1 vs 123 estimated tokens on a single 400-char tool-call turn). Three consequences, all wanted: the latch is gone (occupancy falls after a successful compaction, so the next iteration does not re-fire); `compaction_threshold_pct` finally means what its name says on the SWE-harness path; and `budget_tokens=self._compaction_threshold` is now *correct*, since the compactor targets the same ceiling that triggered it. **This changes `NativeSWEHarness` behaviour** — accepted, and `native_swe_harness.enabled` defaults to `False`, so no shipped behaviour moves and that path gains the fix for free. The estimator is kept module-local rather than imported so the loop keeps its lack of dependency on `session_compactor`. **Honest limit: it is a character heuristic. AD-547b's forcing function — the first false trip diverging >25% from real model counting — still applies and this AD does not discharge it.**

**Defect A — re-compaction dropped the original user task (fixed, DD-6).** `SessionCompactor.compact`'s second pass spliced `head = [compacted[0]]`. When both a system message and an original-user message survived the first pass, `compacted[0]` is the **system** message, so the original task at index 1 was silently discarded — the child lost the task it was given. Both existing tests missed it: `test_compact_preserves_original_user_task` passed no `budget_tokens` and never reached the branch, and `test_compact_re_compacts_when_over_budget` asserted only `len(out) <= 5`. The head is now rebuilt as the identity **pair** `(system_msg, original_user)`, excluding the summary (so the no-head case does not duplicate it) and de-duplicated by identity. `tail_floor` is computed on the first-pass list and consumed before the rebind, so the head change cannot move it — verified against the live code rather than assumed. Issue #1063's "no changes to `SessionCompactor`" fence was overruled by the acceptance list, and the change is fenced to that splice: `preserve_count`, `SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `align_to_group_start` and `estimate_tokens` are untouched. Seven regressions were added, and an AD-1146 test (`test_compact_over_budget_recompaction_keeps_pairing_intact`) that had **encoded the defective index** was corrected — the summary moved from index 1 to index 2 because the original task now occupies index 1.

**DD-4 — compaction is best-effort by contract, not a guarantee.** `align_to_group_start` preserves an AD-1146/1147 tool-call group **whole**, so `preserve_count = 5` is not an upper bound on tail length: one turn carrying up to `PARALLEL_TOOL_CALLS_MAX = 16` unbounded results is preserved intact and can exceed any threshold on its own. No amount of re-compaction converges on that. So the loop **boundary-validates** the compactor's return (it is injected as `Any` — a module boundary, so Defense in Depth applies) and keeps the previous `messages` when it is not a non-empty list; and when occupancy is still at or above the threshold it logs **once** at WARNING naming the estimate, the threshold and the largest single group, then continues. **No retry loop and no raise** — the existing log-and-degrade tier is preserved, and the run proceeding to a possible provider limit is honest degradation rather than silent degradation.

**DD-2 — a per-child compactor, threaded as explicit kwargs; never shared.** `SessionCompactor` is stateless at HEAD (no `__init__`, one class constant, one method), so sharing the `NativeSWEHarness` instance would be safe *today*. Rejected anyway: crew children run concurrently under `asyncio.Semaphore(max_parallel_subtasks)` (default 3, ceiling 64), statelessness is an accident of the current implementation rather than a declared contract, and any future instance state — a cache, a counter, a rate limiter — would become a silent cross-child race with no test to catch it. Construction is free. `CrewTaskExecutor` therefore builds one `SessionCompactor()` per child invocation, spread into `self._executor.run(...)` alongside the AD-1141 kwargs. **Rejected: reading config inside `WorkItemAgenticExecutor.run`** — that method also serves the AD-839 conversational path and the AD-1072 delegation path, so a config read there would change non-crew behaviour (the same trap AD-1141 DD-1 identified for `task_text`). It stays a pure pass-through and the crew executor owns the policy. **Rejected: a compactor on `runtime`** — reaching `getattr(runtime, "compactor", None)` in the hot path violates DIP and repeats the wiring AD-1141 DD-12 moved to constructor injection.

**DD-7/DD-8 — new fields on `AgenticDispatchConfig`, resolved by clamp, never by validator.** `crew_compaction_enabled` (`False`), `crew_compaction_threshold_tokens` (`60_000`, `ge=1_000 le=1_000_000`), `crew_token_budget` (`None`, `ge=1024`). They live on `AgenticDispatchConfig` rather than `AgenticLoopConfig` because the latter is read by *both* loop construction sites, so a crew-only knob there would silently apply to the SWE harness, which already carries its own `token_budget` and `compaction_threshold_pct` — two sources of truth for one harness is exactly the drift `AgenticLoopConfig`'s docstring exists to prevent. **`crew_compaction_threshold_tokens = 60_000` is a starting value, not a derived one**, and the field description says so: the SWE harness compacts at 80 000, and crew children run up to `max_parallel_subtasks` concurrently, so 60 000 at the default 3-way fan-out is 180 000 of simultaneous provider load. It is the first knob to tune if children still fail with `stopped_reason="error"`. The **AD-1147 interaction is stated arithmetically in the description and asserted in tests**: with `tool_result_max_chars = 0` a single turn can cross any threshold and compaction cannot converge; with a non-zero cap the per-turn ceiling is `max_parallel_tool_calls × tool_result_max_chars` characters, which must stay under `crew_compaction_threshold_tokens × 4`. **No validator relates them.** `resolve_crew_compaction_settings` is a clamp following the AD-1151 `resolve_tool_trace_bounds` precedent: `routers/config.py` writes config by `model_dump() → _deep_merge → SystemConfig(**merged)`, which marks every field explicitly set, so a `model_fields_set`-scoped raise would turn an unrelated `POST /config` into a 422 and could then persist a combination that refuses to boot — and `model_copy(update=...)` skips validators outright, so the guarantee would not even hold. A missing / non-integer / negative / `bool` value degrades to the module default (`type(...) is int` also rejects `bool`); a malformed budget degrades to `None` rather than to a number, because silently inventing a spend ceiling would fail children that succeed today. **`crew_token_budget` is deliberately NOT gated on `crew_compaction_enabled`** — the budget is a Safety Budget ceiling useful with or without compaction, and gating it would mean enabling compaction silently introduced a new failure mode. Enabling it **does** change outcomes: a child that would have produced partial output returns `stopped_reason="token_budget"` ⇒ `status="failed"` ⇒ **dependents stay blocked**. That is stated in the field description and proven by test, and is why it defaults to `None`.

**DD-10 — failure isolation.** `resolve_crew_compaction_settings` must not raise, and settings are normalised in `CrewTaskExecutor.__init__` — **outside** the `try` in the child path that persists `stopped_reason="execution_exception"` — so a mistyped compaction knob cannot fail every child of every session (AD-1141 DD-8 precedent). Compaction failure inside the loop remains absorbed at the existing log-and-degrade tier.

**DD-9 — pinned in `PINNED_AGENTIC_LOOP`, not in `sigma_flags.py`.** Only `PINNED_AGENTIC_LOOP` feeds `config_fingerprint`, so pinning there is what records the compaction posture in the ablation artifact; `sigma_flags.py` does not reach the fingerprint. `set_paths` accepts any type (its same-type check passes `NoneType` against the `None` default — verified empirically), whereas `apply_flags` requires every path to resolve to a **`bool`**, which would force the int/`None` knobs out and split the pinning across two files. And compaction is **not a Σ treatment**: a key carrying the same value in both `SIGMA_ON` and `SIGMA_OFF` would keep the structural guard green while misrepresenting a non-Σ knob as an arm dimension. `sigma_flags.py` is byte-unmodified and both its structural guards are green.

**DD-11 — every model-facing string asserted against the real regex.** Compaction inserts `[CONTEXT SUMMARY — earlier exchanges]` and, on LLM failure, `[compaction summary unavailable]` **into a crew child's prompt** — neither had ever been checked against `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE`, because until this AD they never reached a crew child. All three (including `SessionCompactor.SYSTEM_PROMPT`) are asserted clean against the **imported** regex, not a re-typed copy. `"unavailable"` passes because the pattern's alternative is the phrase `not available`; that was proven, not reasoned about (the AD-1140 lesson).

**Default-OFF, proven byte-identical rather than equivalent.** The OFF path was captured under HEAD `668d0be3` and under this build and hash-compared: identical `_loop_kwargs` key list and order, identical types, identical child `run()` kwargs and key order, identical 14-key evidence set. `resolve_crew_compaction_settings` returns `{}` with the gate off and no budget, zero `SessionCompactor` instances are created across a full crew run, and AD-1141's `task_text` / `extra_context` are re-asserted unchanged. **The three crew contracts are untouched** — the exact 14-key `crew_execution` set, the frozen 12-field `SubtaskResult`, and `description` inside the plan-identity hash — and `_STOPPED_REASONS` gains nothing: compaction changes the *distribution* of stop reasons, not the vocabulary.

### AD-1141 (2026-07-25) - Crew loop wired to Σ: consult before, publish after (#1062)

**Context.** AD-1138 made records discoverable, AD-1139 gave agents a read verb, AD-1140 gave them a write verb — and **nothing called any of it**. Crew children at HEAD were pure isolates: `task_text = active_child.description or active_child.title or ""` (`crew_executor.py:890`), run under a bounded semaphore with the finalizer as the sole convergence point. This AD is the keystone that makes the crew actually use the commons. Default-OFF.

**Correction to issue #1062 — `extra_context` does not reach the prompt.** The issue specified that Σ context enters via the existing `extra_context={...}` seam. Traced end to end at HEAD, that is wrong: `agentic_dispatch` validates `extra_context` against a 7-key allowlist and hands it to `loop.run(context=...)`, but `agentic_loop.py:622-624` builds `messages` from `system_prompt` + `user_message` **only**. `context` is the *tool-invocation* context — it is what `Tool.invoke(context=…)` receives (`:753`, `:820`) and what supplies `agent_id` for logging (`:626`). A Σ payload placed there would be visible to **tools** and invisible to the **model**, the exact opposite of the intent, and widening `_AGENTIC_EXTRA_CONTEXT_KEYS` would only make the payload legal to pass and still not delivered. **The correct seam is `task_text`**, a plain local computed at `crew_executor.py:890` that becomes `user_message` and is **never persisted** — the durable value is `WorkItem.description`. Σ context is therefore a runtime prompt injection, never persisted spec/evidence/result state, which satisfies the epic's constraint while actually reaching the producer. `extra_context` is left byte-identical in both arms.

**Criterion #1 — flags off ⇒ byte-identical, proven by test.** Today's isolated-children behaviour **is** the Nooplex §8.3 ablation control arm and the live Σ-off baseline has not been captured yet (AD-1143 shipped the harness with a structural capture only). An OFF path that is merely "equivalent" destroys the control arm with no recovery, and the epic loses its only empirical claim. `_compose_child_task_text(base)` with every optional argument empty returns `base` **by identity**, so the OFF path is provably a no-op rather than a re-render that happens to match. Tests pin: identical `task_text` against a literal recomputation, `extra_context` of exactly the two crew keys, the exact `run` kwarg key set (which is what proves `tool_ids` is unchanged, since it is assembled inside the dispatch from surfaces this AD does not touch), **zero** `OracleService.query` calls, and key-for-key identical persisted evidence ON vs OFF. Because byte-identity is proven, this merge is decoupled from the baseline capture and is safe in either order.

**Three crew contracts held.** The 14-key `crew_execution` evidence set and the 12-field `SubtaskResult` are asserted as literals and unchanged — one extra key breaks AD-1127 recovery on every restart. `description` is **inside** the plan-identity hash (`crew_session.py:1009`/`:1174`/`:1574`), so the enriched string is composed at runtime and **never persisted**; a projection rebuilt from live post-run rows hashes identically and `_validate_contextual_recovery_plan` stays green.

**DD-3 — the gate, and specifically the zero-cost empty path.** Most crew subtasks are mechanical, and injected context that goes unused still consumes attention and can pull a child off-task. Three gates, cheapest first: a **query floor** (composed query under 24 chars ⇒ no Oracle call at all), a **score floor** (`crew_sigma_min_score`, default 0.35), and an **entry cap** (4). **When nothing clears the floor, literally zero characters are injected** — no header, no note, no whitespace delta. AD-1139's `_EMPTY_BODY` exists because an agent that *asked* deserves an answer; a child that never asked must not be told the commons was silent, which would be pure overhead on the majority path. A pointless consult therefore costs one local Oracle call and zero context, converting "always adds tokens and latency" into "adds tokens only when it has a reason to". The empty-consult string is kept defined and asserted clean so a later AD need not re-derive it, and is asserted **never emitted**. The same collapse applies at the budget boundary: a block that cannot fit even one entry renders as `""` rather than as a frame around an empty body.

**`crew_sigma_min_score = 0.35` is a starting value, not a derived one — and the score it filters is not tier-comparable.** Stated in the config docstring as well as here. `OracleService.query` merges six tiers whose scores are computed six different ways and **applies no normalisation** before sorting: records-keyword is `min(raw/10, 1.0)`, records-semantic and semantic are embedding similarity, operational is `min(word_matches/5, 1.0)`, graph is `weight × confidence × hop_proximity`, health is `overlap/len(query_tokens)` — and **archive is scored by recency alone** (`1/(1 + age_days*0.01)`), carrying no relevance term whatsoever, so any archive entry younger than ~185 days clears a 0.35 floor regardless of relevance. A single floor is therefore biased toward whichever tier scores highest and is honestly a **volume control, not a principled relevance threshold**. Normalising the tiers is the real fix and is out of scope here. The floor is the first knob to tune if AD-1143's ON arm shows a null effect.

**DD-5 — the child decides what to publish. The executor writes nothing.** Three alternatives were rejected: executor auto-publish of `outcome.final_text` (every child output becomes a durable record — the noise failure mode in its purest form, plus a new write surface with its own isolation, budget and duplicate story); finalizer publication of the accepted synthesis (publishes the *parent's* synthesis, not the child's finding, the room already holds it, and it touches the convergence path #1062 forbids); and a `final_text` heuristic (a bad classifier run on every child, whose false positives pollute the commons and whose false negatives are invisible). AD-1140 already ships the verb, already department + rank gated, already per-author rate-limited, already deduped, and a tool failure inside the loop is already isolated by `DispatchToolExecutor`. AD-1141's entire contribution to the write half is **the nudge string plus the ship-wide budget** — zero new write path. The criterion lives in the nudge, in the agent's own language: *a durable finding another crew member would want later; a conclusion with its basis, not a status update.* The child is the only party that knows whether it learned something; the finalizer sees outputs, not process. The nudge is omitted when `publish_finding` is not registered — do not point an agent at a verb it does not hold.

**DD-6 — ship-wide publish budget (40/hr), and an honest statement of what it does not bound.** The AD-1140 review flagged that per-author limiting (12/hr) does not bound ship-wide write volume **at all**; AD-1141 is where the budget belongs because AD-1141 is what creates N concurrent authors. A second `deque` on the same `PublishFindingTool` instance (the registry holds exactly one, so instance state *is* ship state), checked **before** the per-author limiter — reversed, a single author consuming the ship budget would be told it hit its *personal* limit, which is false and would send it into exactly the retry loop the limiter exists to absorb. Over-budget ⇒ framed `output=` with `metadata={"published": False, "reason": "ship_rate_limited"}`, no write, and deliberately **not** an `error=`. The ship slot is consumed only once *both* budgets admit the call, so a per-author refusal does not burn ship capacity. **This bounds the RATE, not the dedup window population:** 40/hr against a 72-hour staleness window admits up to ~2 880 entries inside the window, far past AD-550's 20-entry `max_scan_entries` cap. It does **not** make Layer 3 sound and is not claimed to — that is the AD-1151 lesson (an AD justified on a guarantee that did not hold, whose correction cost a whole AD) applied prospectively.

**DD-7 — AD-554 `check_cross_agent_convergence` is deliberately NOT wired, and here is the arithmetic.** The AD-1140 prompt deferred this decision here and warned that "defaulting to 'yes, it seems useful' is the failure mode". **Cost:** `records_store.py:719-736` runs an **uncapped** first pass — `read_text` + `_parse_document` on *every* `.md` in *every* agent directory, **before** the staleness filter at `:730`; only the second pass is capped (`max_scan_per_agent = 5`). Per-publish cost is therefore O(total notebook files on the ship), growing monotonically with exactly the volume this AD exists to increase, and each report is itself a record the next scan reads. **Alert volume:** it fires at `similarity >= 0.5` when `dept != anchor_department`, needing 2 agents across 2 departments — and crew children of one parent goal are assigned **across departments by design** and produce topically-adjacent findings. That is precisely the shape that trips it, so wiring it would make convergence alerts the *expected* output of a normal multi-department session: bridge alert fatigue on day one. Both cost and alert volume scale with the thing this AD increases. If the Captain wants it later it needs its own flag *and* a cap on the first pass — a separate AD. The uncapped first pass is noted here as a latent defect (next free BF is **BF-680** if filed).

**DD-8 — failure isolation.** The consult is wrapped in its own `try/except Exception` **outside** the executor's `try` at `:903`. That try persists `stopped_reason="execution_exception"`; a consult raising into it would mean a commons outage — an unreachable ChromaDB, a corrupt record — **fails every child of every session**. Log-and-degrade to the unaugmented task text, with a contextual warning. The tool-registry lookup behind the nudge is guarded the same way. Publish failures need no new handling: they are tool calls inside the loop and are already isolated.

**DD-9 — `expected_output` reaches the producer.** It was already persisted into child metadata and already read by the verifier, but the producer never saw the criterion it would be judged against. Read from `active_child.metadata`, bounded at 1000 chars, injected under its own framed header — free, additive, no schema change, no hash impact. Gated on the **same** flag as the commons block; a separate flag would create a third arm the ablation does not model.

**DD-4/DD-10 — framing inline, 2 000 chars hard.** `AgenticLoop` renders a bare user message with no consumer-side wrapper, so framing travels **with** the payload in the AD-1139/AD-1140 parenthetical shape; each entry carries source tier, confidence and age so a low-confidence or aged entry is visibly weightable. Every authored string is asserted against the **real imported** `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE` — never a re-typed copy, because `lack` is a bare substring in that pattern and "black hole" / "slack" / "blackhole" all trip it (AD-1140 hit this for real). Total budget is 2 000 chars with 400 per entry — materially smaller than `oracle_query`'s 6 000, because that budget is for a lookup the agent *asked for* while this injection is unrequested and paid on every child. Truncation is visible via the budget note; the injected character count is logged as a metric so the ablation can attribute context growth, and is **not** written into `crew_execution` evidence (14-key contract).

**DD-11/DD-12 — ablation surface.** Exactly **one** new bool path (`agentic_tools.crew_sigma_context_enabled`) enters both `sigma_flags.py` dicts; the four int/float knobs stay out because `apply_flags` requires every path to resolve to a `bool` and adding one would turn the structural guard red — that guard is working correctly and was not loosened. Two rig gaps are closed: `sigma_rig.py` registered `oracle_query` but **never** `publish_finding`, so no child could publish in the treatment arm; and `sigma_reachability_problems` had no crew-Σ check. Both would have let `SIGMA_ON` silently degrade into a second control arm — the failure mode that function's own docstring says live mode must refuse, because it is invisible in the numbers and would be read as "Σ had no effect". `CrewTaskExecutor` takes the Oracle and its bounds by **constructor injection** (DIP) rather than reaching `getattr(runtime, "oracle", None)` in the hot path; `runtime.oracle` is assigned in `ProbOSRuntime.start` before `finalize_startup` is called, and Tiers 5/6/7 are attached to that same instance later in finalize, so the object reference is correct and no provider callable is needed.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad1141_crew_loop_sigma.py` (**58**), organised by acceptance section: byte-identity OFF (identity assertion, literal recomputation, exact kwarg set, zero Oracle calls, evidence key-for-key); crew contracts (14-key and 12-field literals, plan-hash stability, AD-1127 validator green, description unmutated); consult (framed + provenance-marked delivery, zero-character empty path, query floor with zero Oracle calls, entry cap, char budget, `episodic` never in tiers, raising-consult degradation); publish (headline round trip across a freshly constructed `OracleService` with a different agent in a different department, ship budget proven with **two** authors, ship-before-author ordering, no ship-slot burn on an author refusal, bounded deque); `expected_output`; framing against the real regex across success/empty/truncated/no-tool; ablation surface; and sovereignty (zero episodic calls). **Gates:** focused **58 passed**; crew contracts (`ad859`, `ad859a`, `ad1124`, `ad1125`, `ad1126`, `ad1127`, `ad1128`, `ad1130`, `ad867`, `ad860`) **629 passed**; Σ surface + ablation (`ad1139`, `ad1140`, `ablation/`, `ad1143`, `ad1138`, `bf679`) **273 passed, 1 skipped**. One pre-existing AD-1140 test (`test_the_constructor_accepts_no_memory_surface`) pinned the tool's exact constructor parameter set and was extended by the one DD-6 scalar bound; its sovereignty property — that no *memory surface* is reachable through the constructor — is unchanged and restated in the test.

### AD-1140 (2026-07-25) - `publish_finding`: agent contribution to the commons, Σ writable (#1061)

**Context.** AD-1139 gave a crew agent the *read* half of Σ. There was no write half. `Oracle.write_semantic` dispatches five fixed kinds (`agent` / `skill` / `workflow` / `qa_report` / `event`) and none of them is "a thing an agent worked out"; `RecordsStore.write_notebook` is the right substrate but its three call sites are two proactive-loop paths and one Captain-facing HTTP endpoint, none agent-reachable. An agent that discovered something useful mid-task had nowhere durable to put it. This AD ships the verb and its governance; nothing calls it from the crew loop yet (that is AD-1141).

**Decision — governance is a department gate plus bounds, not consensus and not a rank floor.** A publish is additive and fully reversible (git history, `_archived/`, `publish()` promotion), so the Reversibility Preference axiom is already satisfied; ProbOS consensus gates *destructive* operations and no consensus seam exists on the native-tool path (`agentic_dispatch` routes consensus only for **MCP** tools via `McpToolRisk.CONSENSUS`). A per-claim quorum would also not bind the actual risk, which is volume and quality pollution rather than irreversibility. `ensign` holds `write` upward across all six departments — a commons that excludes half the ship is not a commons, and a narrower grant would corrupt the AD-1143 ablation by measuring "some agents had Σ" instead of "Σ vs no Σ". **The DD-7 bounds are therefore load-bearing, not decoration:** 12 publishes/author/hour, 4000-char claim, 200-char title, 1000-char basis, ≤8 tags of ≤32 chars, and a strict single-segment callsign regex. `publish_finding` joins `_GATED_TOOL_IDS` so a raw Captain grant cannot route around the department layer.

**DD-4 — `fleet` is accepted, written at `ship` scope, and stamped `requested_scope: fleet`.** This is a correction to issue #1061 and it is not cosmetic. Both Oracle Tier 2 paths query Ship's Records at `_RECORDS_QUERY_SCOPE = "ship"`, and `fleet` is level 3 against `ship`'s level 2 — the keyword path `continue`s past it and `build_records_scope_filter("ship")` omits it from the permitted `$in` list. A faithful `classification: fleet` write would therefore be durable, committed, indexed and **retrievable by nobody on this node, including its author**, which directly contradicts the epic's outcome. The tool writes `ship` and preserves the intent in the envelope, so the claim is discoverable today and a later federation transport can read `requested_scope` + `source_node` and propagate. For every non-`fleet` classification `requested_scope == classification`, so there is one code path and no special case in the reader. **The confirmation string is truthful about the substitution.** Verified empirically at this HEAD: the exclusion holds for every reader including `captain`, and a regression guard pins it so a future fix forces this DD to be revisited rather than silently leaving the tool writing narrower than asked.

**BF-679 interaction — the classification vocabulary genuinely binds now, so it is kept whole.** BF-679 (shipped between this prompt's drafting and its build) made both Tier 2 retrieval paths honour reader identity. `private` and `department` are consequently enforced on read, not advisory, so the full four-label vocabulary is exposed to the agent unchanged. BF-679 did **not** touch `_CLASSIFICATION_LEVELS` ordering, which is why the DD-4 `fleet` exclusion above is a separate and still-live constraint.
