**`half_life_days` is a reserved, unconsumed slot and this AD says so.** Issue #1061 cites "AD-873 Ebbinghaus decay" as an existing primitive. It is not one for records: AD-873 is the `_composite_recall_score` reranker in `episodic.py`, over *episodes*, and no decay is applied to Ship's Records anywhere. Writing the field is fine as a landing site for a later implementation; claiming it decays anything would be false. Stated in the field's docstring as well as here — this is the AD-1151 lesson applied prospectively rather than retroactively.

**`RecordsConfig.max_episodes_per_hour` is dead and deliberately left dead.** Issue #1061 names it as the rate-limit mechanism. It has **zero readers in `src/`** (verified; the only live constant is `EpisodicMemory.MAX_EPISODES_PER_HOUR`, which throttles Tier 1 episodes and is unrelated). Re-animating an episode-named dead field would change behaviour for a future reader who correctly assumes it is dead, so AD-1140 carries its own tool-scoped budget and the flag plus its bounds live in one place — which is also what the AD-1143 ablation surface needs.

**DD-8 — sovereignty.** The tool imports, references and reaches no episodic surface. Constructor injection is the structural enforcement: it receives a records store, a callsign resolver, its bounds and a node id, and nothing else. Proven by an AST walk over the module's import statements and by a reachable recording episodic double observing zero calls.

**Reuse over rebuild.** The write goes through `write_notebook` into `notebooks/{callsign}/`, because a dedicated `claims/` subdir would route around every curation guard (AD-550 hard-codes the flat `notebooks/{callsign}/*.md` glob, AD-554 iterates `notebooks/*/`, AD-555 aggregates `list_entries("notebooks")`) — silently bypassing the guards is the worse failure. AD-1138 indexing already lives *inside* `write_entry`, so a publish is auto-indexed with no `index_record` call. The AD-550 dedup gate is called **explicitly** at the tool, mirroring `proactive.py`, and degrades to *write* when it raises. The callsign resolver is BF-679's `make_reader_identity_resolver`, reused rather than duplicated, so an agent authors under exactly the identity Tier 2 later resolves it back to.

**Open observation, not fixed here.** `RecordsStore.read_entry` says *"ship and fleet are readable by all crew"* while `RecordsStore.search(scope="ship")` filters `fleet` out. Those two disagree about whether `fleet` is broader or narrower than `ship`. It predates this epic and fixing it changes Tier 2 retrieval for every caller, so it is left alone; the next free BF is **BF-680** if the Captain wants it filed.

**Tests.** `tests/test_ad1140_publish_finding.py` — **98**. The headline is a real round trip on both retrieval paths: agent A (science) publishes, then a freshly constructed `SemanticKnowledgeLayer` + `OracleService` over the same on-disk paths serve the claim to agent B (engineering, different callsign) — once with the real ChromaDB index and once with the keyword path alone, the latter proving the capability is not contingent on Chroma being healthy. A third variant runs it end-to-end through AD-1139's `oracle_query` tool. Adjacent **387 passed / 1 skipped** across `ad1139` / `ad1138` / `records_store` / `ad550` / `ad552` / `ad555` / `ad722d` / `bf675` / `ad1129` / `bf679` / `semantic_knowledge`; ablation **77** including both `sigma_flags` structural guards.

### AD-1151 (2026-07-25) - persist tool OUTPUTS in the durable trace (#1076)

**Context.** `_persist_tool_trace` serialised only `ToolCallRequest` — `name` / `arguments` / `id` / `timestamp`. The corresponding `ToolCallResult.output` was never persisted anywhere durable: what a tool actually returned existed only in the working message history and was discarded when the run ended. **AD-1148 (#1073) DD-2 and AD-1142 (#1063) both justified themselves against Nooplex §3.3 Transparency on the claim that the durable trace kept the full output. That claim was false; this AD supersedes it.** Every context-reduction feature widened the gap.

**Decision.** Capture the full untruncated results at the loop on an additive `AgenticResult.tool_results` field (appended after `error`, defaulted, so both zero-argument construction sites keep working), populated at the same seam that appends `tool_calls` — capture belongs at the loop, persistence at the caller, so the native SWE harness can reach the outputs later. The blob stays a **bare JSON array**; each entry keeps all four legacy request keys unchanged (superset invariant, asserted directly against `dataclasses.asdict`) and gains `output` / `is_error` / `output_chars` / `output_truncated`. Entries join on `ToolCallResult.id == ToolCallRequest.id`, never by index. Versioning is by **key presence**, which is what a bare array admits — no envelope, no second attachment (the 14-key `crew_execution` set may not gain a key and `WorkItemAgenticOutcome` carries exactly one `tool_trace_ref`). `duration_ms` is deliberately **not** persisted: it is wall-clock, so recording it would make two otherwise-identical runs produce different blobs, and it is already observable on `AGENTIC_TOOL_CALL_COMPLETED`. Two new `AgenticLoopConfig` fields bound the cost — `tool_trace_output_max_chars` (8192, per-output, reusing `truncate_tool_output` unchanged) and `tool_trace_max_bytes` (256 KiB, whole blob, shrunk deterministically from the tail with elision marked, never dropping a call record).

**Default-ON as an explicit convention-#14 carve-out.** This is the second documented carve-out after `warm_boot.enabled`, on the same reasoning: unlike AD-1146/1147/1148 — performance/protocol features where OFF is neutral — this one closes a durability gap, and an audit trail that is off by default does not audit. The cost is bounded (≤256 KiB against a 5 GiB store) and the compatibility risk is structurally absent (array shape and every legacy key preserved). Stated in the field description so it is not mistaken for a #14 violation or copied as precedent. `tool_trace_output_max_chars = 0` reproduces the pre-AD-1151 blob byte-for-byte.

**Honest scope — this NARROWS the §3.3 gap, it does not close it.** The carve-out was originally argued as "closes a stated Transparency guarantee gap." That overstates it in exactly the way AD-1148 DD-2 overstated its own case, so it is corrected here rather than repeated. `tool_result_max_chars` ships at `0` — an **unbounded** working context — and no finite durable cap can retain more than an unbounded transcript. On shipped defaults the trace therefore records *less* than the model saw. What AD-1151 actually guarantees is narrower and still worth having: the output **survives the conversation at all**, and the durable rendering is never bounded tighter than the transcript whenever the transcript is itself bounded.

**Three spec corrections (deviations from `prompts/ad-1151-persist-tool-outputs.md`, which is frozen).**

- **DD-4 — the cross-field validator is deleted, not narrowed.** As specified it raised whenever `tool_trace_output_max_chars < tool_result_max_chars`, which with the 8192 default made any config with `tool_result_max_chars > 8192` unparseable. A first repair scoped it to `model_fields_set`; that is unsound. `model_fields_set` is a parse-time artifact that does not survive a dump/revalidate round trip, and `routers/config.py:246-249` does exactly that on every `POST /config` (`model_dump()` → `_deep_merge` → `SystemConfig(**merged)`), marking every field explicitly set. Reproduced: boot with `tool_result_max_chars: 9000` parses, then any unrelated `POST /config` returns **422**, and `_write_yaml_atomic` materialises `tool_trace_output_max_chars: 8192` into `system.yaml` — after which a later hand-raise of the context cap **prevents boot**. `model_copy(update=...)` skips validators outright, so the guarantee did not even hold. The invariant is now enforced at *resolve* time by an upward clamp in `resolve_tool_trace_bounds` (`output_max_chars = max(output_max_chars, tool_result_max_chars)`), which is monotone, round-trip safe and cannot brick a config. The clamp is skipped when the durable cap is `0`, since that value is an explicit "do not persist outputs" opt-out rather than an inversion; re-enabling persistence against it would violate the OFF-path byte-identity guarantee. Both fields keep `ge=0`.
- **DD-5 — the durable head/tail split is derived from the durable cap, not inherited from AD-1148.** As specified, `build_tool_trace_payload` passed `tool_result_head_chars` / `tool_result_tail_chars` straight through to `truncate_tool_output`. But `max_chars` there is a keep-whole *trigger*, not a ceiling on retention: at the defaults `content_budget = 8038 ≥ head + tail = 6000`, so the proportional shrink never engaged and retention was pinned at **6155 chars for every durable cap** — 8 192, 20 000, 50 000 and 150 000 all measured identical. At a 20 000-char context cap the context and durable renderings came out **byte-identical**, so the feature added exactly zero information. `truncate_tool_output` is left untouched (the AD-1148 boundary holds); the builder now derives the slices from the durable cap at the same 2:1 ratio, after reserving the elision marker. Measured after the fix: 8 192 → 8 192, 20 000 → 20 000, 50 000 → 50 000, 100 000 → 100 000 retained; monotone, and durable ≥ context at every pair tested. `head_chars` / `tail_chars` are consequently removed from `build_tool_trace_payload`'s signature and from `_TOOL_TRACE_BOUND_FIELDS` rather than left as dead parameters.
- **DD-5 — the tail-shrink is O(n) serialisations, not O(n²).** The specified loop re-serialised the whole entries list per elision. Measured: 800 calls → 801 serialisations / 1.57 s; 3 200 calls (reachable inside `max_iterations ≤ 200` × `PARALLEL_TOOL_CALLS_MAX = 16`) would have blocked the event loop for tens of seconds inside `async def _persist_tool_trace`. Each output's encoded size is now measured once and subtracted from the overage to choose the elision set, which is serialised in one pass; the exact one-at-a-time loop is retained as a residual backstop that normally runs zero iterations. **2 serialisations at every call count**, 3 200 calls in 33 ms. Termination, determinism and "requests are never dropped" are unchanged, verified against an in-test oracle implementing the old loop across **357 caps with 0 divergences**.

Additionally, a non-`str` `ToolCallResult.output` is now coerced exactly as `ToolCallResult.from_tool_result` does (`None` → `""`). Previously one hostile output raised inside `len()`, the caller's outer `except` degraded, and the **entire trace** — every call record included — was lost, contradicting the DD-5 guarantee this AD exists to protect.

**Tests.** `tests/test_ad1151_durable_tool_outputs.py` — **57**. Adjacent 170 (`ad1148`/`ad1147`/`ad1146`/`ad545`/`ad859a`/`ad1007`/`attachment_reaper`), with `test_ad1148_tool_result_bounds.py` green **unmodified**; evidence-contract guards 88 (`ad1125`); config surface 96 (`config`/`ad741`/`ad468`/`ad549`) since a validator was removed. `ToolCallResult`, the `Tool` protocol, the 14-key evidence set and `stopped_reason` are asserted unchanged.

### BF-674 (2026-07-24) - shared LLM endpoint outage cooldown (#1065)

**Context.** At 10:53:26 VS Code refreshed chat models; from 10:53:30 through 10:54:19 its shared Copilot proxy returned 157 empty HTTP 200 replies. Fresh and six-call concurrent probes were healthy after recovery. ProbOS health marked standard/fast/deep unreachable but did not gate execution, so each queued background request retried and fell through every alias on the same endpoint, converting one external refresh into a retry storm.

**Decision.** Govern background admission by the actual endpoint key, not tier alias. After persistent empty/error outcomes, open a bounded shared cooldown with an outage epoch; admit exactly one half-open recovery owner after expiry; let Captain-critical calls bypass; preserve cache reads and independent endpoints. Only matching epochs may reopen or close an outage, and every cancellation, transport failure, error envelope, persistent empty reply, and health-probe path releases half-open ownership. Surface cooldown telemetry and expose a bounded default-on config with zero as the compatibility escape hatch.

**Tests.** **29 dedicated + 247 compatibility** tests passed. The consolidated suite passed **20,465 / 33 skipped / 7 subtests** in **764.00s**. Architect review: **APPROVED**.

### BF-676 (2026-07-24) - lifecycle-owned agent transport teardown (#1066)

**Context.** SIF correctly identified a removed MCP consensus voter that remained subscribed after pool scale-down. JetStream also had one fewer durable dispatch consumer than local IntentBus subscribers because startup subscription failure returned `None` without retry. Registry, pool, local mesh indexes, tracked NATS recipes, live handles, durable consumers, and recovery tasks had no single symmetric lifecycle owner.

**Decision.** Make AgentOnboardingService the symmetric mesh wire/unwire boundary and ResourcePool the serialized lifecycle owner. Every start, health pass, scale, recycle, exact prune, and stop runs through one cancellation-deferred pool lock. Transport teardown cancels/awaits exact-agent subscription tasks, atomically tombstones/removes both core and dispatch recipes under the NATS mutation lock, retains failed handles for retry, deletes the durable consumer, and only then removes local intent/capability/gossip indexes. Same-ID replacement cannot begin before teardown succeeds. Failed spawn, wiring, stop, unregister, or rollback retains the remaining registry/pool/runtime owner. Shutdown attempts all pools, retains failed owners, always drains IntentBus before NATS stop, and re-raises deferred cancellation only at the tail. Retry transient dispatch-consumer creation three times.

**Tests.** **284 focused** lifecycle/NATS/scaling/shutdown tests plus an independent **8-case** Architect gate passed. The consolidated suite passed **20,465 / 33 skipped / 7 subtests**. Final Architect review: **APPROVED**, zero Required findings.

### BF-677 (2026-07-24) - `crew_trace` provenance retention (#1067)

**Context.** The agentic executor intentionally writes content-addressed execution provenance with origin `crew_trace`, but AttachmentStore did not recognize that origin. Each trace warned and was coerced to `chat_attachment`, corrupting retention classification and flooding logs.

**Decision.** Add `crew_trace` to the canonical known-origin contract and filesystem store. Keep traces durable with no age TTL, but place them below Captain chat attachments in LRU priority so storage pressure removes provenance before user-authored content.

**Tests.** **19 dedicated** attachment/agentic tests and the final **20,465-test** consolidated gate passed. Architect review: **APPROVED**. BF-677 is the new BF ceiling; AD-1133 remains the top-level AD ceiling.

### AD-1133 (2026-07-23) - bounded live CrewSession and room refresh (#1052)

**Context.** AD-1132 exposed durable CrewSession state, but open HXI surfaces refreshed only through initial GETs and legacy polling. The existing `/ws/events` path lacked auth-before-accept, bounded lifecycle ownership, authoritative sequence/generation, message/artifact invalidation, and Crew-safe projections. Highest landed top-level was **AD-1132**; **AD-1133 is the new top-level ceiling**, while **BF-673 remains the BF ceiling**.

**Decision.** Reuse the sole WebSocket path. Add awaited live-only event-listener handles, exact NATS subscription release, owner-first bounded snapshots, generation/sequence envelopes, bounded per-client queues, and per-item failure containment. Emit IDs-only post-commit message/artifact events, project Crew parent/child work events through AD-1132, suppress raw session metadata, and let only visible owners repair via bounded GETs with stale-token guards. Remove BF-644 polling, retain one accessible manual refresh, and preserve exactly-one event ownership between stores/services and routes. Normalize only exact trusted event types; move the immutable CrewTrustEffect contract to consensus.

**Tests.** AD-1133 focused gates passed **678 backend + 155 UI**, production build, and one full-App Playwright flow. Consolidated closeout passed **20,398 Python / 33 skipped / 7 subtests**, **2,221 Vitest / 1 skipped**, a **2,616-module build**, and **8/8 Playwright**. Final reviews were **APPROVED**. Issue #1052 closes on push; parent #1041 closes after remote checks and child reconciliation.

### AD-1131 (2026-07-22) - CrewSession outcome delivery and metrics (#1050)

**Context.** AD-1126 produced terminal verified results and AD-1127 could resume them, but Captain delivery and operational measurement were not durable or idempotent. Replayed terminal events could duplicate notices, and metrics lacked a bounded session denominator.

**Decision.** Persist one delivery fact per terminal session revision beside final publication, reconcile ambiguous commits, and emit one room-linked done/failed/blocked notification while preserving non-session AD-846 behavior. Compute bounded session-denominated rates and percentiles from metadata-only facts; return zero-safe empty windows and never include result bodies, secrets, or artifact bytes. Lifecycle shutdown owns listener cleanup and cancellation.

### AD-1130 (2026-07-22) - outcome-only CrewSession trust (#1049)

**Context.** Legacy room conversation could update trust from linguistic convergence, while CrewSession verification needed trust to reflect actual attempted outcomes. Penalizing a peer for correct rejection, missing authority, cancellation, or governance denial would create lockout feedback loops.

**Decision.** Derive idempotent raw-Beta trust effects only from durable attempted terminal evidence. Reward verified producer success and correct verifier refutation/correction; record producer failure only for attempted work; preserve all neutral/no-attempt paths. Use deterministic bounded Shapley attribution, exact outbox receipts/post-state reconciliation, and overlapping-drain exclusion. Own the immutable `CrewTrustEffect` in consensus while cognitive derivation re-exports the same class.

**Tests.** **1,057 changed-surface** tests and final consolidated gates passed. Review was **APPROVED**.

### AD-1129 (2026-07-21) - governed bounded EventLog query tool (#1048)

**Context.** Crew agents could diagnose only what prompts exposed and could not query already-authoritative EventLog rows without inventing facts or reaching into SQLite. A raw SQL or HTTP export would bypass governance and leak content.

**Decision.** Introduce a narrow injected EventLog query protocol and read-only registered tool. Resolve live identity/department/rank/grants, enforce bounded filters/windows/limits, redact output, audit success and denial safely, and fail closed on partial authority. Expose no arbitrary SQL, raw DB path, network export, write/delete/prune capability, or new agent pool.

**Tests.** The changed-surface batch passed **220** tests and failed three AD-1072 fixture nodes; after repair, those three nodes passed together under `-n 0`. Final consolidated gates passed. Review was **APPROVED**.

### AD-1128 (2026-07-21) - unified CrewSession ingress and dedup (#1047)

**Context.** AD-1127 owned execution lifecycle, but Captain requests, explicit room work, and agent-originated `[CREW]` used separate paths, could duplicate equivalent sessions, and passive UI mounting created tasks. Provenance and partial provisioning recovery were inconsistent.

**Decision.** Make `CrewSessionService.open_or_resume()` the single ingress authority. Validate frozen server-owned principals, canonicalize/fingerprint goals, perform bounded exact-first semantic matching with a double scan around decomposition, and atomically resume or provision one parent, linked room, recovery plan, and lifecycle schedule. Support Captain NL, explicit Start Work, and Lieutenant+ agent ingress; fail closed for Ensign, spoofed provenance, invalid scoring, terminal reopen, and unauthorized blocked retry. Remove passive UI POSTs.

### AD-1127 (2026-07-21) - CrewSession lifecycle recovery (#1046)

**Context.** AD-1126 made verified finalization durable but left CrewSession scheduling, restart recovery, bounded retry, and shutdown ownership dependent on in-process invocation. Highest landed top-level was **AD-1126**; **AD-1127 is the new top-level ceiling**, while **BF-673 remains the BF ceiling**.

**Decision.** Make `CrewOrchestrator` the sole lifecycle owner with one parent-keyed strong task map, independent parent and child concurrency bounds, one globally bounded startup scan, synchronous admission close, bounded typed retry, and cancellation-deferred drain before dependency shutdown. Recover discussing, executing, and verifying sessions from strict phase checkpoints; use deterministic two-stage plan identity, exact child-plan adoption/install transactions, content-addressed execution and finalization records, and exact Artifact reconciliation. Checkpoint graceful cancellation and re-raise the first exact cancellation; never replay ambiguous in-progress child work. Keep the feature default-off and exclude AD-1128+ ingress, authorized retry, EventLog, trust, delivery, API/UI, WebSocket, schema, YAML, and dependency work.

**Context.** AD-1125 intentionally stopped durable sessions in `executing`, leaving independent convergence, stale-child-safe final verification, and durable result publication unresolved. ### AD-1124 (2026-07-17) - durable CrewSession contract (#1043)

**Context.** The AD-858–862 crew-collaboration spine had no durable, bounded session contract tying one parent WorkItem to its collaboration room. Generic workforce consumers depend on the established `draft/open/in_progress/review/blocked/done/failed` vocabulary, so storing session-specific fine states in `WorkItem.status` would break compatibility. Existing whole-column metadata writers also risked clobbering sibling keys, and Python equality is not exact JSON equality because booleans alias integers. Highest landed top-level was **AD-1123**; **AD-1124 is the new top-level ceiling**, while **BF-673 remains the BF ceiling**.

**Decision.** Add one built-in `crew_session` WorkType that starts in `draft`, plus one strict versioned `CrewSessionContract` at `WorkItem.metadata["crew_session"]`. Fine state is authoritative in metadata (`discussing`, `executing`, `verifying`, `blocked_needs_captain`, `done`, `failed`); `WorkItem.status` remains the exact coarse projection (`open`, `in_progress`, `review`, `blocked`, `done`, `failed`). `CrewSessionService` initializes, reads, and transitions only an existing parent bound to exactly one existing `ChatThread` whose `task_id` is the parent id; zero, duplicate, wrong-task, and wrong-thread rooms fail closed. `WorkItemStore.merge_work_item_metadata()` performs shallow top-level merge, JSON-type-exact nested expected-value CAS, and expected work-type/status/assignee checks under one shared runtime-local row-write lock held through commit; metadata and an optional validated coarse status update atomically. The input-attachment and crew-synthesis parent writers use the same primitive. Composition remains behind the existing default-off orchestrator gate. Add no database schema or migration, config/YAML, API/UI, parent/room provisioning, execution, verifier, lifecycle runner, trust, learning, or notification path.

**Tests.** The AD-1124 module contains **57 cases**. Fresh serial/offline Gates 0–2 passed **57 + 221 + 161** with no warnings. The full parallel suite passed **19,643 / 33 skipped / 0 failed** with **455 provenance-only pre-existing warnings and zero changed-path warnings**. Legacy `work_items` columns remained unchanged, frozen excluded paths had no diff, and final review was **APPROVED**. Issue #1043 closes only when this commit is pushed; parent #1041 remains open.

The full parallel suite passed **19,581 / 33 skipped** with **458 provenance-only pre-existing warnings and zero changed-path warnings**. Final Architect review: **APPROVED**. ### AD-1123 (2026-07-17) — bounded federation one-way relay (#1040)

**Context.** AD-722b-5 shipped local avatar-telemetry subscription/rate/callback plumbing, but #659 remained blocked because federation offered only untargeted intent request/response and AD-730-4 directed DM request/response. Neither protocol is appropriate for bounded high-rate one-way state. Highest landed top-level was **AD-1122**; **AD-1123 is the new top-level**, while **BF-672 remains the BF ceiling**.

**Decision.** Add a generic but closed `FederationMessage.type == "relay_one_way"` datagram. Its payload has exactly `{relay_version, target_node_id, topic, payload, hop_count}` with version 1 and hop 0. `FederationBridge.relay_one_way()` addresses one configured connected non-self peer through the existing `send_to_peer()` method; there is no acknowledgement, response, correlation map, retry, queue, replay, ordering promise, fanout, or background worker. An immutable constructor-injected topic registry maps one canonical local name to one exact synchronous validator and async sink. The supplied callable itself must have the exact effective signature and conservative stdlib coroutine classification; ordinary callable/signature/coroutine-metadata failures normalize to exact `ValueError("relay_topics_invalid")`, while lifecycle `BaseException` propagates and no callable is probe-invoked. Sender and receiver independently detach exact built-ins under fixed depth, node, character, aggregate UTF-8, signed-64, and complete-wire byte ceilings; reject cycles, hostile subclasses, nonfinite/binary values, and explicit credential/private-key shapes; give validators isolated copies; and require literal `True`. One relay-local exact-string `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$` predicate admits server-local source/target plus wire source/target before nested work. The receiver applies a finite 64/s sliding window per configured source/topic and invokes exactly one registered sink with server-owned `source_node`; malformed, saturated, rejected, failed, post-stop, or unknown traffic sends no response and touches no intent/event, trust, Hebbian, or learning surface. Real task cancellation propagates. Startup closes admission and clears rate state before wiring, opens only after the gossip task exists, and remains taskless/restartable on wiring failure. Production passes `relay_topics=()` explicitly, so behavior is inert until a child registers a semantic contract. Configured-peer membership is a deployment/transport ACL and is explicitly **not cryptographic source authentication**.

**Tests + gates.** The new module contains **133 cases**. Independent serial/offline Gates 1–4 passed **224 + 466 + 77 + 376** tests; Gate 3 retained only five known BF-326 warnings and Gate 4 only two known dependency deprecations. Ten complete module repetitions passed; independent million-entry, complete-wire, secret false-positive, exact-128, hostile-metadata, 512-key/32,768-sample rate-cardinality, and 100-task rate-concurrency probes passed. All **13/13** frozen bridge/transport executable AST hashes remain exact, no transport file changed, and the tests use real composition/narrow behavioral fakes with no `MagicMock`/`Mock`/`AsyncMock`. Final Architect review: **APPROVED**. This closes #1040. It unblocks #659/AD-722b-5a but does not implement or close the telemetry-specific producer, subscription, validator, receiver sink, or HXI work.

### AD-730-4 (2026-07-17) — directed federated vision DMs (#634)

**Context.** AD-730 enabled local per-agent vision DMs, AD-731 moved image authority from bus bytes to content-addressed attachment references, and AD-731a Option B plus BF-672 made cross-host bytes available through authenticated fetch and prefetch-before-delivery. Federation still lacked a safe way to name one remote node and one exact remote subscriber without the legacy router/broadcast fan-out. AD-730-4 is a pre-reserved AD-730 subdecision; **AD-1122 remains the top-level ceiling and BF-672 remains the BF ceiling.**

**Decision.** Add a DM-only `FederationBridge.forward_direct_message(target_node_id, intent)` path and a correlated `request_peer()` seam in all three transports. The wire names one configured stable node ID plus one exact stable local agent ID, carries bounded DM text and canonical SHA-256 references only, and validates exact seven-key request, two-key response, and six-key result schemas. The receiver admits the configured source/target/DM/params/subscriber before BF-672 prefetch, then calls exact `IntentBus.send()` once with server-owned provenance; it never broadcasts, resolves callsigns, advertises a roster, retries another target, or falls back. Iterative exact-built-in result detachment bounds depth, nodes, string characters/bytes, and final response bytes; all response strings reject a leading case-insensitive `data:image/` prefix. Transport correlation uses unique ownership, registration-before-send, closed admission, and identity-safe cleanup while malformed non-targeted legacy responses retain their peer queue. Sender-local monotonic timestamps are never compared across hosts; TTL is an origin-wait and receiver-local execution budget, not request-age or replay protection. Configured-peer admission is explicitly **not cryptographic source authentication**; generic arbitrary-intent addressing, discovery, signatures, replay state, trust/Hebbian activation, config, and user-facing surfaces are not part of this decision.

**Tests + gates.** The new module contains **229 cases**. Independent serial/offline Gates 1–4 passed **377 + 417 + 370 + 472** tests; Gate 4 retained only the two known third-party deprecation warnings. Coverage includes the two-organized-bridge target-only prefetch path, privacy/no-fallback behavior, exact schemas and safe logs, C1–C9 adversarial bounds, hostile transport markers, pending-map lifecycle races, malformed-ID carveout, serializer parity, and HEAD/worktree legacy validator literal/executable-AST identity. Final Architect review: **APPROVED**. This closes #634 without changing the AD-1122 or BF-672 ceilings.

### AD-731a-1d (2026-07-16) — validated reference-only federation attachment send (#638)

**Context.** AD-731a-1 shipped authenticated HTTP serve/fetch verification, AD-731a-1c shipped receive-side missing-ref resolution, and BF-672 wired that resolver before local broadcast, but the federation send boundary still stripped the rich vision surface. The selected Option-B close path keeps the AD-731 invariant—bus messages carry content-addressed refs while the attachment store carries bytes—without requiring replication. **AD-731a-1d is a pre-reserved AD-731a subdecision, not a new top-level AD; AD-1122 remains the top-level ceiling and BF-672 remains the BF ceiling.**

**Decision.** Replace whole-surface stripping at the single `FederationBridge.forward_intent()` semantic boundary with a validated, reference-only sanitizer. Admit at most eight unique canonical SHAs across singular, plural, and vision surfaces; independently inspect at most 64 plural and 64 vision recognized-candidate positions. Those bounds do not make generic top-level params globally bounded: the existing open mapping still receives a complete exact-key preflight and shallow preservation, while unrelated nested values are not traversed. Exact built-in checks and two-pass approved-field preflights make hostile top-level, message, block, and source keys total without invoking overrides; unsafe mappings degrade only at their specified surface, and reconstructed output contains only approved constant keys and validated values. Make `attachment_ids` the sole API authority for persisted attachment metadata, discard caller-authored `metadata.attachments`, and return HTTP 413 before any side effect when a positively identified group supplies more than eight resolved images; never truncate, and preserve all resolved non-image refs. Extend receive extraction to plural refs. Preserve BF-672 prefetch-before-local-broadcast ordering, AD-731a-1 authenticated MIME/size/SHA verification before store, and last-mile vendor conversion that round-trips the exact origin bytes. NATS Object Store or other replication remains an optional availability follow-up, not a correctness prerequisite and no longer a requirement for retiring the old strip.

**Tests + gates.** Independent final gates passed **276 focused + 159 first-party producer-audit + 163 blast** tests, covering hostile-key totality, scoped 8/64/64 bounds, server-owned metadata, fixed group ingress rejection before side effects, plural extraction, real prefetch-before-broadcast, authenticated fetch verification, and vendor-byte round-trip. Final Architect review: **APPROVED**. This pre-reserved subdecision closes #638 without changing the AD-1122 or BF-672 ceilings.

### AD-1122: Sensorium budget telemetry v2 — truthful units, attributed overages, sustained-warning debounce (#1036)

**Context.** AD-666 counted characters in the two merged chain-sensorium dictionaries but exposed a token-named threshold, warned on every over-budget cycle, and described instruction-space crowding that its measurement seam could not prove. The seam runs after cognitive-state and situation dispatch/merge but before formatted memories, standing orders, prompt construction, or the provider request; it therefore measures neither the full request nor the model window. AD-1122 makes that boundary truthful and makes repeated overages actionable without changing any reasoning input. Highest landed top-level was **AD-1121**; **AD-1122 is the new top-level**, while the BF ceiling remains **BF-669**.

**Decision.** Preserve the exact observe-only `_track_sensorium_budget(cognitive_state, situation) -> int` seam and its single caller. Count each surviving non-empty string as a distinct `(bucket, output_key)` contributor, without deduplicating the same key across cognitive and situation buckets. Emit only `{bucket, output_key, layer, chars, estimated_tokens}` metadata: resolve `layer` from the matching registry paths, use `null` for zero or ambiguous layer matches, sum the existing per-entry token estimates before truncation, sort by `(-chars, output_key, bucket)`, and retain the configured top N. Values, snippets, hashes, digests, embeddings, and content-derived identifiers are forbidden. Make `warning_chars` the canonical config field; canonical-first `AliasChoices("warning_chars", "token_budget_warning")` and a read-only compatibility property preserve legacy input. As a build-specific preservation decision, the tracked operator `config/system.yaml` keeps its legacy key and is untouched; compatibility is implemented in Pydantic rather than by rewriting local configuration. Debounce is bounded per-agent scalar state only: a strict `total_chars > warning_chars` first crossing emits `crossed`; one unconsumed `>= warning_chars * warning_escalation_ratio` transition emits `escalated` before cooldown; `>= warning_cooldown_seconds` emits `sustained`; and only a strict fall below `warning_chars * warning_rearm_ratio` rearms. Initial severe crossings consume escalation, and disable, threshold change, stop, or completed rearm resets the episode. No task, timer, history, persistence, or global map is introduced. Extend the existing `SensoriumBudgetExceededEvent` additively with `estimated_tokens`, `character_threshold`, `reason`, `suppressed_count`, `peak_chars`, and metadata-only `top_contributors`; keep the existing event type and legacy fields. Commit debounce state before warning/event delivery. Logging failures remain non-fatal, and event-sink failure emits a contextual degradation warning without rollback or transition replay. This remains observation only: no prompt content/order/wrapper, sensorium dispatch, context selection, attention, model tier, token cap, LLM request count, truncation, dropping, or enforcement changes.

**Tests + gates.** Five serial, isolated, local/offline, `RuntimeWarning`-strict gates completed with **628 passed / 2 expected local-embedding skips** across config/event behavior, sensorium dispatch and merge, chain execution, attention/prompt invariance, and CognitiveAgent lifecycle/spine coverage. Tests prove canonical/legacy alias precedence and serialization, temporary legacy-YAML loading, metadata privacy and deterministic attribution, exact strict debounce/hysteresis boundaries, per-agent and stop isolation, additive JSON-safe event serialization, logging/event failure containment, and unchanged AD-723/AD-1028 prompt snapshots. Final Architect review: **APPROVED**. Tracker closeout is limited to `PROGRESS.md` and `DECISIONS.md`; no roadmap or era-file update is made.

### AD-1121: Live cascade-confab divergence probe (detection) (#1024)

**Context.** The `CASCADE_CONFAB` anti-pattern is coded in `emergence_taxonomy.py` (`is_anti_pattern=True`) but only ever classified POST-HOC — it never fires live. AD-1119 resolves referents against ship ground truth deterministically; AD-1120 steers the crew to the "unresolvable" close when a central referent is UNRESOLVED. AD-1121 adds the DETECTION half: a SelfCheckGPT-style (arXiv 2303.08896) probabilistic self-consistency probe for the exact case the deterministic resolvers cannot settle — an UNRESOLVED central referent — so the crew's live confabulation is flagged + counted in near-real-time and the Captain is notified. The load-bearing research property (CoVe arXiv 2309.11495): the probe must sample the LLM INDEPENDENTLY and WITHOUT the room context — independent context-free samples of "does `<X>` exist on this ship?" converge for a real referent and fail to consistently affirm for a fabricated one (the live `e77acec7` case); shared poisoned context makes peer "verification" confirmatory (AD-506b can't fire — each message is novel), a context-free probe breaks that dependency. **STEP-0 empirical descope.** The epic sketch bundled "persist room transcripts (in-RAM only, 0-byte WAL)" — but that forensic claim was about `ward_room.db`, NOT the group-chat store. Verified against HEAD: group chat lives in `ChatThreadStore` (`threads/__init__.py`), wired at `runtime.py` L462 with a real on-disk `chat_threads.db`; `_connect()` opens `sqlite3.connect(db_path, isolation_level=None)` = AUTOCOMMIT, so `create_thread`/`append_message` durably commit every message immediately (the Captain empirically recovered a 2026-06-10 thread a month later via `GET /api/threads/{id}/messages`). Rebuilding persistence would duplicate a shipped capability (DRY) → **transcript persistence REMOVED from AD-1121 scope; AD-1121 = probe + detection only.** Highest landed top-level was **AD-1120**; **AD-1121 is the new top-level**; this COMPLETES the cascade-confabulation prevention epic (AD-1119 guard / AD-1120 behavioral / AD-1121 detection).

**Decision.** Five additive pieces, all Tier-2 honest-degrade. **(a) Pure runtime-free probe (DD-1121-2/3/4, DIP).** NEW `src/probos/cognitive/confab_probe.py`: `probe_referent(llm_client, token, ...)` takes the INJECTED `llm_client` (no hard runtime import) and the referent TOKEN STRING ONLY — it has no parameter through which the seed/transcript can reach it, so the CONTEXT-FREE guarantee is enforced BY THE SIGNATURE, not by discipline (mirrors the AD-1119 pure-module + thin-router-wiring pattern). N=3 independent draws (module constants `_CONFAB_PROBE_SAMPLES/_TIER="fast"/_TEMPERATURE=1.0/_MAX_TOKENS=160` — the high temperature is load-bearing for genuinely independent draws) via `asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True)`; each `prompt` carries only the token + a fixed instruction, `system_prompt` is a fixed minimal Ship's-Computer string with NO transcript slot. Divergence = existence-affirmation consistency (black-box, no logprobs): `_classify_existence(text)` AFFIRMs iff the sample has content AND matches NONE of `_CONFAB_DENIAL_RE`; FLAG iff `affirm_rate < 0.5` AND `usable >= 2`; `<2` usable → ABSTAIN. Rationale: a fabricated referent yields EITHER consistent denials (rate → 0) OR divergent hallucinations that mostly fail to affirm one real entity — both caught by low affirm-rate; a real referent yields consistent affirmations (rate → 1). Pure token-overlap alone is WRONG here (consistent denials have HIGH overlap → would miss the dominant fabrication case). **(b) Precision guard = the AD-1119 UNRESOLVED gate (DD-1121-5).** The probe runs ONLY on a central referent AD-1119's resolvers ALREADY marked UNRESOLVED — a real referent they know → RESOLVED → never central → never probed; the residual risk (a real referent both the resolvers AND the base LLM miss) is handled by making the output a Captain notification for human adjudication, NEVER an auto-action. **(c) Reuse the single verdict; central token computed once (DD-1121-6).** The AD-1120 `_select_central_cue` is refactored to a token-selector `_select_central_referent(verdict, seed_text) -> str | None` (same kind/stop-word filter + the ONE git-HEAD availability probe, now returning the TOKEN); `_observe_referent_grounding` computes the central token ONCE for BOTH the probe and the AD-1120 cue return — no second gate build, no second git-HEAD probe. **(d) Surface, don't act; best-effort, non-blocking (DD-1121-7/8).** On a flag `_probe_cascade_confab` (1) records a `CASCADE_CONFAB` observation via a NEW additive public `EvidenceCollector.record_observation(...)` that reuses the AD-454 dedup + gapless `OBS-NNNN.yaml` `_persist` tail (`author_id=thread_id` → one OBS per room per window; skip when the collector is None — honest-degrade), and (2) ALWAYS posts `runtime.notification_queue.notify(..., notification_type="action_required", suggested_action=None)` — NO auto-terminate/close, the verdict is a signal for human adjudication. The probe is scheduled as a best-effort `asyncio.create_task` held in a NEW public `runtime.confab_probe_tasks` set + `add_done_callback(discard)` (async discipline; mirrors `_nats_publish_tasks`) so it NEVER delays the crew reply. `record_observation` is CALLED ONLY by AD-1121 → AD-454 stays byte-identical. **(e) Default-OFF byte-identical (DD-1121-9).** NEW third flag `config.grounding.confab_probe_enabled: bool = False`; `_observe_referent_grounding`'s tail short-circuits `if not (confab_probe_enabled or ground_before_collaborate_enabled): return None` BEFORE any probe work (so the 3 AD-1119 call-site tests still hit `None` with no extra git-HEAD probe, and the AD-1120 B2 cue path is byte-identical), no task is scheduled, `record_observation` is never called. **NOT built (out of scope):** transcript persistence (STEP-0 DRY), room auto-termination/close (surface-only), notification re-architecture, a new LLM tier (reuse `"fast"`), consensus/trust/Hebbian writes, the AD-567f `CASCADE_CONFABULATION_DETECTED` event / counselor, and any edit to `referent_gate.py` / `emergence_taxonomy.py` / `EmergentDetector`.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad1121_confab_probe.py` (10, BF-287 real fixtures — real `SystemConfig()`/`NotificationQueue`/`EvidenceCollector(tmp output_dir)` + a scripted `_ScriptedLLM` recording every request; NO MagicMock at the substrate boundary; git avoided via an `entity`-kind central token `node oracle_probe`): divergent (3 denial samples) → through the seam, after awaiting the scheduled task, exactly one `CASCADE-CONFAB` OBS file + one `action_required` notification naming the token with `suggested_action=None`; consistent (3 affirmations) → no OBS, no notification; **context-free** — a `SECRET_CANARY_TOKEN` seed NEVER a substring of ANY recorded prompt/`system_prompt` (only the referent TOKEN reaches the probe); failure/abstain — every sample raises / `llm_client=None` / 1-usable → `is_divergent=False`, and through `_probe_cascade_confab` no OBS + no notification; `_classify_existence` unit (denials → NOT_AFFIRM, affirmations → AFFIRM, ""/whitespace → NOT_AFFIRM); **default-OFF golden** — `confab_probe_enabled=False` (+ B2 off, gate on) → observe returns None, ZERO tasks scheduled, ZERO probe requests; `record_observation` dedup (two calls in-window → exactly one OBS); **non-blocking** — a slow LLM (awaiting an event) returns the AD-1120 cue immediately with the probe task still pending; `ProbeResult.affirm_rate`; config default OFF. Focused `-q -n 0` → **10 passed**; the MANDATORY regression gate `tests/test_ad1119_referent_gate.py tests/test_ad1120_ground_before_collaborate.py -q -n 0` → **26 passed (15 + 11), UNCHANGED** (the `_observe_referent_grounding` name/None-contract + the AD-1120 B2 cue output preserved); blast radius (9 group-chat/`thread_fanout` files + `test_notifications` + `test_ad1053_actionable_notifications` + `test_ad454_evidence_collector` + `test_ad454_taxonomy` + `test_config`) → **168 passed, 0 regressions**. `get_errors` clean on all 6 created/modified files (`config.py`, `confab_probe.py`, `evidence_collector.py`, `runtime.py`, `thread_fanout.py`, `test_ad1121_confab_probe.py`). Left UNCOMMITTED (LOCAL — the Captain decides the push).

### AD-1120: Ground-Before-Collaborate — injected honest-absence cue + always-on standing order (#1023)

**Context.** AD-1119 shipped the deterministic *guard* half of the cascade-confabulation defense: a default-OFF, observe-only gate that resolves each candidate referent in a group-chat room seed against ship ground truth and logs a gap-clean honest-absence cue for the unresolved ones — but it changes NO behavior (it only logs `AD-1119[observe]` warnings). The live 2026-07-08 forensics case (`e77acec7`, a fabricated node) showed the crew *almost* self-corrected ("treat the membership question as structurally unresolvable") — but only AFTER building an investigation on the fabricated id. AD-1120 closes the behavioral half: make grounding a PRECONDITION and "structurally unresolvable" a REWARDED terminal finding. It depends only on AD-1119's shipped verdict/resolver API — it does NOT build the divergence probe or transcript persistence (AD-1121/#1024). Highest landed top-level was **AD-1119**; **AD-1120 is the new top-level**.

**Decision.** Two halves. **(a) Flag-gated cue injection (DD-1120-1).** Compute the AD-1119 verdict ONCE at the fan-out choke point and RETURN the selected central cue, riding the exact AD-967 `room_roster` param path rather than re-extracting + re-resolving inside each agent (rejected: a second git subprocess per agent, no seed access at the agent seam). `_observe_referent_grounding` KEEPS its name (3 landed AD-1119 tests call it by name and assert the return), KEEPS the AD-1119 first-line `if not referent_gate_enabled: return None` early-return AND the observe loop VERBATIM, changes only its return annotation `None → str | None`, and appends `if not ground_before_collaborate_enabled: return None` AFTER the observe loop → then `return await _select_central_cue(verdict, seed_text)`. So AD-1120 fires ONLY when BOTH `referent_gate_enabled` AND `ground_before_collaborate_enabled` are True (the two-flag dependency); with B2 off the fan-out gets `grounding_cue=None` → no param → byte-identical, and the 3 AD-1119 tests (B2 default-off) hit the new `return None` after the unchanged observe log → stay green. **(b) Central-referent selection (DD-1120-2).** `GroundingVerdict` carries `.unresolved`/`.cues` but not kinds, so re-call `extract_referents(seed)` (PURE — not a re-resolve; the git subprocesses live only in `evaluate`) for the `{token:kind}` map. Central = the FIRST unresolved token (seed order, already preserved) whose kind ∈ `{"hex","entity"}`, `token.lower() not in _GROUNDING_STOPWORDS`, and (for `hex`) git is available. Kind-restricting to hex/entity DROPS the `service` kind entirely — that removes the AD-1119 DD-5 determiner false-positive class (a sentence-initial `"The node …" → service token "The"`, safe to log but unsafe to INJECT) WITHOUT touching the AD-1119 regex (out of scope); the stop-word set is defense-in-depth for a determiner `entity` capture (`"node the" → "the"`). Inject `verdict.cues[central]` VERBATIM — the AD-1119 wording, already `is_capability_gap`-clean. **(c) Resolver-availability gate (DD-1120-3).** `GitObjectResolver` honest-degrades to `False` when git is unavailable → on a git-less deploy every hex reads UNRESOLVED, which would falsely tell the crew every hex is fabricated. Probe git ONCE via `GitObjectResolver().resolve("HEAD")` (reuses the SHIPPED resolver as a positive control — no `referent_gate.py` edit) ONLY when a hex candidate exists; probe `False` → DROP hex candidates (fail safe); `entity` candidates need no git. **(d) Render (DD-1120-1).** NEW overridable `CognitiveAgent._conversational_grounding_cue_block(observation)` (mirrors `_conversational_room_outputs_block`): returns `""` unless `params["is_group_chat"]` AND a non-blank `grounding_cue` is attached, composed in the conversational branch immediately after the BF-651 `_outputs_proto` block. **(e) Standing order (DD-1120-5).** An always-on `<!-- category: core_directives --> ## Ground Before You Collaborate` section in `ship.md` (Tier-2, loaded ship-wide for every crew agent — `compose_instructions` loads ONLY named tiers, so a new `grounding.md` would be a dead file; the AD-729a precedent): no multi-agent investigation proceeds past framing until its central referent is grounded; "there is no such referent; the question is structurally unresolvable" is the correct, VALUED finding → close the room. **Byte-identity scope (DD-1120-4):** the always-on `ship.md` prose DOES change the composed prompt vs HEAD by design (the one constitutional judgment-call worth the Captain's veto, AD-729a precedent); the default-OFF byte-identity guarantee is scoped to the FLAG-GATED CUE PATH (no `grounding_cue` param, hook renders `""`) — deliberately NOT a "full agent prompt == HEAD" golden. `config.py` adds `GroundingConfig.ground_before_collaborate_enabled: bool = False`. NOT built (boundaries): no divergence probe / transcript persistence (AD-1121), no auto-close/delete of threads ("the room closes" is LLM guidance, not a code path), no trust-scoring change, no new consensus path/intent, no `referent_gate.py` edit, no `standing_orders.py` change, no second wiring seam, no HTTP.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad1120_ground_before_collaborate.py` (11, BF-287 real fixtures — real `AgentRegistry()`, a real `tmp_path` git repo (`_init_git_repo`), real `SystemConfig()`, `_RealAgent(BaseAgent)`, `SimpleNamespace` runtimes, `@_requires_git` where git is exercised; NO MagicMock at the registry/git/ward-room boundary): headline hex cue injected (both flags on, real tmp repo, `e77acec7` absent → non-None gap-clean cue containing `e77acec7`); determiner/service token NOT injected (seed `"The membership is degraded."` → `service "The"` dropped → None; PLUS the stop-word `entity` path `"check node the now"` → `"the"` dropped → None); no hex cue when git unavailable (patched `GitObjectResolver.resolve` → None); no cue when the central resolves (real registered `beef1234` → None); default-OFF returns None + zero gate builds; G1-on/B2-off still observe-only (exactly one `AD-1119[observe]` WARNING + None); the render hook emits the cue on the group param + `""` without the group/cue/params; the injected cue AND the `ship.md` section both `is_capability_gap==False`; config default OFF. NOTE the build prompt's test-2 EXAMPLE seed (`"The node membership is degraded."`) co-extracts an `entity` token `"membership"` (verified empirically) that the pinned selection WOULD inject — so it does not isolate the determiner class; corrected to `"The membership is degraded."` (service `"The"` only), faithful to the pinned `_select_central_cue` (only the example seed changed, not the logic). Focused `-q -n 0` → **11 passed**; AD-1119 regression gate `tests/test_ad1119_referent_gate.py -q -n 0` → **15 passed** (unchanged — the `_observe_referent_grounding` name/None-contract preserved); blast radius (13 group-chat/`thread_fanout` files + `test_ad1081_room_todo_tags.py` + `test_config.py` + AD-1119/1120) → **225 passed, 0 regressions**; broader conversational-hook sweep (12 `_conversational_*` files) → **181 passed, 0 regressions**. `get_errors` clean on `config.py`, `routers/thread_fanout.py`, `cognitive/cognitive_agent.py`, `config/standing_orders/ship.md`, and the test. Complies with `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (DIP — the shipped gate is reused `runtime`-free; honest-degrade — every failure path returns `None`/`""`; full type annotations on the new module helper + hook; structured logging with context; layer discipline — the cue rides the existing AD-967 param seam, no new higher-layer import). Left UNCOMMITTED (LOCAL — the Captain decides the push).

### AD-1119: Referent-Grounding Gate (guard G1) — cascade-confabulation prevention (#1022)

**Context.** Live-runtime forensics (2026-07-08) traced a crew "Oracle Health Check" investigation that reasoned at length about node `e77acec7` — a *fabricated* identifier (not a git object, an agent, a ward-room channel, or in any source file / DB). The root mechanism (mechanism #2 of the trace): **no agent verifies that an identifier or entity exists before reasoning about it.** `e77acec7` would have been caught at first mention by a referent gate. This is the `CASCADE_CONFAB` anti-pattern already coded in `emergence_taxonomy.py` — classified post-hoc, never *prevented*. AD-1119 is the highest-leverage prevention: resolve the referent before the crew builds an investigation on it. Research basis (absorbed): MAST *task-verification* failure (arXiv 2503.13657) + Chain-of-Verification (arXiv 2309.11495). AD-1119 is the deterministic *guard* half of a defense-in-depth pair; the behavioral standing order (AD-1120/#1023) and the divergence probe (AD-1121/#1024) follow and depend on this AD's resolver/verdict API — NOT built here. Highest landed top-level was **AD-1118**; **AD-1119 is the new top-level**.

**Decision.** A default-OFF, additive `ReferentGroundingGate` in a new **cognitive-layer, `runtime`-free** module `src/probos/cognitive/referent_gate.py`, wired **observe-only** at exactly ONE seam (`group_chat_fanout`, the choke point where a group cascade begins). (a) `extract_referents(text) -> list[Referent]` is a pure function: it strips fenced ```` ``` ```` blocks then inline `` `code` `` spans FIRST (so a sha inside a code fence is not extracted), then matches three kinds — **hex** `\b(?=[0-9a-fA-F]*[a-fA-F])[0-9a-fA-F]{7,40}\b` (the lookahead requires ≥1 a–f letter, so a plain decimal is excluded), **entity** `node|node id|record|entity <tok>`, and a conservative **service** span (a Capitalized word or `*_service` snake token immediately followed by `service|membership|telemetry|cluster|node`) — orders by first appearance across kinds, dedupes by token (first-seen wins), and caps at 20. (b) DIP: the gate takes a constructor-injected `list[ReferentResolver]` (`typing.Protocol`); the three concrete resolvers take NARROW deps (not `runtime`) and each honest-degrades to `False` — `GitObjectResolver` runs `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec("git", "cat-file", "-e", f"{token}^{{object}}", cwd=repo_root, stdout=DEVNULL, stderr=DEVNULL)` and returns `returncode == 0` (a missing git binary / non-repo cwd / non-zero exit / timeout → `False`, logged, never an exception, never a false-RESOLVED; `^{object}` resolves abbreviations + packed objects so an 8-char prefix like `e77acec7` is checked correctly; `repo_root` is constructor-injected, default `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]`), `AgentResolver` confirms via `registry.get(token)` / `registry.get_by_pool(token)` / `callsign_registry.resolve(token)` (callsign existence is liveness-independent), and `WardRoomResolver` guards `ward_room is None` then `await ward_room.get_channel_by_name(token)`. (c) `async def evaluate(text) -> GroundingVerdict` (frozen `{results, unresolved, cues}` + `has_unresolved`) tries ALL resolvers in order, first `True` → RESOLVED, all-`False` → UNRESOLVED plus a `@staticmethod _honest_absence_cue` that is checked against the decomposer `is_capability_gap` regex (AD-981b reuse — avoids "can't"/"cannot"/"unable to"/"lack*"/"don't have"/"no <X> capability|…"/"not available|supported|possible"); `evaluate` NEVER raises (extraction guarded → empty verdict; each resolver call individually wrapped). (d) A narrow-dep factory `build_default_resolvers(*, registry, callsign_registry, ward_room, repo_root=None)` lets the wiring site build the gate from the runtime without the module ever importing `runtime`. (e) `routers/thread_fanout.py` gains `async def _observe_referent_grounding(runtime, thread, seed_text)` mirroring `_observe_conversation_corrections` — first executable line is the flag early-return (`grounding.referent_gate_enabled`, default False → byte-identical, no gate built / no git run), then it evaluates the seed and emits one `AD-1119[observe]` WARNING per unresolved referent; wired as ONE awaited call at `group_chat_fanout` immediately after `agent_ids = crew_agent_participants(...)`. **OBSERVE-ONLY**: the cue is computed and logged but NEVER injected into any agent's context (that is AD-1120), and `all_replies` is never read or mutated. (f) `config.py` gains `class GroundingConfig(BaseModel)` (`referent_gate_enabled: bool = False`) mounted on `SystemConfig` beside `os_activity`/`device` (default OFF; no `config/system.yaml` edit — model default keeps a default install byte-identical). Deliberately NOT built: AD-1120 (cue injection / standing order), AD-1121 (divergence probe / transcript persistence); no change to `EmergentDetector`/`emergence_taxonomy.py`, no in-process git seam in `codebase_index.py`, no HTTP, no second seam.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad1119_referent_gate.py` (15, BF-287 real fixtures — real `AgentRegistry()`, a real `tmp_path` git repo (`git init` + commit for the git resolver), real `SystemConfig()` for the flag, `ward_room=None`; the only stubs are a real Protocol-implementing `_RaisingResolver` and a real minimal `BaseAgent` subclass — no MagicMock at the registry/git/ward-room boundary): extraction happy (hex/entity/service, first-seen order) + negatives (code-fence + inline-code + decimal + prose + `""` → `[]`) + dedupe; RESOLVED via a real git object (full sha + 8-char abbreviation, and through the gate); RESOLVED via a real registered agent (by id + by pool); the headline `e77acec7` (a real repo but not an object, empty registry, `ward_room=None`) → UNRESOLVED with a non-empty cue AND `is_capability_gap(cue) is False`; a raising resolver does NOT bubble (falls through to UNRESOLVED, failure logged); git-missing/non-repo → `False` (never raises, never false-RESOLVED); the DEFAULT-OFF golden `test_observe_off_is_noop` (a spy proves `build_default_resolvers` is called 0 times and zero `AD-1119` log records are emitted — the flag-gated first-line early-return IS the byte-identity guarantee); flag-ON observe emits exactly one `AD-1119[observe]` WARNING and mutates nothing it was passed; the all-resolved flag-ON path emits nothing; and `SystemConfig().grounding.referent_gate_enabled is False`. Focused gate `-q -n 0` → **15 passed**; blast radius (28 `thread_fanout`-importing test files + `tests/test_config.py`) `-q -n 0` → **297 passed, 0 regressions**. `get_errors` clean on `referent_gate.py`, `thread_fanout.py`, `config.py`, and the test. Complies with `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (async hygiene — the awaited helper is not fire-and-forget; layer discipline — the gate module is `runtime`-free and imports nothing higher; full type annotations on every new public method; structured logging with context on every honest-degrade; DIP resolver injection). Left UNCOMMITTED (LOCAL — the Captain decides the push).

### AD-1072: tool-search + sub-agent delegation tools for the conversational AgenticLoop (#1006)

**Context.** Epic #1006 gives crew agents Cowork/Codex/Copilot parity inside the AD-1065 conversational `AgenticLoop`. AD-1066 added `run_python` (code-exec + artifact capture) and AD-1068 added `use_skill` (the executable-skill bridge). Two gaps remained: an agent could not (a) DISCOVER what tools / skills / mesh-intents exist before acting — so it confabulated verbs that do not exist (the BF-651 / AD-1064 confabulation class) — nor (b) hand a bounded subtask to a better-suited colleague. AD-1072 is the last of the epic's three decomposed ADs (AD-1070 reply-tag retirement and AD-1071 voice streaming are the others).

**Decision.** Two default-OFF, additive keystone tools, both satisfying the AD-423a `Tool` protocol and honest-degrading (never raising out of `invoke`). (1) `SearchCapabilitiesTool` (`search_capabilities`, read-only) calls `list_capability_catalog(runtime)` directly, unifies the tools / skills / mesh-intents axes, keyword-ranks by case-insensitive token overlap (name weight 3, description weight 1), drops zero-score, sorts `(-score, name)`, caps to the top 10, and returns `{results:[{name,kind,description,held_by?}],count}`; an empty query short-circuits to an empty result with a `query required` message. (2) `DelegateTaskTool` (`delegate_task`) hands a bounded subtask to another crew agent by explicit callsign, routed through the SAME governed `WorkItemAgenticExecutor` the task dispatcher uses — so the delegate's tool-permission grants/restrictions, mesh-intent restrictions, consensus gates on destructive intents, and tool-trace persistence all apply unchanged (no governance bypass; no raw `perceive/decide/act`, no `direct_message`, no `QuorumEngine` hand-roll). A depth guard runs FIRST (refuse at `_delegation_depth >= delegation_max_depth` before any nested executor is constructed — the IntentBus fan-out / A→B→A recursion bound); the target is resolved via `runtime.callsign_registry.resolve(to)` then the AD-1076 liveness-independent `runtime.registry.get_by_pool(agent_type)` fallback (a RESTING crew member still resolves — `resolve()`'s `agent_id` is `is_alive`-gated); a self-target is refused. The nested run carries `extra_context={"_delegation_depth": depth+1}` so a delegate that itself delegates stays bounded. `WorkItemAgenticExecutor.run` gained an additive `extra_context: dict|None=None` (default-None → byte-identical) merged into the 4-key loop context; both tools register after the `skill_ids` block, gated on the new `config.agentic_tools` flags, idempotently, extended into the `tool_ids` dedup; the delegate tool reuses the executor's own `self._llm`. `AgenticToolsConfig` (`tool_search_enabled`, `delegation_enabled`, `delegation_max_depth` 0..3 default 1, `delegation_max_iterations` 1..25 default 5, `delegation_tier` "standard") is mounted on `SystemConfig` beside `dm_agentic`; no `config/system.yaml` edit, so a default install is byte-identical. `to` is a required explicit callsign in v1 — auto-routing to a best-match agent is a forward item.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad1072_agentic_tools.py` (16, BF-287 real fixtures — real `ToolRegistry` / `ToolPermissionStore` / `CognitiveSkillCatalog` on disk / `CallsignRegistry` / `WorkItemAgenticExecutor`, scripted-LLM loop, no MagicMock at the registry/executor boundary): search ranking + `kind` narrowing + empty-query + honest-degrade on a raising catalog; the delegation depth guard proven with a COUNTING fake executor that must never be constructed at max depth; the happy path (nested run returns `final_text` into `output["result"]` and carries `_delegation_depth==depth+1`, running AS the target agent); the AD-1076 resting-agent resolution; unknown / non-crew / self callsign → `target_not_found`; missing task/to → honest degrade; registration gating (both flags off → neither tool registered or offered, `tool_ids` byte-identical; flags on → each registered exactly once, idempotent on a second run); and the end-to-end headline (a scripted parent loop emits a `delegate_task` call → a nested governed executor runs the target → the result returns into the parent transcript). Focused gate `-n 0` → 16 passed; blast-radius (`test_ad1066_code_execution_tool.py` + `test_ad1068_use_skill_tool.py` + `test_config.py`) `-n 0` → 25 passed, 0 regressions; `get_errors` clean on the two new tool files, `agentic_dispatch.py`, `config.py`, and the test. AD-1072 is the pre-reserved epic #1006 sub-number (highest landed top-level = AD-1094); NO new top-level AD. The DECISIONS doc-log lags at AD-1054 (the 1055→1071 batch is unlogged pending the Captain's doc-log pass), so this AD-1072 heading is appended out-of-sequence without renumbering. Left UNCOMMITTED (LOCAL — the Captain decides the push).

### BF-640: CloudPicker OAuth postMessage handler verifies event.origin (#1005)

**Context.** The OAuth-completion `message` listener in `ui/src/components/CloudPicker.tsx` validated `ev.data.type === 'oauth_complete'` + `ev.data.provider` but never checked `ev.origin`. Any script/iframe able to `postMessage` to the window could forge an `oauth_complete` and drive the picker's `setAuthorized(true)` + `loadFiles('')`. Impact LOW — the backend holds the actual OAuth token and is the source of truth, so a forged message cannot itself exfiltrate files (the subsequent `/api/cloud-pickers/{provider}/files` fetch fails if the backend never completed OAuth) — but it is a genuine defense-in-depth gap (postMessage handlers should always verify origin, OWASP). Pre-existing since AD-720c (2026-05-17); found in the 2026-06-24 weekly review.

**Decision.** Add a same-origin guard at the top of the handler: `if (ev.origin !== window.location.origin) return;`. The OAuth callback page is served from our own origin, so a cross-origin postMessage is forged and is dropped before `removeEventListener`/`setAuthorized` (the listener stays attached for the legitimate same-origin message).

**Tests + gates.** The associated test posted with a wildcard TARGET origin (`window.postMessage(data, '*')`), which jsdom does NOT translate into a usable `event.origin` — it locked in the insecure behavior. Switched the 3 posts to a `dispatchOauthComplete(provider, origin)` helper that emits an explicit-origin `MessageEvent` (defaulting to `window.location.origin`), plus a `waitFor(window.open)` before each dispatch (the production handler attaches the listener immediately before `window.open`, and `dispatchEvent` is synchronous — unlike the old async `postMessage` — so the listener must be attached first). NEW `ignores a forged cross-origin oauth_complete message (BF-640)`: a `https://evil.example.com`-origin message leaves the picker unauthorized (no file list), and a same-origin message afterward still drives the flow (proving the guard is origin-specific + the early return doesn't detach the listener). CloudPicker 8 passed; full UI 1915 passed / 1 skipped (+1, 0 regressions); `npm run build` clean; `get_errors` clean. `config/system.yaml` UNTOUCHED. Left UNCOMMITTED (LOCAL).

### BF-639: _emit_event_local retains coroutine event-listener task references (#1003)

**Context.** `ProbOSRuntime._emit_event_local` (the AD-637d in-memory event fallback) dispatched coroutine listeners with `asyncio.create_task(fn(event))` and dropped the task reference. The surrounding `try/except` only catches SYNCHRONOUS failures (task creation); exceptions raised later when the coroutine runs are silently swallowed once the un-referenced task is GC'd (worst case a `RuntimeWarning: coroutine never awaited`). Violates the async-discipline standing order ("always hold a reference to tasks created with `asyncio.create_task()`"). The NATS dispatch path ~10 lines above already does it correctly (`_nats_publish_tasks.add(task)` + `add_done_callback`). Found in the 2026-06-24 weekly review (pre-existing, AD-637d-era).

**Decision.** Mirror the `_nats_publish_tasks` pattern: a new `self._event_listener_tasks: set[asyncio.Task]` registry; `_emit_event_local` stores the task + `task.add_done_callback(self._event_listener_tasks.discard)`. Deliberately NOT `_background_tasks` — that set is the AD-824 shutdown-cancel registry for long-lived loops; per-event one-shot fan-out tasks use a per-feature registry (the in-`__init__` comment says so explicitly). The listener-failure log is promoted `debug → warning` with context (the listener + the event type).

**Tests + gates.** The `_FakeRuntime` port in `test_ad637d_system_events_nats.py` (a "Port of runtime._emit_event") had diverged from the real method — updated to stay faithful (BF-287). NEW `test_emit_event_local_retains_then_discards_coroutine_task` (behavioral: a coroutine listener's task is held while in flight, discarded on completion) + `test_real_runtime_emit_event_local_holds_task_reference` (source-contract on the REAL `ProbOSRuntime._emit_event_local` — guards against the port + the real method diverging again). `test_ad637d` 12 passed; `get_errors` clean. `config/system.yaml` UNTOUCHED. Left UNCOMMITTED (LOCAL).

### BF-638: AttentionFaculty._coerce_exogenous_bid copies a caller-supplied AttentionBid (#1002)

**Context.** `_coerce_exogenous_bid` returned a ready `AttentionBid` BY REFERENCE (`return payload`); `_drain_pending_exogenous` then repriced `bid.zone_floor`/`bid.salience` in place. A caller that delivered a reusable `AttentionBid` would have it silently overwritten on the next reuse (a no-side-effects-on-input / Law of Demeter violation). Latent today — the live exogenous path coerces from a mesh dict/string and builds a FRESH bid via `_text_bid`/`_build_event_bid`, so no production caller currently passes a shared instance — but the first that does hits silent state corruption. Found in the 2026-06-24 weekly review of the composable-cognition cluster (AD-1032).

**Decision.** Copy on coercion: `return replace(payload)` (`dataclasses.replace`) so the faculty owns a fresh bid and the in-place reprice never touches the caller's object. `AttentionBid` is a plain mutable dataclass (defaults on all fields), so `replace` is a clean shallow copy (the `render` callable is shared by reference — intended; it is a lazy renderer, never mutated). Preferred over a "consume-semantics" docstring contract — it removes the footgun entirely.

**Tests + gates.** NEW (`test_ad1032_arousal.py`): `test_coerce_exogenous_bid_copies_a_ready_attention_bid` (coercion returns a distinct copy with the same field values) + `test_delivering_an_attention_bid_does_not_mutate_the_caller_object` (deliver via the public `deliver_exogenous` inlet → `arbitrate` drains/reprices → the caller's original keeps `salience=99.0`/`zone_floor=99`). Attention faculty suites (AD-1032 + AD-1029 + AD-1030 + AD-1036) 86 passed, 0 regressions; `get_errors` clean. `config/system.yaml` UNTOUCHED. Left UNCOMMITTED (LOCAL).

### BF-637: A2UI + artifact cards never rendered in the live HXI — the render gate fed the unresolved `threadId` prop (#735)

**Context.** The A2UI epic (AD-811a/b/b-1) and AD-797 artifact cards rendered correctly in vitest but NEVER as cards in the live HXI — they showed as literal `[A2UI: name vN - kind]` / `[Artifact: …]` stub text. `ProfileChatTab` builds each message body via `renderMessageBodyWithArtifacts(msg.text, threadId, …)`, and both card gates require a truthy thread id (`if (a2ui && threadId)` / `if (stub && threadId)`). But the call passed the bare optional `threadId` PROP, and the only live mount — `AgentProfilePanel`'s `<ProfileChatTab agentId={agentId} />` — passes NO `threadId`, so the prop is `undefined` and every card fell through to plain text, in BOTH 1:1 and group threads. The component already computes the correctly-resolved `activeThreadId = resolveProfileThreadId(threadId, activeProfileThreadId, threadIdByAgent, agentId)` (AD-937, the SAME id the send path + transcript selection use) — the render call just wasn't using it. Why it shipped green: the AD-811a source-contract test pinned the EXACT broken call string (`renderMessageBodyWithArtifacts(msg.text, threadId, …)`) as "correct", and every render test passed an explicit `threadId="t1"` or rendered the card in isolation — none exercised the real prop-less mount (a BF-287-class test/prod divergence).

**Decision.** One-token fix at the call site: pass `activeThreadId` (the resolved id) instead of the bare `threadId` prop. At the live mount the prop is undefined, so `activeThreadId` falls through the AD-937 precedence to the active group thread or the per-agent 1:1 thread — truthy whenever a thread exists — so the gate passes and the card renders. Strictly correct: `activeThreadId` is the same id `sendText` posts to and `selectTranscriptMessages` reads, so the rendered card's response routes to the right thread. Lights up A2UI AND artifact cards for 1:1 AND group simultaneously — not group-specific, so a SEPARATE BF from the AD-811c group producer (which it unblocks).

**Tests + gates.** Updated the AD-811a source-contract assertion to pin the CORRECT call (`msg.text, activeThreadId, …`) + a revert guard (`not.toContain('renderMessageBodyWithArtifacts(msg.text, threadId,')`) + a chain assertion (`activeThreadId` derives from `resolveProfileThreadId(threadId, …)`). NEW behavioral `describe` (the real `resolveProfileThreadId`, since `ProfileChatTab` is too audio-heavy to mount under jsdom): an undefined prop + an active profile thread → the group thread; undefined prop + no active + a per-agent map → the 1:1 thread — proving the value now feeding the gate is TRUTHY at the prop-less mount. ### AD-811a: A2UI choice widget (#735)

**Decision.** Activate the AD-811 forward marker with the smallest useful slice: a **single-choice** A2UI widget on the **1:1 DM** path, **default-OFF** (operator opt-in via `communications.a2ui_enabled`, default `False`). A Lieutenant+ crew agent emits `[A2UI]{json}[/A2UI]` carrying `{"kind":"choice","prompt":…,"options":[…]}`; the DM reply pipeline validates it, persists it as an `application/json` artifact through the **AD-797 two-call write**, and leaves an inline `[A2UI: name vN - choice]` stub. The HXI reuses the **AD-797 inline-stub→card** mechanism to render an interactive choice card, and the Captain's click posts the chosen option back through the **existing `sendText` chat route** — NO new response endpoint, NO new artifact store, `ArtifactViewer` stays read-only. This is **not a dead late-bound wire**: the full producer→store→render→response loop is test-proven when the flag is enabled (real `ArtifactStore` + filesystem `AttachmentStore`; a card-click → `sendText`-mirror round-trip), and with the flag off the teaching block is `""`, the pipeline step returns immediately, and the artifact + chat paths are byte-identical. **Net-new surface is intentionally tiny:** the schema (`a2ui/AgentUIChoiceSpec`), the extractor (`dm/a2ui_extractor.py`, mirroring `artifact_extractor.py`), one card (`A2UIChoiceCard.tsx`), and one rank/flag-gated teaching block (`_conversational_a2ui_block`). Rank is derived from the live trust score (BF-263 — `self.rank` is never set on agents); the teaching text is `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE`-clean so it never reads as a capability-gap confession.

**Decomposition (forward markers, NOT built here).** AD-811b — additional widget kinds (text input / multi-select / yes-no / range / date). AD-811c — group-chat producer (the escalation-subset path). AD-811d — per-channel adapter renderers (Slack Block Kit / Discord embeds / Telegram inline keyboards / Teams Adaptive Cards). AD-811e — DecisionQueue (AD-445) decision surfaces → A2UI specs. AD-811f — response correlation back to the originating spec. Generative/LLM-authored UI is out of scope for the whole AD-811 line at this stage.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad811a_a2ui_choice.py` (31 tests, real stores per BF-287): schema validation (too-few/empty-drop/dedupe/over-cap/trim/`kind!="choice"`/empty-prompt/round-trip), extractor (valid/case-insensitive/malformed/invalid/over-`max_options`/cap-1/stub format), two-call write (stub left + tag stripped + artifact persisted + attachment bytes at the expected hash), honest-degrade (store error → text intact, no artifact, no raise), pipeline (`step_4k` OFF→byte-identical, ON→extracts, no-thread→intact, `_full_steps` order regression + absence from `_escalation_steps`), and the teaching block (off/below-rank/no-runtime → `""`, enabled+rank≥min → renders, gap-regex-clean). UI: `a2ui/__tests__/a2uiApi.test.ts` (stub + choice-spec parse), `a2ui/__tests__/A2UIChoiceCard.test.tsx` (render/click/loading/one-shot-lock/no-emoji), `profile/__tests__/ProfileChatTab.a2ui.test.tsx` (A2UI-before-artifact precedence source contract + coexist render + a `sendText`-mirror round-trip posting the chosen option to `/api/agent/{id}/chat`). Gates: focused 31 passed; blast-radius 732 passed / 1 skipped / 0 regressions; full UI 1870 passed / 1 skipped (+23 / 0 regressions); `npm run build` clean. `config/system.yaml` untouched. AD-811a is a pre-reserved #735 sub-number — current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**; no new top-level AD.

### AD-811b: A2UI multiselect + multi-kind dispatch (#735)

**Decision.** Add the 2nd A2UI widget kind — **`multiselect`** — on the AD-811a choice foundation, and generalize the single-kind path to a clean **N-kind dispatch**. The architectural value is the dispatch: a `kind`-keyed registry (`_SPEC_BY_KIND`) + one parse entry point (`parse_a2ui_spec(raw) -> A2UISpec | None`) on the backend, a stub that carries the kind (`[A2UI: name vN - <kind>]`), and a UI renderer switch. Adding a future kind = register its spec class + add a renderer arm — no call-site churn.
