### AD-843a: DeviceNodeAdapter foundation (#818)

**Problem.** The local cognitive mesh is the *brain*; a paired remote device (phone, tablet, kiosk) should be a *limb* the brain can actuate (push a notification, read location, capture a camera frame or the screen). The brain→limb device tier needs a foundation: governed `device.*` intents, a typed actuation contract, a paired-device record, and a pairing/authorization registry — built as low-risk, standalone substrate primitives BEFORE any cryptographic pairing, trust wiring, or consensus routing is layered on.

**Decision.** Ship the STANDALONE, UNWIRED substrate primitives in a NEW `src/probos/substrate/device_node.py` that imports ONLY `probos.types` (top-level) plus stdlib — clean substrate layer discipline (NO consensus/mesh/cognitive/federation/runtime import). Five exports: (1) `DEVICE_INTENT_DESCRIPTORS` — the four `device.*` `IntentDescriptor`s carrying governance metadata only (no handlers in 843a). (2) `DeviceNode` `@dataclass` mirroring `FederationPeer`: `device_id` is the stable identity, `capabilities: frozenset[str]` is the per-device grant (the immutable set of granted `device.*` names), `trust_record_id` is the AD-843b Beta-prior handle (stored-only here), `public_key` is an Ed25519 placeholder (`""` = not crypto-paired), plus `metadata`/`paired_at`. (3) `DeviceNodeAdapter` — a `@runtime_checkable typing.Protocol` (`async actuate(device, intent) -> IntentResult`), the DIP seam concrete OS-native backends implement later. (4) `NoOpDeviceNodeAdapter` — an echo adapter with NO OS backend, satisfying the Protocol structurally. (5) `DeviceNodeRegistry` — a pure in-memory pairing store plus a per-device capability-grant gate (`authorize(device_id, intent_name) -> tuple[bool, str]`) that rejects unpaired and ungranted, mirroring `FederationPeerRegistry.register_peer`'s already-known→False idempotence. `authorize` is the PURE governance-metadata gate — it does NOT call the adapter, TrustNetwork, or QuorumEngine; the `__init__` takes no `trust_network` param in 843a.

**Consensus-flag rationale.** `device.location`/`device.camera`/`device.screen` exfiltrate private sensor data — physical location, camera frames, on-screen secrets — from the paired limb, so each is `requires_consensus=True` (a destructive/sensitive intent requires multi-agent consensus, per the standing rule). `device.notify` is a low-sensitivity outbound push, so `requires_consensus=False`. All four are `tier="domain"`.

**Ed25519 is MISSING at HEAD.** There is no Ed25519 pairing primitive in the codebase to reuse — `public_key` stays `""` in 843a, and AD-843b BUILDS cryptographic pairing on the `cryptography` library (a new build, NOT a reuse of existing code). Trust-prior injection (AD-843b) and consensus/episodic routing + runtime wiring (AD-843c) remain deferred; 843a deliberately ships no OS-native backend (NoOp only), no trust/quorum/episodic, and no wiring.

**Tests.** NEW `tests/test_ad843a_device_node.py` — 8 real-fixture cases (BF-287: real `DeviceNode`/`DeviceNodeRegistry`/`NoOpDeviceNodeAdapter`/`IntentMessage`, no MagicMock): the consensus flags + `tier` + all-four-names-present; `isinstance(NoOpDeviceNodeAdapter(), DeviceNodeAdapter)`; the NoOp async happy-path echo (`success`, `backend=="noop"`, `echo==params`, `agent_id=="device:<id>"`, `intent_id==msg.id`); authorize unpaired-reject; authorize ungranted-reject; authorize granted-ok; register idempotent (second register → False, one device); record stores the exact frozenset grant + `public_key==""`. Gate: `pytest tests/test_ad843a_device_node.py -q -n 0` → 8 passed (pure module, no runtime boot); `get_errors` clean on both files. AD-843a is a PRE-RESERVED #818 sub-number — current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**, NO new top-level AD; AD-843b (pairing + trust prior) and AD-843c (consensus/episodic routing + wiring) remain. `config/system.yaml` UNTOUCHED. ### AD-843b: Ed25519 device pairing + trust prior (#818)

**Problem.** AD-843a shipped the standalone brain→limb substrate primitives with `public_key=""` (not crypto-paired) and no trust wiring. The device tier needs cryptographic enrollment: a device must PROVE possession of its private key before pairing, and a freshly-paired device — like a self-designed agent or a federated peer — should start on a probationary trust footing, not full trust.

**Decision.** Build net-new Ed25519 pairing on the `cryptography` library (Ed25519 was MISSING at HEAD — NOT a reuse of the SHA256 string-id in `substrate/identity.py`, which is a hash, not a signature). NEW `src/probos/substrate/device_pairing.py` (imports `cryptography` + stdlib `base64` ONLY — clean substrate layer discipline) exports five functions: `generate_keypair`, `encode_public_key`/`decode_public_key` (base64 of the 32-byte raw form ↔ key object), `sign_challenge`, and `verify_signature`. A device enrolls by presenting its base64 public key and a base64 signature over a pairing challenge. `DeviceNodeRegistry.pair_device(device_id, public_key, capabilities, *, challenge, signature)` verifies the signature (bad → `None`, the security gate), then on FIRST pairing builds the `DeviceNode` (public_key + capability grant + `trust_record_id=f"device:{id}"`) and seeds a probationary Beta(α, β) prior via an injected `TrustNetwork.create_with_prior` — mirroring `FederationPeerRegistry.register_peer`. Re-pairing a known id is IDEMPOTENT (returns the existing record, no prior reset). NEW `DeviceConfig` (mirrors `FederationPeerTrustConfig`: Beta(1, 3) → E[trust]=0.25) is mounted on `SystemConfig.device`, inert until AD-843c constructs the registry with a real `TrustNetwork`.

**Concrete-`TrustNetwork` injection (`Any|None`).** The `TrustNetwork` is INJECTED into `DeviceNodeRegistry.__init__` as a keyword-only `trust_network: Any|None=None`, never imported — substrate must not import consensus. It is typed `Any` (not a Protocol) because the device tier needs the CONCRETE `create_with_prior`, which a narrow Protocol would not expose. `None` → pair without a prior (honest-degrade). The keyword-only params keep the AD-843a no-arg construction path byte-identical.

**Beta(1,3) prior, idempotent, raw α/β.** First pairing seeds Beta(1, 3)=0.25 (the same probationary footing as self-created agents and federated peers). The prior is stored as raw `(alpha, beta)` (never a derived mean). Idempotence is double-guarded: `pair_device` returns the existing record before touching trust, and `create_with_prior` is itself a no-op for a known id — so a re-pair never resets an evolved score.

**base64 wire format + two-tier exception handling.** The 32-byte raw public key and 64-byte signature are carried as standard base64 `str` (compact, JSON-safe). Exceptions split two ways by call site: `decode_public_key` is a FAIL-FAST boundary (raises `ValueError` on malformed base64 / wrong length), while `verify_signature` is HONEST-DEGRADE (never raises — returns `False` on any bad key/sig, the boolean security gate callers branch on).

**Tests + gates.** NEW `tests/test_ad843b_device_pairing.py` — 12 real-fixture cases (BF-287: a real standalone `TrustNetwork()` with in-memory `_records` — no `start()`, no `PROBOS_DATA_DIR` — and real Ed25519 crypto; all sync): keypair sign/verify round-trip, tampered-challenge/wrong-key/malformed-sig → `False` (no raise), encode/decode round-trip, bad-length → `ValueError`, pair stores pubkey+grant+`device:phone-1`+is_paired, pair seeds Beta(1,3) (raw α==1.0/β==3.0/score≈0.25), bad-sig → `None`+not-paired+no-record, idempotent re-pair (α unchanged after a `record_outcome` shift), none-`TrustNetwork` honest-degrade pairs, and the AD-843a no-arg API intact (register_device + authorize granted-ok). Gate: `pytest tests/test_ad843b_device_pairing.py tests/test_ad843a_device_node.py tests/test_config.py -q -n 0` → **26 passed** (12 new + AD-843a still **8 passed** / 0 regressions + test_config green); `get_errors` clean on all 4 files; import smoke confirms `device_pairing` imports ONLY `cryptography`+stdlib and `device_node` imports `device_pairing` (both substrate), NOT consensus. NO actuation governance routing, `record_outcome`-on-actuation, episodic, IntentBus, runtime wiring, or registry-with-real-`TrustNetwork` construction (all AD-843c); NO OS backend, NO AD-844 mobile client, NO fleet pairing / pubkey rotation / asyncio.Lock. AD-843b is a PRE-RESERVED #818 sub-number — current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**, NO new top-level AD; AD-843c (consensus/episodic actuation routing + runtime wiring) remains. `config/system.yaml` UNTOUCHED. Left UNCOMMITTED (LOCAL — the Captain decides the push).

### AD-843c-1: device actuation governance loop (device.notify) + runtime wire (#818)

**Problem.** AD-843a/b shipped the brain→limb substrate primitives (Protocol + registry + Ed25519 pairing + probationary trust prior) STANDALONE — the registry is never constructed with a real `TrustNetwork`, no handler is wired to the bus, and an actuation never records trust or stores an episode. The device tier needs to close the loop for the NON-consensus `device.notify` intent inside the live runtime: authorize → actuate → record trust → store episode.

**Decision.** NEW `src/probos/substrate/device_service.py` — `DeviceNodeService`, a constructor-injected, bus-agnostic service mirroring `AgentGroupChatService`. It owns the AD-843a/b `DeviceNodeRegistry` + a `DeviceNodeAdapter`; the CONCRETE `TrustNetwork` is injected as `Any` (the trust Protocol lacks `record_outcome`) and episodic memory flows through a late-bind `Callable[[], Any]` provider (episodic is created after the runtime `__init__` that builds the service). `handle_intent` completes the loop for `device.notify` ONLY: the registry `authorize` gate (unpaired/ungranted → `IntentResult(success=False, error=reason)` + an unauthorized episode), then `NoOpDeviceNodeAdapter.actuate`, then `TrustNetwork.record_outcome(device.trust_record_id, success=result.success, source="device")` on the `device:{id}` handle, then an `Episode` per actuation (`anchors=AnchorFrame(channel="device", trigger_type=intent.intent)`, honest-degrade when the provider yields None). The runtime wire (in `__init__`, immediately after the `FederationPeerRegistry` anchor) constructs `DeviceNodeRegistry` eagerly with `self.trust_network` + `config.device` priors (inert until a device pairs) and builds `DeviceNodeService` with `episodic_provider=lambda: self.episodic_memory`; the `device.notify` handler subscribes to the IntentBus ONLY when `config.device.enabled` (NEW, default `False`) → byte-identical when off. Substrate discipline preserved: `device_service.py` imports ONLY `device_node` + `probos.types` + stdlib.

**No governance bypass; the consensus path is DEFERRED.** `handle_intent` returns `None` for any intent other than `device.notify`, so the sensitive consensus intents (`device.location`/`device.camera`/`device.screen`, `requires_consensus=True` from AD-843a) are NOT subscribed and remain UNREACHABLE in c-1. The real commit-on-APPROVED consensus path (`submit_mcp_invoke_with_consensus`, AD-1019c) is NOT reusable for a one-shot device call without a `DeviceConsensusProposer` pool + a `submit_device_actuate_with_consensus` — so the sensitive intents are DEFERRED to AD-843c-2 (mirroring AD-1019c) rather than hand-rolled here. c-1 ships only the non-consensus `device.notify` loop; the sensitive intents are unreachable, not bypassed.

**Tests + gates.** NEW `tests/test_ad843c1_device_actuation.py` — 8 real-fixture cases (BF-287: real `DeviceNodeRegistry` + real `TrustNetwork()` + `NoOpDeviceNodeAdapter` + a capturing async-`store` fake episodic + real Ed25519 pairing): full loop (authorized → `success`, `backend=="noop"`, trust α>1.0 on `device:<id>`, exactly 1 `device_actuate` episode with `anchors.channel=="device"`); unpaired-reject (`"unpaired device"`, no trust record, adapter not called, episode `authorized=False`); ungranted-reject (`"capability not granted: device.notify"`, no actuation, α stays 1.0); episodic-None honest-degrade (actuates + records trust, no crash); non-notify `device.location` → `None` (sensitive unreachable, no actuation/episode/trust); registry constructed with the concrete `trust_network` + `config.device` priors; handler NOT subscribed when `enabled=False`; handler subscribed when `enabled=True` (drives the LIVE `intent_bus.broadcast` → NoOp actuates + trust recorded). Tests 6-8 build a real `ProbOSRuntime(data_dir=tmp_path/"data")` WITHOUT `start()` — the wiring is `__init__`-time (mirrors AD-1019c default-off); test 8 uses `broadcast` (not `submit_intent`) to exercise the live bus without a full boot that would contend with a running live instance. Gate: `pytest tests/test_ad843c1_device_actuation.py tests/test_ad843a_device_node.py tests/test_ad843b_device_pairing.py tests/test_config.py -q -n 0` → **34 passed** (8 new + 843a 8 + 843b 12 + test_config, 0 regressions); `get_errors` clean on all 4 files; `device_service.py` imports confirmed substrate+types+stdlib only. ### AD-843c-2: consensus gate for sensitive device intents (#818)

**Problem.** AD-843c-1 wired the NON-consensus `device.notify` loop and DELIBERATELY left the three sensitive intents (`device.location`/`device.camera`/`device.screen`, `requires_consensus=True` since AD-843a) UNREACHABLE so there would be no governance bypass — but #818 is incomplete until they are reachable through a REAL consensus gate. The genuine commit-on-APPROVED mechanism is the propose-only-pool + runtime-method pattern (`submit_mcp_invoke_with_consensus`, AD-1019c), NOT a direct `QuorumEngine.evaluate(...)` (which only scores already-collected votes — hand-rolling votes there is the bypass this AD must not reintroduce).

**Decision.** Mirror AD-1019c. NEW `src/probos/agents/device_consensus_proposer.py` — `DeviceConsensusProposer`, a faithful propose-only mirror of `McpConsensusProposer` (`tier="utility"`; validates the request shape; returns `requires_consensus=True`; NEVER actuates — it holds no adapter), declaring a NEW INTERNAL proposal intent `device_actuate` on `default_capabilities` + `intent_descriptors` + `_handled_intents`; it imports ONLY `probos.substrate.agent` + `probos.types` + stdlib. THREE new runtime methods (inserted after `_store_mcp_invoke_episode`): `submit_device_actuate_with_consensus(device_id, intent_name, params, *, timeout, policy)` authorizes the per-device grant FIRST (c-1 parity), broadcasts the `device_actuate` proposal through `submit_intent_with_consensus`, and commits `device_node_adapter.actuate` ONLY when `consensus.outcome == ConsensusOutcome.APPROVED` AND `not [v for v in result["verifications"] if not v.verified]` — the EXACT predicate from `submit_mcp_invoke_with_consensus` (the era-4/AD-362 guard; a rejected/insufficient vote performs ZERO actuate); `_store_device_consensus_episode` mirrors `_store_mcp_invoke_episode` (`anchors=AnchorFrame(channel="device", trigger_type=intent_name)`, honest-degrade when episodic is None); `_dispatch_device_consensus_intent` is the runtime-owned bus handler routing the three sensitive intents into the consensus method. The `__init__` NoOp adapter is extracted to a named `self.device_node_adapter: DeviceNodeAdapter` (byte-identical — same instance — shared by the c-1 `device.notify` service AND the c-2 commit).

**Runtime-owned dispatch keeps the service layer-clean.** The sensitive path is a runtime-owned handler (`_dispatch_device_consensus_intent`), NOT folded into `DeviceNodeService.handle_intent` — `device_service.py` is substrate and imports ONLY `device_node` + `types` + stdlib, whereas the commit mechanism (`submit_intent_with_consensus` → `quorum_engine.evaluate` → `adapter.actuate`) lives in `runtime.py` (which legitimately imports consensus). Routing the sensitive path through the service would force a `consensus` import into the clean substrate service. `device_service.py` is UNTOUCHED.

**The `device_actuate` internal intent prevents a dispatch re-broadcast loop.** `IntentBus.subscribe` indexes a handler under each intent name and `broadcast(msg)` routes to handlers indexed under `msg.intent`; if the method re-broadcast a sensitive EXTERNAL name (e.g. `device.location`), the dispatch handler — itself subscribed to `device.location` — would re-receive it and recurse. So the method broadcasts the generic internal `device_actuate` (params carry `device_id`+`intent_name`+`params`), the proposer subscribes to `device_actuate`, and the dispatch subscribes the three external names. `device_actuate` is declared ONLY on the proposer — NOT in `DEVICE_INTENT_DESCRIPTORS` (`device_node.py` UNTOUCHED). The proposer's declared intent MUST equal `"device_actuate"` or quorum gets zero voters → always INSUFFICIENT. The dispatch subscriber id `"device_consensus_dispatch"` is distinct from `DEVICE_NODE_SERVICE_ID` so it does not clobber the c-1 `device.notify` handler.

**Trust recorded ONLY on an attempted actuation; episode on all paths (diverges from "trust on both").** An episode is stored on EVERY path (approved-and-actuated, blocked, rejected, insufficient, and the pre-consensus grant refusal) for audit/learning completeness. But `trust_network.record_outcome(device.trust_record_id, success=committed, intent_type=intent_name, source="device")` fires ONLY inside the APPROVED + no-failed-verification branch, AFTER the actuate try/except (keyed `success=committed`). A REJECTED / INSUFFICIENT / failed-verification / unauthorized path performs no actuation and writes NO trust outcome. Rationale: trust feeds consensus weighting, so writing `success=False` on a governance REJECTION would push the device toward a lock-out death-spiral; an INSUFFICIENT vote means the operator simply did not run the proposer pool and must not penalize the device; and the c-1 parity is that trust reflects an actuation OUTCOME, not the mesh's decision. A genuine APPROVED-but-actuate-fails STILL records `success=False` (an actuation WAS attempted) — that signal is preserved. The unauthorized device is refused BEFORE consensus (episode `authorized=False`, no trust, zero votes) — c-1 parity. This diverges from the BuildSpec's "episode+trust on both paths" per an explicit architect override.

**Default-OFF byte-identical.** The proposer pool + the sensitive-intent subscription live ONLY inside a NEW `async def _wire_device_consensus(*, runtime, config)` finalize helper (mirrors `_wire_desktop_ux`), gated on `config.device.enabled` (default False). When off it returns immediately → no `device_consensus` pool, no `device_consensus_dispatch` subscription → the three intents stay UNREACHABLE = byte-identical to AD-843c-1. The three runtime methods are always present but inert. `config.py` / `config/system.yaml` UNTOUCHED.

**Tests + gates.** NEW `tests/test_ad843c2_device_consensus.py` — 13 real-fixture cases (BF-287: real `ProbOSRuntime`+`start()`+`DeviceConsensusProposer` pool + real Ed25519 pairing + real delegating `_TrustSpy`/`_StoreSpy`/`_CountingAdapter`/`_FailingAdapter`, no MagicMock): 5 proposer-unit (propose valid / reject missing device_id / reject missing intent_name / ignore unhandled / descriptor `requires_consensus`+`tier=="utility"`); approved-commits-single-actuate (trust success=True, score rose vs Beta(1,3), episode `channel=="device"`); rejected via `approval_threshold=1.1` → ZERO actuate, episode `reason=="not_committed"`, NO trust (α/β unchanged — the death-spiral guard); insufficient (no pool) → ZERO actuate, NO trust; unauthorized `ghost-1` → refused pre-consensus, `authorized=False`, ZERO actuate, no trust record; episodic-None honest-degrade; approved-but-actuate-fails (`_FailingAdapter`) → committed=False but exactly 1 actuate attempt + trust success=False recorded (the override penalizes a real actuation failure, not a governance rejection); wire-OFF no-op (no pool, no dispatch sub); device.notify c-1 regression (still routes through `device_node_service`, not `device_actuate`). Gate: `pytest tests/test_ad843c2_device_consensus.py tests/test_ad843c1_device_actuation.py tests/test_ad1019c_consensus.py tests/test_ad1019c_proposer.py -q -n 0` (PROBOS_DATA_DIR-isolated) → **34 passed** (13 new + 843c-1 8 + 1019c consensus 7 + 1019c proposer 6, 0 regressions); blast-radius `-k "device or consensus or quorum"` → **146 passed**; `get_errors` clean on all 4 touched files; proposer imports confirmed substrate.agent+types+stdlib only. NEW `ui/src/hooks/useSwipe.ts`: `useSwipe({onSwipeLeft?, onSwipeRight?, threshold=50}): {onPointerDown, onPointerUp}` — records the start point on pointer-down in a `useRef` (`{x,y}|null`) and, on pointer-up, computes `dx,dy` and fires `onSwipeLeft`/`onSwipeRight` ONLY for a dominant-horizontal gesture (`|dx| > |dy|`) past `threshold`; vertical-dominant gestures and taps are ignored. MODIFY `ui/src/components/mesh/MobileMesh.tsx` ONLY: import `usePrefersReducedMotion`; add module consts (a `BREATH_KEYFRAMES` string `@keyframes meshBreath{0%,100%{transform:scale(1)}50%{transform:scale(1.05)}}`, `BREATH_PERIOD_S=3.5`, `BREATH_STAGGER_S=0.5`, `BREATH_STAGGER_MOD=7`); compute `const animate = !usePrefersReducedMotion()` after the nodes/edges `useMemo`; render `{animate ? <style>{BREATH_KEYFRAMES}</style> : null}` as the FIRST child of the `<svg>`; and change the node map to `nodes.map((n, i) =>` with a per-`<circle>` `style` (motion-allowed only) that runs `meshBreath 3.5s ease-in-out infinite` with a per-node NEGATIVE `animationDelay` stagger (`-(i % 7) * 0.5s`). ### AD-708c-1: pure 2D mesh projection module (#484)

**Problem.** The AD-708b PADD mobile shell is chat-only; #484 (AD-708c) wants it to also show a SIMPLIFIED 2D mesh of the crew. The desktop mesh's visual language (trust→color, confidence→luminance, tier+confidence→size) lives in `ui/src/canvas/scene.ts` (`trustToColor`, `confidenceToIntensity`, `agentNodeSize`) — but `scene.ts` opens with `import * as THREE from 'three'`, and its layout (`useStore.ts` `computeLayout`) is a 3D Fibonacci sphere optimized for the canvas. A mobile module CANNOT import `scene.ts` / `canvas/agents.tsx` (or any three-pulling module): doing so would drag the entire Three.js stack into the mobile Rollup chunk and break the AD-708b lazy-three boundary — the whole point of which is that a phone never loads three.js. A shared-extraction refactor (hoisting the formulas out of `scene.ts` into a three-free module both consume) would touch `scene.ts` and is out of scope for a byte-identical foundation AD.

**Decision.** Add ONLY a pure foundation module, wired NOWHERE — NEW `ui/src/mesh2d/meshProjection.ts` — that RE-DERIVES the desktop formulas as pure TS (read from `scene.ts` at HEAD, NOT imported) returning plain numbers + CSS color strings. The only store reference is `import type { Agent }` (type-only, erased at build). Five exported functions + two interfaces (`MeshNode`, `MeshViewport`): `trustToCss(trust)` re-derives `trustToColor`'s four bands with the SAME hex stops and thresholds (`#e8963c`→`#f0b060` for trust ≥0.7, `#6690b8`→`#88a4c8` for ≥0.35, `#5848a0`→`#7060a8` for >0, `#a0a8b8` silver at 0) via a private componentwise-sRGB `lerpHex(a,b,t)` — the 2D equivalent of the desktop `THREE.Color.lerpColors` — with trust clamped to [0,1] for the band math so an out-of-range value never produces an invalid hex; `confidenceToOpacity(c)` normalizes the desktop `confidenceToIntensity` (`0.4 + c*1.8`, range 0.4..2.2) to `clamp((0.4 + c*1.8)/2.2, 0.25, 1)`, the 0.25 floor keeping low-confidence nodes faintly visible; `nodeRadius(tier, c)` re-derives `agentNodeSize` (`TIER_BASE[tier] + c*0.15`, bases core .22 / utility .28 / domain .35, unknown→.28 fallback) scaled by a `PX_SCALE` const (28) into ~6..14 px; `selectMeshAgents(agents, limit=24)` is the progressive-disclosure (HXI #5) curated subset — crew first (`isCrew`), then trust descending, then callsign ascending as a stable tiebreak, capped at `limit`, pure (sorts a copy, never mutates the input); `computeMeshLayout(agents, viewport)` is a FRESH 2D concentric-ring-by-tier layout that mirrors the desktop tier-radius ordering (3.5 / 5.5 / 7.5) as ring-radius FRACTIONS of `min(width,height)/2` (core .30 inner / utility .55 mid / domain .80 outer), agents evenly angularly spaced within their tier ring, centered on the viewport, deterministic, one `MeshNode` per input agent with `color`/`opacity`/`radius` derived from its agent — a single node sits ON its ring (at the top), not dead-center. The layout does NOT curate internally (the caller composes `selectMeshAgents` → `computeMeshLayout`). The later AD-708c-2 `MobileMesh` SVG component consumes this; it is wired NOWHERE in this AD, so the desktop HXI and the mobile shell are both byte-identical.

**The three-free guard.** Because the entire value of this module is that it does NOT pull three into the mobile chunk, the test suite includes a SOURCE-LEVEL guard: it reads the module's own source (`process.cwd()`-relative, since vitest's jsdom rewrites `import.meta.url` to a non-file scheme that `readFileSync` rejects), strips comments (so the module's explanatory prose — which names the forbidden modules — does not trip the check; only real code is inspected), and asserts the code contains no `from 'three'`, no `canvas/scene`, and no `canvas/agents` import, and positively that the ONLY store reference is the type-only `Agent` import. The desktop formulas were verified against `scene.ts` at HEAD and match exactly — no formula deviation from the spec.

**v1 simplifications.** The 2D projection OMITS the desktop `poolTintBlend` (which mixes a 30% pool tint into the trust color) — trust is the dominant 70% term, so trust alone carries the band semantics for a small curated subset; the pool tint can be added later if needed. There is NO animation here (pulse/flash is the deferred AD-708c-4). These are documented in the module.

**Tests + gates.** NEW `ui/src/mesh2d/__tests__/meshProjection.test.ts` (27 cases, real `Agent` fixtures built as plain typed objects — BF-287, no MagicMock-style stubs): `trustToCss` silver-at-0 / violet·blue·amber band membership / the exact 0.35 & 0.7 boundary stops / >1 & <0 clamps yielding valid hex; `confidenceToOpacity` 0.25 floor / 1.0 cap / mid-range monotonic / out-of-range clamp; `nodeRadius` core<utility<domain at equal confidence / rises-with-confidence / unknown-tier-fallback; `selectMeshAgents` empty / crew-first / trust-desc / cap-at-limit / callsign tiebreak determinism / no input mutation; `computeMeshLayout` empty / single-node-on-ring-not-center / N-nodes-in-bounds-and-distinct / tier-ordering (core nearer center than domain) / per-node derived color·opacity·radius / two-call determinism; plus the source-level three-free guard. ### AD-708f: HXI connect-a-phone discovery card (#484)

**Problem.** AD-708e shipped the BACKEND mDNS advertiser that publishes a stable `<hostname>.local` LAN address for the HXI, but a phone on the LAN still has no way to LEARN that address from the HXI itself — the Captain had to read the server logs or already know the hostname. #484 (AD-708) wants the System view to SURFACE the `.local` address so the Captain can read/copy it and point a phone at the HXI. The question was whether this needs any backend work (a new `/api/discovery` endpoint, a serializer, an "is-advertising" status probe) — and the answer is NO: `/api/config` already returns the full `SystemConfig.model_dump` (which AD-708e extended with the `discovery` block — `enabled`, `hostname`, …), and `useSettingsStore.loadSnapshot()` already loads it into the settings snapshot. The address is ALREADY in the browser; it just was not rendered.

**Decision.** Add ONE pure-UI card — NEW `ui/src/components/bridge/ConnectPhoneCard.tsx` (default-export, fully-typed, no props) — that reads `discovery.{enabled,hostname}` from the settings snapshot via the EXACT `App.tsx:96-97` selector idiom (`useSettingsStore((s) => Boolean((s.snapshot?.config as any)?.discovery?.enabled))` plus the `hostname` sibling with a `?? 'probos'` fallback matching the `DiscoveryConfig` default) and builds the address CLIENT-SIDE: `const port = window.location.port; const url = port ? http://{hostname}.local:{port} : http://{hostname}.local`. `http://` matches AD-708e's advertised scheme — a cert-less `.local` A record is plain http; the port comes from the live HXI origin (no backend round-trip). The card renders the URL as selectable amber monospace plus a copy button (a LOCAL inline-SVG copy glyph — no shared `Copy` glyph exists in `Glyphs.tsx` — swapping to the imported `Check` glyph for ~1.5 s on copy) whose handler is clipboard-GUARDED (`await navigator.clipboard?.writeText(url)` in a try/catch — an insecure context or old browser honest-degrades with no throw), and a dim caveat line noting the server must be bound to the LAN (`--host 0.0.0.0`). It is mounted in `FullSystem.tsx`'s System-view column stack with ONE import + ONE `<ConnectPhoneCard />` line, immediately after `<DesktopConsole />` and before `<ThreadTable />` — no other child touched. **Self-gating (progressive disclosure, HXI #5): `if (!enabled) return null;` runs as the first statement after the hooks, so when `discovery.enabled` is false (the default) the card renders nothing and FullSystem is BYTE-IDENTICAL.** PURE-UI: NO backend change, NO new endpoint, NO `/api/config` change, NO new npm dependency. NO emoji (HXI #3); amber/blue palette; full type annotations. PRE-RESERVED AD-708 sub-number (current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**) — NOT a new top-level AD.

**QR deferred.** The QR-code affordance (a phone scans instead of typing the `.local` URL) needs a new bundled QR library and is the deferred **AD-708f-1**. v1 surfaces the readable/copyable address only — a deliberate no-new-dependency scope.

### AD-708f-1: scannable QR on the discovery card (#484)

**Decision.** AD-708f surfaced the readable/copyable `.local` URL but deferred the QR affordance for lack of a bundled encoder; AD-708f-1 lands it. When discovery is off (the default) the gate returns null before the QR mounts, so FullSystem stays BYTE-IDENTICAL. **Scannability is the load-bearing constraint.** A QR must be high-contrast to scan, and the HXI background is dark (`#0a0a14`); the amber chrome palette would NOT scan as QR modules. So the QR renders DARK modules (`#14141e`) on a LIGHT tile (`#e8e8f0`) — a deliberate "scan target" — with a 4-module quiet zone (`marginSize={4}`), `size={140}`, error-correction `level="M"`, and `title="ProbOS HXI address"`; the amber palette stays on the chrome labels only, never the modules. The `url` build and the `enabled` gate are REUSED UNCHANGED — the QR is purely ADDED inside the gate.

It ships its own `index.d.ts`/`index.d.mts`, so NO `@types/qrcode.react` is added (an `@types` shim would conflict with the bundled declarations). No backend change, no new endpoint, no `/api/config` change. PRE-RESERVED AD-708 sub-number (#484; current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**) — NOT a new top-level AD.

**Tests + gates.** EXTEND `ui/src/components/bridge/__tests__/ConnectPhoneCard.test.tsx` with +2 cases reusing the file's BF-287 real-`useSettingsStore` `seed(...)` helper: renders-a-scannable-QR (the `connect-phone-qr` testid mounts an inline `svg`, and asserts NO `canvas` — the QRCodeSVG-not-Canvas guarantee) when discovery is enabled, and QR-absent when discovery is disabled (the byte-identical-off guard). ### AD-708a: usePadDevice device-class primitive (#484)

**Problem.** #484 (AD-708) is the PADD mobile-companion experience. AD-473 already shipped Web Push + PWA (manifest, service worker, viewport meta) and AD-392 already shipped `useBreakpoint` (width breakpoints), so the genuinely-missing foundation is a *device-class* predicate: "is this client a handheld PADD?" The later mobile shell (AD-708b) and gesture layer (AD-708d) will route on this answer. Routing on viewport WIDTH alone is wrong: a desktop user who snaps a window narrower than 768px would be dumped into the chat-only mobile projection — an untested-UI break the HXI has suffered before. The predicate must distinguish a real phone from a narrow desktop window.

**Decision.** Add ONLY the pure primitive, wired NOWHERE, in TWO NEW FILES with ZERO edits to any existing file (the desktop HXI is provably byte-identical). `ui/src/hooks/usePadDevice.ts` exports three fully-typed symbols: `hasCoarsePointer(): boolean` (pure — `window.matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches`, honest-degrading to `false` when matchMedia is absent or throws, mirroring `prefersReducedMotion`'s guard); `isPadDevice(): boolean` (pure — `hasCoarsePointer() && getBreakpoint() === 'mobile'`, composing AD-392's exported `getBreakpoint` so the width logic is NOT re-implemented — DRY); and `usePadDevice(): boolean` (a subscribing hook that seeds from `isPadDevice()` and re-evaluates on BOTH the `window` `resize` event (width axis) AND the `(pointer: coarse)` `MediaQueryList` `change` event (pointer axis), using the `addEventListener`-with-`addListener`-fallback + try/catch teardown idiom from `usePrefersReducedMotion`, honest-degrading to a stable `false` when matchMedia is unavailable and cleaning up all listeners on unmount). A PADD requires a COARSE primary pointer (touch) AND the `'mobile'` breakpoint — so a narrow desktop window with a fine mouse pointer is excluded by the pointer gate, which is exactly the byte-identical-desktop guarantee. This is the progressive-disclosure (HXI Design Principle #5) DEVICE gate, intentionally distinct from width-only `useBreakpoint`. NO emoji (HXI #3). It is NOT wired into `main.tsx`/`App.tsx`/`CompactApp.tsx`/`useBreakpoint.ts`/any component or store — that routing is AD-708b. AD-708a is a PRE-RESERVED AD-708 sub-number (current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**) — NOT a new top-level AD. Note: AD-708-1 is reserved for the native app; AD-708b (mobile shell), AD-708c (simplified 2D mesh), and AD-708d (swipe gestures) are the follow-on responsive sub-ADs.

**Tests + gates.** NEW `ui/src/hooks/__tests__/usePadDevice.test.ts` (vitest) mirrors `usePrefersReducedMotion.test.ts` (the `vi.stubGlobal('matchMedia', ...)` + `afterEach(() => vi.unstubAllGlobals())` idiom) and the AD-392 GlassAdaptive `Object.defineProperty(window,'innerWidth',{value,writable,configurable})` width convention (captured + restored in `afterEach`). 9 cases: `hasCoarsePointer` → false absent / true coarse / false fine; `isPadDevice` → false at desktop width with a coarse pointer (the width gate), false at mobile width with matchMedia absent (the narrow-desktop-window stays OUT — the byte-identical guard), true with a coarse pointer at 375px; `usePadDevice` → false absent, true coarse+mobile, and an updates-on-resize case (`innerWidth` change + `act(() => window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize')))` proves the subscription). ### AD-841c: HXI deep-link view reader (#816)

**Problem.** The SPA reads `window.location.hash` only ONCE at boot (`ui/src/main.tsx`) to choose CompactApp-vs-App; inside `<App>` all navigation is in-app Zustand flags set by clicks — no URL hint can land the HXI on a management surface. The Electron desktop host (#816) wants tray entries + a Command-Center mode that deep-link to Agents · Skills · Settings · Ward Room · Work · System, but the primitive to READ a `#view=<id>` hint and route it to the existing surfaces did not exist.

**Decision.** Add a PURE, dependency-injected reader `ui/src/deepLinkView.ts` (`ViewTarget` union, `VIEW_TARGETS`, `parseViewTarget`, `dispatchViewTarget`, `applyDeepLinkView`) plus ONE behavior-preserving boot `useEffect` in `App.tsx` calling `applyDeepLinkView(window.location.hash, { store: useStore, settings: useSettingsStore })`. The reader RENDERS the AD-840 surfaces via the EXISTING store actions verified at HEAD — `setState({mainViewer:'work'|'system'})` for Work/System, `setState({shipsLockerOpen:true})` for Skills = Ship's Locker, `void getState().openCrewManifest()` / `openWardRoom()` / `openSettings()` for Agents/Ward Room/Settings — it rebuilds NO panel. Default-OFF: with no `view` param `parseViewTarget` returns null, `applyDeepLinkView` dispatches nothing, and boot is byte-identical. A combined `#compact&view=system` resolves to `system` so a compact hint and a view hint coexist without breaking `main.tsx`'s `includes('compact')`. `desktop/`, every AD-840 panel, and `config/system.yaml` are UNTOUCHED. PRE-RESERVED AD-841 sub-number (current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**) — NOT a new top-level. **AD-841b is reserved for the web-control half; AD-841c is the renumbered Electron-parity primitive.** Tray entries + URL construction are the deferred AD-841d (`desktop/`).

**Why DI-pure.** The store handles are INJECTED via a `deps: { store, settings }` parameter rather than imported-and-called at module top level. The deps are typed with `typeof import('./store/useStore').useStore` (and the settings equivalent) — a fully-erased type-only reference, so NO runtime store import enters the reader's module graph and `deepLinkView.ts` carries no React/zustand runtime coupling. That makes the parse + dispatch logic unit-testable with trivial recording fakes (no React, no jsdom, no real store) and keeps the boot effect the ONLY place the real hooks are wired — App.tsx stays the shell, not a management surface.
