### AD-731a-1c (2026-06-23) — bus auto-resolution-on-receive for cross-host attachments (issue #638)

**Context.** AD-731a-1 shipped the SERVE side (a default-OFF, content-verifying endpoint + a `fetch_remote_attachment` client) but nothing CALLS the fetcher on the receive path. When a host receives a federated `IntentMessage` referencing an attachment SHA it lacks locally (the AD-731 ref shape — bus carries the SHA, store carries the bytes), the local agents that consume the ref dereference a SHA the store never saw → a `failed_to_load` marker (llm_client.py). AD-731a-1c closes that gap: at the single inbound choke point, auto-fetch the missing bytes from the SENDER peer BEFORE the local broadcast. Default-OFF, non-blocking, honest-degrade. AD-731a-1c is a PRE-RESERVED AD-731a sub-number (current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**) — NOT a new top-level.

**Decision.** Add an optional `A2APeerConfig.node_id` + a default-OFF `AttachmentsConfig.auto_resolve_remote_enabled`, a new pure-plus-guarded `federation/attachment_resolve.py`, and ONE call site in `bridge.py:_handle_intent_request`. `fetch_remote_attachment`, the serving endpoint `routers/federation_attachments.py`, the `AttachmentStore` Protocol, the AD-731 ref shape, `forward_intent`'s send-side strip, and `config/system.yaml` are all UNTOUCHED.

**Design decisions.**
- **DD-1 (the load-bearing gap was sender→peer, solved with an optional `node_id`).** The wire payload carries `source_node` (a federation node_id) but A2A http peers were configured with `peer_url` + `auth_token` ONLY — there was NO resolver from a node_id to a fetchable (url, token). The ZMQ/NATS `PeerConfig.node_id` (config.py) is a different, non-http transport (AD-882: "node identity only at config/peer granularity"; AD-1050 keeps A2A disjoint). The minimal enabling primitive is an OPTIONAL `node_id: str = ""` on `A2APeerConfig`: the operator declares "this http A2A peer IS federation node X". Empty (default) = unmapped → `resolve_sender_peer` never matches it → never an auto-resolution source (byte-identical). No new peer-discovery machinery.
- **DD-2 (default-OFF, byte-identical receive path).** `auto_resolve_remote_enabled` defaults False. When off, `resolve_missing_attachments` returns 0 on its first guard — before any store read or network call — so `_handle_intent_request` is identical to today. Pinned by `test_flag_off_byte_identical_no_fetch` (flag off + missing ref + a VALID sender ⇒ the httpx `MockTransport` records ZERO requests and the store stays empty).
- **DD-3 (reuse `fetch_remote_attachment` as-is — no second integrity path).** The orchestrator calls the AD-731a-1 fetcher unchanged: 64-hex validation, `Authorization: Bearer`, `sha256(blob) == content_hash` or reject (tampered/corrupt bytes NEVER stored), store-is-SSOT-on-mime. AD-731a-1c adds NO new verification logic — `test_tamper_rejected_not_stored` proves a sha-mismatched body is still rejected through the resolver. Per-SHA `if await store.exists(sha): continue` makes it idempotent (already-local SHAs cost no network call).
- **DD-4 (guarded orchestrator — NEVER raises, NEVER blocks the broadcast).** Two-tier honest-degrade: a per-fetch try/except (Tier-2 log-and-degrade — one failed peer fetch never aborts the others; local agents fall back to the `failed_to_load` marker) plus an OUTER try/except that logs a warning and returns the count-so-far. `count` is initialized BEFORE the outer try so the except can always return it. The bridge call site ALSO wraps the call in its own try/except — the broadcast proceeds whether resolution succeeds, partially fails, or throws. `test_fetch_failure_swallowed_returns_zero` (peer 500) proves no exception escapes and nothing is stored.
- **DD-5 (pure extraction is forward-safe for AD-731a-1d).** `extract_attachment_shas` reads the bare `params["attachment_ref"]` shape (the ONLY shape that crosses today) AND, defensively, the AD-731 `vision_messages[].content[].source.sha256` block shape — so when the send-side complement lands, the resolver already handles rich chat-fanout refs. It dedups first-seen, drops non-64-hex, and never raises (params may have any shape).

**Caveats.**
- **C-A (send-side strip bounds the live effect — AD-731a-1d forward marker).** `forward_intent` STRIPS `vision_messages` on send (BF-265), so today only the bare `attachment_ref` SHA crosses the wire. The full federated-image path also requires a send-side un-strip (or a ref-only re-attach) — the DEFERRED complement **AD-731a-1d**. AD-731a-1c is the receive half; its live effect is bounded until 1d lands.
- **C-B (A2A-configured sender only).** Auto-resolution fires ONLY when the operator has configured the sender as an `a2a.outbound_peer` tagged `node_id == source_node`. An arbitrary `source_node` with no mapped peer is skipped (no fetch) — there is no resolver from a bare node_id to a URL otherwise.

**Gates.** NEW `tests/test_ad731a_1c_auto_resolve.py` (10, BF-287: real `FilesystemAttachmentStore` on `tmp_path` + real `AttachmentsConfig`/`FederationConfig`/`A2APeerConfig` + httpx `MockTransport` — no MagicMock at the boundary): the 6 orchestrator cases (off-byte-identical / on-fetch-store / idempotent / unmapped-sender / fetch-failure-swallowed / tamper-rejected), 2 pure-function cases (`resolve_sender_peer`, `extract_attachment_shas`), runtime-None, and config-defaults-OFF. `test_ad731a_1c_auto_resolve.py test_ad731a_remote_attachment.py test_config.py -q -n 0` → **26 passed** (the AD-731a-1 byte-identical proof unchanged + config); federation-bridge regression `test_federation.py -q -n 0` → **42 passed** (the receive-path wire-in didn't break the inbound/outbound bridge); import smoke `import probos.federation.bridge, probos.federation.attachment_resolve` → ok. Left UNCOMMITTED.

### AD-841 (2026-06-22) — read-only desktop-integration STATUS console (config-state + derived presence; control deferred to AD-841b)

**Context.** AD-751 wired the Desktop UX Surface (single-instance lifecycle lock, tray, global hotkey, notification center) but exposed NO operator-facing read surface — there was no way to see, from the HXI, what desktop integration is configured or whether it came up this boot. AD-841 v1 is the minimal READ-ONLY first slice: a default-safe status readout of the configured `config.desktop` values plus a derived "wired-this-boot" presence signal. It is deliberately NOT live OS truth, does NOT enumerate apps/windows, and exposes NO launch/start/stop control. AD-841 is a PRE-RESERVED number (current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**) — NOT a new top-level.

**Decision.** Add `routers/desktop.py` (`GET /api/desktop/status`, behind `require_crew_scope`) + a standalone read-only `ui/src/components/desktop/DesktopConsole.tsx`. `config/system.yaml`, the AD-751 desktop lifecycle/tray/hotkey/notification modules, and `DesktopConfig` are all UNTOUCHED. The control/launch half is the deferred AD-841b.

**Design decisions.**
- **DD-1 (config-state + derived presence, NOT live OS truth).** The endpoint reports the operator-configured `config.desktop` settings (enabled, tray autostart, hotkey binding, notification timeout, quiet hours, autostart) — what the operator ASKED FOR — plus a derived `active`/per-subsystem presence signal (was the subsystem wired this boot). It deliberately does NOT probe the live OS (is the tray icon actually painted right now, is the hotkey hook actually installed in the window manager) and does NOT enumerate running apps/windows. A status readout of declared config + boot-time wiring is honest, cheap, and side-effect-free; live-OS introspection is a larger, platform-specific surface deferred with the control half.
- **DD-2 (no-path-leak privacy — basename only, test-enforced).** The single-instance lock path (`config.desktop.lock_file`, default `~/.probos/yeo.lock`) embeds the OS home directory and username. The endpoint returns ONLY `Path(cfg.lock_file).expanduser().name` (the basename, e.g. "yeo.lock") plus a derived `present` boolean — never the full path, home dir, or username. This is pinned by a dedicated `test_no_path_leak` that asserts "yeo.lock" IS present but `os.path.expanduser("~")`, `.probos`, `Users`, and the current `getpass.getuser()` are ALL absent from the serialized body.
- **DD-3 (presence via PUBLIC attributes only — Law of Demeter).** Liveness is read as `getattr(runtime, "<x>", None) is not None` against the four PUBLIC runtime attrs wired in `startup/finalize.py:_wire_desktop_ux` (`desktop_lifecycle`, `tray_manager`, `hotkey_listener`, `notification_center`) — NEVER private fields (tray `_status`, hotkey `_listening`). Reaching into another object's privates to infer liveness would couple the status surface to the subsystems' internals; the public-attribute presence signal is the narrow, stable contract.
- **DD-4 (honest-degrade, never 500).** `cfg is None` (desktop unconfigured) yields a fully-defaulted OFF shape; `lock_path.exists()` is guarded against `OSError`; and the whole body is wrapped so ANY unexpected error returns the defaulted OFF shape with HTTP 200. A status read must never fault the surface that calls it.
- **DD-5 (read-only — control deferred to AD-841b).** This slice has NO launch/start/stop/restart path and writes nothing. The UI panel is standalone and deliberately NOT mounted in App.tsx (it is a surface to be placed deliberately, not auto-wired). Control of the desktop subsystem (start/stop tray, rebind hotkey, acquire/release lock) is the AD-841b slice, behind the operator gate — mirroring the AD-813 BROWSE→AD-813b install posture.

**Gates.** NEW `tests/test_ad841_desktop_status.py` (5, BF-287: real FastAPI `TestClient` + `SimpleNamespace` config-shaped runtime via `dependency_overrides[get_runtime]` — no MagicMock at the boundary): off-shape (presence flags false, config values still reported), on/active-presence (`desktop_lifecycle` + the three public attrs set → `active:true`, presence true, binding reported), `test_no_path_leak` (DD-2), deterministic lock-present (real file in `tmp_path`, containing dir never leaked), honest-degrade no-config → 200. NEW `ui/src/components/desktop/DesktopConsole.test.tsx` (5: enabled/active render, calm off-state, self-gate on fetch-reject + on no-data, no-emoji scan). `test_ad841_desktop_status.py test_distribution.py::TestFastAPIEndpoints::test_create_app_returns_fastapi -q -n 0` → **6 passed** (5 + app-creation mount smoke); focused vitest **5 passed**; full UI **273 files / 1754 passed | 1 skipped (0 regressions)**; `npm run build` clean. STAGED (not committed).

### AD-813 (2026-06-22) — read-only remote skill/pack marketplace BROWSE endpoint (issue #737)

**Context.** AD-1003a/b/c gave ProbOS an installed-pack inventory (the local `GET /api/packs` read surface) but no way to discover packs/skills that are NOT yet installed. AD-813 is the minimal first slice of a remote marketplace: a default-OFF endpoint that FETCHES an operator-configured registry index so the operator can BROWSE what's available. **BROWSE ONLY — nothing is downloaded, written, scanned, loaded, or executed** (install is the deferred AD-813b slice, behind the operator trust gate). AD-813 was a FREE, verified-unused number (git grep of DECISIONS/PROGRESS/src/ui/tests = 0); current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**, so no new top-level number was minted.

**Decision.** Add `SkillsMarketplaceConfig` (default-OFF) next to `PacksConfig`, a new `packs/marketplace.py` (SSRF-guarded fetch + pure parse), and a new `routers/marketplace.py` (`GET /api/skills/marketplace`) mounted in `api.py`. `config/system.yaml`, `routers/packs.py`, `PacksConfig`, the pack scanner/loader/manifest, and `ArdClient` are all UNTOUCHED.

**Design decisions.**
- **DD-1 (config-only-URL is the load-bearing SSRF guard).** The registry host comes ONLY from `config.skills_marketplace.registry_url` (operator config). The endpoint exposes NO `url`/`registry_url` query param — the ONLY request input that reaches the fetch is `query`, appended as `params={"q": query}` (a SEARCH TERM that NEVER changes the host). This mirrors the AD-1046 `ArdClient` posture ("fetches ONLY the operator-configured endpoints, never an entry's `url` field"). `follow_redirects=False` is passed on EVERY request (so an injected client cannot weaken the guard, and a 302 to a metadata-service SSRF target is never dereferenced), and the body is truncated to `max_bytes` BEFORE `json.loads`. Disabled (`enabled=False` OR empty `registry_url`) returns the inert shape with ZERO HTTP calls. The two SSRF properties are pinned by dedicated tests: `ssrf_ignores_request_url` (a hostile `?url=evil` is silently ignored — the captured request host equals the configured registry ONLY) and `no_redirect_follow` (an injected client whose own default is the UNSAFE `follow_redirects=True` still does not follow a 302, because the per-request `False` wins).
- **DD-2 (NO private-IP/loopback block — config-only-URL is sufficient).** Unlike the mesh `http_fetch` agent (which resolves DNS and blocks private/loopback IPs because it fetches caller-supplied URLs), AD-813 deliberately does NOT block private or on-prem hosts. The registry URL is operator-configured, not request-supplied, so a private-IP block would only break the legitimate on-prem registry case (a registry running inside the operator's own network) while adding no security — the host can never come from an attacker. The config-only-URL guard (DD-1) is the complete SSRF defense for this surface.
- **DD-3 (BROWSE only — install deferred to AD-813b).** This slice fetches + parses + returns inert descriptors. `parse_marketplace_index` is a PURE honest-degrade parser (accepts `{"packs":[…]}`/`{"entries":[…]}`/bare list, mirrors the AD-1003b scanner descriptor field names, skips a malformed entry rather than raising), and `MarketplaceEntry.skills`/`agents` are opaque component NAMES — never opened, fetched, or executed. Downloading, verifying, and loading a pack into the live registries is the AD-813b slice behind the operator trust gate, consistent with the AD-1003c read-only / AD-894/AD-900 governed-write posture.
- **DD-4 (honest-degrade everywhere, no internals leaked).** A `>= 400` status → `registry returned N`; a timeout/network failure → `registry unreachable`; invalid JSON → `invalid registry response`. The error string is always SHORT and generic (never an internal message or traceback), and the endpoint always returns 200 with an empty result set rather than raising. DI (`http: httpx.AsyncClient | None`) makes every path testable with `httpx.MockTransport` and no network; an injected client is never closed by the module.

**Gates.** NEW `tests/test_ad813_marketplace.py` (11, BF-287: real `httpx.MockTransport` + real FastAPI `TestClient` + a `SimpleNamespace` config-shaped runtime — no MagicMock at the boundary; the router builds its own `httpx.AsyncClient`, so the tests monkeypatch `httpx.AsyncClient` onto a deterministic `MockTransport` and assert `clients_built == 0` to prove the disabled path makes ZERO HTTP): disabled-off / disabled-no-url (exploding transport never built), happy-path (results mirror the descriptor), query-filter, pagination+cap, timeout / bad-json / non-200 honest-degrade, `ssrf_ignores_request_url`, `no_redirect_follow`, and a pure `parse_marketplace_index` honest-degrade unit. `test_ad813_marketplace.py test_config.py test_distribution.py::TestFastAPIEndpoints::test_create_app_returns_fastapi -q -n 0` → **15 passed** (11 marketplace + 3 config + 1 app-creation mount smoke — the new router mounts without breaking app build). STAGED (not committed).

### AD-731a-1 (2026-06-22) — cross-host attachment distribution v1: fail-closed serving endpoint + content-verifying client (issue #638)

**Context.** AD-731 made attachments content-addressed (sha256) and AD-720 introduced the `AttachmentStore` Protocol seam, but attachment bytes were only ever served to the local HXI (`GET /api/chat/attachments/{sha}`). A federation peer that holds a ref to a content-hash has no governed way to pull the bytes. AD-731a-1 is the minimal first slice: a default-OFF, fail-closed endpoint that serves bytes by content-hash to an *authenticated* peer, plus a client helper that verifies sha256 before storing. Current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**; AD-731a-1 is the **pre-reserved AD-731 sub-number, NOT a new top-level**.

**Decision.** Add a new `routers/federation_attachments.py` serving endpoint (behind `require_crew_scope`) and a new `federation/attachment_fetch.py` verifying client. Add a single default-OFF config field `AttachmentsConfig.serve_remote_enabled`. The `AttachmentStore` Protocol, the AD-731 ref shape, the existing chat attachments route, `require_crew_scope`, and `config/system.yaml` are all UNTOUCHED.

**Design decisions.**
- **DD-1 (default-OFF + fail-closed token hardening).** Two gates, in order: the feature flag (`serve_remote_enabled`, default `False`) 404s when off (byte-identical to "feature absent"; does not leak token state); then, because `require_crew_scope` is a *pass-through* when `auth.crew_scope_token` is empty, the body 403s (`remote_serving_requires_token`) when the token is unset. We never serve bytes through an open gate — an operator who turns on remote serving without configuring a token gets a hard refusal, not silent open access.
- **DD-2 (Defense in Depth, documented status per gate).** After the flag/token gates: 64-hex format → 400 (no store touch on malformed input), existence → 404, size > `max_attachment_bytes` → 413, then serve. Each boundary validates independently rather than assuming the caller checked.
- **DD-3 (Protocol-safe serve path).** `get_path` is confirmed to be ON the `AttachmentStore` Protocol (`async def get_path(content_hash) -> Path`), so the endpoint uses `FileResponse(await store.get_path(sha), media_type=ext_to_mime(path.suffix))` — mirroring the proven `routers/chat.py` GET serve pattern, with the crew-scope auth dependency added. (Had `get_path` been impl-only, the fallback was `Response(content=await store.read(sha), media_type=mime)`.) The store accessor prefers `runtime.attachment_store` (set at startup; injectable on a tmp_path in tests per BF-287) and falls back to the chat-router resolver.
- **DD-4 (client-side integrity is the load-bearing guard).** `fetch_remote_attachment` validates the 64-hex hash BEFORE any network call (`ValueError`), then after the GET it enforces `sha256(received_bytes) == content_hash` and REJECTS (returns False, never stores) on mismatch — tampered or corrupt bytes from a peer can never poison the local store. A peer 404 → False; a non-404 ≥400 → raise; an oversize body → False; an unstorable mime → False (the store is the single authority on mime acceptability via a `ValueError` on write). `store` and `http` are DI for no-network testing.
- **DD-5 (scope discipline).** NATS transport, a mime-fastpath, and auto-resolution (a peer auto-pulling a ref it lacks) are DEFERRED to later AD-731 follow-ups. This slice is serve + verify only.

**Gates.** NEW `tests/test_ad731a_remote_attachment.py` (BF-287: real `FilesystemAttachmentStore` on `tmp_path` + real `AttachmentsConfig`/`AuthConfig` + real ASGI app — no MagicMock at the substrate boundary): 7 serving (200 known-sha; 404 unknown; 404 flag-off byte-identical; 403 token-unset fail-closed; 401 wrong+missing Bearer; 400 bad-sha no-store-call; 413 over-cap) + 6 client (roundtrip-verified-and-stored; tamper-detected-not-stored; 404→False; bad-mime-rejected; malformed-hash-raises-before-network; oversize-rejected). `test_ad731a_remote_attachment.py test_config.py -q -n 0` → 16 passed; app-creation smoke `test_distribution.py` green (the new router mounts without breaking app build). STAGED (not committed).

### AD-962a (2026-06-22) — name the likely first responder in the AD-962 typing beat (Natural Conversation epic #882, #896)

**Context.** AD-962 fills the 10-30s of dead air before the first group fan-out reply with a generic "The crew is thinking…" beat. When the Captain's message directly addresses a crew participant ("@Ezri, what's the read?"), a generic beat under-sells what the UI already knows — the addressed crew member is the LIKELY first responder. AD-962a names them. Client-side, cosmetic only: the real fan-out reply still arrives correctly regardless of the guess. Current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**; AD-962a is the **pre-reserved #882/#896 sub-number, NOT a new top-level**.

**Decision.** Add a pure `ui/src/chat/firstResponder.ts` helper and wire it at the ONE AD-962 beat site in `ProfileChatTab.tsx`. No backend, no store change, no `TypingIndicator` change.

**Design decisions.**
- **DD-1 (mirror the server LEADING-address rule).** `extractDirectedCallsign(text)` mirrors `crew_profile.extract_directed_callsign` rule 1: a LEADING `@cs` / vocative comma (`Yeo,`) / vocative colon (`Yeo:`), lower-cased. A bare leading word ("Data shows …") or a referential mention ("I agree with Yeo.") is NOT an address. Pure (no store/DOM/fetch) so the cosmetic guess unit-tests in isolation and stays off the hot path.
- **DD-2 (resolve to a CREW participant only).** `resolveFirstResponder(text, participantIds, agents)` returns `{agentId, callsign}` only when the directed callsign matches a thread participant who is crew (`isCrew`) with a callsign; excludes 'captain' and non-crew; case-insensitive match (the server returns lower-cased). Returns null otherwise → the caller uses the generic beat.
- **DD-3 (byte-identical generic fallback).** The beat is set inside the existing `>=2`-crew group branch with the SAME `setTypingAgent` payload shape (`{threadId, agentId, callsign, verb:'thinking'}`). When resolved it names the responder (real `agentId`/`callsign`); else it is the AD-962 generic `{agentId:'', callsign:'The crew', verb:'thinking'}` — semantically identical to before. The store `typingAgent` slice already supports a named callsign (AD-952) and `TypingIndicator` already renders "{callsign} is {verb}", so ZERO store/indicator change is needed.
- **DD-4 (cosmetic, not authoritative).** The guess does NOT influence routing, the fan-out request, or which agents actually reply — it only fills dead air, and self-corrects the moment the first real reply lands (AD-960 clears the beat). 1:1 and meeting-voice paths are untouched (the beat is gated to the `>=2`-crew group branch).

**Gates.** NEW `ui/src/chat/__tests__/firstResponder.test.ts` (8 cases) + EXTEND `ProfileChatTab.groupsend.test.tsx` (+2 faithful beat-mirror cases — named on @-mention, generic on no-mention, never-set on a 1:1). Focused vitest 15 passed (2 files); full UI 272 files / 1749 passed | 1 skipped (0 regressions); `npm run build` clean. STAGED (not committed).

### AD-958c (2026-06-22) — peer-corrects-peer DETECT-AND-OBSERVE-ONLY (Natural Conversation epic #882, #894)

**Context.** AD-958 closed the POSITIVE half of the conversational trust loop (a convergent conversation credits each voice). The NEGATIVE half — peer-corrects-peer — was config-encoded (`conversation_trust_negative_weight=0.15`, asymmetry-validated) but deliberately UNUSED in v1. AD-958c builds the negative *signal* but stops SHORT of the trust write: a pure lexical detector cannot reliably distinguish a VALID correction from a corrector who is themselves the wrong one, or from a preference disagreement — and a 0.15 negative (3× a corroboration) on a fuzzy signal would violate Minimal Authority. So v1 is DETECT-AND-OBSERVE-ONLY: detect the correction, emit a structured log, write NOTHING. The actual `record_outcome(success=False)` write is deferred to **AD-958d**, gated on the detector's measured precision over live transcripts. Backend only. Current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**; AD-958c is the **pre-reserved #882/#894 sub-number, NOT a new top-level** (AD-958a exploration + AD-958b independence-quorum already taken).

**Decision.** Add a pure detector to `cognitive/conversation_trust.py` and an observe-only wiring in `routers/thread_fanout.py`, both default-OFF behind a NEW switch separate from the AD-958 positive flag. `trust.py` and `config/system.yaml` are UNTOUCHED.

**Design decisions.**
- **DD-1 (precision over recall).** `_CORRECTION_CUE_RE` is a TIGHT allowlist — an assertion that a prior claim is factually WRONG (`"that's not right/not correct/incorrect/wrong/false/a mistake/an error"`, `"not quite right"`, `"you're wrong/mistaken/incorrect"`, `"correction:"`, `"actually, that's wrong"`). Mere DISAGREEMENT ("I disagree", "I'd weigh it differently", "from my vantage", "I'm not sure", "not necessarily", "I see it differently") must NOT match. A correction we MISS is recoverable; a false negative trust write is not (AD-958d's concern), so the cue errs toward silence. The 6-way parametrized disagreement guard is the forcing function.
- **DD-2 (attribution = explicit cue ∧ directed-at-a-prior-speaker).** A signal fires only when a reply (A) matches the cue AND (B) directly addresses (the AD-951 `extract_directed_callsign` — leading `@cs` / `Yeo,` / `Yeo:`) a peer whose callsign SPOKE EARLIER in the transcript. No self-sourcing (`corrected != corrector`). NOT convergence-gated (a correction is meaningful even in a divergent exchange — the opposite of the AD-958 positive path). Deduped per (corrector, corrected) pair, sorted for determinism, capped at `max_signals`.
- **DD-3 (frozen `ConversationCorrectionSignal`, OBSERVE-shaped).** The signal carries `corrected_agent_id`, `corrector_id`, `cue`, `intent_type` — and deliberately NO `weight`/`success` (those are the deferred write's shape). It is a DETECTION record, not a trust outcome.
- **DD-4 (separate observe switch, default-OFF byte-identical).** NEW `GroupChatConfig.conversation_trust_correction_observe_enabled=False` is a SEPARATE flag from `conversation_trust_enabled` (the positive write) so the Captain can run the correction detector in observe-only mode — emitting a log per detection, writing nothing — to measure precision BEFORE AD-958d flips on any negative write. `_validate_conversation_trust` is UNCHANGED (the new bool has no cross-field invariant). OFF ⇒ `_observe_conversation_corrections` returns on its first line ⇒ the fan-out is byte-identical.
- **DD-5 (observe-only wiring, Tier-2 honest-degrade).** NEW sibling `_observe_conversation_corrections(runtime, thread, all_replies, agent_ids)` wired ONCE right after the untouched `_record_conversation_trust` call, just before `group_chat_fanout` returns. When ON it runs the pure detector and emits one `"AD-958c[observe]"` INFO log per detection (naming corrector + corrected + cue), and calls NO `record_outcome`. Any failure logs a warning and returns — the fan-out result is never touched.
- **Tier-agnostic detector / CORE immunity is the write's concern.** The PURE detector emits a signal even when the corrected agent is a CORE-tier id; immunity (the `record_outcome` early-return for `CORE_INFRASTRUCTURE`) belongs to the FUTURE write (AD-958d), not the detector.

**Deferred (AD-958d).** The negative trust write, with the exact kwargs already documented: `record_outcome(sig.corrected_agent_id, success=False, weight=conversation_trust_negative_weight, intent_type=sig.intent_type, episode_id="", verifier_id=sig.corrector_id, source="conversation")`. Gated on the observed precision of the AD-958c detector on live transcripts.

**Gates.** NEW `tests/test_ad958c_peer_correction.py` — 17 cases: fires-on-directed-correction; the 6-way parametrized DISAGREEMENT false-positive guard (the critical precision test); no-self-sourcing; requires-directed-address; corrected-must-have-spoken-earlier; correction-before-target-speaks; bounded/dedupe/`max_signals=0`; pure determinism; tier-agnostic pure detector; and end-to-end through `group_chat_fanout` against a REAL `TrustNetwork()` (BF-287, NOT MagicMock) — observe-OFF byte-identical, observe-ON logs-but-writes-nothing (`get_score` unchanged), ON-no-correction-no-log. `test_ad958c_peer_correction.py test_ad958_conversation_trust.py test_config.py test_ad935_group_reactivity.py test_ad914_group_chat_fanout.py test_ad955_room_awareness.py -q -n 0` **85 passed** (zero regressions). STAGED (not committed).

### AD-954a (2026-06-22) — thread-keyed group/call surface mount (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#890)

**Context.** AD-965 made the `AgentProfilePanel` a neutral, nameable ROOM when its active thread is a group (>=2 crew), but the panel still MOUNTED off `activeProfileAgent` — the `if (!agentId || !agent) return null` gate keyed the ENTIRE surface to a host agent. AD-954 reframed the meeting toggle as a "call"; a call/room is owned by the THREAD, not by whichever agent happened to seed `activeProfileAgent`. So a group/call surface would vanish whenever `activeProfileAgent` was null or stale, even with a perfectly valid active group thread. AD-954a decouples the mount: the surface is keyed by the thread, and the host anchor is DERIVED from the thread's participants. Frontend-only, ONE component. Current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**; AD-954a is the **pre-reserved #882/#890 sub-number, NOT a new top-level**.

**Decision.** In `AgentProfilePanel`, detect the active group thread from `activeProfileThreadId` (via the AD-919 `isGroupChat`) BEFORE the render gate, and derive `agentId` from it: in group mode `agentId = hostAgentId(thread) ?? activeProfileAgent` (the host id `ProfileChatTab` needs for its 1:1-fallback plumbing + hostCallsign); in a 1:1 `agentId = activeProfileAgent` (byte-identical). The room therefore renders from `thread.id` and survives an absent/stale `activeProfileAgent`.

**Design decisions.**
- **DD-1 (thread-keyed anchor, hook-order safe).** The first selector is renamed back to its store name (`activeProfileAgent`); the thread → `activeGroupThread` / `isGroupSurface` / `agentId` derivation is a plain (non-hook) IIFE placed AFTER the store selectors and BEFORE any `useState`/`useEffect`, so React hook order is unchanged. The duplicate post-gate `activeGroupThread`/`isGroupSurface` block (introduced by AD-965) is removed; only `groupTitle` remains there, now reading the hoisted `activeGroupThread`.
- **DD-2 (a room is not the host's profile).** The host-scoped `/api/agent/{id}/profile` fetch is skipped in group mode (`!agentId || isGroupSurface`) — its data is never shown (the title is the room title and the agent-scoped tabs are collapsed), so the panel is not coupled to the host. `isGroupSurface` joins that effect's dep array.
- **DD-3 (a room is not the host's DM).** `markAgentRead` fires only for a 1:1 (`agentId && !isGroupSurface`) — opening a room must not mark the derived anchor agent's 1:1 conversation read. `isGroupSurface` joins that effect's dep array.
- **DD-4 (1:1 byte-identical).** With no active group thread, `isGroupSurface` is false and `agentId` is exactly `activeProfileAgent`: the gate, the host profile fetch, `markAgentRead`, the agent identity, and the full agent-scoped tab set are unchanged.
- **Scope bound.** ONE component (`AgentProfilePanel.tsx`); `ProfileChatTab` / `GroupChatHeader` / `MeetingView`, all store actions, and the render gate are untouched. The larger separate-window / multi-room window manager (a true call surface that survives navigating away) remains a FUTURE marker, not built here.

**Gates.** NEW `ui/src/__tests__/AgentProfilePanel.threadKeyed.test.tsx` (4 cases, mirrors the AD-965 `groupSurface` harness): (1) thread-keyed mount with `activeProfileAgent` null renders the `group-surface-title` — RED on pre-edit code (the gate returns null), GREEN post-edit (the decoupling forcing function); (2) `markAgentRead` suppressed in group mode, fired on a 1:1; (3) host `/profile` fetch suppressed in group mode, fired on a 1:1; (4) 1:1 byte-identical (identity + full tab set + profile fetched + marks read). `ProfileChatTab` is mocked in THIS file only to isolate the panel's own `/profile` fetch — the child makes its own AD-718 voice-profile `/profile` fetch to the identical URL, which would otherwise pollute case (3). Focused vitest **4 passed**; full UI 271 files / **1739 passed | 1 skipped** (0 regressions); `npm run build` clean (`tsc -b` proves no duplicate-const / hook-order error). STAGED (not committed). Closes the #890 thread-keyed-mount slice.

### AD-958 — conversational trust learning loop (convergence-only v1, epic #882, #894)

**Context.** The group-chat facilitator (AD-915) already ranks the room with a `trust` term and AD-955 surfaces that ranking as an advisory signal, but trust itself only ever moved from VERIFICATION (red-team / DAG outcomes). A convergent conversation — several crew talking a topic through until they agree — is itself corroboration that was being thrown away. AD-958 closes the loop: a CONVERGENT conversation credits each contributing voice with a small positive trust observation, which then feeds back into the facilitator's ranking (AD-955) on the next turn. Backend only. Current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**; AD-958 is the **pre-reserved #882/#894 sub-number, NOT a new top-level** (AD-958a — the exploration term — already shipped under this number).

**Verified `record_outcome` signature (trust substrate, untouched).** `consensus/trust.py:217` — `def record_outcome(self, agent_id, success, weight=1.0, intent_type="", episode_id="", verifier_id="", source="verification") -> float`. SYNCHRONOUS (`def`, called with NO `await`). AD-958 does NOT edit `trust.py` at all: `record_outcome` / `get_score` / `TrustEvent` are consumed exactly as they are.

**Phantom-API guards (recorded so a future AD does not trip them).** (1) `get_score(agent_id)` is **GLOBAL** — there is no `intent_type` score-scoping overload; the per-topic signal lives in `TrustEvent.intent_type`, not in a scoped score. (2) The `source` param is **INERT** — it is never stored or consumed by `record_outcome`; we pass `source="conversation"` for forward intent, but the durable discriminators on the resulting `TrustEvent` are `verifier_id` + `intent_type`, never `source`.

**No self-sourcing (anti-gaming).** An agent can NEVER raise its own trust. In `extract_conversation_trust_outcomes` the distinct contributors are sorted and the verifier for contributor `i` is `distinct[(i+1) % n]`; with `n >= 2`, `(i+1) % n != i` for every `i`, so the verifier is always a DIFFERENT agent. Enforced in code AND asserted in the test (`verifier_id != agent_id AND verifier_id in participants`).

**Convergence-only v1 (positives only); correction deferred to AD-958c.** v1 reuses the facilitator's pure `is_converged` (does NOT re-derive convergence) and emits POSITIVES only. The peer-corrects-peer NEGATIVE path is intentionally NOT built here — `CorrectionDetector` is async-LLM and Captain-corrects-DAG-shaped, the wrong primitive for the synchronous multi-agent case. The heavier negative weight is config-encoded and asymmetry-validated but UNUSED in v1.

**Mayer/asymmetry grounding.** Per the trust literature (Mayer/Davis/Schoorman — trust is slow to build, fast to lose), `conversation_trust_negative_weight (0.15) >= conversation_trust_positive_weight (0.05)`, enforced by a `GroupChatConfig` `@model_validator`. A future correction always outweighs a corroboration.

**The 5-way bounded-runaway analysis (why this can't spiral).** (1) BOUNDED COUNT — at most `conversation_trust_max_outcomes` (4) positives per conversation. (2) SMALL WEIGHT — `positive_weight=0.05` (vs verification's 1.0), and `record_outcome`'s AD-558 progressive dampening/cold-start scaling further shrink it. (3) CONVERGENCE-GATED — nothing is recorded unless the conversation actually converged (`>= min_messages` from `>= min_agents` at mean Jaccard `>= threshold`). (4) NO SELF-SOURCING — an agent cannot bootstrap itself; credit always comes from a distinct peer. (5) CORE IMMUNITY — `record_outcome` already early-returns for `CORE_INFRASTRUCTURE` agents (tier registry), so infrastructure trust is never moved.

**Default-OFF byte-identical (proven with a REAL `TrustNetwork`).** Master flag `group_chat.conversation_trust_enabled` defaults False ⇒ `_record_conversation_trust` returns on its first line (no facilitator build, no extractor, no `record_outcome`) ⇒ the trust network is byte-identical to the pre-AD-958 fan-out. The proof test snapshots `get_score` per agent across a fully convergent fan-out with the flag OFF against a REAL `TrustNetwork()` (NOT MagicMock — BF-287) and asserts the scores and the event log are unchanged.

**The loop closes via the AD-955 global read.** After an ON convergent conversation raises a contributor's score, the next `_assemble_speaker_signals` reads `runtime.trust_network.get_score(aid)` into `SpeakerSignals.trust` — so the corroboration measurably shifts the facilitator's next ranking. Tested end-to-end.

**Honest-degrade.** Any extractor or `record_outcome` failure logs and continues; the `group_chat_fanout` return value (`all_replies`) is never touched.

**Decision.** Add a pure `cognitive/conversation_trust.py` (frozen `ConversationTrustOutcome`, `conversation_topic_tag`, `extract_conversation_trust_outcomes`) + 4 default-OFF `GroupChatConfig` fields with an asymmetry validator + a synchronous `_record_conversation_trust` helper called once before `group_chat_fanout` returns. No `trust.py`, no `config/system.yaml`, no Hebbian/REL_SOCIAL, no AD-853, no AD-955/956/963 change. Closes #894.

### AD-956 — scale-aware facilitation (epic #882, #892)

**Context.** The group-chat facilitator (AD-915) ranks the room every turn and (AD-955) surfaces an advisory room-awareness signal, but ENFORCEMENT is one-size-fits-all: every room uses the configured `max_speakers_per_turn` cap. A 2-3-voice room needs no cap (a hard truncation silences a relevant crew member who would naturally answer), while a large room needs the cap to keep the Captain from being flooded. AD-956 makes enforcement **scale-aware** — the deferred third of the Natural Conversation #892 thread (the AD-955 row recorded it deferred "until the threshold can be calibrated after watching, not guessed"). Backend only. Current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**; AD-956 is the **pre-reserved #892 sub-number, NOT a new top-level**.

**Span-of-control grounding.** The gate threshold is ratified at **5**: classic span-of-control research (and the naval watch-section convention the crew metaphor borrows) puts a comfortable direct-report fan-out at ~5. At or above that a single addressee (the Captain) cannot absorb a simultaneous answer from everyone, so the cap GATES; below it the room self-regulates and the cap is OFF.

**Decision.** A pure size-classifier picks ADVISORY vs GATING; ADVISORY turns the per-turn cap OFF (override 0) for that fan-out and nothing else; the master flag ships OFF so the default is byte-identical to AD-915/955.

**Design decisions.**
- **DD-1 (pure classifier).** NEW module-level `facilitation_mode(participant_count, *, threshold=5, force_min=0) -> Literal["advisory","gating"]` in `chat_facilitator.py` (beside `build_room_signal`, before `class ChatFacilitator`). Total, side-effect-free, no I/O: returns `"gating"` iff `count >= threshold` OR (`force_min > 0` and `count >= force_min`), else `"advisory"`. The docstring carries the span-of-control grounding and the ratified threshold 5.
- **DD-2 (config, default-OFF).** 3 NEW `GroupChatConfig` fields (after `broadcast_weight_trust`): `scale_aware_facilitation_enabled: bool = False` (master flag), `facilitation_gate_threshold: int = Field(default=5, ge=2)`, `force_facilitation_min: int = Field(default=0, ge=0)` (opt-in floor that gates even small rooms). **NO `config/system.yaml` edit** — zero-config boot keeps today's gating-cap behavior; `system.yaml` flips it on.
- **DD-3 (cap-substitution seam).** `ChatFacilitator.from_config` gains a keyword-only `max_speakers_override: int | None = None`; the cap read becomes `max_speakers_override if max_speakers_override is not None else getattr(gc, "max_speakers_per_turn", 0)`. `None` (default) = byte-identical; `0` = cap OFF (advisory widening). `facilitate()` is UNCHANGED — it already treats cap 0 as "all candidates" (only truncates when `_max_speakers > 0`), so the override rides the existing primitive. `_fan_one_round` threads the same kw to `from_config`. The only live caller is `thread_fanout.py` (back-compat add).
- **DD-4 (the compute seam).** `group_chat_fanout` computes `_speakers_override` once, AFTER `broadcast_weights` and BEFORE round 0, gated on `scale_aware_facilitation_enabled`: classify `facilitation_mode(len(agent_ids), …)`; advisory → `0`, gating → `None`. Threaded into BOTH `_fan_one_round` calls (round 0 + the AD-935 cascade) so every round of a small room widens consistently. Honest-degrade (Tier-2): any classify exception → `logger.warning` + `_speakers_override = None` (today's gating cap) — the fan-out is NEVER aborted.
- **DD-5 (THE BOUND — why this was deferred).** ADVISORY sets `max_speakers_override = 0` and NOTHING ELSE. It does NOT raise `max_agent_rounds`, does NOT bypass the AD-915 convergence gate, and adds NO recursive/self-refanning dispatch. The widened fan-out is bounded on TWO axes that AD-956 leaves untouched: the **participant count** is the per-round ceiling (advisory only fires for sub-threshold 2-4-voice rooms ⇒ ≤4 parallel/round), and `max_agent_rounds` is the round ceiling. Replies are still convergence-gated and `[NO_RESPONSE]`-thinned. Bounded widening ≤ participant count — removing either bound would be unbounded fan-out; AD-956 removes neither.
- **DD-6 (default-OFF byte-identical proof).** Flag OFF (default) ⇒ the classifier never runs, `_speakers_override` stays `None`, and every round uses `max_speakers_per_turn` EXACTLY as today. The e2e discriminator asserts a flag-OFF 3-agent room dispatches exactly the cap (1), identical to a config built with no scale fields AND to the per-round dispatch of a flag-ON GATING 5-agent room. No trust-loop (#894/AD-958), AD-951 directed-dispatch, or AD-963a/b terminator/weight-tilt change; no topic-aware threshold (the v2 forward marker); no UI/router/runtime-wiring change; no agent-facing prompt text (log/docstrings only, gap-audited).

**Gates.** NEW `tests/test_ad956_scale_aware_facilitation.py` — 7 pure classifier boundary tests (advisory 1/2/4, gating 5/8, custom threshold up/down, force_min floor, force_min=0 inert) + 6 e2e through `group_chat_fanout` (BF-287 real `GroupChatConfig`/`ChatThreadStore`/`IntentBus`, cap=1, reactivity OFF): flag-ON small room widens to 3, flag-ON large room stays 1, force_min gates + force_min=0 widens, flag-OFF byte-identical, `[NO_RESPONSE]` thins a widened round, classify-failure degrades to gating. **68 passed ×2** deterministic with `test_ad955`/`test_ad915`/`test_ad963a`/`test_ad963b` (the AD-955/915/963 suites unchanged = byte-identical-OFF proof); import smoke `SMOKE OK`; ast.parse clean. STAGED (not committed). **Closes #892.**

### AD-903 — clinical trend read surface + deny-by-default access gate (#866)

**Context.** The Counselor surfaces (`routers/counselor.py`, AD-503/561) were entirely UNGATED — any caller could read a crewman's cognitive profile, assessment history, and wellness summary. The clinical-confidential epic (#866/#867/#868) makes these reads CONFIDENTIAL. AD-903 ships the **shared access gate + a consolidated indicator trend surface**; AD-904 (#867) adds the dedicated clinical-notes store on top of this gate; AD-905 (#868) the UI. Current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**; AD-903 is a **pre-reserved sub-number, NOT a new top-level**.

**Naval grounding.** Minimum-necessary / need-to-know disclosure of a service member's behavioral-health information — DoDI 6490.08 (*Command Notification Requirements to Dispel Stigma*) limits disclosure to the minimum necessary and to those with a genuine need to know. The Counselor (the ship's behavioral-health authority) and the Captain hold standing need-to-know; any other crew member needs an explicit, time-limited, Captain-issued grant; and a crewman never reads their own clinical record.

**Decision.** A new pure gate `src/probos/cognitive/clinical_access.py` (mirrors `federation/ard/access.py:resolve_ard_access`) + a gated consolidated trend endpoint `GET /api/counselor/clinical/{agent_id}`, with all 7 existing counselor endpoints brought under the same gate.

**Design decisions.**
- **DD-1 (deny-by-default ladder, reusing AD-622 scope).** `resolve_clinical_access(*, caller_agent_id, caller_agent_type, target_agent_id, is_captain, active_grants)` returns a frozen `ClinicalAccessDecision(allowed, source, reason)` via a total first-match ladder: (1) `is_captain` → allow `captain`; (2) caller is the subject (non-captain) → DENY `subject_denied` (rung 2 precedes rung 3 so a counselor cannot read their OWN record); (3) caller type in a FRESH `CLINICAL_READ_ROLES=frozenset({"counselor"})` → allow `counselor_role`; (4) an active clinical grant covers the target → allow `grant`; (5) → DENY `default`. The need-to-know grant **reuses the existing AD-622 `ClearanceGrant.scope` field** (`clinical:{target}` or the wildcard `clinical:*`) — **NO ClearanceGrant extension**. AD-635's `clinical_telemetry.CLINICAL_ROLES` ({diagnostician, counselor}) is **untouched** (diagnostician = medical telemetry, not behavioral-health notes).
- **DD-2 (FAIL-CLOSED).** `clinical_access_for_caller(*, …, grant_store)` reads `resolve_active_grants` (AD-622 sync cache read) and wraps the whole resolution in try/except → deny `error` on ANY exception. `_has_clinical_grant` uses direct `.revoked`/`.scope` access on the real `ClearanceGrant`, so a malformed grant raises and is converted to a deny (the fail-closed guard is live, not dead — a dedicated test drives it). Defense-in-depth: the router gates AND the trend assembler re-resolves the gate before assembling (no double-audit; the single audit row is owned by the router gate).
- **DD-3 (intentional ungated→gated, byte-identical for the token-off HXI).** Every endpoint gains `Depends(require_crew_scope)` (pass-through while `auth.crew_scope_token==""`, the single-operator default) + an optional `as_agent_id`. Omitted `as_agent_id` ⇒ Captain authority ⇒ allowed, so the existing same-origin HXI is **byte-identical**. The gate only DENIES when a non-Captain `as_agent_id` is asserted (the intended tightening) — 403 `clinical_access_denied`. Per-target endpoints (`/profile/{id}`, `/assessments/{id}`, `/assess/{id}`) gate on the subject; crew-wide endpoints (`/profiles`, `/summary`, `/interventions`, `/sweep`) gate on `""` (only Captain / counselor-role / `clinical:*` wildcard clear that bar — a per-target grant cannot unlock crew-wide). Every allow AND deny is audited.
- **DD-4 (audit primitive).** A dedicated bounded `runtime.clinical_access_audit: deque(maxlen=1000)` (the in-memory-ring shape from `ClinicalTelemetryService._record_audit`) — NOT a reach into the private `_record_audit` on the default-OFF telemetry service, and NOT a DB dependency (a CONFIDENTIAL gate must never need I/O to record an access).
- **DD-5 (INDICATORS ONLY).** The trend assembler reads trust / cognitive-zone / self-similarity / hebbian-drift / duty stores EXCLUSIVELY (`trust_network.get_events_for_agent`+`raw_scores`; `proactive_loop.circuit_breaker.get_zone_history`; `self_similarity_history.recent`; Counselor `get_profile().drift_trend("hebbian_drift")`+assessments; `duty_schedule_tracker.get_status`+`success_rate`) — it NEVER touches any agent's episodic store. Each stream honest-degrades to []/null when its store is absent; no 503 (the trend endpoint degrades rather than 503s; the wrapped endpoints keep their existing 503 contract).
- **DD-6 (two history additions + duty surface).** `CognitiveCircuitBreaker.get_zone_history(agent_id, n=20)` exposes the full bounded `zone_history` ring (`get_status` caps it at 5); it guards `n<=0 → []` rather than the spec's `[-max(0,n):]` slice, which has the `[-0:]`-returns-everything footgun (caught by the unit test). NEW pure in-memory `cognitive/self_similarity_history.py` `SelfSimilarityHistory` (per-agent `deque` ring of `(ts, sim)`), constructed unconditionally in the runtime ctor and recorded from `proactive._build_self_monitoring_context` at the `result["self_similarity"]=` site (guarded, inside the existing try/except). `DutyStatus` gains `success_count`/`failure_count`; `DutyScheduleTracker` gains `record_outcome(agent_type, duty_id, success)` (outcome counters only — `execution_count`/`last_executed` stay owned by `record_execution`) + `success_rate(agent_type) → float | None` (None when no outcomes). **AD-903a deferral:** the 6 proactive duty capture-point wirings + duty-outcome persistence are NOT wired here.

**Gates.** `tests/test_ad903_clinical_access_gate.py` (pure ladder + real `ClearanceGrantStore(db_path="")`: captain-allows, subject-denied-own incl. counselor-for-own, counselor-role-allows-other, `clinical:{target}` + `clinical:*` grants, wrong-scope/revoked/expired/no-grant denies, fail-closed store-raises + malformed-grant `source=error`) + `tests/test_ad903_clinical_trends.py` (real `TestClient` + BF-287 real-attr `_Runtime` stub: Captain→200, counselor→200, non-counselor→403, subject-own→403, grantee chief→200 + other-target→403, crew-wide `/profiles` non-counselor→403, Captain→503 byte-identical, audit-row-on-every-allow-AND-deny, streams-from-indicator-stores, + `get_zone_history`/`SelfSimilarityHistory`/duty `success_rate` units). **33 passed ×2** deterministic; import smoke + ast.parse clean. Backend only — **no UI** (AD-905), **no AD-904 notes store**, **no `config/system.yaml` edit**. STAGED (not committed). **Closes #866.**

### AD-904 — confidential clinical notes store + gated read/write (#867)

**Context.** AD-903 (#866) shipped the shared deny-by-default clinical-access gate + an INDICATOR trend surface, but the Counselor still had nowhere to persist an actual clinical *note* about a crewman — the free-text `CounselorAssessment.notes` field (AD-503) is part of the indicator-assessment record, not a separately-gated CONFIDENTIAL document. AD-904 adds the dedicated **clinical-notes store + gated read/write endpoints**, built ON TOP of the AD-903 gate. Current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052**; AD-904 is a **pre-reserved sub-number, NOT a new top-level**.

**Naval grounding.** DoDI 6490.08 — the *provider* (the Counselor, the ship's behavioral-health authority) curates the behavioral-health record; the *subject* does not control or self-read it. Read/write is deny-by-default and resolved by the AD-903 gate (Counselor + Captain standing need-to-know; any other crew member needs an explicit, time-limited, Captain-issued `clinical:{target}` grant); the subject never reads their own record.

**Decision.** A NEW `src/probos/cognitive/clinical_notes_store.py` (`ClinicalNote` frozen dataclass + `ClinicalNotesStore`, mirroring `clearance_grants.py`) persisting notes SEPARATE from `CounselorAssessment.notes`, stamped `DisclosureLevel.CONFIDENTIAL` (=3); three gated endpoints on `routers/counselor.py` (`POST /api/counselor/notes/{agent_id}`, `GET …/notes/{agent_id}`, `GET …/notes/{agent_id}/{note_id}`); and always-on startup wiring mirroring `clearance_grant_store`.

**Design decisions.**
- **DD-1 (cloud-ready storage — mirrors AD-622 `clearance_grants.py`).** `ClinicalNotesStore(db_path="", connection_factory=None)` uses the `ConnectionFactory` protocol (default `storage.sqlite_factory.default_factory`), an idempotent `_SCHEMA` (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clinical_notes(...)` + `idx_notes_target`), async `start()`/`stop()`, and WAL/busy_timeout/synchronous pragmas — **NOT a raw `aiosqlite.connect()`** (the `.github/copilot-instructions.md` cloud-ready rule, so the commercial overlay can swap SQLite→Postgres). `write_note(*, target_agent_id, author_agent_id, body, disclosure_level=DisclosureLevel.CONFIDENTIAL)`, `list_notes(target_agent_id, *, limit=50)` (newest-first, `ORDER BY created_at DESC, rowid DESC` so the order is deterministic even when two notes share a coarse-timer timestamp), `get_note(note_id)`. `db_path=""` honest-degrades every read to []/None. No new consensus gate (mirrors the AD-894/AD-900 governed-write posture).
- **DD-2 (REUSE the AD-903 gate; subject never reads own).** The endpoints resolve access through the AD-903 ladder via `clinical_access_for_caller` + `_resolve_caller` (the gate MODULE + helper are reused, untouched). Subject-confidentiality is enforced by the AD-903 ladder's rung 2 (`subject_denied` precedes `counselor_role`), so a crewman — even a counselor reading their OWN record — is denied 403, while that same counselor may read another crewman's notes. `get_note` additionally 404s when the fetched note's `target_agent_id` differs from the path agent (a caller gated for `agent_id` cannot read another crewman's note by id).
- **DD-3 (DENY-BY-DEFAULT + FAIL-CLOSED, defense-in-depth).** Two independent gate resolutions per access: the router-layer `_gate_notes_access` AND a store-layer `_recheck_clinical_access` immediately before touching the store (mirrors the re-check inside `_assemble_clinical_trends`; no second audit row). Any store error on a CONFIDENTIAL notes path fails closed (503 `clinical_notes_unavailable`) and NEVER echoes a note body. Unlike AD-903's fail-SAFE `_gate_clinical_access`, notes use a STRICT `_gate_notes_access` + `_audit_notes_access_strict`: a CONFIDENTIAL *note* access that cannot be recorded (audit ring absent or `append` raising) is DENIED (503), not silently allowed — note bodies demand a stricter audit posture than the AD-903 indicator numbers. AD-903's `_gate_clinical_access`/`_audit_clinical_access` are untouched (AD-903 tests stay green).
- **DD-4 (audit reuses the AD-903 deque).** Every notes read AND write (allow + deny) appends exactly one row to the SAME `runtime.clinical_access_audit: deque(maxlen=1000)` AD-903 established (the `ClinicalTelemetryService._record_audit` entry shape), with `query_type ∈ {notes_read, notes_write}`. NOT the SQLite `ClinicalAuditStore`.
- **DD-5 (always-on startup wiring — mirrors `clearance_grant_store`).** `runtime.py` ctor decl `self.clinical_notes_store: ClinicalNotesStore | None = None` + `comm` assign; `communication.py` constructs `ClinicalNotesStore(db_path=str(data_dir / "clinical_notes.db"))` + `await .start()` adjacent to the grant store + adds the `CommunicationResult` kwarg; `results.py` adds the `CommunicationResult` field; `shutdown.py` stops it. Additive/always-on — **no `config/system.yaml` edit, no config flag**.

**Gates.** `tests/test_ad904_clinical_notes.py` (BF-287 — real `ClinicalNotesStore` on `tmp_path` for the store-level round-trip / `disclosure_level==3` / idempotent-double-`start()` / cross-store persistence, real `TestClient` + real-attr `_Runtime` stub + real `ClearanceGrantStore(db_path="")` + real `deque` for the gating layer; fault injection via REAL `ClinicalNotesStore` subclasses, NO MagicMock): write→list→get round-trip, subject-cannot-read-own (incl. counselor-for-own) + counselor-reads-other, non-counselor→403, counselor/grantee-chief(per-target only)/Captain→200, get-single target-mismatch→404, audit-row-on-every-read-AND-write (allow+deny, `query_type ∈ {notes_read, notes_write}`), store-None→503, fail-closed (store-error AND audit-append-error → no body leak; audit-ring-absent→deny). **17 passed ×2** deterministic (+ AD-903 `33 passed` unchanged ⇒ **50 passed ×2** focused); import smoke + ast.parse clean. Backend only — **no UI** (AD-905), **no `config/system.yaml` edit**. STAGED (not committed). **Closes #867.**

### AD-963b — broadcast department-dominant weight tilt (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

**Context.** AD-963a (the ratified AD-963 recommendation, part a) shipped the broadcast *terminator* (round-robin every crew member once) + the pure `classify_broadcast` cue detector, and AD-951 the directed dispatch — 2/3 of #897. The third piece, the **department-dominant weight tilt** (the domain expert should FRAME a broadcast first), was explicitly **deferred for a live look**. The live look having happened, AD-963b builds it. Resolves the AD-963a deferral and **Closes #897**.

**Decision (mode-aware weights, master-flag gated).** A new master flag `GroupChatConfig.turn_mode_policy_enabled` (Pydantic default **False**; `system.yaml` flips it) turns the 3-mode turn-order policy on. Three parts, all dark until the flag flips:

- **`classify_turn_mode(text, *, directed_callsign) -> Literal["directed","broadcast","discussion"]`** — a pure, total v1 HEURISTIC and the explicit **v2 LLM swap seam**: DIRECTED wins (a leading callsign to a present participant — AD-951 owns the dispatch); else BROADCAST (the shipped `classify_broadcast` cue detector); else the default DISCUSSION. No new LLM call.
- **Department-dominant broadcast profile** — 4 new `GroupChatConfig.broadcast_weight_*` fields (mention 0.20 / recency 0.15 / **department 0.50** / trust 0.10; need not sum to 1). `ChatFacilitator.from_config(config, *, broadcast=False)` gains a keyword-only `broadcast` flag (the only caller is `thread_fanout.py`, so it is backward-compatible); the tilt applies ONLY when `broadcast` AND `turn_mode_policy_enabled` are both on, so a broadcast turn re-weights the facilitator so the domain expert outranks a fresh-but-irrelevant peer and frames the topic first.
- **Wiring** — `group_chat_fanout` HOISTS the cfg + `turn_mode` computation ABOVE round 0 (the round that decides who frames first), reusing the AD-967 roster for the participant-callsign set; `broadcast_weights = policy_on and turn_mode == "broadcast"` flows to round 0 and every AD-935 cascade round via a new `_fan_one_round(..., broadcast=False)` param. The AD-963a terminator's `broadcast_mode` now keys off the hoisted `turn_mode` when the policy is on, else the shipped `classify_broadcast` (byte-identical).

**Default-OFF / byte-identical.** With `turn_mode_policy_enabled=False` (default): `turn_mode` stays None, `broadcast_weights` stays False, `from_config(broadcast=…)` returns the standard facilitator (weights 0.40/0.25/0.25/0.10), and the terminator keys off `classify_broadcast` exactly as AD-963a — identical ranking, dispatch, and stop. No `config/system.yaml` change (ships dark via the Pydantic default). Honest-degrade: the classifier is pure + total, so a classification can never abort the fan-out. Did NOT touch the AD-963a terminator round-robin, the trust network (AD-958), AD-951 directed dispatch, or AD-956 scale-aware enforcement; no LLM classifier (v2 seam only); no UI.

**Gates.** `test_ad963b_broadcast_weight_tilt.py` (9: `classify_turn_mode` directed-precedence/broadcast/discussion; `from_config` broadcast-policy-ON → department 0.50 / mention 0.20; broadcast-policy-OFF → standard 0.25 / 0.40 byte-identical; end-to-end broadcast+policy-ON → domain expert frames first + all crew once; the byte-identical discriminator — same room/turn, policy OFF reproduces AD-963a ordering, policy ON reorders by department; directed+broadcast-cue policy-ON → directed wins, no round-robin; discussion+policy-ON byte-identical). Focused `test_ad963b_* + test_ad963a_* + test_ad915_* + test_ad951_*` **52 passed ×2** (the unchanged AD-963a/915/951 suites are the byte-identical-OFF proof); import smoke + ast.parse clean. Pre-existing sub-number under #897/AD-963 — current highest landed top-level = AD-1052, **NO new top-level**. STAGED (not committed).

### AD-1040 — ARD envelope data model + media-type taxonomy + config scaffold (epic #989)

**Context.** Current highest assigned top-level = **AD-1052**; **AD-1040 is the Captain's pre-reserved ARD-block number** (AD-1040→AD-1051 were reserved below the 1052 ceiling for the ARD Integration epic — a deliberate gap, see the AD-1052 Context note) — so AD-1040 is **NOT a new top-level number**, it is the first landing of that reserved block (#989 Foundation 1/12, issue #990). AD-1040 ships the **types + config scaffold ONLY** for Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD): the catalog envelope data model, the public media-type taxonomy, the `urn:air:` helper, and a default-OFF `FederationArdConfig`. Nothing in the runtime imports the new package — there is **no projector (AD-1041), no `/.well-known` route (AD-1042), no representative-queries (AD-1043), no `/search` (AD-1044), no client (AD-1046)** in this AD.

**Decision.** A new pure-stdlib package `src/probos/federation/ard/` (`catalog.py`, `urn.py`, `media_types.py`, `__init__.py`) + a `FederationArdConfig` nested on `FederationConfig`. The envelope mirrors the public ARD ecosystem so a ProbOS catalog is consumable by generic ARD clients.

**Design decisions (DD-1..DD-8).**
- **DD-1 (default-OFF / byte-identical).** AD-1040 ships TYPES + CONFIG ONLY. `FederationArdConfig.enabled=False`; nothing in `runtime.py` or any router imports the package. The runtime is byte-identical to HEAD.
- **DD-2 (envelope mirrors public patterns).** `CatalogEntry` / `AiCatalog` / `HostInfo` / `TrustManifest` / `Attestation` / `ProvenanceLink` mirror the public A2A agent-card / ai-plugin / JSON-LD / ai-catalog conventions so the envelope is consumable by generic ARD clients (no ProbOS-private shape).
- **DD-3 (media-type taxonomy + URN scheme).** `media_types.py` defines the six `MT_*` constants and `PROBOS_AXIS_TO_MEDIA_TYPE`, mapping ProbOS's capability axes (`built_in`/`extension`→probos-tool, `mcp`→mcp-server-card, `skill`→ai-skill, `mesh_intent`/`agent`→a2a-agent-card, `pack`→ai-catalog) onto the public taxonomy; `urn.py` defines the `urn:air:<publisher>:<namespace>:<name>` scheme.
- **DD-4 (value-or-reference, spec §3.4).** `CatalogEntry.__post_init__` raises `ValueError` when BOTH or NEITHER of `url`|`data` are set — exactly one (a reference or an inline payload) is required.
- **DD-5 (camelCase boundary).** Internal fields are snake_case; `to_dict()` is the ONLY place camelCase appears (`displayName`, `representativeQueries`, `trustManifest`, `updatedAt`, `sourceId`, `documentationUrl`, …) and empty optionals are omitted from the serialized envelope.
- **DD-6 (URN honest-degrade).** `parse_urn` / `publisher_domain` return `None` / `""` on any malformed input and NEVER raise — discovery callers skip a bad URN without a per-site try/except.
- **DD-7 (secrets-never-in-catalog).** `TrustManifest` is a pure DATA CARRIER (identity, attestations, provenance, opaque signature string) — it has NO `sign`/`verify` logic and never holds a private key.
- **DD-8 (layer discipline = byte-identical proof).** `catalog.py` / `urn.py` / `media_types.py` import NOTHING from `probos` (verified: zero `import probos`/`from probos` statements); `__init__.py` only re-exports from the sibling modules. That non-import is the byte-identical proof that AD-1040 is types-only.

**Default-OFF.** `SystemConfig().federation.ard.enabled is False` (well_known_path `/.well-known/ai-catalog.json`, empty `discovery_endpoints`, empty `registry_url`/`publisher_namespace_domain`). `config/system.yaml` untouched (default-OFF ships in `config.py`); no `ui/` change.

**Files.** NEW `src/probos/federation/ard/__init__.py`, `…/catalog.py`, `…/urn.py`, `…/media_types.py`; EDIT `src/probos/config.py` (+`FederationArdConfig`, nest `ard`); NEW `tests/test_ad1040_ard_envelope.py`.

**Tests.** `tests/test_ad1040_ard_envelope.py` (**16**, BF-287 real dataclasses + real `SystemConfig`, NO MagicMock): value-or-reference (both/neither → `ValueError`; url-only / data-only ok); `to_dict` camelCase keys present + empty optionals omitted; full `AiCatalog`(host + tool/skill/agent) round-trip; URN build→parse round-trip incl a colon-bearing name; `publisher_domain` FQDN + malformed→`""`; `parse_urn` malformed→`None`; media-type axis mapping; config default-OFF; `TrustManifest` pure carrier (no `sign`/`verify`). **Gates:** focused `pytest tests/test_ad1040_ard_envelope.py -q -n 0` **16 passed**; import smoke prints **SMOKE OK**; `ast.parse` clean on all six files; DD-8 grep confirms zero `probos` imports in the three pure modules. STAGED (not committed). Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

### AD-1041 — ARD catalog projector: project the live capability surface into an `AiCatalog` (epic #989)

**Context.** Current highest assigned top-level = **AD-1052**; **AD-1041 is within the pre-reserved ARD block (AD-1040→AD-1051)** — NOT a new top-level (#989 Foundation 2/12, issue #991). Builds on AD-1040 (envelope types); projects the live ship capability surface into the AD-1040 `AiCatalog` so AD-1042 can serve it.

**Decision.** New `src/probos/federation/ard/catalog_projector.py` — `async def project_catalog(runtime, *, repr_queries=None) -> AiCatalog`. REUSES the AD-1001 `list_capability_catalog` assembly (tools / skills / mesh-intents) + the AD-1015 `mcp_server_store.list_sync()` + the AD-1003c `list_packs` inventory; attaches AD-1043 representative queries per entry. **Lazy in-function `probos` imports** (`routers.tools`, `routers.packs`) so importing `probos.federation.ard` stays cycle-free. **AD-1040 purity invariant preserved:** the three pure modules (`catalog`/`urn`/`media_types`) are UNMODIFIED and remain `probos`-import-free; `__init__.py` gains the projector + miner re-exports (becoming `probos`-importing — correct for Batch 2, since the probos imports are lazy/in-function so `__init__` load stays cycle-free).

**Design decisions.**
- **DD-1 (value-or-reference).** EVERY `CatalogEntry` sets exactly one of `url`|`data` — an http-MCP server with a URL → `url` (reference); the ship-local axes (tools/skills/intents/packs) + stdio-MCP → `data` (inline). Per-entry `try/except` → a malformed source row is SKIPPED, never raised (honest-degrade); the projector always returns a well-formed catalog (host-only in the worst case).
- **DD-3 (media type + URN per axis).** `PROBOS_AXIS_TO_MEDIA_TYPE.get(origin, MT_PROBOS_TOOL)` for tools (built_in/extension→probos-tool, mcp→mcp-server-card), `MT_AI_SKILL` skills, `MT_A2A_AGENT` mesh-intents, `MT_MCP_SERVER` MCP servers, `MT_AI_CATALOG` packs. The URN name segment uses the HUMAN handle (tool_id / skill name / intent name / MCP name / pack name) consistently across all axes — `urn:air:<publisher>:<tools|skills|intents|mcp|packs>:<name>`.
- **DD-7 (secrets-never-projected).** The MCP projection reads ONLY `id`/`name`/`type`/`url` from each `McpServerRecord` — it NEVER touches `auth_kind`/`credential_ref`/`auth_header_name`/`auth_scheme`/`auth_env_var`/`oauth_json`/`headers`/`env`/`command`/`args`/`cwd` (it deliberately does NOT call `to_public_dict()`, which would emit the non-secret auth metadata). No credential ref or value can reach the catalog.
- **Publisher domain.** `federation.ard.publisher_namespace_domain` → sanitized ship-cert `vessel_name` → `ship_did` → `"probos.local"` (each lookup honest-degrades). `HostInfo` carries the vessel name + ship DID.

**Files.** NEW `src/probos/federation/ard/catalog_projector.py`; EDIT `src/probos/federation/ard/__init__.py` (re-export `project_catalog`); NEW `tests/test_ad1041_catalog_projector.py`.

**Tests.** `tests/test_ad1041_catalog_projector.py` (**7**, BF-287 real fixtures — real `SystemConfig`, real `McpServerStore(db_path="")`, explicit `_Fake*` stubs NOT MagicMock for the tool/skill/mesh read sites): media type per axis (tool→probos-tool, skill→ai-skill, mesh→a2a-agent, http+stdio MCP→mcp-server-card); URNs `urn:air:uss-test:…` from the vessel name; skill `capabilities` = its intents + mesh `requiresConsensus`/`tier`; value-or-reference holds for every serialized entry; http-MCP→`url` reference / stdio-MCP→`data` inline (`serverType`); honest-degrade host-only when accessors absent; host reflects vessel name. STAGED (not committed). Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

### AD-1044 — ARD `POST /ard/search` discovery-service query + DD-4 projection cache (epic #989)

**Context.** Current highest assigned top-level = **AD-1052**; **AD-1044 is within the pre-reserved ARD block (AD-1040→AD-1051)** — NOT a new top-level (#989 Discovery 5/12, issue #994). Makes the ship a conformant ARD discovery SERVICE: a generic ARD client can query the AD-1041 projection by keyword + filter.

**Decision.** EXTEND the existing `routers/ard.py` router (NO new router, NO `api.py` change) with `POST /ard/search` — body `{query:{text, filter:{type, tags}}, pageSize, pageToken}` → ranked `ai-registry+json` (registry conformance mode). The ranking ENGINE is a NEW PURE module `src/probos/federation/ard/registry_query.py` (`search_entries` / `facet_entries`) — **stdlib + `.catalog` ONLY** (AD-1040 purity preserved: zero `probos` imports), modelled on `CodebaseIndex.query` (per-token additive field weighting), NOT a new ML index.

**Route namespace.** `/ard/search` (NOT bare `/search` — verified collision: `/search` is owned by `records.py`/`threads.py`/`work.py`).

**Design decisions.**
- **R-3 PUBLIC + BOUNDED (security).** Reuses the AD-1042 posture: UNAUTHENTICATED (NOT behind `require_crew_scope` — that dep is pass-through while the crew-scope token is empty, the default single-op config → no real bound). Bounded instead by **(a)** a HARD `pageSize` clamp to `_MAX_PAGE_SIZE=50` (honest-degrade — a too-large value is clamped, NEVER a 422); **(b)** the DD-4 short-TTL cached projection so repeated queries don't re-walk inventory; **(c)** `episodic_k=0` mining (zero I/O).
- **DD-4 projection cache (also rewires AD-1042).** NEW `get_cached_catalog(runtime, *, ttl=_CATALOG_CACHE_TTL=10.0)` + `reset_catalog_cache()` in `catalog_projector.py` (the `probos`-importing module, NOT the three pure ones): a single-slot module cache keyed on `id(runtime)` with a `time.monotonic` expiry; `ttl<=0` re-projects and does NOT store (a test lever); mines `episodic_k=0` then `project_catalog`. `serve_ai_catalog` (AD-1042) is REWIRED to call it — behavior-preserving (content identical, just cached). Because the cache is shared module state, every ARD test file gets an autouse `reset_catalog_cache()` fixture (test_ad1041/1042 retrofitted) for isolation against `id(runtime)` reuse.
- **Ranking (relevance only — never trust).** `search_entries(entries, text, *, type, tags)`: filter FIRST (`type` = exact media-type; `tags` = entry must contain EVERY requested tag, AND); then per-entry per-token additive score over `display_name`×5 / `capabilities`×4 / `tags`×3 / `description`×2 / `representative_queries`×1 (lowercased substring); drop score-0; sort `(-score, identifier)` (stable). Empty text → the filtered set (honest-degrade browse).
- **Response + secrets.** `{specVersion:"1.0", conformance:"registry", results:[CatalogEntry.to_dict()…], total, nextPageToken}` (value-or-reference + camelCase preserved); offset pagination via an opaque int `pageToken` (honest-degrade to 0). **DD-6/DD-7 secrets-never:** the SAME projected entries flow through search → no credential value/field-name can leak (asserted).

### AD-1046 — ARD discovery client core (consume side) + pure catalog parser (epic #989)

**Context.** Current highest assigned top-level = **AD-1052**; **AD-1046 is within the pre-reserved ARD block (AD-1040→AD-1051)** — NOT a new top-level (#989 Client 7/12, issue #996). Adds the **consume** side of ARD: fetch + parse remote `ai-catalog+json` envelopes. DD-5 consume-ONLY — no adopt/connect/invoke (AD-1049), no federation modes (AD-1050), no publication (AD-1051).

**Decision.** Two NEW modules. (1) `federation/ard/catalog_parse.py` — the **PURE** inverse of `catalog.to_dict()` kept OUT of `catalog.py` (AD-1040 byte-identical invariant): `catalog_from_dict(d) -> AiCatalog` / `entry_from_dict(d) -> CatalogEntry|None`, imports stdlib + `.catalog` ONLY. DD-6 honest-degrade — every parser NEVER raises; a malformed entry (incl. the DD-4 both-or-neither `url|data` `__post_init__` raise) degrades to `None` and is DROPPED; a malformed catalog degrades to an empty envelope. `data` + `trustManifest.signature` are kept as OPAQUE carriers (never dereferenced, never mined for secrets). (2) `federation/ard/client.py` — `ArdClient` + `@dataclass DiscoveredCatalog(source_endpoint, catalog=None, error="")`.
- **DD-1 SSRF guard** (the guard the mesh `http_fetch` agent deliberately lacks): bounded direct `httpx` with `follow_redirects=False` passed on EVERY request (so an injected client cannot weaken it), `_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=10.0`, and a truncate-then-parse size cap `_MAX_CATALOG_BYTES=2_000_000` (`resp.content[:cap]` BEFORE `json.loads`). Fetches ONLY the endpoints the caller passes — the operator-configured `federation.ard.discovery_endpoints` allowlist — and NEVER dereferences a catalog entry's `url` field. `_well_known_url` maps a base endpoint → `…/.well-known/ai-catalog.json` (pass-through if already `.json`/`.well-known`). `discover(endpoints)` returns one `DiscoveredCatalog` per endpoint with per-endpoint try/except isolation (one bad endpoint never breaks others); `search_registry(endpoint, *, text, page_size)` POSTs `{query:{text}, pageSize}` → `{results:[…]}` → `catalog_from_dict({entries:results})`.
- **Injectable seam** (BF-287): `ArdClient(*, http=None, timeout=…)` — a self-created client is built+closed inside `async with`; an injected client (e.g. wrapping `httpx.MockTransport`) is NEVER closed (caller owns its lifecycle).
- **Operator endpoint** `GET /ard/discovered` (`routers/ard.py`, `dependencies=[Depends(require_crew_scope)]` — OPERATOR-facing because it triggers OUTBOUND fetches; gate→404 `feature_disabled`): fetches `discovery_endpoints` via `ArdClient().discover` → `{specVersion, conformance:"registry", discovered:[{source, error, catalog}]}` (`MT_AI_REGISTRY`), outer try/except → `discovered:[]`.

### AD-1047 — ARD entry trust verification (verify-only; "score ≠ trust") (epic #989)

**Context.** Current highest assigned top-level = **AD-1052**; **AD-1047 is within the pre-reserved ARD block (AD-1040→AD-1051)** — NOT a new top-level (#989 Client 8/12, issue #997). Verifies a discovered entry's published provenance and seeds a probationary trust prior — WITHOUT treating verification as an observed execution.

**Decision.** NEW `federation/ard/trust_verifier.py` — `verify_entry(entry, *, endpoint_host, base_alpha=1.0, base_beta=3.0) -> VerificationReport` + `seed_trust_prior(trust_network, entity_id, report) -> float`. DI: the trust network is a PARAM (no direct `consensus` import).
- **DD-2 verify-only** ("score ≠ trust"): `verify_entry` checks `domain_match` (URN `publisher_domain` == serving `endpoint_host`, case/port-insensitive), `has_attestations` (manifest ≥1 attestation), `signature_present` (manifest signature string). `alpha` accrues evidence above `base_alpha` (`_W_DOMAIN=1.0` / `_W_ATTEST=0.5` / `_W_SIGNATURE=1.0`); `beta=base_beta` (probationary Beta(1,3)=0.25). `report.score = checks_passed/3` is a verification CONFIDENCE — a DIFFERENT number from the trust value `trust_network.get_score(id) = alpha/(alpha+beta)`. `seed_trust_prior` calls `trust_network.create_with_prior(id, alpha, beta)` (consensus/trust.py:204 — a NO-OP if the id already exists, so re-verifying NEVER resets an entity's evolved trust) and returns `get_score`; it does NOT call `record_outcome` (verification is not an observed execution).
- **JWS honest-degrade (v1):** there is NO JWS/JOSE verifier-key infrastructure in `src/probos` (confirmed) → `signature_verified` is ALWAYS `False` with an explanatory note; a present-but-unverified signature does NOT raise trust. No signature ISSUANCE (commercial).

**Files.** NEW `src/probos/federation/ard/trust_verifier.py`; EDIT `src/probos/federation/ard/__init__.py` (re-export `verify_entry`/`seed_trust_prior`/`VerificationReport`). NEW `tests/test_ad1047_ard_trust_verify.py`. NO `config/system.yaml`.

**Tests.** `tests/test_ad1047_ard_trust_verify.py` (**12**, real `TrustNetwork` no-DB): domain-match raises α (and case/port-insensitive), domain-mismatch notes + no α bump, no-publisher notes, attestations raise α by 0.5, signature present-but-`signature_verified=False` v1 (+note, no α bump), `score=2/3` fraction, no-manifest `score=1/3`; `seed_trust_prior` creates-with-prior + returns `α/(α+β)`, **`report.score != trust`** (score≠trust), idempotent no-op if exists, **re-verify does NOT reset evolved trust** (record_outcome bumps it, re-seed leaves it). STAGED (not committed). Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
