### AD-1049 — governed discovery-before-design + explicit gated adopt/connect (epic #989)

**Context.** Current highest assigned top-level = **AD-1052**; **AD-1049 is within the pre-reserved ARD block (AD-1040→AD-1051)** — NOT a new top-level (#989 Consume 10/12, issue #999). Adds the consume-side ACTIONS AD-1046 deliberately stopped short of — but every action is GOVERNED and default-OFF.

**Decision.** NEW `federation/ard/adoption.py` (imports ONLY sibling pure ARD modules + stdlib). Two surfaces.
- **`surface_discovery_candidates(runtime, intent_meta) -> list[dict]`** — the discovery-before-design hook. BEFORE the self-mod pipeline designs a new agent for a capability gap, it SURFACES already-published resources (the ship's own `get_cached_catalog` projection + the operator-configured discovery endpoints via `ArdClient().discover`) that may already satisfy the gapped intent, so a human can connect an existing resource instead of growing the population. Verifies each external hit with the PURE `verify_entry` (NO trust seed — there is no agent identity at DESIGN time), emits an advisory `runtime.emit_event("ard_discovery_candidates", …)` (a STRING event — NO new `EventType`), caps at `_MAX_SURFACE_CANDIDATES=5`. It NEVER permission-checks and NEVER adopts. Whole-body **Tier-2 honest-degrade** → `[]` so the design path proceeds unchanged.
- **`connect_candidate(runtime, *, agent_id, catalog, resource, entry, endpoint_host, min_trust=0.4, headers=None) -> ConnectResult`** — the EXPLICIT gated adopt. **DD-1 strict ordering permission → trust → connect:** (1) `ard_access_for_agent` FIRST → `permission_denied` if not enabled, BEFORE any trust seed — a denied connect must NEVER have a side effect (a test asserts `trust_network.get_record(id) is None` after a denied connect); (2) `verify_entry` + `seed_trust_prior` (seed the probationary Beta prior ONCE) → `trust_below_threshold` if score < `_DEFAULT_ADOPT_MIN_TRUST=0.4` (domain-match seeds Beta(2,3)=0.40, allowed; no-domain seeds Beta(1,3)=0.25, blocked); (3) connect — v1 = MCP-http only: `MT_MCP_SERVER`+`url` → `runtime.mcp_bridge.register_server(url, headers)` (`mcp_registered` / `mcp_register_failed` on dup/empty / `mcp_bridge_unavailable` when the bridge is off); any other type honest-degrades to `connect_not_supported_v1` (no A2A/skill invocation in v1, no signature issuance).
- **Runtime hook (byte-identical-when-off, CRITICAL).** A call-site `if` guard in `runtime.process_natural_language` (after the existing `if intent_meta:`, before the `# Build execution context` comment): `_ard_cfg = getattr(getattr(self.config, "federation", None), "ard", None); if _ard_cfg is not None and getattr(_ard_cfg, "discovery_before_design", False): … surface_discovery_candidates(self, intent_meta)`. When the default-`False` flag is off the guard short-circuits BEFORE the lazy import + any work → textually/behaviorally byte-identical. The existing `handle_unhandled_intent` call is unchanged and still runs AFTER.

**Files.** NEW `src/probos/federation/ard/adoption.py`; EDIT `src/probos/config.py` (+`discovery_before_design: bool = False`), `src/probos/federation/ard/__init__.py` (re-export `surface_discovery_candidates`/`connect_candidate`/`AdoptionCandidate`/`ConnectResult`), `src/probos/routers/ard.py` (+`POST /ard/adopt` — `ArdAdoptBody{agent_id,catalog,resource,endpoint_host,entry:dict}`; `entry_from_dict`→422 `invalid_entry`; `connect_candidate`→`asdict`), `src/probos/runtime.py` (the guarded hook). NEW `tests/test_ad1049_ard_adoption.py`. NO `config/system.yaml`.

**Tests.** `tests/test_ad1049_ard_adoption.py` (**12**, BF-287 real `ToolPermissionStore`/`TrustNetwork`/fake bridge; surface seams substituted with real async stubs returning real `AiCatalog`/`DiscoveredCatalog`, NOT MagicMock): surface own-catalog match, external verify (score+domain_match), advisory emit, own-axis-failure honest-degrade→[], 5-cap; runtime-hook guard off-by-default (mirrors the call-site predicate, default `False`, enabled `True`); connect permission_denied-NEVER-seeds-trust (`get_record is None`), trust_below_threshold (0.25, no bridge call), mcp_registered (0.40, `register_server` called), mcp_register_failed, mcp_bridge_unavailable, connect_not_supported_v1 (A2A passes trust but unsupported). ### AD-1052 — Browser/Web-App Workstation (v1: embedded-iframe + unifying mode model) (epic #965)

**Context.** Current highest LANDED top-level AD: **AD-1038** (#987); **AD-1039 is RESERVED** (AD-1038 DD-7, the deferred "know"-down-weighting in consensus) and **AD-1040→AD-1051 are RESERVED** for the ARD Integration epic drafts (`prompts/ard-epic-decisions-draft.md`, none landed) — so the next free top-level is **AD-1052** (verified: no `### AD-1052` heading exists at HEAD `b39ff727`). AD-1052 is the **third and last** workstation type of epic #965 (HXI Workspaces), alongside the AD-1021 `monaco` editor and the AD-1024 `mcp-app` gallery. The backend `browser` type is **already registered** — `startup/finalize._wire_workstation_types` (finalize.py:217) baselines `(("monaco","Code Editor","monaco"),("browser","Browser","browser"),("chat","Chat","chat"))` as native types gated on `WorkstationsConfig.enabled` (default-OFF) — so, exactly as in AD-1021's situation, the AD's only job is to supply the `browser` React component + register it in `nativeWorkstations.ts`. **Pure-UI, default-OFF, ZERO backend (no `src/probos/**`, no `config/system.yaml`, no new npm dep).**

**Research synthesis — one type, one contract, three modes.** The Captain's requirement is one browser workstation flexible enough for headless (agent drives, human watches), bridge/external (control a real separate Chrome), and embedded/shared (a browser surface inside the HXI). The absorbed mature-tool patterns: Playwright `chromium.launch({headless})` + a screenshot→action loop, with live view via CDP `Page.startScreencast` (headless/watch); Playwright `connectOverCDP('http://localhost:9222')` attaching to a user-launched Chrome started with `--remote-debugging-port` (bridge); a VS Code webview = "an `<iframe>` the extension controls" — but arbitrary cross-origin sites that send `X-Frame-Options`/`frame-ancestors` CSP **cannot** be iframed (embedded, with that honest limit); and the Anthropic Computer-Use navigate·click·type·scroll·screenshot vocabulary (= the **AD-706** engine vocabulary already shipped). **Synthesis:** a single `browser` type with `mode ∈ {embedded, watch, bridge}` over ONE observation/action contract — the AD-706 vocabulary (observation: screenshot + indexed state + url + title; action: navigate/click/type/scroll/key/back/forward). The three modes are different transports over the same contract: *embedded* = a native sandboxed iframe (the live page IS the observation; the human drives it natively, no forwarding); *watch* = an MJPEG observation of an AD-706 headless session; *bridge* = the same vocabulary aimed at an attached external Chrome. **v1 ships the `embedded` surface + the mode model that names `watch`/`bridge` as visible-but-disabled follow-ons; the AD-706 engine is REUSED (never rebuilt) by the later slices that drive it.**

**Decision.** Additive across eight UI files (mirrors AD-1021 exactly). **(1)** NEW `components/workstation/BrowserWorkstation.tsx` — a self-contained native component (`{ typeId }: NativeWorkstationProps`; ignores `doc`, mirroring the AD-1024 mcp-app adapter): a toolbar with a 3-segment **mode selector** (Embedded active; Watch/Bridge `disabled` with `title="Available in AD-1052a"`/`"…1052b"`), a URL textbox (`browser-url-input`) + Go button (`browser-go`); the body renders a sandboxed `<iframe data-testid="browser-frame" sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-popups" referrerPolicy="no-referrer">` ONLY after a URL is committed, else a static honest-degrade empty-state (`browser-empty`) noting some sites refuse to embed (X-Frame-Options/CSP); an exported pure `_normalizeUrl(raw)` (http/https only — prepend `https://` when scheme-less; reject `javascript:`/`data:`/`file:`/`blob:`/`about:`/`vbscript:` → `null` → an inline `browser-url-error` notice). **(2)** NEW `components/workstation/BrowserWorkstationPanel.tsx` — mirrors `WorkstationPanel` exactly: store-flag `browserWorkstationOpen` gated (`if (!open) return null;`), full-screen overlay (`position:fixed; inset:0; zIndex:30`), header browser glyph + "BROWSER WORKSTATION" + close (`browser-workstation-close`), Escape-to-close, body `<BrowserWorkstation typeId="browser" />`; root `browser-workstation-panel`. **(3)** `nativeWorkstations.ts` += `browser: BrowserWorkstation` (auto-composes into the AD-1023 WorkspacePanel + is what the AD-1022 launcher seam resolves). **(4)** `store/useStore.ts` += `browserWorkstationOpen: boolean` (type + default `false`, beside `mcpAppsOpen`/`workstationOpen`; no action — toggled via `useStore.setState`). **(5)** `App.tsx` mounts `<BrowserWorkstationPanel />` after the other panels. **(6)** `bridge/stations.tsx` += an Engineering `{ id:'browser-workstation-toggle', label:'Browser', onInvoke:()=>useStore.setState({browserWorkstationOpen:true}) }` action (auto-surfaces in the AD-946 command palette).

**Design decisions.** **DD-1 (one type, one mode model, one contract).** A single `browser` type with `mode ∈ {embedded, watch, bridge}` over the AD-706 observation/action contract; v1 ships `embedded`, names `watch`/`bridge` as disabled selector segments. **DD-2 (reuse, don't rebuild).** v1 embedded is a UI surface (sandboxed iframe) touching NO browser engine; the AD-706 Playwright engine (already shipped) is reused **only by the follow-on slices** (1052a/b/c). v1 adds **zero** Python. **DD-3 (embedded = iframe, not screencast).** v1 renders a native sandboxed `<iframe>` (VS Code Simple-Browser pattern) — works for embeddable URLs, human-driven, no engine. True shared-screencast of arbitrary cross-origin sites (CDP `startScreencast`→canvas + `Input.dispatch*` forwarding) = AD-1052a + AD-1052c; stated honestly because `X-Frame-Options`/CSP block arbitrary iframing. **DD-4 (self-contained component, no `WorkstationDoc` churn).** v1 ignores `doc` (mirrors AD-1024); no kind-union expansion. Doc-driven initial URL = the named AD-1052e. **DD-5 (reachable host = a dedicated overlay).** Mirror AD-1021's `WorkstationPanel`; the AD-1022 launcher / AD-1023 container compose the same component via `nativeWorkstations` (proven by the launcher-seam test). **DD-6 (security / defense-in-depth).** `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-popups"` — for a cross-origin frame, `allow-same-origin` grants the framed site only its OWN origin storage (Same-Origin Policy still blocks any access to the parent HXI origin); the `http(s)`-only URL-scheme allowlist blocks `javascript:`/`data:`/`file:` injection; `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"`. The high-risk surfaces — bridge (drives the human's real browser) and input-forwarding (Computer-Use on a shared browser) — are destructive-capable and **gated behind a HookBus/consensus consent model in AD-1052b/c**, never in v1. **DD-7 (default-OFF, non-disruptive).** Backend type registration is gated on `WorkstationsConfig.enabled` (already so); the overlay is gated on `browserWorkstationOpen=false`. Both off ⇒ byte-identical; the only always-on changes are the inert `nativeWorkstations` map entry + the Engineering launch action (both no-ops until workstations are enabled / the panel is opened). **No `config/system.yaml` change.**

**Slice boundary (named, not built).** **AD-1052a** — watch/screencast mode: mount the already-built AD-706a `BrowserStreamPanel` (MJPEG `<img>`), add `GET /api/browser/sessions` + `BrowserTool.list_sessions()`, and wire the crew-scope token into the HXI (an honest security decision — there is no crew-scope token anywhere in `ui/src` today; `require_crew_scope` is pass-through only while the token is empty). **AD-1052b** — bridge-external mode: `connectOverCDP` to a user-launched Chrome behind a HookBus/consensus consent gate. **AD-1052c** — bidirectional input-forwarding (the human drives the shared browser via CDP `Input.dispatch*` / AD-706c-2 `compute_use_click`); destructive-capable → governance; builds on 1052a. **AD-1052d** — proxied embedding for arbitrary cross-origin (a server-side reverse proxy stripping `X-Frame-Options`/CSP). **AD-1052e** — doc-driven initial URL (a `WorkstationDoc` deep-link).

**Default-OFF / byte-identical-when-OFF.** With `browserWorkstationOpen=false` (default) the panel returns `null` (no iframe loads); with `WorkstationsConfig.enabled=false` (default) the backend `browser` type is absent from the AD-1022 catalog — unchanged backend behavior. `config/system.yaml` untouched; no new npm dependency; no `src/probos/**` edit.

**Files.** NEW `ui/src/components/workstation/BrowserWorkstation.tsx`, `…/BrowserWorkstationPanel.tsx`, `…/BrowserWorkstation.test.tsx`, `…/BrowserWorkstationPanel.test.tsx`; EDIT `…/nativeWorkstations.ts`, `store/useStore.ts`, `App.tsx`, `components/bridge/stations.tsx`, `components/bridge/__tests__/paletteCommands.test.ts` (obsolete-contract bump).

**Tests.** `+14 vitest` (deps-injected where applicable, `EMOJI = /\p{Extended_Pictographic}/u` guard, NO global fetch — the component is self-contained). NEW `BrowserWorkstation.test.tsx` (**8**): Embedded active + Watch/Bridge disabled (the mode model); the empty/honest-degrade state before a URL (mentions X-Frame-Options, no iframe); a valid URL commits → a sandboxed iframe with the normalized `src` + the exact `sandbox`/`referrerpolicy` attrs; a scheme-less host gets `https://` prepended; `javascript:` → the `browser-url-error` notice + no iframe; `_normalizeUrl` enforces the http(s) allowlist (`file:`/`data:`/`about:`/blank → null; `ok.test`→`https://ok.test`); a disabled mode segment keeps Embedded active; the no-emoji + data-testid guard. NEW `BrowserWorkstationPanel.test.tsx` (**6**): null when closed; the overlay + the BrowserWorkstation when open; Escape closes; the header X closes; the AD-1022 launcher seam (mount `WorkstationLauncher deps={{ nativeComponents: nativeWorkstations }}` + a `browser` type → asserts `BrowserWorkstation` renders, NOT the honest-degrade placeholder); no-emoji. The new Engineering `browser-workstation-toggle` action auto-surfacing in the palette bumped two obsolete-contract assertions in `paletteCommands.test.ts` (count 15→16; the Engineering list gains `Browser` after `Workstation`) — the AD-1021/AD-1024 precedent for a palette-surfacing Engineering action. **Gate:** focused (4 files) **32 passed**; full UI suite **258 files, 1644 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed** (was 256/1630 — +2 files, +14 tests, 0 regressions incl. WorkspacePanel/WorkstationLauncher/McpApp* green); `npm run build` (tsc -b + vite) **clean**; `config/system.yaml` confirmed untouched, no `src/probos/**` edit, no new npm dep. ### AD-1052a — Browser Workstation WATCH mode (epic #965)

**Context.** Current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052** (`ea5c4e7b`); **AD-1052a is a sub-AD (no new top-level number)** — the watch/screencast slice the AD-1052 "slice boundary" named. AD-1052 v1 shipped the embedded-iframe surface + the disabled `watch`/`bridge` selector segments; AD-1052a lights up `watch` by mounting the **already-built AD-706a `BrowserStreamPanel`** (MJPEG `<img>`) inside the HXI so the Captain can SEE the live browser an AD-706 agent drives. Read-only; the AD-706/706a engine is REUSED, never rebuilt.

**DD-1 (same-origin, NO token — the AD-1052 security flag resolved by NOT minting a token).** The AD-1052 boundary flagged "wire the crew-scope token into the HXI." VERIFIED at HEAD: the HXI already calls `require_crew_scope`-guarded endpoints same-origin with **no token** — e.g. `useSettingsStore.ts:114` does a bare `fetch('/api/config')` yet `routers/config.py` guards `GET /api/config` with `Depends(require_crew_scope)` (`require_crew_scope` is pass-through while `auth.crew_scope_token==""`, the default). **Decision:** WATCH reuses that exact pattern. The new `GET /api/browser/sessions` is `require_crew_scope`-guarded (consistent with the stream it feeds); the HXI calls it same-origin with no token; `BrowserStreamPanel.token` stays OMITTED. NO token is minted/stored/exposed to browser JS (a vitest guard asserts the stream `<img src>` carries no `token=` query param). A configured `crew_scope_token` honest-degrades the watch surface to "unavailable" exactly like every other HXI surface (the HXI-wide pre-existing gap; no stream-auth change, no `config/system.yaml` edit).

**Decision (additive — 3 Python, 1 UI, 0 config).** **(1)** `tools/browser/session.py` — NEW public `agent_id` property. **Deviation (benign):** the spec STEP 1 earmarked BOTH `agent_id` + `last_url` properties as phantom (to be created), but the `last_url` property **already existed at HEAD** (`return self._last_url`, identical to the spec body), so per the STEP-1 verify-first guard + DRY it was NOT duplicated — only `agent_id` was added. **(2)** `tools/browser/tool.py` — NEW `list_sessions() -> list[dict[str, Any]]` projecting each active session's PUBLIC surface (`session_id`, `agent_id`, `get_streaming_url()`, `last_url`); sync, no page access. **(3)** `routers/browser_stream.py` — NEW `GET /api/browser/sessions` on the SAME router (paths disjoint from `/sessions/{id}/stream`, no collision; `api.py` already includes the router), `require_crew_scope`-guarded, honest-degrading to `{"enabled": false, "sessions": []}` when `runtime.browser_tool` is unset. **(4)** `workstation/BrowserWorkstation.tsx` — flip the `watch` selector segment enabled; an injectable `fetchSessions` (defaults to the same-origin no-token fetch) loads the session list on watch-enter + on a manual Refresh (NO `setInterval` — the MJPEG `<img>` is itself live); a session-picker renders `<BrowserStreamPanel streamingUrl=… />` (no token) for the selected session; a one-line DD-5 privacy note ("Watching surfaces whatever the agent browses").

**Honest-degrade chain.** `runtime.browser_tool` unset → endpoint `{enabled:false}` → "Browser tool is disabled." · enabled + no sessions → "No active browser session." · sessions present but `streaming_enabled=false` → `streaming_url=null` → `BrowserStreamPanel` "Streaming not enabled." · all on → live MJPEG `<img>`. · fetch reject (401 set-token / network) → "Browser streaming unavailable." Default-OFF proven: `BrowserToolConfig.enabled=false` → `finalize._wire_browser_tool` returns early → `runtime.browser_tool` never set → `{enabled:false}`.

**Slice boundary (named, not built).** **AD-1052b** bridge-external (`connectOverCDP` behind a consent gate); **AD-1052c** bidirectional input-forwarding (the human drives the shared browser; destructive-capable → governance, builds on 1052a); **AD-1052d** proxied embedding for arbitrary cross-origin. v1052a does NOT forward input, bridge external Chrome, mint/store/expose any token in JS, change any stream-endpoint auth, or touch `config/system.yaml`.

**Tests.** Python `tests/test_ad1052a_browser_sessions.py` (**7**, BF-287 real fixtures — real `BrowserToolConfig`/`BrowserSession`/`BrowserTool`, real `SystemConfig()` at the auth boundary, sessions seeded into `tool._sessions` directly, no Playwright): `agent_id` property; `last_url` defaults `""`; `list_sessions` empty; `streaming_url` None (disabled) vs the `/api/browser/sessions/<sid>/stream` path (enabled); endpoint honest-degrade `{enabled:false}` when `browser_tool` unset; endpoint lists 2 seeded sessions + a configured `crew_scope_token` + no token → 401. UI `BrowserWorkstation.test.tsx` extended **+8** (8→16): 2 obsolete-contract rewrites (Watch now `disabled:false`; the disabled-segment click repointed to `bridge`) + watch-switch-calls-fetch, list-renders + select-mounts-stream-`<img>`-with-NO-`token=` (DD-1 guard), `streaming_url:null`→unavailable, 3 honest-degrades (disabled/empty/reject), Refresh re-fetches (no auto-poll), no-emoji watch surface. **Gates:** Python `test_ad1052a + test_ad706a` **18 passed**; focused vitest **16 passed**; full UI suite **258 files, 1652 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed** (was 1644 — +8, 0 regressions); `npm run build` (tsc -b + vite) **clean**. `config/system.yaml` untouched; no new npm dependency; no token in browser JS. ### AD-1052b — Browser Workstation BRIDGE mode (epic #965)

**Context.** Current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052** (`ea5c4e7b`); **AD-1052b is a sub-AD (no new top-level number)** — the bridge-external slice the AD-1052/1052a "slice boundary" named. The Captain launches their OWN Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port=9222`; the already-shipped AD-706 `BrowserTool` attaches over CDP (`chromium.connect_over_cdp(endpoint)`) so an agent can drive the user's **real** browser (with their logged-in sessions). HIGH-RISK → gated behind a default-OFF `bridge_enabled` flag (SEPARATE from `enabled`), an explicit `confirm:true` consent step, and an SSRF host allowlist. v1 embedded + AD-1052a watch unchanged; the AD-706 engine + AD-706a stream are REUSED, never rebuilt.

**DD-1 (connect path; disconnect-not-close — the headline safety property).** `BrowserSession.connect(endpoint)` does `connect_over_cdp(endpoint)` and reuses the browser's **existing** `contexts[0]`/`pages[0]` (the user's real logged-in session — a fresh `new_context()` would be cookie-less, defeating the purpose; mirrors the in-repo `task_sessions/browser.py:88` precedent). `stop()` for a connected session (a new early-return branch at the top, gated on `self._connected`) calls `browser.close()` — which over a `connect_over_cdp` browser **disconnects** from the browser server (Playwright docs: *"In case this browser is connected to, clears all created contexts … and disconnects"*), it does **NOT** quit the user's Chrome — plus `playwright.stop()`, and **never** closes the user's `page`/`context`. Gated by the new `bridge_enabled` flag.

**DD-2 (consent — headline DEVIATION, flagged + justified).** The AD-1052/1052a slice-boundary prose pre-committed AD-1052b to a *"HookBus/consensus consent gate."* Verify-first shows that is the **wrong primitive** and it is **SUPERSEDED**: (a) `runtime.submit_mcp_invoke_with_consensus` (runtime.py:3201) is a multi-agent **quorum** vote + red-team for **agent-initiated** MCP invokes — a Captain connecting to the Captain's **own** browser is not the subject of an agent vote (the Captain **is** the authority); wrong authority model. (b) the HookBus `PRE_TOOL_USE` gate (hooks/bus.py:48, fired finalize.py:3383) gates **agent dispatch / tool invocation** inside the cognitive pipeline — the HXI connect endpoint does not flow through agent dispatch; threading the HookBus into a UI router is over-engineering. (c) the AD-706 tier-3 `_pending_confirmations` flow (tool.py:76) is a per-**action** Captain ACK, not a session-creation consent. **DECISION:** the right-sized primitive for "a one-time per-bridge-session Captain approval" is the **explicit-confirm endpoint gate** — a default-OFF `bridge_enabled` config flag + an explicit `confirm:true` body param (sent only on the explicit Connect gesture) + a `BROWSER_BRIDGE_CONNECTED`/`REFUSED` **audit event** reusing BrowserTool's existing `_safe_emit`/`EventType` surface (the AD-706 governance plane). Honest: the Captain is the authority, consent is one-time-per-connect, and it reuses existing AD-706 governance rather than inventing a consent system. The three rejected primitives were evaluated above; **the slice prose's "HookBus/consensus consent gate" is superseded by this entry.**

**DD-3 (SSRF allowlist).** `BrowserTool._validate_cdp_endpoint(endpoint)` enforces `BrowserToolConfig.bridge_allowed_hosts` (default `["127.0.0.1","localhost","[::1]"]`, localhost-only) in the **backend** (the authoritative gate — not just the UI): it accepts only http/https/ws/wss schemes and exact-matches the `urlparse(...).hostname` against the allowlist (case-insensitive), refusing arbitrary remote CDP endpoints AND the `http://127.0.0.1.evil.com:9222` host-suffix bypass (exact match, not suffix).

**DD-4 (honest-degrade chain).** `enabled=False` → endpoint "Browser tool is disabled" · `bridge_enabled=False` → "Bridge mode is disabled" · `confirm!=True` → "Connection consent is required" · host not in allowlist → "Endpoint not allowed" · `connect()` raises → "Could not connect to <endpoint>" · connected + `streaming_enabled` off → `BrowserStreamPanel` "Streaming not enabled" · all on → live MJPEG of the user's real browser.

**DD-5 (default-OFF / non-disruptive).** Bridge lights up only under `enabled` + `bridge_enabled` + `confirm`. `BrowserSession.start()` and the LAUNCHED `stop()` path are **byte-identical** (the bridge adds a sibling `connect()` + a `self._connected` early-return branch at the top of `stop()`); v1 embedded + AD-1052a watch unchanged; no existing surface changes; **`config/system.yaml` untouched** (Pydantic defaults give zero-config boot).

**DD-6 (reuse the watch surface — free).** The AD-706a stream (`browser_stream._generate`) produces frames via `await page.screenshot(type="jpeg", quality=…)` — page-bound, NOT CDP `Page.startScreencast` — so it works over **any** Playwright `Page`, including a `connect_over_cdp` page. When `streaming_enabled` is on, the bridge "connected" view reuses the AD-1052a `BrowserStreamPanel` with **zero** new streaming code; when off, `get_streaming_url()` returns `None` → `BrowserStreamPanel` honest-degrades while still connected.

**Decision (additive — 5 Python, 1 UI, 0 config).** **(1)** `events.py` — 3 new EventTypes (`BROWSER_BRIDGE_CONNECTED`/`REFUSED`/`DISCONNECTED`) after `BROWSER_RECORDING_FAILED`. **(2)** `tools/browser/session.py` — `self._connected` handle, a sibling `connect()` (connect_over_cdp + reuse `contexts[0]`/`pages[0]`), an `is_connected` property, and the connected early-return branch in `stop()` (disconnect, never close). **(3)** `config.py` — `BrowserToolConfig.bridge_enabled` (default False) + `bridge_allowed_hosts` (default localhost-family). **(4)** `tools/browser/tool.py` — `_validate_cdp_endpoint()` (allowlist/SSRF) + `connect_bridge_session(endpoint, *, agent_id, confirm)` (consent + allowlist + `_session_factory` connect + audit events). **(5)** `routers/browser_stream.py` — `BridgeConnectRequest` + `POST /api/browser/bridge/connect` on the SAME router, `require_crew_scope`-guarded, honest-degrading `{"connected": false, "reason": "Browser tool is disabled."}` when `runtime.browser_tool` is unset (a thin adapter — all policy lives in `BrowserTool`). **(6)** `workstation/BrowserWorkstation.tsx` — the `bridge` selector segment flipped enabled; an injectable `connectBridge` (default same-origin POST with `confirm:true`, NO token — DD-1); a `renderBridge()` with an endpoint input (`browser-bridge-endpoint`, default `http://127.0.0.1:9222`), an explicit consent note (`browser-bridge-consent-note`), a Connect button (`browser-bridge-connect`); on connected → `<BrowserStreamPanel>` under `browser-bridge-stream` (no token), on refused → `browser-bridge-reason`.

**Deviation (benign, flagged — IPv6 allowlist normalization).** The spec's Section-3 `_validate_cdp_endpoint` (exact `host in allow`) was inconsistent with both the Section-2 config default `["127.0.0.1","localhost","[::1]"]` AND test 9's enumeration of `[::1]` as "ok": `urlparse("http://[::1]:9222").hostname` returns `"::1"` (brackets stripped), so a literal exact-match would REJECT the IPv6 loopback the config advertises (a dead default entry + a failing test). Per the verify-first guard, `_validate_cdp_endpoint` bracket-normalizes BOTH the parsed host and the allowlist entries before comparison — making the config default work and passing test 9 while **preserving** the exact-host SSRF guard (`127.0.0.1.evil.com` still refused). Config Section 2 kept verbatim.

**Slice boundary (named, not built).** **AD-1052c** bidirectional input-forwarding (the human drives the shared browser via CDP `Input.dispatch*` / AD-706c-2 `compute_use_click`; destructive-capable → governance; builds on 1052a). **AD-1052d** proxied embedding for arbitrary cross-origin (a reverse proxy stripping `X-Frame-Options`/CSP). v1052b does NOT forward input, build a reverse proxy, rebuild the AD-706/706a engine, invent a new consent system, wire HookBus/consensus for the connect (explicitly rejected — DD-2), or mint/store/expose any crew-scope token in browser JS (AD-1052a DD-1 stands).

**Tests.** Python `tests/test_ad1052b_browser_bridge.py` (**13**, BF-287 real fixtures — real `BrowserToolConfig`/`BrowserSession`/`BrowserTool`, real `SystemConfig()` at the auth boundary, NO real Chrome): session `connect()` reuses `contexts[0]`/`pages[0]` (monkeypatched `async_playwright`, asserts `new_context`/`new_page` NOT called); connected `stop()` disconnects (`browser.close` awaited) and NEVER closes `page`/`context` + emits `BROWSER_BRIDGE_DISCONNECTED`; launched `stop()` unchanged (DD-5 regression guard); tool refuses on disabled/no-consent/bad-host/unreachable (each with the matching `BROWSER_BRIDGE_REFUSED` reason, no session stored) + localhost happy-path (`BROWSER_BRIDGE_CONNECTED`, session stored, `streaming_url`); `_validate_cdp_endpoint` allowlist (localhost-family incl. `[::1]` ok; `evil.com` / the `127.0.0.1.evil.com` bypass / `file:///x` / `""` rejected) + custom allowlist; endpoint honest-degrade (`browser_tool` unset) + endpoint connects (real `BrowserTool` + `_FakeSession`) + a configured `crew_scope_token` + no token → 401. UI `BrowserWorkstation.test.tsx` extended **+6** (16→22): 2 obsolete-contract rewrites (Bridge now `disabled:false`; the disabled-segment-click repurposed to a Bridge-switch-shows-endpoint) + Bridge-shows-endpoint/consent-note/Connect, Connect-calls-connectBridge-and-mounts-stream-`<img>`-with-NO-`token=` (DD-1 guard), `streaming_url:null`→unavailable, refused→`browser-bridge-reason`, reject→"Could not connect", no-emoji bridge surface + consent-note present (DD-2). **Gates:** focused Python (`test_ad1052b + test_ad1052a + test_ad706 + test_ad706a`) **53 passed, 1 skipped**; full Python `tests/ -q -n 4` **17234 passed, 23 skipped, 0 failed** (902s; 0 regressions vs clean HEAD); focused vitest **22 passed**; full UI suite **258 files, 1658 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed** (was 1652 — +6, 0 regressions); `npm run build` (tsc -b + vite) **clean**. `config/system.yaml` untouched; no new npm dependency; no token in browser JS. STAGED (not committed). Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

### AD-1052c — Browser Workstation INPUT-FORWARDING (the human drives the shared browser) (epic #965)

**Context.** Current highest landed top-level = **AD-1052** (`ea5c4e7b`); **AD-1052c is a sub-AD (no new top-level number)** — the input-forwarding slice the AD-1052/1052a/1052b boundary named. AD-1052a lets the Captain *watch* the live AD-706 browser (read-only MJPEG); AD-1052c is the second half of the Captain's "embedded and shared like VS Code browser sharing": the human clicks + types + scrolls on the watch canvas and those events forward to the actual Playwright `page` (`page.mouse.*`/`page.keyboard.*`), making the shared browser **bidirectional** (agent drives + human takes the wheel) — for BOTH a headless watch session and an AD-1052b bridged external browser. The AD-706 engine + AD-706a stream are REUSED, never rebuilt.

**DD-0 (reuse-vs-add — verified).** There is no session-level coordinate-dispatch method at HEAD. The coordinate-click primitive exists only inside `compute_use.py:325-329` wrapped in an LLM-vision predict + `action_verify` handshake (wrong shape — the human already knows where they clicked; the LLM adds latency + a model dependency), and `actions.py` clicks are selector/index-based (wrong — human input is normalized-coord). **Decision: ADD `BrowserSession.forward_input(event)`** — a thin coord-mapping dispatch that REUSES the SAME Playwright primitives the agent path uses (`getattr(page,"mouse"/"keyboard",None).click/move/wheel/type/press`), NOT the `compute_use_click` flow. Invents no new dispatch.

**DD-1 (coordinate protocol — resolution-independent, no viewport leak).** The UI sends NORMALIZED `(nx,ny)∈[0,1]` (= img-relative px ÷ rendered img size) + the event kind; the backend de-normalizes via `_resolve_viewport()` = `page.viewport_size` (a Playwright Page **property**, dict|None — None for many `connect_over_cdp` pages) → fallback to the new `BrowserToolConfig.viewport_width`/`viewport_height` (defaults 1280/720). `vx = round(_clamp01(nx) * vw)`. The MJPEG frame IS `page.screenshot` of the viewport, so the aspect matches and `mouse.click`/`viewport_size` are both CSS px. The new config fields are **read-only fallbacks — NOT wired into `new_context()`**, so `start()` stays byte-identical and Playwright keeps its 1280×720 default. No viewport size is leaked to browser JS.

**DD-2 (event model — v1 scope).** v1 forwards `click` (+ button left/right/middle), `type` (literal text), `key` (allowlist), and `scroll` (`mouse.move` + `mouse.wheel`). Deferred to a later slice: `move`/hover, `drag`, file-drop, modifier-combo keys.

**DD-3 (forward path; honest-degrade, never raises).** `BrowserSession.forward_input(event)` returns `{"forwarded": False, "reason": ...}` (never raises) on `no_page`/`no_mouse`/`no_keyboard`/`key_not_allowed`/`unknown_kind`, and `{"forwarded": True, ...}` with the mapped viewport coords on success.

**DD-4 (governance — default-OFF + explicit Drive toggle + per-episode audit).** The human IS the Captain (direct authority — same model as AD-1052b's connect, not an agent quorum). The gate = a new default-OFF `BrowserToolConfig.input_forwarding_enabled` flag + an explicit UI **Drive** toggle (`browser-watch-drive`, `aria-pressed`, rendered ONLY when the flag is on — watch stays read-only by default) + an audit event: `BROWSER_INPUT_FORWARDED` emitted ONCE per drive-episode (the first forward per `session_id`, tracked by `BrowserTool._driven_sessions`) and `BROWSER_INPUT_REFUSED` on every refusal — NOT per keystroke (no event spam). The endpoint refuses when the flag is off or the session is gone.

**DD-5 (default-OFF / non-disruptive).** The Drive toggle only appears/activates under `input_forwarding_enabled`; the new viewport fields are read-only fallbacks (NOT in `new_context`) so `start()` is byte-identical; `BrowserStreamPanel` with NO `driveEnabled`/`onForwardInput` props is byte-identical; v1 embedded + AD-1052a watch + AD-1052b bridge are unchanged when the flag is off; **`config/system.yaml` untouched**.

**DD-6 (security / defense-in-depth).** Normalized coords are clamped to `[0,1]` backend-side (`_clamp01`) before de-normalizing — out-of-range input can't reach outside the viewport; the `key` kind is checked against `_FORWARD_KEY_ALLOWLIST` (Enter/Tab/Backspace/Delete/Escape/Arrows/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown — no modifier combos like `Control+w`); forwarded `type` text is capped at `_FORWARD_TEXT_MAX` (4096). Playwright treats text/keys as literal synthetic input (no `eval`, no injection vector). The endpoint is `require_crew_scope`-guarded and the UI POSTs same-origin with NO token (AD-1052a DD-1 stands).

**Decision (additive — 5 Python, 2 UI, 0 config).** **(1)** `events.py` — `BROWSER_INPUT_FORWARDED`/`BROWSER_INPUT_REFUSED` EventTypes. **(2)** `config.py` — `BrowserToolConfig.input_forwarding_enabled` (default False) + `viewport_width`/`viewport_height` (read-only fallbacks). **(3)** `tools/browser/session.py` — module helpers (`_FORWARD_KEY_ALLOWLIST`, `_FORWARD_TEXT_MAX`, `_clamp01`, `_as_float`), `_resolve_viewport()`, and `forward_input(event)` (click/type/key/scroll over the reused primitives). **(4)** `tools/browser/tool.py` — `_driven_sessions` set, the public `input_forwarding_enabled` property, and `forward_input(session_id, event, *, agent_id)` (the flag→session→dispatch→per-episode-audit gate, mirroring `connect_bridge_session`). **(5)** `routers/browser_stream.py` — `InputForwardRequest` + `POST /api/browser/sessions/{session_id}/input` (`require_crew_scope`, honest-degrade when `browser_tool` unset — a thin adapter), and `GET /sessions` extended with the additive `input_forwarding_enabled` flag. **(6)** `browser/BrowserStreamPanel.tsx` — exported `ForwardInputEvent` union + pure `_normalizePointer(clientX,clientY,rect)` (null on zero-area rect); optional `driveEnabled`/`onForwardInput` props → when present the `<img>` gains `tabIndex`/`data-driving`/`cursor:crosshair` + `onClick`/`onWheel`/`onKeyDown` capture (absent ⇒ byte-identical). **(7)** `workstation/BrowserWorkstation.tsx` — the Drive toggle (flag-gated) + injectable `forwardInput` (default same-origin POST, no token) wired to BOTH the watch and bridge panel mounts.

**Slice boundary (named, not built).** **AD-1052d** proxied embedding for arbitrary cross-origin (a reverse proxy stripping `X-Frame-Options`/CSP). v1052c does NOT build the proxy, add move/hover/drag/file-drop/modifier-combo input, rebuild the AD-706/706a/1052a/1052b engine·stream·governance, mint a token in JS, or wire `viewport_*` into `new_context`.

**Tests.** Python `tests/test_ad1052c_browser_input_forward.py` (**17**, BF-287 real fixtures — real `BrowserToolConfig`/`BrowserSession`/`BrowserTool`, a `_FakePage` with mouse/keyboard recorders + a settable `viewport_size`, NO real browser): click 0.5/0.5@1280×720→(640,360); `viewport_size=None`→config fallback 1000/500→(500,250); clamp 1.5/-0.2→(1280,0); scroll→`move`+`wheel(0,120)`; `type` 5000 chars→capped 4096; `key` Enter→`press`; `Control+w`→`key_not_allowed` (no `press`); `_page=None`→`no_page`; unknown kind; gate OFF→refusal + `BROWSER_INPUT_REFUSED` + page untouched; `session_not_found`→REFUSED; two clicks→exactly one `BROWSER_INPUT_FORWARDED` (per-episode); the `input_forwarding_enabled` property reflects config; endpoint `browser_tool` unset honest-degrade; endpoint happy path 200 (get_runtime override); `GET /sessions` surfaces the flag (both branches); a configured `crew_scope_token` + no token → 401. UI: `BrowserStreamPanel.test.tsx` (NEW) `_normalizePointer` midpoint/clamp/zero-rect-null + the driving `<img>` gains `tabIndex`/`data-driving` and click calls `onForwardInput` (mocked `getBoundingClientRect`); `BrowserWorkstation.test.tsx` extended — the Drive toggle hidden when the flag is false, shown + `aria-pressed` when true, no-emoji + data-testid guards. **Gates:** focused Python (`test_ad1052c + test_ad1052b + test_ad1052a`) **37 passed**; full Python `tests/ -q -n 4` **17251 passed, 23 skipped, 0 failed** (969s; +17 vs the AD-1052b baseline, 0 regressions); focused vitest **38 passed**; full UI suite **259 files, 1674 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed** (was 258/1658 — +1 file, +16 tests, 0 regressions); `npm run build` (tsc -b + vite) **clean**. `config/system.yaml` untouched; no new npm dependency; no token in browser JS. STAGED (not committed). Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

### AD-1019d: MCP toolbox HXI — tier authoring + department lockers + resolved toolbox (UI-only over AD-1019e; closes #964, epic #955)

**Context.** Current highest LANDED top-level AD: **AD-1038** (#987). **AD-1019d is the number issue #964 carries** (a free sub-AD of the AD-1019 family — it does NOT mint a new top-level number). AD-1019e shipped the backend authoring surface (per-tool risk set/clear/read, department-locker stock/unstock/list, the 3-source `resolve_mcp_access` fold that resolves `source="department"`) but **nothing surfaces it to the Captain**. AD-1019d is that operator HXI — **UI-only, additive, default-OFF**, consuming the AD-1019e endpoints verbatim (NO backend / config / store / migration change). The verified API map (re-confirmed by reading `routers/mcp_servers.py` + `routers/mcp_departments.py` at HEAD `5f18b15e`): `GET /{id}/tools` → `{tools:[{name,description?,risk?,risk_source?}],count,error?}` (risk fields OMITTED when no risk store); `PUT/DELETE /{id}/tools/{tool}/risk` (`{risk}`→`{server_id,tool,risk}` / `{cleared}`); `GET /{id}/agents/{aid}/access` → `{server_enabled,tools:[{name,enabled,source}]}` with `source∈tool|server|department|default`; `GET /api/mcp/departments/grants` → `{grants:[{grant_id,department,tool_id,is_restriction,enabled}]}`; `POST /{department}/tools` (`{server_id,tool?,enabled}`→single grant); `DELETE /grants/{grant_id}`→`{revoked}`; all gated `management_enabled` → 404 `feature_disabled` (UI honest-degrades the 404 to disabled/hidden).

**Decision.** Four UI surfaces, all mirroring the established `McpServersPanel`/`McpAgentAccess` pattern (inline api + `Deps` interface + `_fn = deps?.x ?? apiX`, stroke-SVG glyphs, no emoji, a `data-testid` on every element, honest-degrade). **(1)** `McpAgentAccess.tsx` — one-line `sourceColor()` fix: a `department` source now resolves green `#40b890` (was falling through to the grey default — the visible GAP). **(2)** NEW `McpToolRisk.tsx` — per-tool risk authoring as an expandable "Tool risk" section in each `ServerRow` (sibling to "Agent access"): three stroke-SVG glyphs hammer(`open`)/sidearm(`confirm`)/torpedo(`consensus`), the active tier amber, a "Default" reset (clear override), a read-only `risk_source` badge (override amber / default dim). **(3)** NEW `McpDepartmentLockers.tsx` — department-tier authoring: the department picker is the distinct set of `RosterAgent.department`, a stock form (department + server + optional tool → `POST stock`), and the locker list grouped by department with per-grant `Unstock`. **(4)** NEW `McpAgentToolbox.tsx` — the resolved read-only payoff: pick an agent, iterate the *enabled* servers, fetch `/access`, list only the `enabled` tools, each with a 3-bucket provenance badge. **(5)** `McpServersPanel.tsx` — a tab strip (`servers`|`lockers`|`toolbox`, default `servers`) gated on `!error && !disabled`; the existing servers list/form blocks are view-gated under `view === 'servers'` (default → existing testids byte-identical); lockers/toolbox mount on their tabs.

**Design decisions.** **DD-1 (single entry = the existing MCP panel).** Lockers + toolbox surface as a **tab strip inside `McpServersPanel`** — NO new overlay, store flag, `stations.tsx`/`App.tsx`/`useStore.ts` change. The one MCP management overlay (`mcpServersOpen`) gains two tabs; the default `servers` view is byte-identical to HEAD. **DD-2 (risk in `ServerRow`, server-tool-scoped).** Risk authoring is a per-row expandable section (mirrors the AD-1019a "Agent access" section), keyed on `(serverId, tool)` — the same key the AD-1019e PUT writes and the AD-1019c dispatch reads (DD-1 of AD-1019e). **DD-3 (three stroke-SVG glyphs, no emoji — HXI #3).** `open`/`confirm`/`consensus` render as hammer/sidearm/torpedo inline SVG (`viewBox 0 0 24 24`, `strokeWidth 1.5`, round caps, no fills) — escalating consequence, amber active / dim inactive. **DD-4 (`McpAgentAccess` department color fix).** The smallest-blast change (one `sourceColor` line + the type comment) closes the visible department-grey gap that motivated #964. **DD-5 (3-bucket toolbox badge).** `toolboxSource(raw)` collapses the 4 resolver sources into 3 operator buckets: `tool`|`server`→`agent` (amber `#f0b060`), `department`→`department` (green `#40b890`), `default`→`ship` (blue `#50a0d0`). **DD-6 (inline api, deps-injectable, reuse exports).** Each component carries its own inline api defaulted into a `Deps` seam (no separate `*Api.ts`); the lockers + toolbox REUSE the exported `fetchRosterApi`/`fetchServersApi`/`fetchAgentAccessApi`/`fetchServerToolsApi` as their defaults (the `McpServersPanel ↔ child` import cycle is safe — `fetchServersApi` is a hoisted `async function`). **DD-7 (default-OFF honest-degrade).** With `management_enabled=false` every fetch 404s → each surface shows its disabled note (the tab strip + per-row sections are gated on `!disabled`, so they never render); with `mcpServersOpen=false` the panel returns `null` (no fetch). `config/system.yaml` untouched.

**Default-OFF / byte-identical-when-OFF.** Management OFF (default) → `mcp-disabled` shown, NO tab strip, NO child mounts (all gated `!error && !disabled`); the children's own fetches all 404 → honest-degrade to disabled. Panel closed (default) → `null`, no fetch. Default `view === 'servers'` keeps every existing `McpServersPanel`/`McpAgentAccess` testid + assertion green.

**Tests.** `+20 vitest` (deps-injected, `EMOJI = /\p{Extended_Pictographic}/u` guard, NO global fetch): NEW `McpToolRisk.test.tsx` (**7** — three tiers render, PUT `setRisk` for consensus + confirm, DELETE `clearRisk`, the `risk_source` override/default badge, 404→disabled, no-emoji); NEW `McpDepartmentLockers.test.tsx` (**6** — distinct-sorted department picker, stock a single tool + a whole server `{server_id,tool?,enabled}`, locker render + unstock, 404→disabled, no-emoji); NEW `McpAgentToolbox.test.tsx` (**5** — iterate enabled servers only / filter disabled tools, the 3-bucket badge maps tool→agent/department→department(green `rgb(64,184,144)`)/default→ship, per-server honest-degrade, servers-404→disabled, no-emoji); `McpAgentAccess.test.tsx` **+1** regression (a `department`-sourced tool renders the badge color `rgb(64,184,144)`, not grey); `McpServersPanel.test.tsx` **+1** smoke (default `view==='servers'` keeps all existing assertions; `mcp-view-lockers`/`mcp-view-toolbox` switch; `mcp-risk-section-{id}` toggles the risk section — the tab-mounted children stub global fetch→404 so they honest-degrade). **Gate:** focused (5 files) **53 passed**; full UI suite **256 files, 1630 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed** (was 253/1610 — +3 files, +20 tests, 0 regressions); `npm run build` (tsc -b + vite) **clean**; `config/system.yaml` confirmed untouched. ### AD-1019e: MCP authoring endpoints (risk tiers + department lockers) — HTTP authoring surface over the AD-1019b stores (risk set/clear/read + department locker stock/unstock/list); stores pre-existing, NO migration, gated management_enabled; unblocks #964/AD-1019d (epic #955)

**Context.** Current highest LANDED top-level AD: **AD-1038** (#987). **AD-1019e is a free sub-AD of the AD-1019 family** (highest sub was AD-1019c) — it does NOT mint a new top-level number. **Scope-inversion finding:** issue #964 (AD-1019d, the MCP toolbox HXI) declares *"No backend change (consumes AD-1019b/c endpoints)"* — but that premise was **false**. AD-1019b shipped the three-tier authorization *substrate* (the `McpToolRiskStore`, the `DepartmentToolGrantStore`, the 3-source `resolve_mcp_access` fold, the `default_risk` column) and AD-1019c shipped the *invoke* path, but the AD-1019b review **explicitly deferred the authoring endpoints** ("NO new API endpoints — issue-dept-grant/set-risk are AD-1019d authoring"). There is therefore NO HTTP surface to *set* a per-tool risk tier or *stock* a department locker — the AD-1019d UI would have nothing to POST to. AD-1019e is that missing authoring surface (backend-only), unblocking AD-1019d. Additive over `a44b0795`, default-OFF, the stores are consumed (NOT modified).

**Decision.** Backend-only, additive, gated on `config.mcp.management_enabled` (404 `feature_disabled` when off → every existing flow byte-identical). **(1) Risk read** — `GET /api/mcp/servers/{id}/tools` augments each enumerated tool with `risk` (the effective tier via the pure `resolve_tool_risk(McpToolRisk(record.default_risk), get_risk_sync(...))`) + `risk_source` (`"override"`|`"default"`); honest-degrade: with no `mcp_tool_risk_store` the two fields are OMITTED (existing shape byte-identical). **(2) Risk authoring** — `PUT /{id}/tools/{tool}/risk` (`RiskBody{risk}`; 404 unknown server, 400 `invalid_risk` for a value outside the enum, 503 no risk store, else `set_risk` → `{server_id, tool, risk}`) + `DELETE /{id}/tools/{tool}/risk` (`clear_risk` → `{cleared}`), mirroring the AD-1019 per-agent grant endpoints (L880/L920). **(3) Server default risk** — `McpServerUpdateBody` gains `default_risk: str | None = None`; the existing `model_dump(exclude_unset)`→`replace`→`validate_record` merge + `store.update`'s generic column write apply + persist it end-to-end (`validate_record`'s `_VALID_RISK_TIERS` already guards the value). **(4) Department lockers** — NEW `routers/mcp_departments.py` (prefix `/api/mcp/departments`): `GET /grants` (list active dept grants), `POST /{department}/tools` (`{server_id, tool?, enabled}` → resolve the server `name` → composite `mcp:{name}[:{tool}]` tool-id → `issue_grant`), `DELETE /grants/{grant_id}` (`revoke_grant` → `{revoked}`); included unconditionally in `api.py`'s flat loop (gate 404s when off). The dept-grant `tool_id` uses the composite-id convention so the AD-1019b three-source resolver folds it: an agent in the department resolves `source="department"` — the loop that closes #964.

**Design decisions.** **DD-1 (key consistency — id vs name, VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY).** The `McpToolRiskStore` keys on `(server_id, tool_name)`, and the AD-1019c dispatch reads it by the server **RECORD ID**, NOT its name: `mcp_workbench.py` builds the `_McpTool` adapter with `server_id=record.id` (L299) and both `MCPWorkbench._effective_risk` (L187) and `agentic_dispatch._McpTool.effective_risk` (L258) read `get_risk_sync(record.id, tool)`. The authoring path's `{server_id}` path param IS the record id (the existing agent endpoints `await store.get(server_id)` with it), so PUT/DELETE/GET-read all write/read the SAME key the dispatch resolves at invoke time — an authored override actually takes effect. A `set→dispatch-read` parity test asserts this (had they mismatched, the endpoint would be useless). **NOTE:** the department-grant `tool_id` deliberately uses the server **NAME** (the composite `mcp:{name}` convention that `resolve_mcp_access` folds) — two different, both-correct keying schemes (risk keys on id; grants key on the composite name). **DD-2 (server default via the existing PUT).** No new endpoint for the server default — one field on `McpServerUpdateBody`; the generic merge already validates + persists it. **DD-3 (standalone departments router).** Department lockers get their own `/api/mcp/departments` router (NOT folded into `mcp_servers.py`) — a department is not a child of a server (many-to-many), so the resource path is department-rooted; the gate + honest-degrade helpers are replicated (4 lines) so the module is self-contained (no private-symbol import from a sibling router). **DD-4 (honest-degrade on every axis).** Every store read is `getattr(...)`; the risk-read OMITS its fields when the store is absent (byte-identical), the authoring endpoints 503 when their store is absent, the gate 404s first. **DD-5 (NO migration / NO store change).** The `McpToolRiskStore` + `DepartmentToolGrantStore` + the `default_risk` column all pre-exist (AD-1019b); this AD only adds HTTP handlers + one optional Pydantic field — no schema, no migration, no new store, no `config/system.yaml`.

**Default-OFF / byte-identical-when-OFF.** With `management_enabled=False` (default) all new endpoints 404 `feature_disabled` (the gate is the first statement in every handler) and `GET /tools` is unchanged (the risk-read only runs when the store is present, which only happens when management is enabled); the departments router is included unconditionally but inert. The only always-on additions are one optional `McpServerUpdateBody` field and one always-404-when-off router. `config/system.yaml` untouched.

**Tests.** `tests/test_ad1019e_mcp_authoring.py` (**11**, BF-287 — REAL `McpServerStore`/`McpToolRiskStore`/`DepartmentToolGrantStore`/`ToolPermissionStore` over real `tmp_path` DBs, a `_Fake*` bridge whose `list_tools()` returns a fixed set, REAL `_Registry`/`_Ontology` stubs, a real `TestClient` mounting BOTH routers): PUT risk happy/invalid-400/unknown-server-404; DELETE risk `{cleared:true}`-then-`{cleared:false}`; `GET /tools` reports default+`risk_source:"default"` then override+`"override"` (sibling stays default); **DD-1 parity** (the PUT key == the dispatch's `get_risk_sync(record.id, tool)` key); dept stock → grant → `GET /grants` lists it → **`get_agent_access` for a member resolves `source="department"`** (the #964 integration loop); dept `DELETE /grants/{id}` `{revoked:true}`; dept POST unknown server 404; **gate-off** all five new endpoints 404 `feature_disabled`; a real-DB **reopen** proving `_row_to_grant` reload + `revoke_grant` rowcount True-then-False. **Gate:** focused **11 passed** (`-n 0`); back-compat `-k "mcp or ad1015 or ad1019"` **393 passed** (the only 2 failures — `test_ad1019c_default_off`/`test_ad1019c_consensus` — reproduce on clean HEAD with this AD stashed ⇒ **pre-existing, unrelated**); `import probos.api; import probos.runtime` clean. STAGED (not committed). Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

### AD-1024: MCP-app workstation type + gallery — register a native mcp-app type in the AD-1022 registry + a read-only /api/mcp-apps gallery launching apps into the existing McpAppFrame; default-OFF, reuses the AD-597 engine (#968, epic #965)

**Context.** Current highest LANDED AD at authoring: **AD-1038** (#987); **AD-1024 is the number issue #968 carries** (pre-assigned — does NOT mint a new top-level number). The AD-597 engine already ships everything needed to *render* an MCP app — the `MCPAppRegistry` (internal + boot-discovered external app tools), the `McpAppFrame` sandboxed iframe, and `GET /api/mcp/resource?uri=` — but nothing *surfaces* the catalog to the Captain or registers an MCP-app *workstation type*. AD-1024 closes that gap with two thin additions over the existing engine: a read-only gallery API + a native `mcp-app` workstation type. The heavier runtime external-app re-discovery + the AD-1018 connection UX is the deferred **AD-1024a** slice (the gallery already surfaces *boot-discovered* external apps via `list_tools()`). Additive over `58c1bb1e`, default-OFF, reuses the AD-597 engine (does NOT rebuild it).

**Decision.** Architect→Builder, additive across backend (3) + UI (8) + tests (3). **Backend.** (1) NEW `routers/mcp_apps.py` — `GET /api/mcp-apps` (prefix `/api/mcp-apps`, `get_runtime` dep), gated by a `_require_enabled` that 404s `feature_disabled` unless `config.mcp_app_host.enabled` (mirrors `mcp_servers._require_enabled`); honest-degrades 503 when `runtime.mcp_app_registry` is absent; projects `registry.list_tools()` to `McpAppView{name,description,resource_uri,external,server_id}`, **filtering** entries whose `_meta.ui.resourceUri` is empty (a tool with no launchable UI is not a gallery app). (2) `startup/finalize._wire_workstation_types` — registers a native `WorkstationType(id="mcp-app", label="MCP Apps", tier="oss", render=native, component_key="mcp-app")` into the AD-1022 registry when `config.mcp_app_host.enabled`, **before** the workstations early-return (so it exists even when `workstations.enabled=False`; the AD-1022 catalog still hides it until workstations are enabled). (3) `api.py` — include the router in the flat loop. **UI.** (4) NEW `mcp/mcpAppsApi.ts` — `fetchMcpAppsApi()` (mirrors `fetchServersApi`: 404 → `{apps:[],disabled:true}`). (5) NEW `mcp/McpAppGallery.tsx` — deps-injectable inner surface (list+active, mirrors `WorkstationLauncher`): fetch-once on mount, honest-degrade on throw, click an app → `McpAppFrame` with that app's `resource_uri`/`external`. (6) NEW `mcp/McpAppsPanel.tsx` — store-flag overlay (`mcpAppsOpen`, default `false`; mirrors `McpServersPanel`), header X + Escape, embeds the gallery; `useStore` gains `mcpAppsOpen`; `App.tsx` mounts `<McpAppsPanel />`; `stations.tsx` adds an Engineering `mcp-apps-toggle` action. (7) `workstation/nativeWorkstations.ts` — a thin `mcp-app` adapter renders `McpAppGallery` via `createElement` (the module is `.ts`, not `.tsx`), so the registered native type composes into the AD-1023 WorkspacePanel host. (8) co-located vitest.

**Design decisions.** **DD-1 (native, NOT iframe).** The `mcp-app` *type* is registered `render=native, component_key="mcp-app"` — NOT an iframe type. The AD-1022 catalog never serializes a render target (tier-safety, DD-4 of AD-1022), so the per-app launch URIs cannot ride the type catalog; the native gallery component resolves them instead. **DD-2 (the gallery API is the URI source).** Per-app `resource_uri` comes from `GET /api/mcp-apps` (`MCPAppRegistry.list_tools()` `_meta.ui.resourceUri`), NOT the workstation-type catalog — a clean separation between *which type exists* (catalog) and *which apps it can open* (gallery). **DD-3 (`resource_uri` is safe to emit here).** Unlike the AD-1022 catalog, `/api/mcp-apps` MAY emit `resource_uri`: every listed app belongs to the single OSS-gated MCP App Host feature (no commercial-tier render target can leak — there is no tiering on this surface). **DD-4 (standalone overlay; the AD-1023 entry is deferred).** `McpAppsPanel` is its own store-flag overlay (mirrors `McpServersPanel`) so the gallery has a reachable host now; the nativeWorkstations adapter ALSO composes the same gallery into the AD-1023 container — two hosts, one component. **DD-5 (nativeWorkstations adapter via `createElement`).** `'mcp-app'` maps to `(_props) => createElement(McpAppGallery)` (ignores typeId/doc) — `createElement`, not JSX, because `nativeWorkstations.ts` is a `.ts` module. **DD-6 (discovery-source-agnostic).** The gallery surfaces whatever `list_tools()` returns — boot-discovered internal AND external apps — without itself triggering discovery; NO modification to `McpServersPanel`/`WorkstationLauncher`/`WorkspacePanel`/the AD-1022 registry internals.

### AD-1023: Rich Workspace container + AD-998 backing-store binding — the HXI Workspace overlay hosting multiple AD-1022 Workstations over one work context; default-OFF, byte-identical when OFF, UI-only (#967, epic #965)

**Context.** Current highest LANDED AD at authoring: **AD-1038** (#987); **AD-1023 is the number issue #967 carries** (pre-assigned — does NOT mint a new top-level number; the entry-point/persistence slice is the deferred AD-1023a). UI-only, default-OFF, additive over `843bf967`.

**Decision.** Architect→Builder, additive across eight UI files. (1) `store/types.ts` — NEW `Workspace { id; label; backingStoreRef?; participants[]; workstations[] }`, `WorkspaceWorkstation { typeId; label?; doc? }`, and `WorkspaceFolder`/`WorkspaceFolderFile` (the AD-998 response view model). (2) `store/useStore.ts` — `workspaceOpen:boolean` (default `false`) + `activeWorkspace:Workspace|null` (default `null`) beside `workstationOpen`, plus `openWorkspace(ws)` / `closeWorkspace()` (mirrors AD-1021). (5) NEW `workspace/workspaceApi.ts` — `fetchWorkspaceFolder(agentId)` hits the AD-998 endpoint (the Experience layer reaches the folder through the runtime API only, never importing `execution.workspace`). (6) NEW `workspace/WorkspacePanel.tsx` — the container overlay (mirrors the AD-1018/1021 store-flag overlay): single-active-tab rail, each tab resolved via `WorkstationRender` with its own `doc`, a backing-store strip, honest-degrade on every boundary. (5) NEW `components/workstation/WorkstationPanel.tsx` — mirrors `McpServersPanel` exactly (`open = useStore(s => s.workstationOpen); if (!open) return null;`, full-screen overlay, header X + Escape → `closeWorkstation()`, `data-testid="workstation-panel"`, stroke-SVG, no emoji), body `<CodeWorkstation typeId="monaco" />`. (6) `App.tsx` — mount `<WorkstationPanel />` unconditionally beside `<McpServersPanel />`. (7) `components/bridge/stations.tsx` — Engineering action `{ id:'workstation-toggle', label:'Workstation', onInvoke: () => openWorkstation({kind:'scratch', …}) }` (auto-surfaces in the AD-946 command palette). (8) `components/IntentSurface.tsx` — an `data-testid="open-in-workstation"` button on the `msg.buildProposal && status==='review'` card → `openWorkstation({kind:'build', …, changes: file_changes})` (language inferred from the first change's path extension).

**Design decisions.** **DD-1 (type id `monaco`, lazy self-hosted Monaco engine).** The registry/launcher key is `monaco` (the AD-1022 contract is preserved); the engine is a **lazy-loaded `@monaco-editor/react` + `monaco-editor` (both MIT)** surface, **self-hosted** (local-first: `loader.config({ monaco })`, NO CDN loader) with an `editor.worker?worker` shim. `MonacoSurface.tsx` is the **sole** `monaco-editor` importer and is reached only through `React.lazy`/`Suspense` (CodeWorkstation dynamic-imports it), so the multi-MB core is confined to a dedicated `monaco-vendor` Vite `manualChunks` branch (mirrors `stt-vendor`/`avatar-vendor`) — never the main HXI bundle. Read-only for `build`/`artifact` docs, editable for `scratch`; `vs-dark` theme, minimap off, NO LSP / IntelliSense / file tree / extensions (the IDE trap stays excluded). The component is named `CodeWorkstation`. **DD-2 (register via the AD-1022 seam, reach via a new overlay).** `nativeWorkstations = { monaco: CodeWorkstation }` IS the `nativeComponents` map the launcher consumes; since the launcher is unmounted (AD-1023), the reachable v1 host is `WorkstationPanel`. Same component, two hosts; the launcher seam is proven by a test that mounts `WorkstationLauncher deps={{ nativeComponents: nativeWorkstations }}` and asserts `CodeWorkstation` opens for `monaco` (not the honest-degrade placeholder). **DD-3 (`kind ∈ {build, scratch, artifact}`).** scratch = editable textarea; build/artifact = read `<pre>`. Output actions are Copy + Download ONLY — no write-back, no save-to-artifact in v1. **DD-4 (modify vs create — badge only, NO DiffEditor).** `mode:'modify'` → a MODIFY badge + `after_line` anchor (NOT a true diff — no original source without a read endpoint, so the Monaco `DiffEditor` stays deferred to AD-1021b); `create` → a CREATE badge. Multiple `file_changes` → a left rail of path buttons (THIS proposal only — NOT a file tree). **DD-5 (entry points).** (a) "Open in Workstation" on the IntentSurface build-proposal card → `openWorkstation({kind:'build',…})`; (b) the Engineering "Workstation" palette action → `openWorkstation({kind:'scratch',…})`. **DD-6 (default-OFF / non-disruptive).** `workstationOpen` defaults `false`; the panel is mounted-but-null when closed; no existing HXI behavior changes when unopened; `ArtifactViewer` is untouched (additive references only).

**Forward markers (named, not built).** AD-1021b — write-through of edits, save-to-artifact, and a TRUE repo-file `DiffEditor` (needs a read endpoint). AD-1021c — agent co-editing. AD-1021d — trim the ~8.9 MB of dead monaco language-service worker chunks (`ts`/`css`/`html`/`json`, emitted by the full `monaco-editor` barrel but never loaded — the `getWorker` shim returns only the base `editor.worker`) by importing `monaco-editor/esm/vs/editor/editor.api` + a curated `basic-languages` set; preserves syntax highlighting but needs a real-browser highlight check (can't be verified headless, so deferred). AD-1023 — the Workspace container that mounts `WorkstationLauncher` into App (at which point the launcher and the overlay share `CodeWorkstation`).

**Default-OFF / non-disruptive (NON-NEGOTIABLE).** With `workstationOpen=false` (default) `WorkstationPanel` returns `null` (CodeWorkstation never mounts → no artifact fetch); the only always-on additions are two inert store fields, one palette action, and one card button — no existing HXI surface changes until the Captain opens it. `config/system.yaml` is untouched (UI-only); `package.json` gains two MIT deps (`@monaco-editor/react`, `monaco-editor`) that are **lazy-loaded** into the `monaco-vendor` chunk, so the main bundle does not grow and nothing loads until the Captain opens the panel.

### AD-1025b: sweep the remaining CWD-relative paths to the install root — six FIXED via in-module `_install_root()` (mirrored `parents[N]`); install-root anchoring (NOT `runtime.data_dir`) preserves byte-identical-at-repo-root; portability bug (#972, AD-1025 family)

**Context.** Third in the AD-1025 portability family (AD-1025 anchored the Piper binary/voice + AD-690 rejection-cache paths; AD-1025a anchored the voice-listing endpoint). AD-1025's DD-5 audit enumerated six remaining CWD-relative paths as report-only; this AD fixes them. Each built a `data/…` (or `tools/rg`) artifact relative to the **process CWD**, so launching `probos serve` from a sibling folder silently relocated the artifact — the same launch-from-a-sibling-folder failure class AD-1025/1025a fixed for TTS.

**KEY FINDING (decisive, verified).** `runtime.data_dir` (AD-468) is the **platform** data dir (`_platform_data_dir()` → `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ProbOS\data`), **NOT** `<repo>/data`: `__main__.py` constructs `ProbOSRuntime(data_dir=str(data_dir or _default_data_dir()))` where `_default_data_dir()` is the platform dir. Anchoring these raw-relative consumers to `runtime.data_dir` would therefore **relocate** today's `<repo>/data/…` artifacts and **fail** the required byte-identical-at-repo-root contract. Every fix instead anchors to the **install root** (the mirrored `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[N]` pattern — `__main__.py`'s `project_root` / `piper_backend._probos_root`, the bundled-`tools/` anchor), which reproduces today's `<repo>/data/…` paths exactly when CWD == repo root.

**Decision.** Six FIXED paths, each via an in-module `_install_root()` helper mirrored 1–2 lines per file — NOT a cross-module import of the TTS helper (a layer violation + nonsensical coupling); this matches how `__main__.py` and `piper_backend.py` each independently mirror the anchor. **(1)** `agents/code_search.py` (`parents[3]`) — the ripgrep fallback `Path("tools/rg")` → `_install_root()/"tools"/"rg"` (the PATH-first `shutil.which("rg")` leg untouched). **(2)** `naval/captains_log.py` + **(3)** `naval/plan_of_day.py` (`parents[3]`) — the `write_to_disk` consumption `Path(self._config.output_dir)` → `_anchor_under_root(self._config.output_dir)` (new in-module helper mirroring `piper_backend._anchor_path`: absolute as-is, relative under root, NEVER CWD). **(5)** `proactive.py` (`parents[2]`) — `DailyBriefingScheduler` default `state_path or Path("data/briefing_state.json")` → `… or (_install_root()/"data"/"briefing_state.json")` (an explicit `state_path` is honored unchanged). **(6)** `cognitive/session_manager.py` (`parents[3]`) — module-constant `_SESSION_DIR = Path("data/sessions")` → use-time `_default_session_dir()` (`_install_root()/"data"/"sessions"`, resolved on each call, never at import) + `SessionManager.__init__(sessions_dir=…)` default flipped to a `None` sentinel (auto-fixes `shell.py:136`'s no-arg construction; `runtime.py`'s two absolute constructions unaffected; `_SESSION_DIR` had no other reader/importer). **(7)** `routers/security.py` (`parents[3]`) — `_get_audit_log` `Path(getattr(runtime, "_data_dir", Path("data")))` → the PUBLIC `runtime.data_dir` property (Law of Demeter) with the degenerate fallback anchored `_install_root()/"data"`.

**Dispositions.** FIXED: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7. **RESOLVED-no-op: path 4** (`config.py` `agent_probes.db` default) — NOT touched: `startup/finalize.py` rebases it via `Path(sd_cfg.db_path).name` under `runtime.data_dir`, so the `data/` prefix is discarded (no double-resolve, no CWD dependency). **The 2 & 3 Pydantic defaults are KEPT** (`config.py` `output_dir = Path("data/captains_log")` / `Path("data/plan_of_day")`) — they are **test-locked** by `test_ad477_naval.py` (asserts the exact `Path("data/…")` values); only their CONSUMPTION sites change. `config.py` is untouched.

**Default byte-identical at repo root (NON-NEGOTIABLE).** Each fixed path's install-root anchor, when CWD == repo root, resolves to exactly the same filesystem location as the old CWD-relative `Path("data/…")` (the `*_byte_identical_at_repo_root` tests pin this for all six). `__main__.py`'s SessionManager constructions (absolute), `experience/shell.py` (auto-fixed by the `None` sentinel), `startup/finalize.py`, and `config/system.yaml` are all untouched.

**Tests.** `+20 pytest` (`tests/test_ad1025b_path_anchoring.py`, BF-287 discipline — real config objects [`CaptainsLogConfig`/`PlanOfDayConfig`/`DutyPolicyConfig`/`SecurityInfraConfig`] + `SimpleNamespace` runtimes + a real `DutySchedule`, NO MagicMock at the boundary; mirrors the AD-1025/1025a `monkeypatch.setattr(<module>, "_install_root", …)` + `monkeypatch.chdir(elsewhere)` pattern): a depth-lock test (counts every `parents[N]` against drift); per FIXED path an anchors-to-root-not-CWD test, an absolute-used-as-is / PATH-first-precedence test, and a byte-identical-at-repo-root test; `session_manager` adds a use-time-resolution test (two patched roots → two dirs). **Gate:** focused **20 passed**; family + regression (`test_ad1025_path_anchoring` + `test_bf291_piper_voice_catalog` + `test_ad477_naval`) **37 passed** (the naval defaults prove 2/3 unchanged); touched-module blast `-k "code_search or session or proactive or security or naval or ad1025"` **748 passed**; `import probos.runtime` + the 6 modules clean; `ast.parse` on all 6 edited modules + the test file clean. ### AD-1037: affect-salience capture — populate Episode.affect_salience at encoding via a deterministic store-time lexicon scorer; default-OFF, byte-identical when OFF (#986, Oracle recall epic #902)

**Context.** Current highest LANDED AD at authoring: **AD-1038** (#987 live remember/know render, at HEAD `d378a9dc`); **AD-1037 is the number issue #986 carries**. AD-979f shipped the *storage slot* `Episode.affect_salience: float = 0.0` AND a *dormant consumer* — the AD-873 composite reranker's affect term (`recall_rerank_weights["affect"]`, default `0.0` → skipped, byte-identical) — but **explicitly deferred the populator**: the slot was "NOT measured affect yet — the storage slot." So every episode stored `affect_salience == 0.0` and the affect axis could never influence recall even if an operator weighted it. AD-1037 builds the populator: a deterministic store-time lexicon scorer that fills the slot from the episode's own arousal vocabulary.

**Source triage (why a lexicon, not an existing signal).** Three candidate affect sources were evaluated. **(c) BLOCKED — AD-1032 arousal:** the closest existing arousal signal is not wired to a usable store-time hook (blocked upstream); unavailable. **(a) REJECTED — AD-737 `intent_emotion`/`EmotionalIntent`:** the emotion tag is a *valence* signal computed on the avatar/divergence path and **never reaches `EpisodicMemory.store()`** (it is absent at all 18 `Episode(` construction sites that funnel into store), and valence ≠ arousal (salience is about *charge*, not *direction*). **(b) CHOSEN — pure store-time lexicon:** mirror the SHIPPED AD-598 `importance_scorer` exactly — a deterministic, no-LLM/no-network function (store() is hot) that reads the episode's own `user_input` + `reflection` text and scores arousal-vocabulary magnitude. Cheap, dependency-free, and lives where the data already is.

**Decision.** Architect→Builder, additive across four source files. (1) NEW `cognitive/affect_scorer.py` — a single pure `score_affect(episode) -> float` (mirroring `importance_scorer.compute_importance`'s shape: `from __future__ import annotations`, `TYPE_CHECKING` Episode import, module-level disjoint `_HIGH_AROUSAL`/`_MODERATE_AROUSAL` frozensets + `_TAU = 2.0`, whole body wrapped in `try/except → 0.0`). (2) A **one-line** capture hook in `store()`, inserted immediately after the AD-598 importance `dataclasses.replace` block (the precedent AND the anchor), gated `if getattr(self, "_affect_capture_enabled", False) and episode.affect_salience == 0.0:` → `score_affect` → `dataclasses.replace(episode, affect_salience=…)` only when `> 0.0`. (3) `MemoryConfig.affect_capture_enabled = False` (co-located after `recall_rerank_weights`). (4) The flag threaded through `EpisodicMemory.__init__` (defaulted param + `self._affect_capture_enabled` assignment) and the PRIMARY `__main__.py` boot construction (the `__main__.py` rebuild-CLI ctor threads no AD-979x/AD-10xx flag → left default-False).

**Design decisions.** **DD-1 (signal source = deterministic store-time lexicon).** No LLM, no network — `store()` is hot. NOT the AD-737 emotion tag (never reaches store), NOT AD-1032 arousal (blocked). **DD-2 (orthogonal to `importance`).** `importance` keys on trigger_type/channel/outcome = *retention priority*; affect keys on arousal *vocabulary* = *emotional charge*. The two are independent axes (Test 9 pins it: a captain status-check string with importance-vocabulary but no affect words scores `0.0`). **DD-3 (MAGNITUDE not valence).** Both positive ("thrilled") and negative ("devastated") high-arousal words contribute POSITIVELY to `[0,1]` — salience is charge, not direction (Test 6: the two score equal and `> 0`). **DD-4 (capture at `store()` ONLY).** The single chokepoint; NO backfill of pre-existing episodes (deferred AD-1037a, named not built). **DD-5 (normalization).** `raw = 1.0*high_hits + 0.5*moderate_hits + exclam_bonus + caps_bonus`, where `exclam_bonus = min(0.5, 0.1*text.count("!"))` and `caps_bonus = min(0.5, 0.25*(# of ALL-CAPS alpha tokens, len≥3))`; token-multiset counting (repeats count); `affect_salience = clamp01(1 - exp(-raw/TAU))` with `TAU = 2.0`; `raw == 0 ⇒ exactly 0.0`. Empirically verified: 1 high word → `1-exp(-0.5)=0.3935`; 2 high → `0.6321`; 1 moderate → `0.2212`. **DD-6 (gate = `affect_capture_enabled = False`, double-safe OFF).** Capture runs ONLY when the flag is True AND `episode.affect_salience == 0.0` (mirrors the `importance == 5` guard — never clobbers a caller-set value). OFF ⇒ scorer never called ⇒ slot stays `0.0` ⇒ the AD-979f rerank term (weight `0.0`) is already skipped ⇒ byte-identical. To affect ranking the operator must SEPARATELY set `recall_rerank_weights["affect"] > 0` (both default-OFF). **DD-7 (forward markers, named-not-built).** AD-1037a (backfill of pre-existing episodes); a richer/multilingual scorer.

**The 18-sites → 1-chokepoint rationale.** `Episode(` is constructed at ~18 sites across 13 files, but ALL funnel through the single `EpisodicMemory.store()` chokepoint. The capture therefore hooks ONE place (store()) — NOT the 18 constructors. No `Episode(` constructor signature changes (the `affect_salience` field already exists from AD-979f); no frozen-dataclass contract change.

**Default-OFF / byte-identical-when-OFF (NON-NEGOTIABLE).** With `affect_capture_enabled=False` (default) the `store()` gate short-circuits → `score_affect` is never invoked → `affect_salience` stays `0.0` → the AD-979f composite affect term (weight `0.0`) is already skipped (`x**0 == 1` idiom) → recall ordering is byte-identical to pre-AD-1037. `config/system.yaml` is untouched (the default-OFF ships in `config.py`; AD-979f already added the `affect` rerank weight). **Flip path:** set `affect_capture_enabled: true` AND `recall_rerank_weights["affect"] > 0` under `memory:` in `config/system.yaml`, then restart (capture is store-time → only new episodes get scored; backfill is AD-1037a).

**Tests.** `+16 pytest` (`tests/test_ad1037_affect_capture.py`, BF-287 discipline — a REAL `_FakeCollection` stub, NOT MagicMock, + the `EpisodicMemory.__new__` + manual-attribute pattern from `test_ad598` Test 9; no embedding model / LLM / network): **A. score_affect purity (9)** — empty→`0.0` exactly; neutral→`0.0`; 1 high→`≈0.3935`; 2 high→`≈0.6321`; 1 moderate→`≈0.2212`; DD-3 magnitude (devastated == thrilled, both `>0`); `!!!` intensity (`>` plain, `≤1.0`); monotonic (1<2<3 words, all `∈[0,1]`); DD-2 orthogonality (importance-vocab, no affect → `0.0`). **B. capture-in-store() (3)** — flag True + high-affect episode → captured metadata `affect_salience > 0`; **byte-identical-OFF** (flag False, same episode → `0.0`, scorer never invoked); caller-set respect (flag True but `affect_salience=0.5` already → stays `0.5`). **C. metadata round-trip (1)** — `0.7` survives `_episode_to_metadata` → `_metadata_to_episode`. **D. ranking e2e (2)** — pure `_composite_recall_score`: `affect=1.0` weight → high ranks above neutral; `affect=0.0` → equal (byte-identical OFF at ranking). **E. default-OFF structural (1)** — `MemoryConfig().affect_capture_enabled is False`. **Gate:** focused **16 passed**; blast (AD-598 importance + AD-567a anchor metadata + AD-579b temporal validity + AD-605 enhanced embedding — the shared store()/metadata path) **69 passed**; `import probos.runtime` clean; `ast.parse(episodic.py + affect_scorer.py)` clean. STAGED (not committed).

**Deviation from spec (one token, gate-required).** STEP 3's literal `if self._affect_capture_enabled` was changed to `if getattr(self, "_affect_capture_enabled", False)`. The literal form raised `AttributeError` on the precedent's own `__new__`-based store tests (`test_ad598` Tests 8/9, `test_ad605` store test bypass `__init__` so never set the attr) — i.e. the literal STEP 3 text contradicted the spec's own Gate B requirement that `test_ad598` pass. The `getattr` form is the established `store()` idiom for every optional subsystem (`_storage_gate`, `_anomaly_window_manager`, `_tcm`, `_reconsolidation_scheduler`, `_retroactive_evolver`), preserves exact gating semantics (default `False` = no capture = byte-identical), and protects any other `__new__`-based store test. `__init__` still sets the attribute in production.

### AD-1038: live remember/know render — surface the agent's OWN AD-979f Tulving remember/know type into its response as a gap-safe metacognitive cue; render/gate-only, default-OFF, byte-identical when OFF (#987, Oracle recall epic #902)

**Context.** Highest AD heading observed at authoring: **AD-1034** (the Composable-Cognition spine; **AD-1038 is the number issue #987 carries** — the deferred *live-render* follow-on to AD-979f/#908, which shipped the `RecallConfidence.recall_type` classifier + the `remember_know_typing_enabled` gate but **never rendered the type into a live prompt**). AD-981b's DD-7 explicitly earmarked this as out of its scope ("no #987/AD-1038 remember/know render (no `recall_type` wiring)"). The classified type was therefore observable in tests but **dead on the live path** — an agent that *remembers* (strong + episodically grounded) and one that merely *knows* (familiarity without grounded specifics) spoke identically, so a "know" recall could be voiced with invented concrete detail. AD-1038 turns the existing type into an explicit, gap-safe cue in the agent's own answer.

**Decision.** Architect→Builder, contained to ONE file (`cognitive/cognitive_agent.py`) — **no `episodic.py` / ranking / classifier / consensus change**. It **reuses the AD-981b rail**: AD-981b's `_recall_confidence_band` probe is refactored into a thin band-only delegator over a new shared `async _recall_confidence_probe(self, *, query, mem_id, k=5) -> RecallConfidence | None` (the single `recall_for_agent_with_confidence` round-trip that already produces BOTH the AD-979a band AND the AD-979f `recall_type`). (1) A new gap-safe `@staticmethod _remember_know_note(recall_type)` (instructions-first cue for `remember`/`know`; `""` for `none`/`""`) + `_remember_know_segment(observation) -> list[str] | None` (the testable render-decision unit reading `observation["_recall_recall_type"]`). (2) The AD-981b probe call site in `_recall_relevant_memories` becomes a **combined-gate single probe**: it runs once when EITHER `recall_confidence_gating_enabled` OR `remember_know_typing_enabled` is on, independently stashing `observation["_recall_fok_band"]` and/or `observation["_recall_recall_type"]` (a both-on config costs one round-trip). (3) A render injection at **both** the DM and WR episodic sites in `_build_user_message`, as a sibling to the AD-981b `_emit("recall_confidence", …)`: `_rk_seg = self._remember_know_segment(observation); if _rk_seg: _emit("remember_know", _rk_seg)`. A `RecallConfidence` `TYPE_CHECKING` import was added for the probe's return annotation.
