Gate (bf632 + bf631 + bf630 + ad567b + ad981c) = 59 passed. Activates on next reboot. **Follow-up:** audit the ward_room / group-fanout recall query (the `_recall_relevant_memories` ward_room branch also reads `params["text"]`) for the same prepend contamination — likely the same root cause behind #900's patchy group recall. Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

### BF-631: filter "query-echo" recalls from per-message DM recall + recall observability (#974)

**Context.** After BF-630 fixed the keyword axis, a fresh-boot test STILL failed (Yeo: *"I don't have any memories that mention your dogs"*). An offline reproduction against a point-in-time COPY of the live store (read-only, no reboot) — with the agent's real ENHANCED-tier params (Yeo is LIEUTENANT→ENHANCED) and the exact `config.memory.recall_weights` — proved `recall_weighted` NOW returns the dog answer "Captain: My dog, Grim, is a giant snouser" (anchor_confidence 0.483, passes the 0.3 gate; owned by Yeo's sovereign id `d00cb0bd`, passes the shard filter). So the recall PLUMBING works. The failure is recall QUALITY: the answer ranks 4th of 5 because the top 3 slots are the Captain's OWN prior identical askings of "What do you know about my dogs?" — query-echoes that match the query text near-perfectly (cosine 0.527 vs the answer's 0.363) yet carry zero information for answering it. `_format_memory_section` renders ALL recalled episodes, so the answer DID reach the prompt, but buried under three copies of the question (and flagged `unverified`), the agent denied. **Decision.** Builder. New pure module-level `_filter_query_echoes(episodes, query) -> list` in `cognitive_agent.py`: drops episodes whose normalized (case/whitespace-insensitive) `user_input` contains the normalized current query verbatim — a near-certain echo, low false-positive risk. Substantive-query gate (>=12 normalized chars) and never-strip-to-empty (all-echo ⇒ keep originals; there is no answer to surface anyway). Called in `_recall_relevant_memories` right before the `if episodes:` render block (after the recall_weighted + AD-603 merge, so it filters the FINAL recalled set); logs `BF-631: dropped N query-echo recall(s)` when it fires. End-to-end offline validation against the live store: the rendered recalled set goes from `[echo, echo, echo, ANSWER, baseline]` to `[ANSWER, baseline]` — the answer becomes the TOP memory. Also adds a concise INFO recall-observability line (`BF-631 DM-recall: agent=… q=… n=… :: <summaries>`) for `direct_message`, since the system had no visibility into what per-message recall actually feeds the prompt (this investigation spanned three diagnoses while flying blind). **Tests.** `test_bf631_query_echo_filter.py` (7): the dog scenario (3 echoes dropped, answer+baseline kept), case/whitespace-insensitivity, all-echo→originals, short-query no-op, empty inputs, non-echo unaffected, no input mutation. Gate (bf631 + bf630 + ad567b + ad979c + ad981c) = 69 passed. Activates on next reboot. Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

### BF-630: keyword_search OR-expands natural-language queries before FTS5 MATCH — fixes the live 1:1 recall keyword axis (#974)

**Context.** AD-981c wired hybrid recall onto the SOVEREIGN `recall_for_agent_with_confidence`, but a fresh-boot gold-standard test still failed: after a clean restart (runtime confirmed on AD-981c code — process started 30 min AFTER the commit), Yeo still could not recall the Captain's two giant schnauzers (*"you haven't mentioned dogs to me"*). Live-log forensics were dispositive: the only recall that fired for the dogs DM was the session-SEEDING query `'1:1 conversation with Captain'` (generic, no dog tokens) via `agent_chat_history`; the per-message recall the 1:1 DM actually runs is `handle_intent` → `_run_cognitive_lifecycle` → `_recall_relevant_memories` → **`recall_weighted`** (ENHANCED tier) — NOT `recall_for_agent_with_confidence`, so AD-981c's hybrid never touched the live path. `recall_weighted` DOES have a keyword (FTS5) axis (AD-567b/c, BF-134) with a sovereign shard filter — but it called `keyword_search(query)` with the RAW Captain message. `keyword_search` passed that straight to FTS5 `MATCH`, where a conversational string is a *phrase* query and the trailing `?` is a hard `fts5: syntax error` (caught → returned `[]`). A read-only probe against the live `episode_fts.db` proved it: `MATCH 'What do you know about my dogs?'` → `syntax error near "?"`; the OR-expanded form `"what" OR … OR "dogs"` → 6 hits including *"[1:1 with yeoman] Captain: My dog, Grim, is a giant snouser"*. So the keyword axis was DEAD for every natural-language question; only the dense axis ran, and when it under-ranked the episodes the agent honestly reported no memory. The FTS index is `tokenize='porter unicode61'`, so `dogs`→`dog` stems and matches once the query is OR-expanded. **Decision.** Centralize the natural-language→FTS5 translation INSIDE `EpisodicMemory.keyword_search`: it now applies `fts_or_query(query)` (OR-of-quoted-tokens) before MATCH and returns `[]` when no usable tokens remain. This fixes ALL three NL callers at once — `recall_weighted` (the live DM path), the AD-603 anchor-merge (`keyword_search(semantic_query)`), and any future caller — instead of each site remembering to pre-expand (the DRY smell that caused this: 2 of 4 callers manually pre-expanded, 1 forgot, 1 was the bug). The two hybrid fusers (`_fuse_dense_sparse` AD-979c, `_fuse_dense_sparse_for_agent` AD-981c) drop their now-redundant local `fts_or_query` and pass the raw query — byte-identical net MATCH string. OR-of-keywords is a strict SUPERSET of the prior phrase/AND behaviour, so every episode the old path found is still found (proven: all AD-567b/c/d + AD-979c + AD-981c suites green unchanged). Activates on the next reboot with no config change (the seeding query stays generic by design, but the per-message `recall_weighted` keyword axis is now live). **Tests.** `test_bf630_keyword_search_nl.py` (6, BF-287 real `EpisodicMemory` + real ONNX MiniLM + real FTS5 sidecar): punctuated NL question surfaces the keyword-matched episode (the exact failing case); OR-superset multi-word match; single-word unaffected; stopword/empty → `[]`; `recall_weighted` end-to-end surfaces the dog episode for "What do you know about my dogs?" with the semantic axis blocked (`relevance_threshold=0.99`); and the sovereign shard guard (another agent's keyword match does not leak). Gate `test_bf630 + test_ad567b + test_ad567c + test_ad567d + test_ad979c + test_ad981c` = 116 passed. Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

### AD-981c: wire AD-979c hybrid retrieval onto the sovereign recall path — shard-aware (#974)

**Context.** AD-979c's dense+sparse Reciprocal-Rank-Fusion and AD-981a's agent-scoped Feeling-of-Knowing were built into the GLOBAL `recall_with_confidence`, but the crew's live per-message recall runs through the SOVEREIGN `recall_for_agent_with_confidence` (agent-scoped, AD-397 isolation), which ignored the already-enabled `hybrid_recall_enabled` flag and stayed dense-only. The proven incident: the Captain told Yeo (1:1) about two giant schnauzers; after a clean restart Yeo could not recall them (*"you haven't mentioned dogs to me"*) though the episodes ARE stored — read-only FTS proved it. Root cause: the dense/cosine sovereign axis under-ranked the dog episodes and the FTS5 sparse axis that catches the "dogs"→"schnauzer" vocabulary gap by keyword was wired only on the global path. `config/system.yaml:117` already had `hybrid_recall_enabled: true`. **Decision.** Builder. **DD-1 (no new flag):** gate the sovereign fusion on the SAME `self._hybrid_recall_enabled and self._fts_db is not None` condition the global path uses — `config.py` default stays `False` ⇒ byte-identical default installs; the Captain's `true` activates it on next reboot (the immediate fix). **DD-2 (sovereign-leak guard, load-bearing):** new `EpisodicMemory._fuse_dense_sparse_for_agent(agent_id, query, dense_episodes, k)` mirrors `_fuse_dense_sparse` (`fts_or_query` → `keyword_search` → `reciprocal_rank_fusion` over the owned dense ids + sparse ids → hydrate sparse-only ids via `get_by_ids`) but `keyword_search` runs over the GLOBAL FTS index and `get_by_ids` is not shard-scoped, so every fused episode is POST-FILTERED to ones the agent owns (`agent_id in episode.agent_ids`) **BEFORE** the k-cap (filter-then-cap, never cap-then-filter — capping first could drop an owned episode that sits below a non-owned keyword hit and silently under-return the agent's own memories). **DD-3 (FoK band stays dense):** the gated tail is appended to `recall_for_agent_with_confidence` AFTER the AD-981a FoK band/logging + activation-tracker blocks and BEFORE `return` (mirrors the global tail), so the agent-scoped band/`best_sim`/log line stay the DENSE distribution — hybrid changes WHICH owned episodes return, not the cosine confidence. Tier-2 honest-degrade: an empty/failed sparse axis returns the dense list unchanged (try/except mirroring `_fuse_dense_sparse`). The global `_fuse_dense_sparse` and `recall_with_confidence` are untouched (AD-979c byte-identical); `recall_for_agent` is still a byte-identical shim. **Tests.** `test_ad981c_sovereign_hybrid.py` (10, BF-287 real `EpisodicMemory` on `tmp_path` + real ONNX MiniLM + the real FTS5 sidecar — no MagicMock at the store boundary): the gate (an owned buried-keyword episode dense-sub-threshold at ~0.19 < 0.25 is surfaced ON, absent OFF) + the mandatory SOVEREIGN-LEAK guard (a counselor-owned keyword match is NOT in the yeoman's hybrid recall while the counselor still recalls its own) + FoK band/`best_sim`/`candidate_count` unchanged by fusion (returned `RecallConfidence` and the logged AD-981a line) + default-off byte-identical (shim == core, keyword-only episode excluded ⇒ pure dense) + honest-degrade (raised/empty/no-usable-token sparse → dense unchanged). Focused gate `test_ad981c + test_ad979c + test_ad981a` 36 passed; recall/sovereign/episodic blast green; AD-979c + AD-981a suites unchanged. Forward: AD-981b (FoK-band-gated consult on the sovereign path) still earmarked. Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

**Context.** The OSS↔commercial overlay infra (AD-697/698) is live but a *sentinel* — flipping `probos-mode.ps1 oss↔overlay` flips `is_commercial_loaded()` but nothing visible changes. HXI `ui/src/components/workstation/WorkstationLauncher.tsx` (deps-injectable, stroke-SVG, no emoji): fetches the catalog, renders a `native` type via an OSS component map (honest-degrades to a "not yet available" placeholder — monaco/browser/chat React land in AD-1021 et al.), and an `iframe` type through the already-built sandboxed `McpAppFrame` (AD-597a, `external=true`) — the OSS bundle never imports commercial React. Layer discipline: the registry imports no `execution`/commercial symbol; the launcher is not mounted into a container this AD (AD-1023). Default-OFF ⇒ API dormant + surface hidden ⇒ **byte-identical**. **Tests.** `test_ad1022_workstation_registry.py` (22, real registry + real `SystemConfig` + the real AD-697 `reset_for_tests()`/`run_finalize_hooks` seam — no MagicMock at the overlay boundary): register/resolve/`list_available` incl. tiered resolution (commercial wins iff loaded) + availability gating + same-id dedupe; the handler dormant-when-disabled / OSS-only / commercial-appears / **render-target-never-serialized**; the **mode-toggle proof** (demo absent in OSS mode, present in overlay mode) via a real finalize-hook registration; default-OFF; `_wire_workstation_types` dormant-vs-enabled. `WorkstationLauncher.test.tsx` (8, deps-injected): list/empty/loading, native placeholder vs registered-component, iframe→sandboxed frame (`external`, `resourceUri=id`), error honest-degrade, no-emoji. `-k "workstation or ad1022 or ad697 or extensions"` = 139 passed; `npm run build` clean. The commercial demo registration ships as a separate commit in the private commercial overlay repo (`probos_enterprise`).

No backend file touched.

### AD-1019: per-agent + per-tool MCP enablement — authorization + enumeration substrate (#960, epic #955)

**Context.** AD-1015 shipped the MCP server CRUD store + API, AD-1017 made auth live, and AD-1018 added the HXI management panel — but there was no way to say *which agents* may use a server, let alone *which tools* on it. This AD adds the per-agent + per-tool enablement substrate. Like `IntentGrantStore` was built before enforcement, this is the **authorization + enumeration** layer: MCP tools are not yet agent-callable, so the actual tool-call gating (MCP-tool INVOCATION wiring into the agent tool-call path) is a separate follow-up **AD-1019b**; the HXI surface is **AD-1019a**. **Decision.** Architect→Builder. **Reuse the audited `ToolPermissionStore` (AD-423b/AD-894) — no new grant store** — with **composite tool ids**: server-level `mcp:{name}` (all tools) and tool-level `mcp:{name}:{tool}` (one tool). New pure `integrations/mcp_bridge/access.py` `resolve_mcp_access(grants, server_name, tool_name) -> (enabled, source)` folds an agent's active grants into a decision with `source ∈ {tool, server, default}`; precedence is **tool-level overrides server-level, restriction beats grant at the same level**: tool-restriction → tool-grant → server-restriction → server-grant → `(False, "default")` (MCP is **opt-in per agent**). Matching is exact composite-id equality (kebab-case server names carry no colons, so the two id shapes never collide); an empty `tool_name` folds to the server/default branches only (the router computes `server_enabled` that way). Pure, no I/O — exhaustively unit-testable. `routers/mcp_servers.py` adds four endpoints, all gated on `config.mcp.management_enabled` (404 `feature_disabled` when off → existing paths byte-identical) and honest-degrade on every axis (never 500): `GET /{id}/tools` (resolve record → `bridge.get_client(_bridge_key(record))` → `await client.list_tools()` → `{tools:[{name,description}],count}`; an unregistered/disabled row or a connection failure → `{tools:[],count:0,error}` via the never-raising `_enumerate_tools` helper); `GET /{id}/agents/{agent_id}/access` (enumerate tools + `perms.get_active_grants_sync(agent_id)` → `{server_enabled, tools:[{name,enabled,source}]}` via `resolve_mcp_access`; no perm store → every tool resolves `default`); `POST /{id}/agents/{agent_id}` body `{enabled, tool?}` → composite `tool_id` → `perms.issue_grant(agent_id, tool_id, permission=WRITE if enabled else NONE, is_restriction=not enabled, reason="mcp enablement")`, **503 if no perm store**, returns the grant id; `DELETE /{id}/agents/{agent_id}?tool=` → `get_active_grants_sync(agent_id, tool_id)` → `revoke_grant` each → `{revoked:n}`. `ToolPermission` imported from `probos.tools.protocol`; `runtime.tool_permission_store` read via `getattr` (honest-degrade). **No new store, no secrets, AD-894/AD-1015/AD-1017 behavior unchanged.** Tests: `test_ad1019_mcp_enablement.py` (24, BF-287 real `McpServerStore` + real `ToolPermissionStore` + real `MCPBridge` `stdio_enabled=True` + AD-1014 echo fixture + real `TestClient` as a context manager so the spawned echo subprocess spans the register→enumerate requests, deleted in `finally`): all 9 `resolve_mcp_access` branches; `GET /tools` enumerates echo's three tools + honest-degrade `{tools:[],error}` when not registered; `POST` server-level → `GET /access` all enabled source `server`; tool-level disable → that tool `enabled:false` source `tool`, siblings still `server`; `DELETE` reverts to `default`; composite-id grants recorded in the real `ToolPermissionStore` (asserted via `get_active_grants_sync`); no perm store → 503; `management_enabled=False` ⇒ the four endpoints 404. Parity `-k "mcp or ad1015 or ad1017 or permission or ad894"` 343 passed (319 **unchanged** + 24). Scope: no HXI (AD-1019a), no MCP-tool invocation wiring (AD-1019b), no new grant store, no secrets.

### AD-1018: HXI MCP Servers management panel (#959, epic #955)

**Context.** AD-1015 shipped the MCP server CRUD store + API and AD-1017 made auth live (static tokens + OAuth), but the only operator surface was the **read-only** Ship's Locker MCP list. This AD adds the **HXI management panel** — the operator-facing surface to add/edit/remove/enable/disable MCP servers, test the connection, and configure auth — consuming the AD-1015/AD-1017 endpoints **as-is** (UI only, no backend changes). **Decision.** Architect→Builder. New `ui/src/components/mcp/McpServersPanel.tsx` mirrors `ShipsLockerPanel` (zustand `useStore` open-flag `mcpServersOpen`, rendered **unconditionally** in `App.tsx` alongside `<ShipsLockerPanel />`, returns `null` when closed; deps-injectable `_fn = deps?.x ?? apiX`; honest-degrade; Escape-to-close) + `RolePicker` (typed interfaces, stroke-only chrome, amber `#f0b060`/dim `#666680`, **no emoji**, `data-testid` on every interactive element). Surface: a **list** (name, http/stdio type badge, url/command summary, enabled toggle → enable/disable, `auth_kind` badge, Test button rendering `OK · N tools`/`FAILED` as **text**, not emoji); a **create/edit form** (type selector → http url+headers-rows / stdio command+args+env-rows+cwd; name; timeout; client validation mirroring the backend `validate_record` — kebab `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` name, http⇒url, stdio⇒command; **no secret inputs**); a **credential modal** (radio static|oauth; static → **write-only** password token + header_name/scheme [+ env_var for stdio] → `putCredential`; oauth → non-secret client config + **write-only** client_secret → a `Connect` button → `startOAuth` → `window.open(auth_url)` + a `window` `message` listener for `{type:'oauth_complete'}` → refresh, plus a `Refresh token` → `refreshOAuth`, and a `Remove credential` → `deleteCredential`); **delete-with-inline-confirm** → `deleteServer`; and a **stdio trust note** "Runs a local command on this machine" (Copilot trust-dialog ethos; the AD-1014 HookBus is the enforcement). **Secrets discipline (HARD):** no token/secret value is ever rendered back — the token / client_secret inputs are write-only (cleared after save, never echoed); the panel shows only an `auth_kind` badge + the non-secret config thereafter (the backend `to_public_dict` never emits a secret). **Honest-degrade:** `GET` 404 (`feature_disabled`) → "MCP management is disabled"; a fetch rejection → error state (mirrors ShipsLockerPanel). The 10 injectable deps (`fetchServers`/`createServer`/`updateServer`/`deleteServer`/`setEnabled`/`testServer`/`putCredential`/`deleteCredential`/`startOAuth`/`refreshOAuth`) each default to a real `fetch` so the Vitest suite injects `vi.fn()` (no real network). **Scope:** no backend changes, no per-agent/per-tool grants (AD-1019), no device-code UI. **Tests.** `McpServersPanel.test.tsx` (20): list/empty/disabled(404)/error states; create http + stdio with the exact shape; client validation blocks a non-kebab name + a urlless http server (deps **not** called); edit (PUT)/delete(confirm-step)/enable-disable call the right deps; test-connection `OK · N tools` + `FAILED — …`; static credential → `putCredential` called with the token **and the token is absent from the DOM after save** (`queryByDisplayValue` null + `document.body.textContent` excludes it); oauth → `startOAuth` + mocked `window.open`; no `input[type=password]` in the list view; no-emoji guard. `paletteCommands.test.ts` updated (12→13 Captain-facing launches; the new Engineering `MCP Servers` action). `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) clean; bridge+personnel regression 90 passed. Default-off backend ⇒ the panel shows the disabled note.

### AD-1017: MCP server authentication — static tokens + OAuth authorization-code (#958, epic #955)

**Context.** AD-1015 shipped the MCP server registration store with `auth_kind` (none|static|oauth) + `credential_ref` as **inert** strings, and AD-1016 added the keychain credential backend; this AD makes auth **live** — resolve a server's stored credential and inject it at register time, with **secrets only in the credential vault by ref, never in the store row, never in any API response, never logged.** **Decision.** Architect→Builder. New `integrations/mcp_bridge/mcp_oauth.py` `McpOAuthProvider` modeled on the AD-720c `CloudPickerProvider` (reuses `OAuthTokenBundle` by **import only** — cloud-picker code untouched), parameterized by the record's non-secret `oauth_json` (client_id/authorize_url/token_url/scopes/redirect_uri) + the vault-stored `client_secret`: `start_authorization(*,state)→url`, `async handle_callback(*,code)→OAuthTokenBundle` (httpx POST `grant_type=authorization_code`), `async refresh(*,refresh_token)→OAuthTokenBundle` (`grant_type=refresh_token`); a self-contained `McpOAuthError` (no coupling to the cloud-picker error taxonomy); **token values are never logged** (failures log only status code / exception type, never the response body). `store.py` `McpServerRecord` gains four **non-secret** fields — `auth_header_name`("Authorization")/`auth_scheme`("Bearer")/`auth_env_var`("")/`oauth_json`("") — added to the schema, `to_public_dict`, `_row_to_record`/`create`/`update`/`_record_to_params` round-trip, and a migration-safe `_migrate_ad1017()` (`ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` with defaults, `sqlite3.OperationalError` swallowed when already present); the four columns are appended **after** `created_at`/`updated_at` in the `CREATE TABLE` so a fresh DB and an `ALTER`-migrated AD-1015 DB share identical positional column order (the positional `_row_to_record` indices stay valid). `validate_record`'s secret-key denylist is unchanged — it still refuses credential-bearing header/env *values*. `routers/mcp_servers.py` adds `_resolve_auth_headers`/`_resolve_auth_env` (+ a shared `_resolve_secret_value` vault read; `none`/vault-miss → `{}` + warning, honest-degrade) merged into a runtime-aware `_register` (http `headers={**record.headers, **auth}`, stdio `env={**record.env, auth_env_var:value}`) — `auth_kind=="none"` resolves to `{}` so register is **byte-identical to AD-1015**. New endpoints (all gated on `management_enabled`, 404 when off): `POST/DELETE /{id}/credential` (static — store/delete the token in the vault by ref `mcp:{id}`, persist non-secret header/scheme/env-var, re-register; 503 when no vault); `POST /{id}/auth/start` (persist `oauth_json` + vault the `client_secret` under `mcp:{id}:oauth_secret`, mint CSRF state via a lazy per-runtime `_get_state_store` mirroring `cloud_pickers.py:59` + `_clear_state_stores()` test hook, return `{auth_url,state}`); `GET /{id}/auth/callback?code=&state=` (consume state → 403 on invalid, exchange, store the bundle under `mcp:{id}:oauth`, flip `auth_kind="oauth"`, return the **same popup-close HTML** as the cloud-picker callback); `POST /{id}/auth/refresh` (reactive — read bundle, `provider.refresh`, re-store, re-register; 400 when no refresh_token). **Scope (named, not built):** device-code → AD-1017a; HXI → AD-1018; per-agent grants → AD-1019. **No secret ever reaches the store row / a response body / logs.** **Tests.** `test_ad1017_mcp_auth.py` (38, BF-287 real `McpServerStore` + real `EncryptedFileCredentialVault` on tmp_path + real `MCPBridge` + real `TestClient`; only the external httpx token exchange is `MockTransport`-mocked): static store/resolve/inject/custom-header/bare-scheme/delete-purges-vault/503-no-vault/404; **token never in row/response (asserted), never in logs (caplog asserted)**; OAuth start→callback→resolve-Bearer/invalid-state-403/exchange-502/refresh-restores/no-refresh-400/token-never-in-response; `auth_kind=="none"` byte-identical; gate-off ⇒ all 404; provider unit tests (authcode/refresh/non-200/no-access-token/transport-error); store migration reads a pre-AD-1017 row with column defaults + fresh-DB round-trip of the four fields. New 38 green; parity `-k "mcp or ad449 or ad597 or ad1015 or credential or cloud_picker"` **384 passed** (346 **unchanged** + 38). Default `auth_kind="none"` ⇒ byte-identical.

### AD-1017a: MCP OAuth device-code (RFC 8628) (epic #955)

**Context.** AD-1017 shipped MCP server auth (static tokens + OAuth authorization-code) but its ship note named **device-code "not built — AD-1017a"**: the authorization-code grant requires a browser redirect, so it cannot complete on a **headless** host (a common ProbOS deployment). RFC 8628 (the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant) is the only flow that authenticates without a local browser — the user approves on a *second* device against a short `user_code` while the host polls. This AD adds it; **current highest landed top-level = AD-1052, so AD-1017a is a sub-AD (no new top-level).** **Decision.** Architect→Builder. `McpOAuthProvider` (`mcp_oauth.py`) gains a `device_authorization_url` ctor kwarg + two methods: `async start_device_authorization() -> dict` (POST `client_id`/`scope` [+`client_secret` when set] to the device endpoint; returns the provider payload carrying `device_code`/`user_code`/`verification_uri`; raises `McpOAuthError` on transport/non-200/missing-field) and `async poll_device_token(*, device_code) -> OAuthTokenBundle | None`. `routers/mcp_servers.py` gains a per-runtime `_DEVICE_FLOWS` map (mirrors `_STATE_STORES`), `DeviceStartBody`/`DevicePollBody`, `_merge_device_oauth_config`, the `device_authorization_url` wiring in `_build_oauth_provider`, and two endpoints: `POST /{id}/auth/device/start` (vault the `client_secret`, persist the non-secret device config, start the grant, hand back an opaque `flow_id` + the user-facing fields) and `POST /{id}/auth/device/poll` (resolve `flow_id` → held `device_code` → poll → `{status:pending}` | persist+`{status:authenticated}` | terminal error). **DD-1** no config change — the device + token URLs live in the per-server **non-secret** `oauth_json`, so `config/system.yaml`/`MCPConfig` are untouched. **DD-2** the `device_code` is a poll **secret** held SERVER-SIDE in `_DEVICE_FLOWS` keyed by `id(runtime)`; the client receives only an opaque `flow_id` — `device_code` is never in any response body. **DD-3** RFC 8628 returns HTTP **400** for `authorization_pending`/`slow_down` — *non-terminal* "keep polling" signals — so `poll_device_token` does **NOT** reuse `_token_post` (which raises on every non-200): it returns `None` for pending and raises `McpOAuthError(status=400)` only on a terminal error (`access_denied`/`expired_token`/`invalid_grant`/transport, or an unparsable error body → terminal). **DD-4** poll-success persistence is **identical** to the auth-code callback — vault `_oauth_ref(id)` + `store.update(auth_kind="oauth", credential_ref=ref)` + `_reregister` — so `/auth/refresh` + Bearer resolution work on a device-obtained bundle. **DD-5** honest-degrade / default-OFF — both endpoints 404 `feature_disabled` when `management_enabled` is off (byte-identical when off), 503 when no vault, 404 on unknown server/flow. **DD-6** secrets discipline — `client_secret` + token values never in any response/store-row/log; response bodies are never logged (only status codes). **Scope.** Backend-only (mirrors the AD-1017 backend → AD-1018 UI split); the HXI device-code modal is **AD-1018a**. **Tests.** `test_ad1017a_mcp_device_code.py` (BF-287 real `McpServerStore` + `EncryptedFileCredentialVault` + `MCPBridge` + `TestClient`; only the external httpx via `httpx.MockTransport`) — provider start/poll happy + pending/slow_down→None + terminal→raise + the router start/poll/security (`device_code`/token never in any response or log). Staged for review, not committed.

### AD-1018a — MCP OAuth device-code HXI modal (epic #955)

**Context.** AD-1017a shipped the headless device-code (RFC 8628) backend — two provider methods + `POST /{id}/auth/device/start` and `POST /{id}/auth/device/poll` — but had **no operator surface**: the AD-1018 credential modal only offered static-token + OAuth authorization-code (the browser-redirect flow that cannot complete on a headless host). This AD adds the HXI for device-code, completing the last slice of epic #955. **UI-only — no `src/probos/**`, no `config/system.yaml`, no new npm dependency** (mirrors the AD-1017 backend → AD-1018 UI split). **Current highest landed top-level = AD-1052, so AD-1018a is a sub-AD (no new top-level).** **Decision.** Builder, additive over `McpServersPanel.tsx`. The `CredentialModal` `kind` radio widens from `'static'|'oauth'` to a third `'device'` (the static + auth-code flows are **byte-identical** / unchanged; the `kind` ternary becomes an explicit 3-way so each section is mutually exclusive). New `DeviceStartInput`/`DeviceStartResult`/`DevicePollResult` types + `startDeviceAuthApi`/`pollDeviceAuthApi` same-origin fetchers (terminal failures — 404 `unknown_flow`/`access_denied`/expired — throw; a 200 carries `{status: pending|authenticated}`); these + an injectable `schedulePoll` extend `McpDeps`. **DD-2 (poll discipline):** the poll loop runs in a `useEffect` that schedules on the server-provided `interval` via the **injectable `schedulePoll`** (default `setTimeout`, returns a cancel fn); exactly one timer is live at a time, the effect cleanup cancels the latest timer under a `stopped` guard (no leaked timers, no setState-after-unmount), and a `deadline` from `expires_in` stops a stale grant. **DD-3 (write-only secret):** `client_secret` is sent once to `/device/start` then immediately `setClientSecret('')` — never retained, never rendered (a write-only password input). **DD (device_code never in the browser):** the modal holds only the opaque `flow_id` + display fields (`user_code`, `verification_uri[_complete]`); the `device_code` poll secret stays server-side (AD-1017a). **Honest-degrade:** the panel already 404→degrades when `management_enabled` is off; a terminal poll error stops polling and re-enables Connect as **Retry**. **HXI:** stroke-SVG (no emoji), amber/dim palette, a `data-testid` on every interactive element, reusing the existing `IconClose`/`fieldStyle`/`labelStyle`/`btnStyle`/`_AMBER`/`_DIM`/`_RED` helpers. **Tests.** `McpServersPanel.test.tsx` +6 (via `makeDeps` + a `makeSchedule` capture-scheduler — **no real timers, no real network**): switches to the device section (OAuth Connect gone), starts a flow + renders `user_code`/verification link/waiting, polls pending→authenticated then closes + reloads (`pollDeviceAuth` ≥2×), terminal error re-enables Connect, cleanup cancels the timer on close, and the `client_secret` is never retained after start. Focused 22→28 green; full UI 1674→1680 passed (1 skipped, 0 fail); `npm run build` (tsc -b + vite) clean. **Epic #955 is now fully built (closeable).**

### AD-1021b — Monaco workstation write-through (epic #965)

**Context.** AD-1021 shipped the code/text Workstation as a *viewer* (build proposals + scratch) and named write-through / save-to-artifact as deferred. This AD adds the **governed write-through**: a host that passes an `agentId` can Load a file from that agent's AD-997 workspace folder into the editor and Save it back through consensus. **Current highest landed top-level = AD-1052, so AD-1021b is a sub-AD (no new top-level).** **Decision.** Architect→Builder, additive. **Read** `GET /api/agent/{id}/workspace/file?path=` mirrors the AD-998 gate (`enabled` ∧ `persistent_workspaces` ∧ `workspace_root`) and honest-degrades to `found:false` (off / ephemeral / absent / over-cap), decoding UTF-8 with `errors="replace"`. **Write** `POST /api/agent/{id}/workspace/file` (`WorkspaceFileWriteRequest{path,content}`) is gated by a **new default-OFF master switch `ExecutionConfig.workspace_write_enabled` (=False)** — a switch SEPARATE from `enabled` so editing a consensus-gated workspace text file does not require opting into arbitrary code execution; `503` when the switch is off or the folder is ephemeral/unrooted, `413` over the 1 MiB `_MAX_WRITE_BYTES` cap. **Governance:** the write is NEVER performed in the router — it routes ONLY through `runtime.submit_write_with_consensus(path=str(target), content=...)` (the CONSENSUS-tier governed write: `FileWriterAgent` proposes, quorum + red-team gate the commit). **DD-3 (dual-layer path confinement):** `WorkspaceManager.resolve_file(owner, rel, *, create_parents=False)` confines via `resolve() + is_relative_to(base.resolve())` (symlink-escape-safe; `None` on empty/absolute/NUL/traversal/the-folder-itself), AND the API endpoint rejects `resolve_file→None` with `400` **before** governance — so a traversal returns 400 and `submit_write_with_consensus` is never called (asserted). **Consensus is synchronous + terminal — there is NO PENDING outcome:** the response is `{outcome:"committed"}` or `{outcome:"refused", consensus_outcome, approval_ratio}` (a governance exception honest-degrades to `refused`/`consensus_outcome:"error"`, never 500); the UI "pending" surface is only the in-flight await ("Saving — awaiting consensus…") resolving to committed/refused. **UI:** `CodeWorkstation` gains **optional** `agentId`/`loadFile`/`saveFile` props (so it stays assignable to `ComponentType<NativeWorkstationProps>` in `nativeWorkstations.ts`); the path input + Load/Save (stroke-SVG, `data-testid`) + the `workstation-save-status` banner (committed/refused/disabled/in-flight) render ONLY when `agentId` is present — the AD-1021 scratch/prop-doc experience is **byte-identical** when `agentId` is absent. `loadFile`/`saveFile` default to same-origin, no-token `workspaceFileApi` helpers (503→`{outcome:'disabled'}` honest-degrade); **no token in browser JS**. **Lands dark:** the default host (`WorkstationPanel`) passes no `agentId`, so the feature is reachable only once a host wires it (the AD-1023 container or a follow-on) AND the operator flips `workspace_write_enabled`. **No `config/system.yaml` change** (the new Pydantic default ships dark). **Tests.** `tests/test_ad1021b_workspace_write.py` (12, BF-287 real `ExecutionConfig` + real `WorkspaceManager` on tmp_path; `submit_write_with_consensus` mocked at the runtime boundary — read found/missing/disabled, read traversal+absolute 400, write 503-when-off, write traversal 400 ∧ submit NOT called, committed-routes-with-confined-abs-path, refused→`rejected`, governance-exception→refused-never-500, >1 MiB 413, `resolve_file` confinement unit) + `ui/.../CodeWorkstation.test.tsx` (7 — no-agentId byte-identical scratch, Load seeds editor, Save committed, Save refused→"refused: rejected", Save disabled, Load not-found, no-emoji). **Remaining before #965 closes:** AD-1021c (agent co-editing).

### AD-1021c — Agent co-editing / presence in the Monaco workstation (epic #965)

**Context.** AD-1021 shipped the code/text Workstation as a viewer; AD-1021b added the governed Load/Save against an agent's AD-997 workspace folder. AD-1021c adds the **agent co-editing / presence** surface — the last child of epic #965, which is now **FULLY BUILT (closeable)**. **Current highest landed top-level = AD-1052, so AD-1021c is a sub-AD (no new top-level).** **Decision.** Architect→Builder, additive, **reuse-not-rebuild**: presence reuses the **AD-930** ambient slices (`store.presence` + `store.agents`) and `PresenceDot`; Accept reuses the **AD-1021b governed write** (`saveWorkspaceFile` → `POST /workspace/file` → `runtime.submit_write_with_consensus`). **NOT an IDE:** NO CRDT, NO operational transform, NO websocket, NO live char-by-char co-editing, NO multi-cursor — a crew agent proposes a FULL replacement body for one file, and the human Previews / Accepts / Dismisses it in **discrete governed actions**. **Substrate.** A thin additive `execution/workspace_suggestions.py`: a frozen `WorkspaceSuggestion{id,owner,path,content,author_id,author_callsign,note,created_at}` + an in-memory `WorkspaceSuggestionStore` (`add`/`list`/`dismiss`/`clear`, per-`(owner,path)` bound default 50 oldest-evict, honest-degrading, volatile by design — a restart clears pending proposals). Attached **EXPLICITLY** on the runtime (`self.workspace_suggestions = WorkspaceSuggestionStore()` near the chat-thread-store attach) — NOT a `getattr` lazy-create, so the endpoints rely on a real store at any phase and the tests bind a real instance (BF-287; a MagicMock runtime would auto-fake `.add`). **Endpoints (3, under `/api/agent/{id}`)** mirror the AD-1021b read/write asymmetry but gate the **WHOLE surface on the EXISTING `ExecutionConfig.workspace_write_enabled`** (NO new config field, NO double-gate — the same switch that governs Accept's write governs proposing/viewing): `GET /workspace/suggestions?path=` honest-degrades to `[]` when off/ephemeral/unrooted (400 on traversal); `POST /workspace/suggestions` is `503` when off → `413` over the 1 MiB `_MAX_WRITE_BYTES` cap → `400` traversal **before** the store (a traversal is never queued — asserted via a `wraps` spy on `add`) → else `store.add`; `POST /workspace/suggestions/{sid}/dismiss` is `503` when off → else `store.dismiss → {dismissed:bool}` (a stale dismiss is a no-op `false`, not a 404). Path confinement reuses `WorkspaceManager.resolve_file` at the boundary BEFORE the store on every path-bearing route. **Governance:** agents never silently write — Accept routes the suggestion's full content through the AD-1021b consensus write (`committed`→drop, `refused`/`disabled`→keep + banner), Dismiss drops it; Preview loads it into the scratch editor (`onPreview→setScratch`) — human-in-control throughout. **UI:** new `CoEditPanel.tsx` (deps-injectable: `presence`/`agentsById` props + injectable `listSuggestions`/`dismissSuggestion`/`saveFile`) renders a presence strip (`present` = owner ∪ distinct suggestion authors, each a `PresenceDot`) + the suggestions list with Preview/Accept/Dismiss; new same-origin `workspaceSuggestionsApi.ts` (list/post/dismiss, honest-degrade, **no token in browser JS**). `CodeWorkstation` reads the AD-930 store slices, hydrates presence via `fetchPresence`, and renders `<CoEditPanel>` **ONLY when `agentId` is present** → **byte-identical to AD-1021/1021b when absent** (asserted: `workstation-presence-strip` null with no `agentId`). **HXI:** stroke-SVG glyphs (no emoji), `data-testid` on every interactive element, honest-degrade empties. **No `config/system.yaml` change, no new npm dep.** **Lands dark** (no default host passes `agentId`; the flag is OFF). **Tests.** `tests/test_ad1021c_workspace_suggestions.py` (12: list off→`[]` / on→items / traversal-400; post 503-off / traversal-400-store-untouched / 413-store-untouched / adds-when-on; dismiss 503-off / removes-true / missing-false; store bound-eviction + add/list/dismiss/clear unit — BF-287 real `ExecutionConfig` + real `WorkspaceManager` + real `WorkspaceSuggestionStore`, `wraps` spies prove "traversal never enters the store") + `ui/.../CoEditPanel.test.tsx` (10: present dedup, list, blank-path no-fetch, Preview→onPreview, Accept committed-drop / refused-keep / disabled-keep, Dismiss-drop, list-throw honest-degrade, no-emoji) + `CodeWorkstation.test.tsx` (+2 byte-identical: strip null without `agentId`, strip present with it).

### AD-1016: Credential backend abstraction — OS keychain backend (#957, epic #955)

**Context.** The credential layer (AD-706f) had a single backend: `EncryptedFileCredentialVault` (Fernet over a JSON sidecar, KEK derived from `auth.crew_scope_token`). The MCP management UX epic (#955) needs secrets to optionally live in the **OS keychain** (Windows DPAPI / macOS Keychain / Linux libsecret) instead of an app-managed encrypted file — operator-selectable. Consumers (`cloud_pickers.read`, `actions.materialize_to_temp`) already depend only on the `CredentialVault` Protocol, so a second backend is a drop-in. AD-1015's `McpServerStore.credential_ref`/`auth_kind` resolve against this layer (AD-1017 wires them). **Decision.** Architect→Builder. New `security/keyring_backend.py` `KeyringCredentialBackend` implements the `CredentialVault` Protocol **exactly** (5 async, keyword-only methods; `inspect.signature`-equal to `EncryptedFileCredentialVault` — verified structurally substitutable). Secret *values* live only in the OS keychain via the AD-754 `CredentialEncryptor` (`keyring`); the OS keychain is a `service+username→value` KV store with **no list and no metadata**, so the backend keeps a **non-secret metadata sidecar** (JSON `{"refs": {ref: {scope, created_at, last_read_at, read_count}}}` — **values NEVER in the sidecar**) with the file-vault's atomic tmp+rename write + `threading.RLock`. `keyring` is synchronous → every keyring call is wrapped in `await asyncio.to_thread(...)`; `store` writes the keyring **first** (so a failed write leaves no orphan metadata) and raises a clear `RuntimeError` on keyring failure; `read`/`delete`/`list_refs` honest-degrade (None/[]) on `NoKeyringError`/any keyring error and never crash the runtime. **Crew-token gating (RESOLVED):** the keychain is already encrypted at rest by the OS and the sidecar holds no secrets, so the keychain backend requires `enabled=True` but **not** `crew_scope_token` (the file vault still requires the token for its KEK). `config.py` `CredentialVaultConfig`: `backend` description → `"file" (default) | "keychain"` + a `@field_validator("backend")` rejecting other values, plus `keyring_index_path="data/credential_keyring_index.json"` and `keyring_service_name="probos.credentials"`. `finalize.py` (AD-706f block) switches on `vault_cfg.backend`: `"file"`/unset → today's `EncryptedFileCredentialVault` path **unchanged** (needs `enabled`+token); `"keychain"` → `KeyringCredentialBackend(service_name, index_path)` when `enabled` (token optional); both honest-degrade to None. **Scope discipline:** no MCP auth/OAuth wiring (AD-1017), no HXI (AD-1018), no per-agent grants (AD-1019); the Protocol surface, `EncryptedFileCredentialVault` behavior/wire format, `credential_encryption.py`, `cloud_pickers.py`, and `actions.py` are untouched. Default `backend="file"` ⇒ the keychain branch is skipped, file-vault construction + warning run exactly as before ⇒ **byte-identical**. **No secret value can reach the sidecar** (values flow only to the keychain; the sidecar stores scope/timestamps/count only). **Tests.** `test_ad1016_keyring_backend.py` (22, BF-287 — real dict-backed fake of `keyring.set/get/delete_password`, sidecar on `tmp_path`, NOT MagicMock): Protocol-signature parity vs `EncryptedFileCredentialVault` (5 methods, `inspect.signature`-equal + `iscoroutinefunction`), store→read, wrong-agent/expired/unknown scope→None, delete removes value **and** sidecar entry, list_refs metadata-only, read bumps read_count+last_read_at, **secret never in the on-disk index JSON** (`test_secret_value_never_in_sidecar`), materialize_to_temp writes the value (0600 best-effort), honest-degrade (keyring `get` raises → read None, list_refs still works), store raises a clear `RuntimeError` + no orphan metadata when keyring `set` raises, config `backend` default `file`/accepts `keychain`/rejects `bogus`/keyring defaults. Gate `-k "credential or vault or 706f or 754 or config"` **645 passed** (623 prior **unchanged** + 22). Tree left uncommitted (Builder hand-off).



**Context.** MCP servers were **static config + read-only** (`config.mcp.servers` registered once at boot via AD-449/AD-1014). The MCP management UX epic (#955) needs a **persisted, runtime-mutable registration store** + an HTTP CRUD surface so an operator can add/edit/remove/enable/disable servers without an edit-config-and-restart cycle. This AD is that foundation; the rest of the epic (credentials AD-1016, OAuth AD-1017, HXI AD-1018, per-agent grants AD-1019) builds on it. **Decision.** Architect→Builder workflow. New `integrations/mcp_bridge/store.py` `McpServerStore` mirrors `IntentGrantStore` exactly (`ConnectionFactory` + WAL/`busy_timeout`/`synchronous` PRAGMAs + in-memory `_cache` for sync reads + `db_path=""` cache-only for tests), with a frozen `McpServerRecord` + `to_public_dict()` (the **single serialization seam — never emits a secret**) and async `create`/`get`/`list`/`update`/`delete`/`set_enabled` + `list_sync`; `name` is the UNIQUE axis (dup → `ValueError`). A pure `validate_record(record, *, command_allowlist)` is the first gate: `http⇒url`, `stdio⇒command ∈ allowlist`, kebab-case `name`, and a **structural secret-key denylist** — a *non-empty* value on a known credential-bearing header key (`authorization`, `x-api-key`, `cookie`, …) or env key (`endswith {_token,_key,_secret,_password,_apikey,_api_key}` / exact `{token,secret,password,apikey,api_key}`) is refused with `secret_value_not_allowed` pointing the operator at `auth_kind`+`credential_ref` (AD-1016 resolves credentials at registration); empty values and all non-secret pairs pass through. New `routers/mcp_servers.py` (prefix `/api/mcp/servers`) is included **unconditionally** but gated per-endpoint on a new `MCPConfig.management_enabled=False` (404 `feature_disabled` when off → existing paths byte-identical): `GET ""`/`POST ""`(201, 400 on validation, 409 on dup name)/`GET {id}`/`PUT {id}` (re-register on a connection-affecting change)/`DELETE {id}` (best-effort unregister + delete; AD-1016 credential-cleanup TODO left)/`POST {id}/enable`+`/disable` (toggle registration, keep the row)/`POST {id}/test` (transient client, `initialize()`+`list_tools()`, **closed in `finally`** — no leaked subprocess; `{ok,tool_count}` or `{ok:false,error}` at HTTP 200, honest-degrade). Single bridge-key rule `key = url if type=="http" else name`; the http register path is **sync** (`register_server`), the stdio register/unregister paths are **async**. The **only** `bridge.py` change is a new `async unregister_server(key)` (pop + `await client.close()`, mirroring `close_all`). `finalize.py` builds the store inside `if config.mcp.enabled:` when `management_enabled`, direct-assigns `runtime.mcp_server_store`, and seeds each **enabled** stored row **after** the config-server loops — config wins (the bridge returns `False` on a duplicate key, so the seed never double-registers); a fresh DB has an empty cache ⇒ no-op ⇒ byte-identical boot. `shutdown.py` teardown mirrors `intent_grant_store`. `credential_ref`/`auth_kind` are **inert stored strings** this AD. **Scope discipline:** no HXI (AD-1018), no credential storage/reads (AD-1016), no OAuth (AD-1017), no per-agent grants (AD-1019); `routers/tools.py` catalog stays config-only (AD-1018 unions store rows). The AD-1014 pack-`mcpServers`-wiring forward-references (DECISIONS body + PROGRESS L3) are re-pointed from "AD-1015" → **AD-1020** (this AD is the stronger claim on the number). Default-OFF (`management_enabled=False`) ⇒ the router 404s, no store is constructed/seeded, **byte-identical**. **No secret value is ever persisted or returned** (the `validate_record` denylist + `to_public_dict` are the guards). **Tests.** `test_ad1015_mcp_server_store.py` + `test_ad1015_mcp_servers_api.py` (56, BF-287 — real `McpServerStore` `db_path=""` + a real-DB round-trip, real `MCPBridge`, real `TestClient`, AD-1014 stdio echo fixture for live-register/test-connection): store CRUD + dup-name `ValueError`, the full `validate_record` matrix (each error code + secret-guard accept/reject incl. empty-value-allowed + non-secret pass-through), gate-off-404, create/list/get/put-re-register/delete/enable-disable, transient test-connection ok (echo, `tool_count=3`) + honest-degrade `{ok:false}` at HTTP 200, config/store dedup (config's client wins). Parity gate `-k "mcp or ad449 or ad597"` **286 passed** (230 prior **unchanged** + 56 new); config regression **574 passed** (573 prior unchanged + 1 new whose name matches `config`). Default-OFF ⇒ byte-identical.

### AD-1014: stdio/subprocess MCP transport — marketplace launch parity (#954)

**Context.** ProbOS spoke MCP over HTTP only (`MCPClient` hardcoded to `httpx`, `MCPBridge.register_server(url)`). Marketplace MCP servers (the official registry, Smithery, Anthropic Directory — 15k+) are overwhelmingly **stdio**, launched as a subprocess (`uvx`/`npx`/`command`), and the MCP spec says *"clients SHOULD support stdio whenever possible."* Without a stdio transport ProbOS cannot install the bulk of the ecosystem (nor the servers a Capability Pack bundles in its already-parsed `mcpServers` field, #948). Researched against the MCP spec (2025-06-18), GitHub Copilot/VS Code, Claude Code, and Hermes Agent (Nous Research) — all four converge on `type`+`command`/`args`/`env`, a trust gate before first launch ("local MCP servers run arbitrary code"), per-server timeouts, tool-name namespacing, stderr→logs, and **install-into-isolation, never host** (the subprocess is the isolation; none pip-install into their own process). **Decision.** Architect→Builder workflow. Introduce a `Transport` Protocol behind `MCPClient` so HTTP and stdio are peers: `transport.py` adds `HttpTransport` (the existing HTTP wire body lifted **byte-identically**, incl. request-direction `Mcp-Session-Id` self-management + response-header capture) and `StdioTransport` (spawn via `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec`, **NDJSON** framing per the stdio spec, skip-until-matching-id read so `notifications/*` aren't mistaken for the response, held stderr-drain task, `close()` = stdin-close → terminate → kill-fallback). `MCPClient.__init__(transport=None)` defaults to `HttpTransport` so `register_server` + all AD-449/AD-597 tests stay **unchanged** (`_http` kept as a back-compat property proxy). `MCPServerConfig` gains a `type` discriminator (`http` default | `stdio`) + `command`/`args`/`env`/`cwd`/`timeout_seconds` with a `model_validator` (`http`⇒`url`, `stdio`⇒`command`); `MCPConfig` gains `stdio_enabled=False` (the default-OFF gate) + `command_allowlist=[uvx,npx,python,node,docker]`. `MCPBridge.register_stdio_server` enforces guards **in order, all before any spawn**: `stdio_enabled` → duplicate → **command allowlist** (refuse + `MCP_BRIDGE_FAILED` reason=`command_not_allowed`, no subprocess) → **consent** (`consent_fn`, refuse → `consent_denied`) → spawn. Startup wires `consent_fn` to the AD-1004/1012 HookBus `PreToolUse` gate (fail-safe: refuse on ASK and DENY) and adds an **inert-by-default** stdio registration loop. **Scope discipline — mechanism only:** no pack `mcpServers` auto-launch (AD-1020), no OS sandbox (#936 Tier-2), no marketplace UI, no runtime-venv installs; `external_discovery` (transport-agnostic) untouched. Default-OFF (`stdio_enabled=False` + empty `servers`) ⇒ **byte-identical** to prior behavior. **Tests.** `test_ad1014_stdio_mcp_transport.py` (24, BF-287 real `MCPBridge` + a real in-repo NDJSON echo subprocess fixture): handshake/list/call round-trips, `close()` terminates the proc, command-not-allowlisted → no spawn, consent-deny → no spawn, bad-JSON/timeout honest-degrade, config validator, and a focused fake-httpx test locking the request-direction `Mcp-Session-Id` injection (the #1 regression risk). HTTP parity gate: existing `-k "mcp or ad449 or ad597"` **230 passed unchanged**; config regression 573 passed.

### AD-1013: skills-only Capability-Pack loader (#948)

**Context.** First write-side slice of the Capability-Pack loader, and the lowest-risk tier. The read-side is complete (AD-1003a–f: parse → scan → inventory API → Ship's Locker list → component preview). A pack declares skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers; of these, **skills are the only non-executing component** — a `SKILL.md` is markdown *instructions* the LLM reads at reasoning time, not code that runs. So the skills tier can load with zero code-execution risk while the agent/.py + hooks/MCP tiers (which execute) wait for the AD-1014 self-mod-chain loader. **Decision.** `packs/loader.py` `load_pack_skills(pack_dir, catalog, *, origin_prefix="pack")` walks a pack's declared folder-skills (a subdir with `SKILL.md`, via the AD-1003e `preview_pack` inventory) and loads each through the **existing AD-596d `CognitiveSkillCatalog.import_skill`** path — which validates the `SKILL.md`, dedup-guards by name, copies the skill into the catalog skills dir, and registers it. Reuse over reinvention: the loader is only the orchestration; the validated import path is unchanged. Each skill is tagged `origin="pack:<name>"` for provenance (identify/remove a pack's skills as a unit). Returns a frozen `PackLoadResult` (`loaded[]`, `skipped[(name, reason)]`). **Honest-degrade:** a duplicate or invalid skill is *skipped with a reason*, never raised; a standalone `.md` (no `SKILL.md` folder) is skipped (the AgentSkills.io importer needs the folder shape); agent `.py`/`.json`/`.md` are never touched by this tier. **Consent + gating live in the caller** — a caller must check `config.packs.enabled` (default OFF) and obtain operator consent (the Ship's Locker preview is the review surface) before invoking; the loader is pure mechanism (mechanism-first, mirroring AD-1004), so it adds no live behavior on its own. **Tests.** `test_ad1013_pack_skills_loader.py` (8, BF-287 real `CognitiveSkillCatalog` cache-only + real tmp_path packs): loads-declared-folder-skills, origin-tag-provenance, custom-prefix, no-manifest→None, standalone-md-skipped, duplicate-skipped-not-raised, agents-not-loaded (a `rogue.py` is never registered/executed), partial-load mixes loaded+skipped. Pack + skill-catalog regression 191 passed.

### AD-1012: lifecycle-hook bus PreDispatch wiring — the pluggable capability gate (#949, #944)

**Context.** AD-1004 (#949) shipped the `HookBus` substrate (`HookEvent`, `HookDecision`, most-restrictive-wins aggregation, honest-degrade) but deliberately left it *unwired* — firing with no handlers is a no-op. The per-agent capability gate (AD-1007/1008) meanwhile enforced inline at two origination sites (`reply_pipeline.step_4h`, `agentic_dispatch`). The held decision (Captain-confirmed 2026-06-15): wire the bus as the canonical `PreDispatch` gate with **block** semantics, **default-OFF**. **Decision.** New `hooks/handlers.py` `make_capability_gate_handler(intent_grant_store)` — a pure policy adapter returning `HookResult(DENY)` only on an explicit `resolve_sync == "restricted"` (agent-precedence Captain disable), `ALLOW` on `granted`/`no_opinion`, `None` (abstain) on a malformed context. The bus is instantiated in `startup/communication.py` **only when `config.hooks.enabled`** (default False); when on, the capability gate is registered on `HookEvent.PRE_DISPATCH` and exposed as `runtime.hook_bus` (threaded via `CommunicationResult.hook_bus`, torn down in shutdown). `reply_pipeline.step_4h` now routes through `hook_bus.fire(PRE_DISPATCH, …)` when wired, else falls back to the inline `IntentGrantStore` check — **byte-identical default behavior** (bus is None unless the flag is set). This makes the gate the shared lifecycle point where Capability-Pack hooks (#948) and a future consensus handler attach with the same most-restrictive-wins aggregation. **Scope discipline:** the conversational [MESH] origination path is wired; the agentic-loop `PreToolUse` fire and command-based pack hooks remain follow-up slices. **Tests.** `test_ad1012_hook_bus_wiring.py` (10, BF-287 real `HookBus` + real `IntentGrantStore` cache-only): handler restricted→deny / granted→allow / no_opinion→allow / `intent` alias / missing-agent→abstain / missing-intent→abstain; bus denies-restricted, allows-ungranted, allows-granted, restriction-is-agent-scoped. AD-1004 15 + AD-1012 10 = 25 green; touched-path regression (reply_pipeline / ad1005/1007/1008 / intent_grant / mesh_read / hook / config) **714 passed**. Default-OFF → no live behavior change.

This wires the two so the operator can expand a pack to see what it declares — before the deferred loader exists. **Decision.** `ShipsLockerPanel` valid-pack rows become clickable (`+`/`−` toggle); expanding fetches `GET /api/packs/{name}` (`fetchPackDetail`, deps-injectable) and renders the pack's declared `skills:` / `agents:` component names inline. ### AD-1003e: pack content preview — read-only enumeration of a pack's declared components (#944, #948)

**Context.** Fifth Capability-Pack slice. The read-side (parse → scan → API → HXI, AD-1003a–d) lists *which packs* are installed; before the deferred loader (which executes pack code, held for the operator trust gate), the operator should be able to inspect *what a pack contains*. This is the read-only inventory the loader will consume — surfaced now so a pack can be reviewed before loading. **Decision.** `packs/scanner.py` `preview_pack(pack_dir)` loads the manifest (AD-1003a) and enumerates the actual component files under its declared `skill_paths`/`agent_paths`: a subdir with a `SKILL.md` is a folder-skill, standalone `.md` are skills, agent files are `.md`/`.json`/`.py`. Returns `PackContents` (frozen: name + `PackComponent[]` for skills/agents + hooks/mcp flags). `describe_pack_contents` is the serializable form. `GET /api/packs/{name}` (resolves by *manifest* name, not folder) returns it; 404 when disabled / not-found / no-valid-manifest. **Read-only — component files are LISTED, never opened, parsed, imported, or executed**; directory traversal is guarded (a declared path that escapes the pack dir via `..` is skipped). Paths are normalized to POSIX (`as_posix()`) so the API is cross-platform. Honest-degrade: missing dir / invalid manifest → `None`; never raises. **Tests.** `test_ad1003e_pack_preview.py` (10, BF-287 real tmp_path packs): folder-skills + agent files by ext, standalone-md skills, missing-declared-dir→empty, hooks/mcp flags, no-manifest→None, invalid-manifest→None, path-traversal-blocked, frozen component, `describe_pack_contents` shape + None. `test_ad1003c_packs_api.py` +3 (detail endpoint: lists-components-by-manifest-name, 404-disabled, 404-not-found). Pack suite 48 passed; smoke clean. The Capability-Pack read-side is now complete through component-level preview; only the loader (write-side, trust-gated) remains on #948.

**Context.** Third Capability-Pack slice: surface the AD-1003b scanner over HTTP, the cross-tool "installed plugins" list (VS Code / Copilot CLI / Claude Code). **Decision.** `PacksConfig` (config.py, default OFF, `packs_dir="data/packs"`); `routers/packs.py` `GET /api/packs` — when `packs.enabled=False` returns `{enabled:false, packs:[], counts:{0,0,0}}`; when enabled, resolves `packs_dir` against the runtime data dir (BF-628 lesson: relative paths resolve to the platform data dir, not cwd) and returns `describe_scan(...)` + `enabled:true` + `packs_dir`. ### AD-1011: ship-wide skill coverage — the civilization skill-registry view (#815)

**Context.** #815 asked for two HXI surfaces over the skill framework: (1) a **ship-wide skill registry** view (which agents hold each skill, coverage/gap) and (2) a per-agent skill-assignment surface. View 2 already shipped (Profile Service tab skill toggle AD-983b/c + SkillLibrary CRUD AD-898). View 1 was the gap.

**Decision.** Backend `GET /api/skills/coverage` ([skills.py](src/probos/routers/skills.py)) — inverts every **crew** agent's skill profile (`is_crew_agent` filter) into a `skill_id → holders[]` map, joined against the full registry so unheld skills surface as gaps. Each row: `{skill_id, name, category, holder_count, holders:[{agent_id, callsign, proficiency, proficiency_label}], gap}`; plus `crew_count` + `gap_count`. Profiles gathered concurrently (`asyncio.gather`); per-agent failure skipped, missing registry/service → empty set (honest-degrade, never raises). Sorted most-held-first. UI `SkillCoverage.tsx` — a read-only coverage lens above `SkillLibrary` in the Ship's Office skills pane: per-skill coverage bar (width = holders/crew), red `GAP` flag for unheld skills, expandable holders list with proficiency. The per-agent *assignment* stays the Service tab; this is the read-only civilization lens.

**Tests.** `test_ad1011_skill_coverage.py` (5, BF-287 real `SkillRegistry` + `AgentSkillService` on tmp SQLite + real registry/ontology/callsign stubs): inverts-profiles-to-holders (most-held-first + gap), holder carries callsign + proficiency, all-gaps-when-none-acquired, honest-degrade-no-service, non-crew-agents-excluded. `SkillCoverage.test.tsx` (5, deps-injected): summary line, per-skill row + gap flag, expand holders, empty-state, no-emoji. `CrewPersonnelConsole.test.tsx` unchanged (8). Backend 5, UI 13, `npm run build` clean. Closes #815 (view 1 + view 2 complete).

### AD-1003b: Capability-Pack scanner — read-only installed-pack inventory (#944, #948)

**Context.** Second safe slice of Capability Packs (after AD-1003a's manifest parser). The cross-tool tools (VS Code / Copilot CLI / Claude Code) all surface an "installed plugins" list; ProbOS needs the read-side inventory before any loader. **Decision.** `packs/scanner.py`: `scan_packs(packs_dir)` walks the immediate subdirectories, treats any subdir where `find_manifest` (AD-1003a) locates a manifest as a pack, and `load_manifest`+`describe_pack`-es it into a `PackEntry` (frozen: `path` + `summary` | `error`, `.ok`/`.name` helpers). A malformed/invalid manifest becomes an **error entry** (honest-degrade) so one bad pack never hides the rest. `describe_scan(packs_dir)` returns the serializable inventory (`packs[]` + `counts{total,valid,error}`) — the shape a future `GET /api/packs` / UI list consumes. **Read-only — nothing installed, loaded, executed, or wired.** Honest-degrade: missing/non-dir/unlistable `packs_dir` → `[]`, never raises. The pack loader (map into the live registries behind the operator trust gate) and execution remain later slices. **Tests.** `test_ad1003b_pack_scanner.py` (9, BF-287 real tmp_path pack dirs): empty/missing dir, valid packs sorted by manifest name, non-pack subdirs skipped, bad-pack→error-entry-scan-continues, malformed-JSON→error, Claude-format detection, `PackEntry` helpers, `describe_scan` shape + counts + empty. AD-1003a regression 21 green; import smoke clean.

### BF-629: conversational web_search/read_page synthesis — reason over results, don't paste links (#953)

**Context (Captain live test, 2026-06-14).** Asked Ezri the same question as GitHub Copilot (*"web search the Fable LLM, latest news"*). Copilot returned a synthesised briefing (what it is / breaking news / capabilities / sources / bottom line); Ezri returned a **raw list of links** and only synthesised after the Captain pushed back ("you gave me links but didn't reason over the articles"). Repeated across several turns — the Captain was manually driving the search→reason→summarise loop turn by turn.

**Root cause (verified).** Ezri's conversational reply uses the AD-869 Tier-2 **do-and-report** `[MESH web_search …]` affordance, not an agentic tool-use loop. `reply_pipeline.step_4h_mesh_read_parse` sends the intent to a **separate** `WebSearchAgent` and pastes its result **verbatim** via `_render_mesh_read_result`; the originating agent never reasons over it. `WebSearchAgent.instructions` say "present the results clearly" → it **lists** (title/url/snippet). The tell: the Captain's *next* turn synthesised — because by then the results were in conversation history and a normal reply pass reasoned over them. Contrast: Copilot and ProbOS's own `AgenticLoop`/`WorkItemAgenticExecutor` (AD-545/856) keep the tool result in the *same* model's context and continue reasoning — the conversational path took the fast delegate-and-paste shortcut.

**Decision.** Add a **synthesis pass** to `step_4h_mesh_read_parse`: after a `requires_reflect` read — `_MESH_READ_SYNTHESIZE_INTENTS = {web_search, read_page}`, exactly the network/LLM-bound reads — a new `_synthesize_mesh_read` helper makes ONE LLM pass through `runtime.llm_client` (mirroring the AD-934 deliberate re-roll) so the **originating** agent reasons over the result in its own voice, with the Captain's question + the rendered results as context, producing a synthesised answer (key findings + inline sources) instead of the raw list. Verbatim reads (`read_file`/`list_directory`/`stat_file`/`search_*`) skip synthesis — the raw output IS the answer. `DmMeshSynthesisConfig` (`enabled`/`tier=standard`/`max_tokens=700`) defaults **OFF in the model** (deterministic tests, safe-by-default) and **ON in `config/system.yaml`** (the running instance gets the Copilot-parity behavior — the AD-935 ship-it pattern).

**Honest-degrade (and the empty-content interaction).** A disabled flag, missing client, empty `rendered`, or an empty/raised LLM response all return the verbatim `rendered` unchanged — so a degraded LLM **never drops the Captain's results**, it falls back to the raw list. This is also the exact protection for the **BF-289/612 empty-content proxy surface** the Captain hit in the same session (a wedged keep-alive socket returns HTTP 200 empty): BF-612's socket-recycle is the primary mitigation; this fix ensures that even if the synthesis pass itself hits an empty response, the search results still reach the Captain rather than "(no reply)".

**Scope fence.** Conversational `[MESH]` path only. No change to the `WebSearchAgent`/`PageReaderAgent` themselves, the Tier-3 `[CREATE_TASK]` async path, the agentic loop, or the verbatim local-IO reads. The AD-935 OFF-in-model/ON-in-yaml default keeps every existing test deterministic (default-OFF) with zero obsolete-contract updates.

**Tests.** `test_bf629_mesh_synthesis.py` (9, BF-287 — real `DmReplyPipeline` + real `DmSanityGate` + real config-shaped runtime; fake intent-bus + LLM only at the I/O edges): web_search + read_page synthesise; prompt carries the Captain's question + rendered results + agent voice + tier; disabled→verbatim (no LLM call); read_file not synthesised; empty-LLM / no-client / raising-LLM all fall back to verbatim; a failed read never synthesises. Regression: AD-869 mesh-read + AD-870/933/934 pipeline 48 passed; AD-726 pipeline + capability 44 passed; config defaults OFF + `system.yaml` loads ON.

### AD-1009: role templates — view a role's loadout + apply it as a starting template (Agent Customizations epic #944, #952)

**Context.** The Captain's role-framework directive: *"assign a role to an agent like 'Counselor' — that role has tools and capabilities already assigned (a template) — use that as a template to start with, then enable/disable per agent which overrides the role."* The role→skills→tools engine already exists at agent birth (`ACM.commission`, AD-889); per-agent override of tools/skills/capabilities already exists (AD-894/AD-983b/AD-1007). What was missing: **visibility** of what a role grants, and an **explicit apply action** (commission only ran at birth).

**Decision (backend).**
- **`GET /api/crew/roles`** — enumerate every role from the ontology assignments, each with: `role_id` (post_id), `agent_type`, `callsign`, post `title`/`department`, required `skills` (from `RoleTemplate`), the `tools` those skills resolve to (AD-888 `resolve_tools_for_skill`, honest-degrade `[]`), and the mesh `capabilities` the role's `agent_type` serves (from live `intent_descriptors`). Read-only, derived — no new role config. The complete "what does this role include as a template" view.
- **`POST /api/crew/{agent_id}/apply-role`** (`ApplyRole{role_id?}`) — apply a role's skill+tool template to an agent via `ACM.commission`. `role_id` selects which role (resolved post→agent_type via `get_agents_for_post`); omitted → the agent's own role (refresh from template). Additive + reversible (grants are revocable) → no consensus gate (Minimal Authority). Capabilities stay governed per-agent (AD-1007); they are not stamped by a role.
- **AD-889 commission guard fix (agent-precedence on re-apply).** The tool-grant idempotency check changed from `if any(not g.is_restriction for g in existing)` to `if existing` — i.e. skip if ANY active per-agent decision exists (a grant OR a manual Captain restriction). Re-applying a role template therefore never clobbers a per-agent override: a manual *disable* survives re-apply. Byte-identical at birth (no decisions exist yet); only re-apply benefits.

**Deferred (follow-ons).** Role-level capability/tool DISABLE *authoring* (so a role can disable a capability by default, activating the grant-overrides-role-disable direction end-to-end) needs a role-defaults store + UI — not built (today a CAN-REQUEST capability's role default is "enabled/reachable," so the live action is a per-agent disable, AD-1007). The Personnel Console role-picker UI (apply-role from the Ship's Office, role template browser) is the AD-1010 UI slice.

**Tests.** `test_ad1009_roles.py` (10, BF-287 real route handlers + real `SimpleNamespace` ontology/registry + a recording ACM stub): served-intent grouping + no-registry degrade; `list_roles` view assembly (title/dept/skills/served-caps/tool-degrade) + no-ontology degrade + dept/title sort; apply-role own-role / explicit-role-id-resolution / unknown-role-404 / unknown-agent-404 / no-acm-503. `test_ad889_commission_chain.py` +1 (`test_recommission_preserves_manual_restriction` — real `ToolPermissionStore` + `SkillRegistry` + `AgentSkillService`: a manual restriction survives re-commission, scanner NOT re-granted). Regression across acm/commission/capability/tool-cert: 85 passed. Import smoke clean.

### AD-1008: per-agent capability toggle in the profile — CAN-REQUEST rows enable/disable (Agent Customizations epic #944, #952)

**Context.** AD-1007 added the backend capability gate; the Captain wants to drive it from the agent profile "like GitHub Copilot." **Decision.** `CapabilityPanel.tsx`: the **CAPABILITIES — CAN REQUEST** rows gain an On/Off toggle that issues a per-agent capability grant/restriction via the AD-1007 `kind="capability"` set endpoint (optimistic with revert-on-failure, the AD-982 pattern; disabled rows render dim + strikethrough). The **SERVES** rows stay read-only — a served intent's enablement is governed by the agent's role (the AD-1009 role layer), not a per-agent origination gate, so toggling it here would imply an enforcement that does not exist. `MeshIntent` carries `granted`/`source` from AD-1007; `setCapability`'s `kind` widens to `tool|skill|capability`. **Tests.** `CapabilityPanel.test.tsx` +3 (CAN-REQUEST toggleable / SERVES read-only, optimistic POST `kind=capability`, revert-on-failure); UI suite + `npm run build` clean.
