### AD-983b: per-agent capability enablement — per-agent skill grants + unified /capabilities API (#915)

**Context.** The "each crew agent independently enables different tools and skills" piece of the AD-983 epic (#913). Tools already had per-agent enablement (`ToolPermissionStore`, AD-423b — grant/revoke/restrict, enforced at the agentic loop). Cognitive skills did NOT: `CognitiveSkillCatalog` gated only by `department` + `min_rank`, so a skill could not be enabled on one agent and withheld from its department peers. And there was no unified read/write surface for an agent's capabilities.

**Decision (three parts).** (1) **`SkillGrantStore`** (`cognitive/skill_grants.py`) — the skill counterpart to `ToolPermissionStore`, mirroring it exactly (SQLite + WAL + in-memory cache, `issue_grant`/`revoke_grant`/`get_active_grants_sync`/`list_grants`, soft-revoke for audit, lazy expiry) minus the permission level (a cognitive skill is binary). `SkillAccessGrant` dataclass. (2) **Catalog overlay** — `CognitiveSkillCatalog.set_grant_store()` (injected at startup, mirroring `tool_registry.set_permission_store`) + `effective_entries_for_agent(agent_id, *, department, min_rank)` = the dept/rank defaults PLUS explicitly-granted skills (even outside the agent's dept/rank) MINUS explicitly-restricted skills. Back-compat: with no grant store wired it is byte-identical to `list_entries(department, min_rank)`. The onboarding intent-subscription path (`agent_onboarding.py`) now resolves an agent's skill intents through `effective_entries_for_agent`, so per-agent grants drive what the agent can actually reach. (3) **Unified API** (`routers/agents.py`) — `GET /api/agent/{id}/capabilities` → `{tools: [...], skills: [...]}` each with `granted` + `source` (`grant`/`restriction`/`role_default` for tools; `grant`/`restriction`/`dept_default` for skills); `POST /api/agent/{id}/capabilities/set` `{kind: tool|skill, id, enabled, reason}` (`enabled=False` issues a restriction that overrides a default), audit-logged via the new `CAPABILITY_ACCESS_RESOLVED` event — the generalization of the AD-982 vision `set` endpoint. New `SetCapability` Pydantic model (`kind` pattern-validated).

**Wiring.** `SkillGrantStore` created in `startup/communication.py` (`data/skill_grants.db`), injected into the catalog, threaded through `CommunicationResult` → `runtime.skill_grant_store`, stopped in `startup/shutdown.py`.

**Independence proven.** A skill granted to agent A is in A's effective set and NOT in a same-department peer B's; a restriction removes a default the agent would otherwise hold. Tests: `test_ad983b_capability_enablement.py` (16, BF-287 real `SkillGrantStore` + real `CognitiveSkillCatalog` with on-disk `SKILL.md`): store issue/restrict/revoke/persist-across-restart; the headline grant-one-agent-not-its-peer; restriction-removes-default; no-store back-compat; and the API (GET shape + source tags, POST grant→restrict, 404 unknown agent/skill, 422 invalid kind). The 5 BF-326 MagicMock-dir warnings are the known config-boundary noise (auto-cleaned), consistent with the AD-982a API tests. Regression blast over skill-catalog/onboarding/acm/tool-permission/agents green. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed. Next: AD-983c (#916) the Capability panel UI.

### AD-983a: capability affordance layer — the tool carries its own manual (#914; supersedes AD-957/#893)

**Context.** The headline of the AD-983 Copilot-harness-parity epic (#913). A capability's *affordance* — "how to invoke a tool you hold" — was authored into ONE agent's behavior rules: the `[MESH ...]` do-and-report teaching lived in `YeomanAgent` (BF-599 capability block + AD-870 task-protocol tiers). Every other crew agent held the same capabilities through the mesh and had no idea how to reach them (the web-search incident — Ezri couldn't look things up). That is a category error: the affordance should travel WITH the capability and surface to whoever can reach it (the Copilot tool-schema model), not be written into a behavior rule. The right pattern already existed — `_conversational_notebook_protocol` (AD-912) is generalized to all crew AND substrate-gated — it just had not been applied to tools.

**Decision (three moves, one sub-AD).** (1) **`IntentDescriptor.usage_hint: str = ""`** — an optional AGENT-FACING invocation manual declared once on the capability (`description` serves the decomposer/planning; `usage_hint` serves the agent at reply time). Declared on the five AD-869 `[MESH]`-backed read intents: `list_directory`, `read_file`, `search_files` (on their core agents), `web_search`, `read_page` (on the web agents). (2) **`CognitiveAgent.capability_affordances()`** — a derived `{intent: usage_hint}` map built from the LIVE registry: walk `registry.all()`, read each agent's declared `intent_descriptors`, collect the ones with a `usage_hint`, dedupe by intent name. **Substrate-gated by construction** — only agents actually serving contribute, so a capability whose pool is down is absent (the BF-599 honest-degrade generalized off Yeo's `_available_mesh_read_intents`). (3) The base **`_conversational_capability_block`** (previously returned `""`) now renders those hints (deterministically sorted) into EVERY crew agent's conversational prompt, so any agent — not just Yeo — is told it can fetch a web search / read a page / list a directory / read a file this turn. **Folds in AD-957 (#893)**: generalizes "web search for everyone" to "every reachable capability, for everyone."

**Yeo retirement.** Removed Yeo's `_conversational_capability_block` override and the `_available_mesh_read_intents` helper (the base now provides live-capability grounding to all crew). Yeo's `_conversational_task_protocol` keeps only its genuinely role-specific delegation JUDGMENT — the Tier-3 `[CREATE_TASK]` write-it-down threshold (gated on a work-item store) + the rule-of-thumb; its quick-lookup tier now points at the ship-capability tags the base renders above, rather than re-enumerating the `[MESH ...]` forms. Net: the affordance is universal; only the delegation judgment stays Yeo's.

**Gates.** New `tests/test_ad983a_capability_affordances.py` (18, BF-287 real `AgentRegistry` + real `IntentDescriptor`: affordance collection/dedup/substrate-gating/no-runtime; base block render/order/empty/gap-safe; a non-Yeo CounselorAgent gets the web affordance with no override — the headline; the five real read descriptors ship hints). `test_ad870_*` rewritten (task protocol now teaches `[CREATE_TASK]` only; `[MESH]` moved to the base affordance). `test_bf599_*` rewritten (descriptor-driven, generalized — Yeo gets the web affordance from a live web agent via the base hook). AD-845/AD-869 Yeo tests green. Backend regression blast over yeoman/cognitive_agent/dm/decomposer/web_agent/capability green. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed. Next in the epic: AD-983b (#915) per-agent skill grants + unified `/capabilities` API.

### AD-984 + BF-622: meeting voice/chat experience wave — hide-chat toggle, interruptible scroll, Captain-local time, scaffolding-echo guard (#882, #918-#923)

**Context.** A live group-meeting test produced a design conversation (Captain + Ezri + Yeo) with one organizing insight: a meeting is **one conversation**, and voice is the Captain's chosen *interface* to it — so the text chat should be able to recede when voice is the interface. The voice-first loop is already in place (AD-921/922/923/949 + BF-621); the gap is the presentation layer. This wave ships the build-ready slice of the AD-984 epic plus a robustness bug. AD-984b (condensed-sidebar presentation + WCAG 2.1 AA) stays design-deferred.

**AD-984a — hide-chat toggle in meeting mode (frontend).** New session-scoped store flag `meetingChatVisible` (default **true** = byte-identical) + `setMeetingChatVisible`, mirroring the AD-949 `callAudioEnabled` slice (no localStorage). `GroupChatHeader` renders a `data-testid="chat-visibility-toggle"` speech-bubble stroke-SVG button **only while `meetingActive`** (amber shown / dim+slash hidden, `aria-pressed`, no emoji / no `Glyphs.tsx` export). `ProfileChatTab` gates the transcript message-list on `showTranscript = !(meetingActive && !meetingChatVisible)` — `MeetingView` (avatars) + composer stay; only the transcript collapses. Persistence and the BF-621 voice reveal are unaffected (replies still land + are spoken; re-showing reveals the full transcript).

**AD-984c — interruptible auto-scroll (frontend).** New pure helper `chat/scrollAnchor.ts` `isPinnedToBottom(el, threshold=80)` (a non-overflowing or at-bottom container is pinned). `ProfileChatTab` tracks a `pinnedToBottomRef` via an `onScroll` handler on the message-list container, and the auto-scroll effect moves the view ONLY when pinned — so a new message never yanks the Captain down while they are reading an earlier turn. Starts pinned (fresh view); returning to the bottom re-engages.

**AD-984d — Captain-local timezone in crew context (backend).** New `TemporalConfig.captain_timezone: str = ""` (IANA name). When set, `_build_temporal_context` adds a "Captain's local time: …" line (converted via `zoneinfo.ZoneInfo`) alongside the UTC line — a FACT provided to the crew, removing the confabulation source (the crew inferred "3am" from UTC when it was 9pm Mountain). Unset = unchanged (UTC only; the crew must not assert a local time). A bad/unknown zone name honest-degrades to no extra line. **`tzdata` added to dependencies** — Windows has no system IANA database, so `zoneinfo` needs it (a silent honest-degrade would have hidden the feature on the Captain's OS).

**BF-622 — scaffolding-echo guard (backend).** The AD-978/AD-733a `--- Current Visual Context --- … --- End Visual Context ---` block is prepended to the LLM INPUT so an agent can describe what it sees; it leaked into the chat once when a degraded LLM proxy echoed its own input prompt back as the completion. New pure `strip_visual_context_block(text)` in `working_memory.py` (regex on the exact delimiters `render_for_prompt` emits — single source of truth) removes the span before persist. Applied at both reply chokepoints (`thread_fanout._send_one` group path, `routers/agents.py` 1:1 path), guarded on the `"Current Visual Context"` substring so normal replies are untouched; a reply that was ONLY echoed scaffolding degrades to the non-reply sentinel.

**Gates.** New tests: `GroupChatHeader.meeting.test.tsx` +3 (AD-984a hidden-when-no-meeting / shown+`aria-pressed` / click hides), `chat/__tests__/scrollAnchor.test.ts` (7, AD-984c pure helper), `test_ad984d_captain_timezone.py` (6, BF-287 real `SystemConfig` + real `_build_temporal_context`), `test_bf622_strip_visual_context.py` (8, incl. the round-trip that the strip matches the real `render_for_prompt` delimiters). Full UI **1453 passed / 1 skipped** (+10 over the 1438 baseline, zero regressions), `npm run build` clean; backend blast over perception/temporal/thread_fanout/vision/cognitive/dm/agents **1266 passed / 0 failed** (pre-existing BF-326 MagicMock-dir warnings only). ### BF-617 + BF-618 + BF-619: live group-meeting test fixes — shared vision, paced text, end-of-turn hand-offs (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

**Context.** The Captain's first live group-meeting test of the AD-976/978 wave surfaced three bugs that the mocked unit tests missed (the recurring AD-933a integration-gap lesson — scripted handlers don't exercise real perception/voice/cascade wiring): (1) "Yeo can't see me but Ezri can"; (2) all reply text appeared at once instead of landing as each agent spoke; (3) Ezri ended a turn with "Yeo, anything on your end?" and Yeo never answered.

**BF-617 — shared meeting vision.** Root cause: perception frames fan out only to REGISTERED observers (crew with `vision_capable=True` — only `counselor`/`architect`), so the yeoman's working-memory ring was empty and AD-978 rendered the BF-294 "camera not active" sentinel even with a live feed. A shared-camera meeting has ONE feed that everyone present should see. `VisionConsumer` now records the latest observation it produces (`_last_observation` + `latest_shared_observation()`), and `_render_agent_scene_block` falls back to it when an agent's own ring is empty — sharing the frame into that agent's ring on the render path. Meeting-scoped: it does NOT `register_observer` the agent, so there is no ambient-perception enrollment, no added per-frame fan-out cost, and no proactive-emit behavior change. An observer with its own ring still renders that; with no frame described yet, the honest sentinel still shows.

### BF-620: shared meeting vision survives restart (follow-up to BF-617, #882)

**Context.** The Captain's RE-TEST after BF-617 shipped STILL showed "Yeo can't see but Ezri can." BF-617's mechanism (the `_render_agent_scene_block` fallback to `latest_shared_observation()`) is correct in isolation (its tests pass) but failed live — the recurring integration-gap lesson again: the fallback's *source* was wrong post-restart.

**Root cause.** `VisionConsumer._last_observation` is in-RAM and starts `None` after a restart, but a vision-capable observer's ring **hydrates from disk** (AD-742f persistence) on first access. So right after the Captain's pre-test restart, Ezri (observer) renders a hydrated scene while the yeoman's fallback reads `_last_observation == None` → the BF-294 "camera not active" sentinel → "I can't see." The Captain restarts before every test, so it reproduced every time. BF-617's own tests use a `_FakeConsumer` returning a fixed obs, so they never exercised the in-RAM-vs-hydrated split.

**Fix.** `latest_shared_observation()` now, when `_last_observation` is unset, falls back to the most-recent observation any REGISTERED OBSERVER currently holds (scanning their real rings, hydrated or live) — so a non-observer borrows the live shared feed regardless of restart. Strictly additive: when a fresh in-RAM describe exists it is returned directly (zero change to the warm path). Tier-2 per-ring scan (a failed ring read is skipped).

**Gates.** `test_bf620_shared_meeting_vision_restart.py` (5, BF-287 real `VisionConsumer` + real `VisionWorkingMemory` rings: last-obs-wins-when-set; observer-ring fallback after restart; none-anywhere → None; most-recent-across-observers; non-observer borrows feed end-to-end through `_render_agent_scene_block`). BF-617 (6) + AD-978 (13) + AD-733a (26) regression green (50 total). COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

**BF-618 — paced meeting text reveal.** Root cause: the original AD-976 coupled the text reveal to TTS `speakingAgentId` events; when speech fired fast or didn't pace (cold Piper / muted / autoplay-blocked), the staged reveals burst to all-at-once. Replaced with the SAME timer-paced progressive reveal text chat uses (`revealRepliesProgressively`, built-in inter-reply spacing — cannot burst), in both meeting and text-chat paths. Voice (`speakMeetingReplies`) is now kicked off BEFORE the awaited reveal so it runs concurrently rather than after. The fragile staging apparatus (per-agent staging map, reveal-on-speaking effect, ref bridge) is removed. Exact word-level karaoke sync remains forward marker AD-976a (needs Piper streaming timing metadata).

### BF-621: meeting text reveal follows speech — "hear, then see" + "is speaking" label (#882)

**Context.** The Captain's re-test of BF-618: text was "more delayed now, but still not what I expected" — it said "{callsign} is typing" *while the agent was speaking*, and the timer-paced reveal drifted from the voice. The Captain's decision: in a live meeting with voice, label it "{callsign} is **speaking**…", and reveal each reply's text **after** that agent finishes speaking (hear the response, then see it land in the chat).

**Root cause of the drift.** BF-618 ran two independent clocks concurrently: `speakMeetingReplies` (voice) and a timer-paced `revealRepliesProgressively` (text). With voice audible they are uncorrelated, so text and speech diverge and the "typing" label is simply wrong while the agent talks.

**Decision.** When a meeting is live AND call audio is ON, drive the reveal off the AD-921 voice sequencer's per-utterance completion — the sequencer is the single clock (it already awaits each utterance one at a time), so text strictly follows speech and cannot drift or burst (the BF-618 burst was a *separate* timer racing the voice, not the voice itself). Mechanism: `MeetingVoiceDeps` gains `onUtteranceStart(reply)` (fired before each utterance, with the full reply for the callsign) and `onUtteranceEnd(reply)` (fired after the utterance completes AND after `onSpeakingChange(null)`); `speakRepliesSequentially` calls them around `_speakAndWait`. `useMeetingVoice.speakReplies(replies, hooks?)` forwards them gen-guarded (a superseded batch never labels/reveals stale text). `ProfileChatTab.sendText` branches: meeting+audio → `onUtteranceStart` sets `typingAgent` `{verb:'speaking'}`, `onUtteranceEnd` clears it and appends that reply (hear → label clears → text lands); audio OFF/muted or text chat → the AD-960 timer-paced reveal is unchanged. `TypingIndicator` + the `typingAgent` slice gain the `'speaking'` verb. A reply skipped by `shouldContinue` is neither spoken nor revealed (correct — stale). Honest-degrade: if audio is on but TTS fails, `onUtteranceEnd` fires on the BF-615 length-proportional safety timeout, so text still lands (never lost). Word-level karaoke sync stays AD-976a.

**Gates.** `meetingVoice.test.ts` +3 (start-before-speak; end-after-`speaking:null` timeline; superseded batch reveals nothing), `ProfileChatTab.ad976.test.tsx` rewritten to the BF-621 branch (voice-driven vs timer; speaking-label→clear→append order; muted-meeting + text-chat fall back to timer), `TypingIndicator.test.tsx` +1 (`'speaking'` verb). Full UI **1443 passed / 1 skipped** (+5 over the 1438 baseline, zero regressions), `npm run build` clean. Frontend only — no backend change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

**BF-619 — end-of-turn hand-off detection.** Root cause: AD-951's `extract_directed_callsign` matches a LEADING vocative only, but a natural hand-off comes at the END of a turn ("... Yeo, anything on your end?"), so the cascade's addressed-set was empty, no AD-961 extension fired, and the addressed peer never spoke. New `extract_handoff_callsign` also detects a final-sentence leading vocative and a trailing comma-vocative ("what do you think, Yeo?"), while keeping the BF #467 discipline (a message ABOUT a peer — "I agree with Yeo." — is not a hand-off; the comma/colon is the discriminator). The group cascade now uses it for addressed-detection, so an end-of-turn hand-off hard-includes the peer and (past the round cap) earns the AD-961 address-extension. Traced against the live transcript: Ezri's final-sentence "Yeo, ..." now resolves to `yeo`, extends one round, and Yeo answers.

**Gates.** `test_bf619_handoff_callsign.py` (leading parity + the end-of-turn case + the referential-mention negatives) + `test_bf617_shared_meeting_vision.py` (observer renders own ring; non-observer falls back to the shared feed + ring populated; no-frame sentinel; disabled/no-consumer degrade) + rewritten `ProfileChatTab.ad976.test.tsx` (voice-before-reveal ordering; always-progressive, no instant-dump branch). Backend blast across fanout/group/perception/AD-951/961/crew_profile green; full UI **1429 passed / 1 skipped**, build clean.

### AD-976: Meeting-mode text follows the voice — reveal each reply as its agent speaks (Natural Conversation epic, #899)

**Context.** In a live (audio-on) meeting the AD-921 voice sequencer speaks the crew's replies one at a time, but the text path dumped ALL replies into the transcript instantly (`for (const r of replies) appendReply(r)`). The Captain read the whole room's answers before the voices had said them — "shouldn't see the text until you've said the words."

**Decision (frontend only).** Reveal a reply's text as its agent STARTS speaking, off the existing `useMeetingVoice` `speakingAgentId` seam (AD-923) — leaving the working voice hook untouched (lowest risk). `ProfileChatTab` now: (1) reads `callAudioEnabled` reactively; (2) in the send handler, branches `meetingActive && callAudioEnabled` → STAGE the round's replies in `pendingMeetingRepliesRef` (a `Map<agent_id, reply>`) and clear `revealedSpeakingRef`, instead of dumping them; (3) an effect on `speakingAgentId` reveals each staged reply exactly once as its agent begins to speak (a `revealedSpeakingRef` set guards against re-entry). The handler-scope `appendReply` closure is bridged to the render-scope effect via `appendMeetingReplyRef` (the file's stale-closure ref discipline). A MUTED meeting (no voice to pace the reveal) and TEXT chat both fall back to the existing AD-960 progressive reveal, so text never silently fails to appear. `speakMeetingReplies` is unchanged — it drives `speakingAgentId`, which now drives the reveal.

**Gates.** `ProfileChatTab.ad976.test.tsx` (8, the faithful-mirror convention used for this heavy component: the reveal-mode decision — audio-on→speech-synced, muted/text→progressive; staging keyed by agent_id dropping blank ids; speech-synced reveal in speaking order, exactly-once on re-entry, no-op for an unstaged speaker). Full UI suite **1434 passed / 1 skipped** (+8), `npm run build` clean. No backend change. Forward marker AD-976a: sentence-level karaoke sync (needs Piper streaming timing metadata).

### AD-980c: Dream interpretation — an agent interprets its own dream (Agent self-interpretation epic, #912)

**Context.** The novel loop Ezri's question pointed at: sleep -> dream -> wake -> interpret -> revise-self. AD-980b gives a dream a dreamer (per-agent reflection episodes); AD-980a is the interpretation engine. AD-980c closes the loop: an agent interprets ITS OWN dream and stores the interpretation as an agent-owned episode that feeds its self-model. No published agent system has a sovereign agent interpret its own distinct consolidation artifact as a dream.

**Decision.** New `CognitiveAgent.interpret_own_dream(*, k=5)`: gathers the agent's recent `MemorySource.REFLECTION` episodes (the AD-980b-attributed dreams) via `recent_for_agent` (scanning a wider window so non-dream episodes don't crowd the dreams out), then runs the shared interpretation engine over them with a dream-specific focus ("what these dream reflections reveal about how you work and what matters to you"). The AD-980a `interpret_recall` body was refactored into a shared `_run_interpretation(episodes, focus, store)` engine (no gate) that both public entrypoints call after their own flag gate — `interpret_recall` gates on `recall_interpretation_enabled`, `interpret_own_dream` on `dream_interpretation_enabled`. Honesty-bound (AD-592): the dreams are real consolidated material; with none, nothing to interpret (`None`); the stored interpretation is the same agent-owned `[interpretation]` REFLECTION episode as AD-980a. Opt-in (default **False**, an extra LLM pass per agent per dream); not auto-invoked in the dream cycle — an explicit call (the Captain enables the flag + the loop is driven on wake/idle), keeping the behavior observable.

**Gates.** `test_ad980c_dream_interpretation.py` (7: disabled→None, no-dreams→None, empty-window→None, interprets only the REFLECTION episodes in the window and stores an agent-owned `[interpretation]` REFLECTION, dream-specific focus in the prompt, no-LLM→None, k bounds the dreams) + AD-980a (9) + AD-980b (5) green together (21) — the `_run_interpretation` refactor kept AD-980a byte-identical. **The full sleep->dream->wake->interpret loop (AD-980a+b+c) is built and tested.**

### AD-980b: Per-agent dream attribution — give a dream a dreamer (Agent self-interpretation epic, #911)

**Context.** The subjectivity gap behind Ezri's dream question: dream-consolidation reflections (AD-599 `_step_15_reflection_promotion`) were stored with `agent_ids=[]` — ownerless. Dream consolidation is a system-wide pass, so there was no "Ezri's dream"; an agent could not recall *its* dream because it did not have one. A dream needs a dreamer before it can be interpreted (AD-980c). Crucially, each reflection candidate ALREADY computes its `involved_agents` (the agents whose episodes it was consolidated from — e.g. a convergence report's agents, or a cluster's participating agents) and records them in `dag_summary["involved_agents"]` — but then threw that away at storage by hardcoding `agent_ids=[]`.

**Decision.** When `DreamingConfig.per_agent_dream_attribution_enabled` is set, the reflection episode is stored with `agent_ids=list(involved_agents)` instead of `[]`, so `recall_for_agent` (which filters on `agent_ids`) returns it for each dreamer — one episode, multi-owner, recallable by each participant. A reflection with NO involved agents (an emergence/notebook snapshot — genuinely system-level) stays ownerless even when the flag is on (not every reflection has a dreamer). Default **OFF** → `agent_ids=[]` (byte-identical to AD-599); the Captain enables it to turn on the dream-interpretation loop. This is the prerequisite for AD-980c.

**Gates.** `test_ad980b_dream_attribution.py` (5: flag-off keeps reflections ownerless + provenance in dag_summary; flag-on attributes a convergence reflection to its agents and a cluster reflection to its participating agents; an agentless emergence snapshot stays ownerless even when on; default is off) + the AD-599 suite (18) green — the default-off gate keeps every AD-599 `agent_ids == []` assertion intact.

### AD-980a: Reflective recall interpretation — the meaning-making rung above metamemory (Agent self-interpretation epic, #910)

**Context.** Ezri (Counselor) asked whether crew agents can interpret their dreams; the question generalizes to memories and Oracle recall. AD-979 made recall *honest* (the Feeling-of-Knowing signal — do I know this, how sure?); AD-980a adds the rung above it: *meaning* (what do I make of it?). Recalled episodes were injected into context and reasoned over implicitly — there was no first-class act where an agent stands back and interprets its own memories. The mechanism already existed and was pointed elsewhere: `propose_appearance` (AD-721d) does instructions-first LLM reflection over the agent's own state for self-image. AD-980a points that same shape at recalled memories. Prior art: Generative Agents (Park 2023) synthesizes reflections from memory clusters — ProbOS had absorbed Park's retrieval *scoring* (AD-873) but not the reflection *synthesis*; this adds it, plus the honesty bound prior art lacks.

**Decision.** New `CognitiveAgent.interpret_recall(episodes, *, focus="", store=True) -> str | None`: an instructions-first LLM pass that returns a brief first-person interpretation of the agent's OWN recalled episodes, and (via `_store_interpretation_episode`) optionally persists it as an **agent-owned** reflection episode (`agent_ids=[sovereign]`, `MemorySource.REFLECTION`, `[interpretation]`-prefixed reflection, `importance=6`, the interpretation carried as the outcome `response` so the AD selective-encoding gate retains it). Honesty bound (AD-592): the system prompt instructs the agent to ground every statement in the memories shown and to say plainly when they do not support a conclusion; with **no episodes there is nothing to interpret, so it returns `None`** (honest by construction, never invents). The instruction text is gap-regex-safe (does not trip `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE`). Opt-in `CommunicationsConfig.recall_interpretation_enabled` (default **False** — it is a real extra LLM pass, unlike the pure-prompt-text knobs), and the method is not yet wired into the live path (AD-980c will drive it over a per-agent dream). Tier-2: any LLM failure returns `None`.

**Gates.** `test_ad980a_recall_interpretation.py` (9: disabled→None, no-episodes→None honest no-op, enabled produces interpretation with recalled material in the prompt, LLM-failure→None, stored as agent-owned `[interpretation]` REFLECTION with the text in both reflection and outcome response, `store=False` persists nothing, focus reaches the prompt, system+user prompts gap-regex-safe, reflection-only episodes usable). Real `CommunicationsConfig` + recording episodic + scripted fake LLM (no MagicMock).

### AD-977: Group-thread episodic continuity — index the agent's own reply so it can recall group conversations (Natural Conversation epic, #900)

**Context.** Both crew agents flagged (honestly, no confabulation) that recall of GROUP conversations was patchy. Investigation: AD-933a writes a group episode per reply, but the embedded document (`EpisodicMemory._prepare_document`) and the FTS5 sidecar index `user_input` + `reflection` — NOT `outcomes[].response`. The AD-933a group episode set `user_input = "[group chat] <trigger>"` (the Captain's prompt) and **no `reflection`**, so the agent's OWN reply lived only in `outcomes[]` and was never embedded or FTS-indexed. Net: a group episode was findable by the Captain's trigger text but never by the agent's contribution — the group-vs-1:1 gap. (The 1:1 `_store_action_episode` already indexes the response via `reflection="<callsign> handled <intent>: <response>"`.)

**Decision.** Mirror the 1:1 pattern: the AD-933a group episode now sets `reflection="<callsign> said in group chat: <reply[:240]>"`. Because `_prepare_document` and the FTS5 dual-write both index `reflection`, the agent's own room contribution becomes recallable by its own words (dense AND — with AD-979c — keyword). Additive: `user_input` (the trigger) and `outcomes[].response` (the full reply, untruncated to 500) are unchanged, so existing AD-933a anchoring/labeling is byte-identical apart from the added reflection. Tier-2 honest-degrade on the store call is unchanged.

**Gates.** `test_ad977_group_recall.py` (3: reflection carries the agent's reply + names the speaker; reflection is distinct indexable content from the trigger; `outcomes[].response` preserved) + the AD-933a suite (7) green together. Composes with AD-979a/b/c (a group episode that still recalls weakly now also benefits from the hybrid keyword axis and the confidence signal).

### AD-979c + AD-979b: Hybrid dense+sparse retrieval (RRF) + metacognitive control loop (Oracle recall epic, #905, #904)

**Context.** Two follow-ons to AD-979a, both on the recall path. **AD-979c** targets the *vocabulary-mismatch gap*: recall was purely cosine over embeddings, so a memory encoded under different words than the query scored below `relevance_threshold` and was dropped even when relevant. **AD-979b** targets what to *do* about a weak recall: a human, on a Feeling-of-Knowing, keeps searching differently (Nelson & Narens 1990 — the monitor signal drives a control action), where recall previously had no recourse but to report uncertainty.

**AD-979c — hybrid dense+sparse retrieval.** Two pure helpers: `fts_or_query(query)` turns a natural query into an FTS5 OR-of-quoted-keywords MATCH string (so the sparse axis surfaces a memory by ANY shared keyword), and `reciprocal_rank_fusion(rankings, *, k=60)` fuses ranked id lists by `sum 1/(k+rank)` — rank-based, so a cosine ranking and an FTS ranking fuse without score-scale calibration, and a SINGLE ranking is returned in its original order (the byte-identical-when-sparse-empty guarantee). `recall_with_confidence` gains a gated tail: when `hybrid_recall_enabled` and the FTS5 sidecar is present, `_fuse_dense_sparse` unions the dense episode ranking with `keyword_search` (the existing AD-567b FTS axis) via RRF, hydrating sparse-only ids through `get_by_ids`. The Feeling-of-Knowing signal is intentionally left as the DENSE distribution (hybrid changes *which* episodes return, not how confident the cosine recall was). New `MemoryConfig.hybrid_recall_enabled` (default **False** → byte-identical) + `hybrid_rrf_k` (60). Prior art absorbed as patterns (permissive, no vendoring): Mem0's parallel semantic+BM25 fusion, RRF (Cormack 2009).

**AD-979b — metacognitive control loop.** Pure `decide_recall_control(band)` maps the AD-979a monitor band to an action: `strong→accept`, `weak→expand`, `none→abstain` — so only the *invisible miss* triggers work (zero cost on the happy path and on genuine absence). Pure `recall_expansion_variants(query, *, max_n)` produces bounded, deduped re-query variants, highest-value first: a content-word "soup" (query stripped of scaffolding to its content tokens — often embeds closer to a terse stored episode) then the AD-584 question→declarative reformulation. `recall_with_control(query, k, *, max_expansions=1)` runs the monitor (`recall_with_confidence`), and on a `weak` band issues at most `max_expansions` re-queries, adopting a variant only when it is strictly more accessible (higher best similarity) and stopping early at `strong`. Returns `(episodes, confidence, actions)` where `actions` is the audit trail (e.g. `["expand", "requery:weak", "requery:strong"]`) so the agent can report honestly (AD-592): a still-weak/none final band means "I looked, expanded, and remain uncertain," never a fabrication. The mechanism is built + tested but NOT yet wired into the live conversational recall path (a follow-up activation AD, mirroring how `recall_with_confidence` is available but the live path still calls `recall_for_agent`) — the conservative boundary keeps a behavior change observable.

**Gates.** `test_ad979c_hybrid_retrieval.py` (16: pure `fts_or_query` + `reciprocal_rank_fusion` incl. single-ranking identity, plus real-store fusion surfacing a keyword-matched episode the cosine axis missed, flag-off byte-identical) + `test_ad979b_control_loop.py` (15: the pure policy + expansion generator + real-store loop — strong accepts with no expansion, empty store abstains, weak triggers bounded re-query, three-tuple shape). The three AD-979 suites together: **44 passed**. AD-979a's episodic blast (804 passed) already covered the shared recall path; AD-979c adds only a default-off branch and AD-979b only new methods.

### AD-979a: Recall-confidence Feeling-of-Knowing signal — make the invisible miss visible (Oracle recall epic, #903)

**Context.** `EpisodicMemory.recall()` computed `similarity = 1.0 - distance` for every candidate and then *discarded* it (a silent `continue` below `relevance_threshold`), returning only `list[Episode]`. So a caller could not distinguish "I have NOTHING on this" (fast-absence) from "the best match was 0.65, just under the bar" (the *invisible miss*) — the crew (Yeo/Ezri) flagged exactly this as a confidence-calibration gap at a session wrap-up. Cognitive-science framing: a Feeling-of-Knowing (Hart 1965) is *computed from the accessibility* of partial retrieved information (Koriat's accessibility hypothesis, 1993) — which is precisely the similarity distribution `recall()` already had and threw away.

**Decision.** Surface the signal `recall()` already computes. A new frozen `RecallConfidence` dataclass (`band`, `best_similarity`, `candidate_count`, `query`) and a pure `classify_recall_confidence(best_similarity, candidate_count, *, relevance_threshold, weak_floor)` classifier: `candidate_count <= 0` → `none` (fast-absence); `best >= relevance_threshold` → `strong` (== what `recall()` returns); `best >= weak_floor` → `weak` (the invisible miss); else `none` (slow-gap — candidates present but too distant). The band is **accessibility-derived, never self-reported** (the literature's anti-inflation invariant, same discipline as AD-955 outcome-derived trust). New `recall_with_confidence(query, k) -> tuple[list[Episode], RecallConfidence]` is now the single source of truth for the query+filter+rerank path; **`recall()` is a thin byte-identical shim** over it (returns just the episodes), so every existing caller is unchanged. The `candidate_count` split makes the fast-absence vs slow-gap distinction explicit — the slow-gap is the AD-979c hybrid-retrieval (vocabulary-mismatch) case, and a `weak` signal is what AD-979b's metacognitive control loop will act on. New `MemoryConfig.recall_confidence_weak_floor` (default 0.45, above the AD-655 contrastive 0.4 floor), wired through `__main__.py`.

**Gates.** `test_ad979a_recall_confidence.py` (13: the pure classifier across all bands + the fast-absence/slow-gap boundary, plus real-`EpisodicMemory`-on-tmp_path integration proving the signal is consistent with the classifier at the store's own thresholds, `recall()` is a byte-identical shim, empty store = fast-absence, populated store + unrelated query = slow-gap not fast-absence). Episodic/recall regression blast: **804 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed**.

### AD-978: Camera scene-context injected into the group fan-out — the crew can SEE in a group chat (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

**Context.** The Captain reported that the camera feed was invisible to the crew in a group chat, even though the camera→perception→describe pipeline works (the 1:1 chat preview shows live scene descriptions). Root cause (verified): the AD-733a scene-context injection lives ONLY in the 1:1 DM path (`routers/agents.py` prepends `get_or_create_working_memory(agent_id).render_for_prompt()` to the message). The group fan-out (`routers/thread_fanout.py` `_send_one`) never pulled each agent's `VisionWorkingMemory`, so the visual block never reached the dispatched agents' prompts. (AD-916 `vision_messages` is a separate concern — image *attachments* on a message, not the ambient camera.)

**Decision.** Mirror the 1:1 injection into the group fan-out, respecting the multi-agent shape: (1) a new `_maybe_force_describe_frame(runtime)` runs ONCE per round in `_fan_one_round`, before the parallel `asyncio.gather` — the shared camera frame is described once (and `force_describe_current_frame` writes the same observation to every observer's WM), so N speakers don't trigger N redundant describes of the same frame; (2) a new `_render_agent_scene_block(runtime, agent_id)` renders THIS agent's own ring (each agent owns a `VisionWorkingMemory` keyed by `agent_id`) and notes per-agent DM engagement (AD-733c-5, so a group turn doesn't transition the whole mesh), and `_send_one` prepends the block to `params["text"]` (what the LLM receives) while leaving `trigger_body` clean for the episode/pipeline (the stored episode records the Captain's actual message, not the ephemeral scene). Both are gated on `perception.enabled` (Pydantic default **False** → byte-identical when the subsystem is off, exactly the 1:1 gate). BF-294 confabulation guard is preserved: an empty ring renders the non-empty "Camera not active … Do NOT describe what you cannot see" sentinel, never a silent omission, so an agent can't invent a scene. Tier-2 honest-degrade throughout (any failure logs at debug and the round proceeds text-only).

**Gates.** `test_ad978_group_perception.py` (13: the two helpers in isolation — disabled/enabled/empty-ring-sentinel/per-agent/degrade/per-agent-engagement — plus end-to-end through `group_chat_fanout` proving the scene block reaches each dispatched agent's `params["text"]`, force-describe fires once per round not per agent, and byte-identical text when perception is off). Regression blast over fan-out / group-chat / perception / AD-733 vision-context: **410 passed, 0 failed**.

### AD-975 + AD-963a: Turn-taking self-knowledge + broadcast terminator (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

**Context.** The Captain ran a live 3-person room (Captain + Ezri + Yeo) and reviewed the transcript. It validated the recent fixes (AD-967 roster grounding, AD-935/950/951/955 self-regulating turn-taking — the crew read the floor, hand off by name, and don't address absent peers). It also surfaced two refinements, both built here. The transcript was captured as the **first AD-956 calibration data point** on #892 (the threshold work stays deferred — N=3 has not yet exposed the collision seam, only a correct prediction of it).

**AD-975 — crew turn-taking self-knowledge.** In the test the crew reasoned accurately about reading the floor but assumed possible **simultaneity** ("two of us could respond before either sees the other's reply"). In reality `group_chat_fanout` is sequential + synchronous: one speaker per turn, each later speaker receives every prior reply in full before its own turn, so two crew never answer the same point at once. **Decision (instructions-first, DP#6):** extend the AD-935/967 `_conversational_group_chat_protocol` hook with a "How turn-taking works here" paragraph teaching the real mechanism — turns are sequential (you see completed replies, never simultaneous), collisions are structurally impossible so build with confidence on prior turns, there is no live "typing" cue from a peer (a turn arrives when they finish), and addressing a colleague by name invites them to take the next turn (the AD-951 hand-off). Gated on `is_group_chat` (1:1 unaffected); composes with the AD-967 roster + AD-935 decline guidance; gap-regex-safe. Tests: `test_ad975_turn_taking_self_knowledge.py` (7, pure hook assertions).

**AD-963a — broadcast turn-mode terminator.** The AD-935 cascade stops at `max_agent_rounds` or the convergence gate — correct for a DISCUSSION, but wrong for a BROADCAST ("what do you ALL think?") where the Captain wants EACH relevant crew member to answer once. In the test only 2 of 3 agents got turns because the round cap, not completeness, bounded a plural ask. **Decision (the ratified AD-963 recommendation, build-split part a):** a pure `classify_broadcast(text)` cue detector (conservative — only clear plural-address cues like "you all" / "everyone" / "each of you" / "whole team" match; everything ambiguous stays DISCUSSION) drives a broadcast terminator in `group_chat_fanout`: when a broadcast is detected, the cascade round-robins every crew participant **exactly once** (cumulative exclude of all prior speakers, relevance-ordered by the existing facilitator rank, each seeing prior answers), naturally bounded by the participant count — bypassing the discussion cap + the AD-961 address-extension budget. Directed addresses remain AD-951's job; the default (Discussion) classification is byte-identical to AD-935/961. New `GroupChatConfig.broadcast_terminator_enabled` (Pydantic default False; `system.yaml` enables it). The Broadcast department weight tilt (AD-963b) is deferred for a live look, as is parallel round-0 (deprioritized — agents must see each other to avoid echo; genuine independence is AD-958b's quorum, for decisions not chat). Tests: `test_ad963a_broadcast_terminator.py` (8: classifier match/miss/non-string; broadcast lets all crew speak once; discussion capped; flag-off byte-identical).

**Gates.** AD-975 + AD-963a suites + AD-935/951/955/961/967 cascade regressions green in isolation; broad backend blast green; full UI unchanged (no UI change). The trust-ledger-write core (AD-958), the AD-956 threshold, the AD-963b weight tilt, and the AD-954a dedicated window all remain correctly deferred to further live observation.

### AD-972 → AD-974: Meeting/call UX polish — faster TTS start, one mic, resizable video (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

**Context.** The Captain tested the improved group-chat/call experience and reported three issues: (1) a long delay between seeing the crew's messages and hearing TTS; (2) two microphone buttons in a call (only one is wanted, the one next to Send); (3) no way to enlarge the video portraits.

**AD-972 — cut the seen-message → TTS-start delay.** The meeting voice path spoke each reply only after `await resolveProfile(agent_id)` — a cold `GET /api/agent/{id}/profile` fetch — and `speakResponse` then probed `/api/avatars/tts/status` before the Piper synth POST. So the FIRST utterance was gated on two network round-trips before synthesis even began, and every subsequent speaker paid the profile fetch as an audible gap. **Decision (frontend only):** (1) `useMeetingVoice` now prewarms when the meeting opens — it calls a new `prewarmTts()` (exported from `voice.ts`, idempotent over the cached one-time probe) and prefetches every room participant's voice profile (passed as `participantAgentIds` from `ProfileChatTab`), so by the time replies arrive (seconds later, after LLM generation) the profile cache is warm and the status probe is done. (2) `createVoiceProfileResolver` now caches the in-flight PROMISE (not just the resolved value) so the prewarm and the per-utterance resolve dedupe to one fetch. (3) `speakReplies` also kicks off all reply profile fetches up front. Net: the first agent speaks as soon as the synth returns (no profile/status round-trip first) and inter-speaker gaps are gone. The Piper synth latency itself is server-side and inherent. Tests: `useMeetingVoice.test.tsx` +2 (prewarm fires on open / not when inactive); `meetingVoice.test.ts` resolver cache contract preserved.

**AD-973 — one microphone, next to Send.** A live call showed TWO mic affordances: the composer dictation mic (the `MicIndicator` button by Send) AND a separate centered push-to-talk (`MeetingMicButton` + `useMeetingMic`, AD-922). Both captured one VAD-bounded utterance and auto-submitted via `sendText`; the composer mic also has the BF-300 echo guard and works in every context. **Decision (frontend only):** stop rendering the redundant `MeetingMicButton` (and drop its `useMeetingMic` hook + imports) so a call shows exactly one mic — the one next to Send, as the Captain asked. The `MeetingMicButton`/`useMeetingMic` files (and their standalone tests) are left in place as a tested, reusable PTT primitive. No behavior lost — voice input in a call still flows through the composer mic.

**AD-974 — drag-to-resize the video gallery.** The meeting gallery slots were a fixed 120×160 (112×132 portrait). **Decision (frontend only):** `AvatarSlot` and `CaptainSlot` take a `scale` prop that multiplies the portrait box, wrapper, and caption width; `MeetingView` holds a `galleryScale` (clamped [1,3], persisted to `localStorage` as `hxi_meeting_gallery_scale`) and renders a drag handle (`ns-resize`, amber grip) BELOW the gallery — dragging DOWN enlarges the portraits (UP shrinks), at 220px per +1.0 scale. The handle sits outside the scaled content so the screen-pixel drag math is unaffected, and the scale restores on reopen. Tests: `MeetingView.test.tsx` +4 (handle renders, drag-down enlarges + persists, clamps to [1,3], restores persisted scale).

**Gates.** Full UI suite **1426 passed / 1 skipped** (+6 over the 1420 baseline), `npm run build` clean, Playwright e2e **4/4**. No backend change.

### AD-966 → AD-971: Agent-initiated group-chat bug cluster — make agent-started rooms first-class conversations (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

**Context.** The Captain live-tested agent-initiated group chats (AD-924/925) and surfaced a cluster of six bugs that are all facets of one reality: agent-initiated rooms could be *created* but were never wired into the live conversation loop the Captain-driven path uses. Each is a distinct, sequentially-numbered AD; they ship together because they are one user-visible failure ("the agents can't actually hold a group conversation they start themselves").

**AD-966 — ≥2-participant floor (Bug: a room with an absent peer).** An agent emitted `[GROUP_CHAT title="…" @peer]` where no named ref resolved to a crew peer (the peer was addressed only in prose, or the callsign was unknown/hallucinated — e.g. "Vance"). `AgentGroupChatService.create_group_chat` minted a room with ONLY the creator — an incoherent 1-participant "group chat" talking to an absent peer. **Decision:** after resolving participants, if `len(final) < 2` return `GroupChatCreateResult(ok=False, error="no_participant_resolved")` instead of creating the room. The service is the right chokepoint — it guards all three callers (proactive AD-924, crew_executor AD-925 task rooms, the bus `handle_intent`); the AD-925 task-room path always passes ≥2 crew so it is unaffected; the proactive path already records a `group_chat_suppressed` action. Tests: `test_ad966_group_chat_participant_floor.py` (9, BF-287 real store); 10 obsolete-contract AD-918 tests (whose premise was a creator-only room) updated to the new ≥2 contract.

**AD-967 — present-participant room roster (Bug: agents address absent peers).** In a group chat the agents had no idea who was actually present — they addressed peers who were never invited (asking "Sentinel" a question in a room Sentinel was not in) and assumed a peer named in prose had been added; the conversation stalled waiting on an absent member. **Decision:** inject a roster of PRESENT participants into each dispatched agent's group prompt by extending the AD-935 `_conversational_group_chat_protocol` hook — "Present in this room: X, Y, and Z. … address only present members … to bring in a colleague, ask the Captain to add them" — gap-regex-safe. The roster rides a new fan-out param `room_roster`, built once in `group_chat_fanout` from `_resolve_callsigns(agent_ids)` (+ "the Captain" when joined) and threaded through `_fan_one_round` at both call sites. Honest-degrade: absent roster ⇒ byte-identical to pre-AD-967. Tests: `test_ad967_room_roster.py` (12: roster grammar, address guidance, gap-safety, backward-compat, end-to-end delivery, Captain-inclusion).

**AD-968 — the Captain auto-joins a room they post into (Bug: "Join" on chats I'm already in).** Posting a Captain message never added `captain` to the participant set, so `captainJoined` stayed false and the sidebar kept showing the Join button on a room the Captain was actively conversing in. **Decision:** in the `POST /messages` handler, on a Captain post into a GROUP (≥2 crew) OR an agent-created room, `store.add_participant(thread_id, "captain")` before fan-out. Scoped to group/agent-created rooms — the 1:1 default thread keeps its single-participant invariant that the task-promote (`assigned_to` inference) and auto-name paths rely on. Idempotent. Tests: `test_ad968_captain_autojoin.py` (5: group join, idempotent, agent-room join, 1:1 NOT joined, 1:1 stays single-participant).

**AD-969 — add-participant mints a new thread ONLY for the 1:1 home DM (Bug: "adding Vance made a new chat").** The AD-937 add-control branched on crew count: `< 2 crew` opened the NewChatModal (minting a SEPARATE thread). That convert was designed for the Captain's per-agent 1:1 default thread, but it also fired for agent-created rooms (which often have 1 crew), so adding a member to an agent room minted a brand-new chat instead of joining the existing one. **Decision (frontend):** branch on `metadata.is_default` (the Captain's 1:1 home DM) — ONLY the home DM mints via the seeded NewChatModal; EVERY other room (group OR agent-created) adds the participant in place via `addParticipant` (the Teams behavior). Tests: `GroupChatHeader.test.tsx` updated (is_default 1:1 opens the seeded picker; agent-created room adds in place).

**AD-970 — agent-initiated kickoff (Bug: an agent opens a room but the invited crew never reply).** An agent's opening message is persisted as `role="agent"`, and the AD-914 fan-out gates on `role=="captain"`, so an agent-created room sat silent until the Captain posted. **Decision:** fan an agent's opening out to the other participants — the agent-initiated analogue of a Captain turn — by reusing `group_chat_fanout` with a new `opener_id` param so the opener is excluded from round 0 (it just spoke). Triggered from the proactive create path (`_extract_and_execute_group_chats` → new `_kickoff_group_chat` helper) when the agent opened with a first message. Gated on `GroupChatConfig.agent_initiated_kickoff_enabled` (Pydantic default False; `system.yaml` enables it), bounded by the SAME AD-935 backstops (cap / convergence / `[NO_RESPONSE]` / max_agent_rounds). Lifts the deliberate AD-918 "no auto-reply on create" boundary now that the bounded cascade exists. Tests: `test_ad970_agent_kickoff.py` (5: round-0 opener exclusion, no-opener parity, gated-on fires, gated-off no-op, honest-degrade on missing store).

**AD-971 — added participants survive close + reopen (Bug: added crew vanish on reopen, list row stale).** The Captain added Lyra + Sentinel, closed the chat, reopened it — they were gone, and the CHATS list row never updated. Root cause: `ChatsPanel.handleOpen` called `setChatThread(staleListObject)` using the local `listThreads()` snapshot, which CLOBBERED the freshly-added participants in the store (the backend *had* persisted them via `addParticipant`). **Decision (frontend):** (1) new `getThread(id)` wrapper (`GET /api/threads/{id}`); `handleOpen` is now async and re-fetches the thread's CURRENT persisted state before hydrating — authoritative, and robust across a full page reload. (2) ChatsPanel rows prefer whichever thread version is fresher by `last_active_at` (the live `chatThreads` store vs the list snapshot), so a header add reflects in the sidebar row immediately. Tier-2: a failed fetch falls back to the passed thread. The history-context ask is already satisfied — `_build_session_history` feeds recent thread turns to every participant on their turn, so a newly-added member is contextualized on its next reply. Tests: `ChatsPanel.reopenPersist.test.tsx` (3: backend hydrate no-clobber, fetch-failure fallback, fresher-row merge); 3 ChatsPanel suites updated for the now-async open.

**Gates.** Python: AD-966/967/968/970 suites + AD-918/924/935/955/914/913 regressions green in isolation. UI: AD-969 GroupChatHeader (22) + AD-971 ChatsPanel suites (45) green. Full gates + commit follow.

### AD-958a: Exploration / anti-rich-get-richer term — a domain-relevant newcomer is surfaced to earn trust (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#894)

**Context.** AD-958 (#894) is the conversational trust learning loop. Its sub-part **AD-958a** is the one piece the issue says needs no live calibration and writes nothing to the trust ledger — so it is the safe, high-value first build. The prior-art survey (and my own observation of the Ezri+Yeo room) found that trust/confidence-weighted speaker selection risks **monopolisation**: a high-trust agent keeps being surfaced and a low-trust but domain-relevant agent never gets a chance to *earn* trust. The **Minimal Authority** governance axiom requires earned trust with a path for everyone.

**Decision (backend only, `chat_facilitator.py` + `config.py` + `system.yaml`).** Add a deterministic exploration bonus to the pure `ChatFacilitator.rank()`: `weight_exploration × department_relevance × (1 − trust)`. This is **optimism under uncertainty** (UCB-style), not ε-greedy randomness — the facilitator stays pure and deterministic (load-bearing for testability + reproducibility). The shape encodes the intent precisely: the bonus grows with *relevance* (gated on `department_relevance`, so an off-topic agent is never boosted) and with *un-provenness* (`1 − trust`, so a fully-trusted agent already carried by the trust term gets ~0). A domain-relevant newcomer is surfaced to earn trust; a proven agent isn't double-counted. Bounded **below** the mention weight (`weight_exploration = 0.15` live vs `weight_mention = 0.40`), so a direct address (AD-951 rule 1a) always still wins. New `GroupChatConfig.weight_exploration` (Pydantic default **0.0** = off, ranking byte-identical to pre-AD-958a; `system.yaml` sets 0.15 for the live system). It rides the existing `factors` dict (`factors["exploration"]`) for diagnostics.

**Why this is safe to build before the live observation.** It touches ONLY the facilitator ranking — it never calls `record_outcome`, so there is zero risk of poisoning the load-bearing trust ledger (the issue's chief constraint). The trust-ledger *write* core (correction/endorsement → `record_outcome(source="conversation")`) is deliberately deferred until the live Ezri+Yeo room can ground it. AD-958a only changes *who is advised/surfaced*, bounded and default-off, with all AD-915 backstops (cap, convergence, `[NO_RESPONSE]`) intact.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad958a_exploration.py` — 8 tests (pure facilitator, no fixtures): off-by-default byte-identical; surfaces the unproven domain-relevant agent over the proven one; ~0 for a high-trust agent; 0 for an irrelevant agent; never beats a direct mention (the AD-951 bound); the exact `w×dep×(1−trust)` formula is deterministic on re-run; `from_config` reads the weight; config default is 0.0. 48 passed across AD-958a + AD-915 facilitator + AD-955 room-awareness; group-chat/config blast green. No UI change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-954: "Start call" reframing — the meeting toggle is a call (Teams mental model) (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#890)

**Context.** #890 asks for a first-class group/call surface: a dedicated thread-keyed window + a "Start call" step that turns the chat into a video call. AD-965 already delivered the dedicated-room *identity* (neutral group title + Chat-only surface, decoupled from the host agent's profile chrome), and AD-920/921/947/949 already shipped the live "meeting" (avatar gallery + per-agent call voice + face framing + call audio). The remaining naming gap: the control was labelled "Start/End meeting," which doesn't match the Captain's Teams mental model ("turn this chat into a call").

**Decision (frontend only, `GroupChatHeader.tsx`).** Reframe the existing meeting toggle (already a video-camera glyph, already wired to `set_meeting_active` → the AD-947 gallery + AD-949 call audio) from "Start/End meeting" to **"Start/End call"** (`aria-label` + `title`). The `data-testid="meeting-toggle"`, the persisted `metadata.meeting_active` flag, the AD-923 end-of-meeting transcript marker, and all wiring are byte-identical — this is a label change that aligns the surface with the call mental model. The underlying "meeting" terminology stays in the backend flag/marker (no migration).

**Scope note (the larger AD-954 piece remains).** A fully separate group window keyed by `thread.id` and decoupled from `activeProfileAgent` (so a group needs no host agent set at all) is a larger architectural refactor that #890 itself says to sequence last. AD-965 already achieves the first-class *visual* surface (the panel presents as a neutral room, not a host profile), so the user-visible Teams feel is delivered; the host-agent *binding* refactor is tracked as the remaining #890 sub-task (forward marker AD-954a). This AD closes the "Start call" + dedicated-identity portion.

**Tests + gates.** `GroupChatHeader.meeting.test.tsx` +1 (the toggle reads "Start call" inactive / "End call" active); the AD-941 `group-chat-open.spec.ts` e2e updated to assert `aria-label="Start call"`. Full UI suite **1416 passed / 1 skipped**, `npm run build` clean, all **4 Playwright e2e passed**. No backend change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-965: Neutral, nameable group surface — a group is a room, not the host agent's profile (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#898)

**Problem (Captain group-chat test, 2026-06-10).** Starting a group with Ezri + Yeo opened *Ezri's* `AgentProfilePanel` — the title bar read "Ezri (Counselor)" with her department dot, and the 6 agent-scoped tabs (Chat / Work / Memory / Profile / Health / Self-image) framed the room as one participant's profile with a second person bolted on. A group should be a neutral, nameable surface like a Microsoft Teams group chat.

**What already existed (AD-917).** The `GroupChatHeader` (rendered inside `ProfileChatTab`) already shipped the editable room title (click-to-rename → `patchThread` → `set_title(lock=True)`), the participant avatar strip, add/remove participant, the meeting toggle, and the AD-949 in-call mute. The `ChatThread.title` field + `PATCH /api/threads/{id}` endpoint already exist, and `chatDisplayName` already derives the Teams-style "callsign, callsign" name (honoring a Captain-locked custom title). So AD-965 is the **surfacing** layer, not new plumbing.

**Decision (frontend only, `AgentProfilePanel.tsx`).** Detect the group context: when `activeProfileThreadId` resolves to a thread that `isGroupChat` (≥2 crew), the panel is a ROOM. (1) **Identity** — the title bar shows the group title (`chatDisplayName`, Teams-style or the Captain's locked name) with a neutral dot, instead of the host agent's name + department framing. (2) **Tabs** — `visibleTabs` collapses to Chat-only (the work/profile/health/memory/self_image tabs are agent-scoped and meaningless for a room); `effectiveTab` falls back to `chat` in group mode. The `GroupChatHeader` inside the chat tab still owns the participant strip + rename + meeting controls (no duplication). A 1:1 (no group thread) is byte-identical — the agent identity and full tab set are unchanged.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/AgentProfilePanel.groupSurface.test.tsx` — 4 render tests (R3F/voice mocked per the AD-721d pattern): group title shows the participant-derived name (not the host agent); a Captain-locked custom title ("Bridge Sync") wins; the tab bar collapses to Chat-only on a group; a 1:1 keeps the agent identity + full tab set. Full UI suite **1415 passed / 1 skipped** (+4 over the 1411 baseline, zero regressions), `npm run build` clean. No backend change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-962: Typing indicator during backend generation — fill the dead air before the first reply (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#896)

**Problem.** AD-960 paces the *reveal* of crew replies at human speed, but the backend group cascade (`group_chat_fanout`) takes ~10–30s of real LLM time to produce ANY reply, and the `POST /api/threads/{id}/messages` call is fully synchronous — so from the instant the Captain sends until the first reply lands there is NO on-screen signal at all. That silent window is the most "is it broken?" moment in the experience; the AD-960 pacing improvement is undercut by it.

**Decision (frontend only, additive — extends AD-952).** Reuse the AD-952 `typingAgent` store slice + `TypingIndicator` component for a generic pre-reply beat. (1) `TypingIndicator` gains an optional `verb: 'typing' | 'thinking'` (default `'typing'`) so the label reads honestly — the crew is being *asked*, no reply exists yet, so it's *thinking*, not typing. (2) The `typingAgent` slice gains an optional `verb` field (still session-scoped, no localStorage). (3) `ProfileChatTab.sendText` group branch sets `setTypingAgent({threadId, agentId:'', callsign:'The crew', verb:'thinking'})` the instant it enters the ≥2-crew path, BEFORE the fetch — so "The crew is thinking…" shows within a frame of send. It is cleared the moment the first reply arrives (right after the AD-960 `setSending(false)`), at which point the text path's `revealRepliesProgressively` immediately re-sets a per-agent "{callsign} is typing" beat (the AD-960 reveal), and the meeting path leaves it cleared (AD-921 voice + AD-923 speaking indicator pace the crew there). The error path also clears it so it never sticks after a failed send.

**Scope.** v1 is a generic whole-crew "thinking" beat (we don't know who will respond first until the backend runs the facilitator). Naming the likely first responder via a pre-flight facilitator rank is a v2 forward marker (AD-962a), and true streaming reply delivery remains AD-935a. The indicator's render site (threadId-guarded, after the message list) is unchanged from AD-952.

**Tests + gates.** `TypingIndicator.test.tsx` +2 (default verb "typing"; "thinking" verb renders + aria-label), `useStore.typingAgent.test.ts` +1 (the verb round-trips through the slice). Full UI suite **1411 passed / 1 skipped** (+3 over the 1408 baseline, zero regressions), `npm run build` clean. No backend change → no pytest. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-961: Cascade-extend-on-address — a directed peer hand-off is always answered (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#895)

**Problem (Captain group-chat test, 2026-06-10).** AD-951 routes a directed address ("Ezri, …" / "@ezri …") to that peer as the next cascade speaker, but only WITHIN `group_chat.max_agent_rounds` (default 2). When the address landed in the LAST normal cascade round, the addressed peer never got a turn — the Captain had to manually re-prompt ("Ezri, can you respond to Yeo?"). A hand-off that goes unanswered is the opposite of natural: a human who is directly asked a question answers it.

**Decision (backend only, `thread_fanout.py` + `config.py`).** The bounded cascade in `group_chat_fanout` was a fixed `for _ in range(max_agent_rounds)`; it is now a `while` loop with a round counter that grants up to `GroupChatConfig.max_address_extensions` (new, default **1**) EXTRA rounds PAST the cap, each consumed only by a fresh **answerable** directed address, so a hand-off is always answered — bounded so a chain of mutual hand-offs (Ezri→Yeo→Ezri…) can't ping-pong forever (the absolute ceiling is `max_agent_rounds + max_address_extensions` cascade rounds). Within the normal cap the loop is byte-identical to AD-935/AD-951 (no answerability gate — the existing rounds run regardless). The extension is **only** meaningful with `agent_next_speaker_selection_enabled` on, so `max_addr_ext` is forced to 0 when that flag is off, and the default of 1 never changes a zero-config boot (the whole cascade is off there).

**The answerability gate (the subtle correctness bit a test caught).** `extract_directed_callsign` matches any leading comma/colon word, so a conversational opener like "Agreed, the variance is fine." or "Well, …" yields a phantom callsign ("agreed"/"well"). In AD-951 that is harmless (it hard-includes nobody downstream), but using the mere *presence* of an address to decide whether to EXTEND would let an opener spuriously burn an extension round. So the extension fires only when an addressed callsign resolves (via `_resolve_callsigns`, lower-cased) to a REAL participant agent_id that is NOT in the round's own speakers — a peer who can actually take the turn. Tier-2: an empty resolution map means no extension ever fires (degrades to pre-AD-961).

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad961_cascade_extend.py` — 6 tests, BF-287 discipline (real `ChatThreadStore`/`IntentBus`/registry, scripted handlers, real `GroupChatConfig`): address-in-last-round-answered-via-extension (the core fix, Scout→Ops→Scout); extension-disabled-drops-the-handoff (`max_address_extensions=0` == pre-AD-961); mutual-hand-offs-bounded-no-pingpong (every reply addresses the other → bounded at exactly `max_rounds+ext`); extension-inert-without-next-speaker-selection (forced 0 when the flag is off); no-address-in-last-round-does-not-extend (the false-opener guard — a leading "Agreed," does NOT extend); config default == 1. 37 passed across the AD-961 + AD-951 + AD-935 cascade suites; group-chat blast (fanout/thread/ad914/915/933/935/948/951/955/961/chat/config) green. No UI change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### BF-615 + BF-616 + AD-964: three group-chat test fixes — voice cutoff, [NO_RESPONSE] leak, per-height avatar centering (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

Three Captain-reported issues from a 2026-06-10 group-chat test, shipped together (all small, all in the group-chat surface). A fourth issue — the group window is bound to the host agent's profile instead of a neutral nameable surface — is filed as a design issue (AD-965, #898) rather than built.

**BF-615 — voice cutoff on long/chained replies (frontend, `ui/src/audio/meetingVoice.ts`).** The AD-921 meeting voice sequencer awaits each utterance's TTS `'end'` event, with a FIXED 20s per-utterance safety timeout for the case where TTS is unavailable and `'end'` never fires. But a long crew reply (~180 words ≈ 60–70s of speech) runs well past 20s, so the timer fired mid-utterance, the sequencer advanced to the next reply, and that reply's `speakResponse` called `speechSynthesis.cancel()` — truncating the still-speaking prior one. The LAST reply has no successor to cancel it, so it completed: exactly the Captain's "every reply cut off except the last." Fix: a new pure `computeUtteranceTimeout(text)` scales the cap with word count at a conservative slow TTS rate (`UTTERANCE_MS_PER_WORD=460`, ~130 wpm) × `UTTERANCE_HEADROOM=1.5`, floored at the old `UTTERANCE_TIMEOUT_FLOOR_MS=20000` (so short replies keep the 20s net). `_speakAndWait` uses `deps.utteranceTimeoutMs ?? computeUtteranceTimeout(reply.text)` — real speech still resolves early on `'end'`; the cap only fires when `'end'` genuinely never arrives, now sized to the actual reply. +4 Vitest (`meetingVoice.test.ts`): floor for short/empty, scales-above-floor for a 180-word reply, monotonic growth, option overrides.

**BF-616 — [NO_RESPONSE] leaked into the transcript (backend, `src/probos/routers/thread_fanout.py`).** The group fan-out decline check matched only a reply that was EXACTLY the marker (`reply_text.strip().upper().replace("[","").replace("]","") == "NO_RESPONSE"`). But models routinely EXPLAIN their decline in prose and then append `[NO_RESPONSE]` instead of emitting the bare marker — so "prose + marker" slipped the equality check and the marker (plus the decline-meta prose) leaked into the visible room (Ezri's "…I'll let that question breathe rather than pile on. [NO_RESPONSE]"). Fix: a module-level `_NO_RESPONSE_RE = re.compile(r"\[NO_RESPONSE\]", re.IGNORECASE)` and a substring check (`_NO_RESPONSE_RE.search(reply_text)`), matching the established `proactive.py` contract (`"[NO_RESPONSE]" in response_text`) — any decline marker anywhere suppresses the WHOLE reply (a human who decides not to respond says nothing). +2 pytest (`test_ad935_group_reactivity.py`): prose-plus-marker fully suppressed (neither marker nor prose reaches the transcript), case-insensitive marker suppressed.

**AD-964 — per-height avatar head centering (frontend, `CrewVRM.tsx` + `MeetingView.tsx`).** AD-947 framed the gallery camera at a FIXED face height (1.42m) for every avatar, so crew of different statures were cropped inconsistently (a tall avatar showed mid-chest, a short one too much headroom). Fix: `CrewVRM` gains an optional `onHeadY` callback that measures the posed scene's bounding-box crown (top-of-head, hair included; computed AFTER the A-pose + VRM0 rotation, local-Y == world-Y since each slot renders at the origin) and reports it once after load (Tier-2 — any failure skips the callback and the slot keeps default framing). `MeetingView.AvatarSlot` holds the reported `headTopY` in state; `FaceFraming` now takes a per-avatar `targetY` (crown − `_HEAD_CENTER_DROP` 0.12 = face center), positions the camera level with it and aims there, defaulting to ~1.42 until measured (prior framing preserved). MeetingView test mock camera extended with `position.set`. UI suite 1408 passed / 1 skipped (+4 BF-615), `npm run build` clean; group-chat pytest blast 576 passed. Forward marker: AD-965 (#898) neutral nameable group surface. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-960: Human-paced group-chat reveal — think-time + 60 wpm typing, and free the composer during the reveal (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

**Problem (Captain group-chat test, 2026-06-09).** AD-952 paced the group-reply reveal, but the cadence was a fast char-based beat (`[360,2400]ms`) tuned to "not all at once," not to "reads like a human." The Captain's spec: a crew reply should arrive at roughly human speed — a brief think-time, then a "typing" beat proportional to length at ~60 wpm. Separately, the composer was disabled for the WHOLE reveal (`disabled={sending}`), which at the old fast pace was a few seconds but at human pace would lock input for 20–40s.

**Decision (frontend only, additive — refines AD-952).** (1) `ui/src/chat/staggerReplies.ts` timing model reworked from char-based to a two-part word-based model with exported single-source constants: `computeTypingDelay(text)` now estimates composing time at `TYPING_MS_PER_WORD = 1000` (60 wpm), clamped `[TYPING_MIN_MS 800, TYPING_MAX_MS 9000]`; a new pure `computeProcessingDelay(index)` returns the think-time beat — `PROCESSING_FIRST_MS = 5000` for the first revealed reply (the crew reading the Captain's message), `PROCESSING_CASCADE_MS = 2500` for later reactions in an already-engaged exchange. `revealRepliesProgressively` shows the "{callsign} is typing" indicator for the WHOLE `processing + typing` window (no dead air), then clears it the instant the message lands, then appends — and it counts the revealed-index over NON-empty replies so an empty leading reply doesn't consume the longer first beat. (2) `ProfileChatTab.sendText` group branch calls `setSending(false)` the moment `per_agent_replies` arrives — the composer is released so the Captain can read and reply WHILE the reveal paces in the background, instead of being locked for the full (now human-speed) reveal; the reveal is still awaited so the AD-921 meeting-voice ordering is unchanged, and the `finally` `setSending(false)` stays as an idempotent error-path safety.

**Why sequential, not parallel.** The reveal stays one-at-a-time in AD-915 facilitator order. This is temporally correct for the current relay cascade (with `max_speakers_per_turn=1`, the second agent is reacting to the first, so it MUST come after), and the Captain's own observation is that sequential is often *better* than parallel — it forces each speaker to "listen" (see the prior turn) before responding, avoiding the human group-chat failure where someone answers too fast. True parallel round-0 responses are deferred to the turn-order design issue (#897, AD-963) rather than built here.

**Tests + gates.** `staggerReplies.test.ts` reworked to the new model: word-based `computeTypingDelay` (60 wpm, clamps, overrides), `computeProcessingDelay` (first > cascade, overrides), and reveal-order asserting the new `typing → clear → append` per-reply sequence plus the first-reply-waits-longer and empty-leading-reply-doesn't-consume-first-beat invariants — 19 tests. Full UI suite **1404 passed / 1 skipped** (+7 over the 1397 baseline, zero regressions), `npm run build` clean. No backend change. The values are exported constants so the feel is trivially tunable. Forward markers: AD-961 cascade-extend-on-address (#895), AD-962 typing indicator during backend generation (#896), AD-963 group-chat turn-order policy (#897). COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-959: Lean shutdown consolidation — defer LLM-bound idle steps so shutdown never trips the AD-820 partial marker

**Problem (observed in production, 2026-06-09).** A packaged-instance shutdown stamped `shutdown_status.json` with `consolidation_result=partial, note="phase1_elapsed=39.0s"`, which AD-820 treats as not-clean → the next normal boot refuses with `UncleanShutdownDetected` (SystemExit 3) until `--force-unclean`. Root cause: the Tier-3 shutdown handler called the FULL `DreamingEngine.dream_cycle()` under the `shutdown_consolidation_timeout_s` 30s budget. `dream_cycle` is the 15-step idle-time pipeline, and at real episode volume its **LLM-bound stages** — Step 7 procedure extraction (one model call *per* success cluster), 7b evolution, 7c negative extraction, 7c-2 failure distillation, 7e observational learning, Step 11 spaced-retrieval therapy — routed through the model proxy and overran 30s. The cancelled mid-flight cycle is exactly the failure mode AD-820 was built to flag, and historically the half-written ChromaDB collection tore the HNSW index (#750). The marker even recorded a procedure (`vision_observation_collaborative_workflow`) born mid-shutdown — proof Step 7 was actively grinding when the budget blew. As episode volume grows (the active `events.db` is ~82MB) this recurs on every sleep/wake shutdown.

**Why the full cycle was never needed at shutdown.** Episodes are already persisted at creation time (BF-207); shutdown only needs the cheap learning-weight updates. Per the BF-207 design note, "partial consolidation is fine — episodes are already stored... the micro_dream handles incremental consolidation." Steps 6–15 (clustering, procedure extraction, metrics) are pure idle-time optimization that re-runs on the next dream cycle — running them inside a hard shutdown budget was unintended scope inherited from reusing `dream_cycle()` as the single consolidation entry point.

**Decision (backend only, additive).** A new `DreamingEngine.consolidate_for_shutdown() -> DreamReport` runs ONLY the in-memory, non-LLM steps the shutdown path needs — Step 0 micro-dream Hebbian replay, Step 2 weight prune, Step 3 trust consolidation — and SKIPS every LLM-bound and Chroma-writing idle step. It performs **no episodic-collection writes** (it reads `recent()` for trust, never `store()`), so it completes in well under a second and lets the subsequent `episodic_memory.stop()` close the index cleanly. Honest-degrade throughout (each step wrapped; a failure logs and the rest still run) because a clean `DreamReport` return is what lets the shutdown handler stamp a `full`/clean marker. `startup/shutdown.py` Tier-3 swaps `engine.dream_cycle()` → `engine.consolidate_for_shutdown()`; the BF-303 shield, the 30s `wait_for` (now a safety net the lean path won't hit), and the AD-820 marker logic are otherwise untouched. The deferred idle-time learning is not lost — it runs on the next normal dream cycle.

**Tests.** `tests/test_ad959_shutdown_light_consolidation.py` — 10 tests, BF-287 discipline (real `HebbianRouter` / `TrustNetwork` / `DreamingConfig` + a real `_FakeEpisodicMemory` stub and a `_RecordingLLMClient`, NOT MagicMock): returns a `DreamReport`; **never calls the LLM even with success clusters**; **makes no episodic writes** (the torn-HNSW guarantee); real trust boost for a success-dominant agent; prunes below-threshold weights; micro-dream strengthens the replayed pathway; empty-memory zeros; honest-degrade when `recent()` raises; does not invoke `dream_cycle`; and a source-level wiring guard asserting `engine.consolidate_for_shutdown()` is present and `engine.dream_cycle()` is gone from the shutdown path. Two obsolete-contract shutdown-ordering tests updated to the new method name (the ordering invariant — consolidation before episodic close; close → stop_gracefully → consolidation — is preserved): `test_bf207_…::test_dream_consolidation_before_episodic_stop`, `test_bf296_…::test_phase_a_runs_before_stop_gracefully`. Blast radius (dream/shutdown/consolidat/ad820/ad828/bf207/bf303/ad825/bf296/bf602/ad959/ad551/ad567/ad568/ad572/ad574/ad428b/ad609/ad541c) green. No UI change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-955: Advisory room awareness — the facilitator as a sense organ, not a director (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

**Idea (Captain + Counselor Ezri, weighted-trust frame).** Each agent's turn carries a confidence-weighted read of what the *room* needs next, and that weight shifts with who's shown relevant expertise, who's been dominating, who's been quiet too long. The social truth: the one who's been talking a lot feels the pull to hold back; the domain expert feels the pull to speak up; and an agent that recognizes a peer has higher authority *here* can defer gracefully — not "I have nothing to add," but "Forge's signal is stronger here, I'll let that land."

**Problem this fixes — a backstop doing a director's job.** The `ChatFacilitator` (AD-915) ALREADY computes exactly this weighting every round (`SpeakerScore.factors`: mention 0.40 / recency 0.25 / department 0.25 / trust 0.10) — but it was thrown away after gating. Today an unselected agent isn't asked to defer, it's *silenced*; turn-taking in the Ezri+Yeo room isn't the agents choosing to alternate, it's `max_speakers_per_turn=1` *forcing* it. A safety cap is doing a director's job (works at 2 agents, produces "one speaks, rest mute" at 5). The fix: **determinism in PERCEPTION is fine; determinism in AGENCY is what feels robotic.** Keep the deterministic backstops (cap, convergence, max rounds), but move the *driver* into the agents' reasoning.
