**Decision (instructions-first, advisory — NO dispatch change).** Surface the facilitator's per-speaker ranking to the dispatched speaker as an ADVISORY signal; the agent reasons over it. (1) Pure `chat_facilitator.build_room_signal(...)`: from the ranking + recent authorship it yields a per-agent dict — `recent_share`/`recent_window` (how much you've carried the room), `this_is_your_area` (department relevance ≥ threshold), `room_would_value` (callsign of the highest-ranked OTHER candidate = a defer/hand-off target). Returns `None` when nothing is salient. (2) `thread_fanout._fan_one_round` captures `result.scores` and, per dispatched agent, builds the signal and rides it on `IntentMessage.params["room_signal"]` (small struct, beside `is_group_chat`); a new `_resolve_callsigns` helper names the peer. Tier-2 throughout — any failure yields no signal. (3) `CognitiveAgent._conversational_room_awareness_protocol` renders it on the GROUP `direct_message` path, tying each fact to a MOVE: been carrying the conversation → lighter touch / hand off; a better-placed peer present → **defer to them by name** (an AD-951 hand-off, so deference *gives them the floor* next round) — reframed "teamwork, the mark of a confident colleague, never a shortfall" to dissolve the ego problem. The framing leads with "for your judgment, not a directive" and "most turns, simply contribute as yourself" so it self-regulates WITHOUT going quiet.

**Why advisory not gating (the naturalness bet).** A facilitator that PICKS speakers is a central scheduler for conversation — against the agent-native grain; one that PUBLISHES the room's state and lets autonomous agents decide is a sense organ feeding self-organizing agents (the Nooplex shape). And the deference Ezri described only exists if the agent has the agency to make the call — *you can't defer if you were never asked.* The hard cap stays in place: this is the lower-risk half of a two-step. **AD-956** (scale-aware enforcement: advisory below a small-N threshold, gating above) is deliberately deferred — the threshold is empirical, to be CALIBRATED after watching self-selection run *with the cap still on*, not guessed from the inside.

**Config.** `CommunicationsConfig.room_awareness_enabled: bool = True` — pure prompt text (no cost), ships ON so the Captain can observe self-selection emerge; the off-switch if the room ever reads as over-deferential.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad955_room_awareness.py` — 19 tests, BF-287 (real `CommunicationsConfig`/`ChatThreadStore`/`IntentBus`, NOT MagicMock): the pure helper (share counting, window cap, domain threshold, top-other-with-callsign selection skipping self + missing callsigns, None-when-nothing-salient); the hook (inert off-path / 1:1 / no-signal / flag-off; peer + no-peer renderings gap-safe; share numbers; the "teamwork … never a shortfall" ego-reframe regression guard; default-on; config default True); and end-to-end through `group_chat_fanout` (the dispatched agent's params carry a `room_signal` naming the OTHER crew member; flag-off attaches none). Both renderings audited against the real `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE` — clean. Blast-radius `-k "facilitat or fanout or thread or chat or group or cognitive_agent or config or dm or reply or pipeline or reactiv or callsign or crew_profile or ad955 or ad951 or ad950 or ad935 or ad915"` **2063 passed** (the only 4 failures are the pre-existing `TestSkillPipeline` serial-isolation flakes — same 4 seen before this work, orthogonal to a `direct_message` instruction hook), zero real regressions. No UI change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-953: Conversational memory & callbacks — continuity without confabulation (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#889)

**Problem.** Agents replied each turn as if meeting the Captain for the first time — no "you mentioned that last time," no picking up a thread from a past exchange. A continuing presence with a shared history is one of the strongest "this is a real person" signals; an amnesiac one is an instant tell. The recalled material is already there (episodic memories + session history are injected into the reply context by AD-573/AD-723a-1), but nothing told the agent to USE it conversationally — and naively encouraging callbacks risks the opposite failure: a fabricated "as you said last week…" that never happened (the AD-592 confabulation hazard).

**Decision (backend only, instructions-first — Design Principle #6).** A new overridable hook `CognitiveAgent._conversational_memory_protocol(observation)`, sibling to the AD-950 proactivity hook, returns `""` unless `intent == "direct_message"` AND `CommunicationsConfig.conversational_memory_enabled` (default **ON**, read via `getattr(..., True)` so on even when config is absent). When active it appends guidance to draw on what the agent GENUINELY recalls — the recalled memories + running conversation in its context — and weave it in naturally (pick up an earlier thread, call back to what the other person said before, let shared history shape how it addresses THIS person = recipient design), framed as the thing that makes a conversation feel continuous rather than amnesiac. The guidance carries a **hard AD-592 honesty bound stated as the top rule**: reference ONLY what is actually in the recalled material; if uncertain whether something happened, treat it as if it did not and do not bring it up; never manufacture a shared memory, a prior promise, or a callback — an invented "as you told me last week…" breaks trust far worse than no callback; when nothing genuine surfaces, speak to the present moment. The hook is invoked in the `is_conversation` instruction assembly immediately after the AD-950 proactivity hook, so it composes with (does not replace) the proactivity + group decline guidance.

**Why a cognitive_agent hook + why honest by construction.** Same surface reasoning as AD-950 (the DM/group reply path composes the CognitiveAgent `instructions` with `hardcoded_instructions=""`, so a standing order is dead here). And the instruction is grounded: the agent receives genuine recalled episodes (the `_build_user_message` sensorium renders the AD-723a-1 memory section for DM consumers), so "call back to recalled material" points at real content rather than inviting invention — the honesty bound then fences the failure mode.

**Config.** `CommunicationsConfig.conversational_memory_enabled: bool = True` — pure prompt text (no extra LLM pass, no cost), ships ON for the richness the North Star demands; the Captain's tuning knob if callbacks ever read as forced.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad953_conversational_memory.py` — 9 tests, BF-287 discipline (real `CommunicationsConfig`, the real hook bound to a `SimpleNamespace` self per the AD-950 pattern, NOT MagicMock): inert for `ward_room_notification`/`proactive_think`; 1:1 non-empty + capability-gap-safe (incl. the `lack` token); teaches callbacks ("call back"/"you mentioned" + "continuous"); recipient design ("this person"/"shared history"); honesty ("never manufacture" + "uncertain") — the anti-confabulation regression guard; applies on the group path too + gap-safe; flag-OFF == `""` for 1:1 and group; default-ON when config absent; `CommunicationsConfig().conversational_memory_enabled is True`. The rendering is audited against the real `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE` (decomposer.py) — clean. Blast-radius `-k "cognitive_agent or dm or reply or pipeline or standing or group or facilitat or config or ad950 or ad953"` **1531 passed** (the only 4 failures are the pre-existing `TestSkillPipeline` serial-isolation flakes — green in isolation, unrelated to AD-953), zero real regressions. No UI change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-952: Human response dynamics — progressive group-reply reveal + typing indicator (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#888)

**Problem.** The AD-914 group fan-out returns ALL of a round's `per_agent_replies` synchronously in one POST, and the UI rendered them in a single tight `for` loop — every crew reply materialising in the same instant. That is the single clearest "this is a bot" tell in a group chat: real people don't all answer in the same millisecond, and a wall of simultaneous text breaks the illusion the epic is chasing (a stranger couldn't tell the crew are AI).

**Decision (frontend only, additive).** Reveal the replies one at a time, each preceded by a brief "{callsign} is typing" beat whose length scales with the reply. (1) NEW pure, dependency-injected sequencer `ui/src/chat/staggerReplies.ts`: `computeTypingDelay(text)` returns a length-proportional delay clamped to `[360ms, 2400ms]` (a short "Aye." flashes by; a paragraph lingers, capped so it never stalls the room); `revealRepliesProgressively(replies, deps)` loops the replies in AD-915 facilitator order, calling `setTyping({agentId, callsign})` → `await sleep(delay)` → `setTyping(null)` → `appendReply(reply)` per reply. It builds no UI and reads no store directly (mirrors the AD-921 `speakRepliesSequentially` shape), so it is unit-testable with a fake clock; Tier-2 throughout (a throwing dep never breaks the queue; the indicator is ALWAYS cleared in `finally`, even on abort/error; `shouldContinue()` lets a thread switch stop an in-flight reveal). (2) NEW session-scoped store slice `typingAgent: {threadId, agentId, callsign} | null` + `setTypingAgent` (mirrors the AD-949 `callAudioEnabled` pattern — no localStorage). (3) NEW `ui/src/components/profile/TypingIndicator.tsx` — three amber (`#f0b060`) dots pulsing in sequence via a self-contained `@keyframes hxi-typing-blink` (the app has no global CSS file; the component carries its own motion), label "{callsign} is typing", `aria-live="polite"`, HXI #3 (no emoji) + #4 (motion = state). (4) `ProfileChatTab.sendText` group branch: the synchronous `for` loop is extracted into a shared `appendReply` closure (DRY across both paths), then — in a LIVE MEETING the AD-921 voice sequencer + AD-923 speaking indicator already pace the crew one at a time, so the text renders instantly there (byte-identical to before); in TEXT chat it runs `revealRepliesProgressively` with the real `setTypingAgent` + a real `setTimeout` sleep. The transcript renders `<TypingIndicator>` after the message list, **threadId-guarded** so a reveal only shows the beat in the thread it belongs to.

**Scope coordination.** Variable LENGTH is already taught at the instruction level by AD-950 ("Match your length to the move"); AD-952 owns the TIMING + the typing affordance, so there is no duplicate length-clause. True streaming reactivity remains the AD-935a forward marker — AD-952 paces the already-returned synchronous replies, it does not change the backend cascade.

**Tests + gates.** `staggerReplies.test.ts` (12: delay scaling/clamp/empty/overrides; reveal order, skip-empty, finally-clear, abort-before + mid-queue stop, throwing-dep resilience, empty-array), `TypingIndicator.test.tsx` (5: callsign + "is typing", aria label/live, blank-callsign fallback, no-emoji guard, pulse-motion), `useStore.typingAgent.test.ts` (4: default null, set/clear, no-localStorage). Full UI suite **1397 passed / 1 skipped** (+21 over the 1376 baseline, zero regressions), `npm run build` clean, the 4 AD-941 Playwright specs **4 passed** (the group-reply reveal is off their mocked-empty-`per_agent_replies` path — unaffected). No backend → no pytest. Forward markers: AD-952a a per-thread "natural pacing" off-switch if a power user wants instant; AD-935a real streaming once a live-refresh exists. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-951: Agent next-speaker selection — turn-allocation rule 1a for agent-to-agent hand-offs (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#887)

**Problem.** AD-950 taught agents to "hand the floor to a specific crew member ... address them directly by name (their callsign)," but nothing made that hand-off mechanically pick the next speaker. In the AD-935 reactivity cascade the next round's speakers are chosen by the AD-915 facilitator's relevance ranking (capped to 1/turn by BF-614), so when Scout says "Ops, what's your read on the variance?" the facilitator might pick Bones instead — the conversation ignores who was actually addressed. In Conversation Analysis (Sacks/Schegloff/Jefferson 1974) this is turn-allocation **rule 1a** ("current speaker selects next"): a direct address confers both the right and the obligation to speak next. The facilitator already does rule 1a for the CAPTAIN's @-mentions; AD-951 extends it to AGENT-to-AGENT hand-offs.

**Decision (backend only, routing — no new prompt text).** A new pure helper `crew_profile.extract_directed_callsign(text) -> str | None` detects a LEADING directed address — the chat-native `@yeo …` form AND, crucially, the VOCATIVE `Yeo, …` / `Yeo: …` forms (essential for AD-921 VOICE meetings, where you cannot speak an `@`). It mirrors `is_directed_mention` / BF #467 discipline: only a message *to* a peer (leading address) is a hand-off; a message *about* a peer ("I agree with @yeo") is not. In `group_chat_fanout`'s cascade loop, each prior-round reply's CLEAN text (AD-948 already stripped the `<intent>` tag) is scanned; a detected callsign other than the speaker's own is added to an `addressed` set, threaded into `_fan_one_round` → `_assemble_speaker_signals`, where a candidate whose callsign is in the set is hard-included (`mentioned=True`) exactly like a Captain @-mention. The AD-915 facilitator ALWAYS honors `mentioned` speakers (front, overriding the per-turn cap AND convergence), so the addressed peer speaks next — still bounded by `max_agent_rounds` (no infinite loop). **Honest-degrade:** a non-participant callsign matches no candidate and is silently ignored (no error, no phantom speaker); no directed address → the cascade is byte-identical to AD-935.

**Config (transitional flag, convention #14).** `GroupChatConfig.agent_next_speaker_selection_enabled: bool = False` — ships OFF (zero-config boot = AD-935 relevance-ranked), flipped `true` in `config/system.yaml` for the live system (mirroring how BF-614 enabled `agent_reactivity_enabled`). Off → the directed-address scan never runs.

**Why this composes safely.** The cascade's own-speaker exclusion (`exclude_ids = spoke_ids`) removes the round's speakers BEFORE candidates are assembled, and the addressed peer did NOT speak in the round that addressed them — so the hard-include is never cancelled by the exclude set. The scan runs on the AD-948-cleaned reply text, so the stripped `<intent>` tag can't leak a false callsign.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad951_next_speaker_selection.py` — 16 tests, BF-287 discipline (real `ChatThreadStore` on `tmp_path`, real `IntentBus(SignalManager)`, real-but-fake registry/agents with scripted `direct_message` handlers, real `GroupChatConfig`; real `_WARD_ROOM_CREW` types scout/diagnostician/counselor): the pure helper (@/vocative-comma/vocative-colon/lowercasing/end-of-string forms; bare leading word, about-mention, empty → None); `_assemble_speaker_signals` hard-include wiring (addressed → mentioned, None → no hard-include, non-participant → ignored); end-to-end through `group_chat_fanout` with a deterministic ON-vs-OFF discriminator (flag ON → vocative "Ops," pulls counselor into round 1 over the lower-order Bones; flag OFF → default pick Bones, proving the gate); non-participant hand-off ignored; no-address inert; `GroupChatConfig().agent_next_speaker_selection_enabled is False`. Blast-radius `-k "fanout or facilitat or reactiv or crew_profile or callsign or group or thread or chat or config or ad951 or ad935 or ad915 or ad914"` **1381 passed**, zero regressions. No UI change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-950: Conversational proactivity — teach agents to ADVANCE a live conversation (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#886)

**Problem.** Sovereign agents answered and then stopped. On the live 1:1/group `direct_message` reply path the agent produced a competent answer and ended its turn — no follow-up question, no proposal, no "what about you?" — so a conversation died between Captain turns and the burden of keeping it alive fell entirely on the human. A stranger could tell instantly: humans in an engaged exchange take the conversation somewhere; a Q&A service waits to be asked. This is the CORE Turing-test lever of the epic.

**Decision (backend only, instructions-first — Design Principle #6).** The behavior lives in the CognitiveAgent INSTRUCTIONS, never in `decide()`/`act()`. (1) A new overridable hook `CognitiveAgent._conversational_proactivity_protocol(observation)` returns `""` unless `intent == "direct_message"` AND `CommunicationsConfig.proactive_conversation_enabled` (default **ON**, read via `getattr(..., True)` so it's on even when config is absent). When active it appends calibrated guidance: end an ENGAGED turn with ONE forward move — a genuine follow-up question, an observation that invites a reply, or a concrete proposal/offer that gives the other party an easy opening — using recipient design (react to the SPECIFIC thing said, name it, build on it). Explicitly NOT every turn: calibrated to the Captain's engagement and the agent's own personality so it reads as conversation, not interrogation; a turn may rest when that's natural. Honest, respectful disagreement is welcomed (reflexive agreement reads as hollow); every follow-up must be grounded in what was actually said — **never invent** a question or proposal about something that did not occur (honesty preserved, AD-592). (2) When the fan-out param `params["is_group_chat"]` is set, an additional paragraph permits handing the floor to a named peer by callsign (sets up AD-951's next-speaker selection — AD-950 only PERMITS the address, it does not make the peer speak next). (3) The hook is invoked in the `is_conversation` instruction-assembly block AFTER the AD-935 group decline protocol (`_group_proto`), so it composes with — not replaces — the existing reply-only-when-substantive guidance.

**Why a cognitive_agent hook, not a standing order.** The DM/group reply path composes the CognitiveAgent `instructions` with `hardcoded_instructions=""` — a `federation.md`-style standing order is DEAD on this surface (AD-924's group standing order lives on the *proactive* path, a different surface). The only place that reliably shapes the live reply is the instruction assembly itself, so AD-950 is a hook there.

**Config flag.** `CommunicationsConfig.proactive_conversation_enabled: bool = True` — pure prompt text (no extra LLM pass, no cost, no structural change), so it ships ON for the richness the North Star demands; it is the Captain's tuning knob / off-switch if the proactivity ever reads as over-eager, not a transitional behavioral flag.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad950_conversational_proactivity.py` — 9 tests, BF-287 discipline (real `CommunicationsConfig`, the real hook bound to a `SimpleNamespace` self per the AD-934/935 pattern, NOT MagicMock): inert for `ward_room_notification`/`proactive_think`; 1:1 non-empty + capability-gap-safe + omits the group marker; teaches "forward move"/"follow-up"; calibration ("NOT on every turn" + "personality") and honesty ("never invent") clauses present (regression guards against silently becoming relentless or fabricating); group includes "hand the floor" + "callsign" + gap-safe; flag-OFF == `""` for both 1:1 and group; default-ON when config absent; `CommunicationsConfig().proactive_conversation_enabled is True`. Both renderings audited against the real `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE` (decomposer.py) — clean (no can't/cannot/don't have/unable to/not able to). Blast-radius `-k "cognitive_agent or dm or reply or pipeline or standing or group or facilitat or config"` **1519 passed / 1 skipped**, zero regressions. No UI change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-949: Call-scoped group/meeting voice — decouple from the Ship's-Computer `voiceEnabled` (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#885)

**Bug.** Group/meeting voice was silent even though 1:1 voice works, because the two paths gate on DIFFERENT flags. The 1:1 composer has a per-agent speaker override (`localStorage hxi_chat_tts_{agentId}`), so a 1:1 speaks regardless of any global flag. The meeting path (`useMeetingVoice.ts:50`) gated on the **global `voiceEnabled`** — the Ship's-Computer / `IntentSurface` voice that the AD-945 Engineering → Environment "voice output" toggle sets, which defaults `false`. So group/meeting voice piggybacked on the ship-computer flag and was off unless the Captain enabled the Engineering voice AND was in a meeting — exactly what BF-614 saw and triaged as "the AD-945 voice-output toggle was likely off, not a code bug." AD-949 is the structural fix.

**Decision (frontend only — a gate-flag swap + an additive in-call control).** Give the call its OWN audio gate, decoupled from `voiceEnabled`. (1) A new store flag `callAudioEnabled: boolean` (default **`true`**) + `setCallAudioEnabled` mirror the `voiceEnabled` slice MINUS the `localStorage` line — **session-scoped** (a fresh page load is audible; the Captain can mute mid-session; persisting the preference is the **AD-949a** forward marker). Default-ON is the single decoupling that fixes the bug: the hook's `meetingActive` self-gate (`useMeetingVoice.ts:49`, runs FIRST) already silences everything when no meeting is active, so `meetingActive && callAudioEnabled` means *starting a call is audible by default* WITHOUT enabling the Ship's-Computer voice. (2) `useMeetingVoice.ts:50` swaps `voiceEnabled` → `callAudioEnabled` (the one functional line; the `meetingActive` self-gate, the AD-921/922/923 `speakRepliesSequentially` sequencer, the per-agent AD-718 voice profiles, the AD-923 `speakingAgentId` seam, and the AD-922 mic echo gate are byte-for-byte intact — only the flag the gate reads changes; two JSDoc/comment lines corrected for accuracy). ### AD-947: Avatar camera framing — focus on faces, not feet (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#883)

**Bug.** In the meeting avatar gallery (`MeetingView` `AvatarSlot`), the crew VRM rendered showing only the **feet**. Root cause: the gallery `<Canvas camera={{ position: [0, 1.45, 0.85], fov: 28 }}>` sets the camera POSITION but no lookAt, so react-three-fiber points the camera at the default origin `[0,0,0]` (floor) — the avatar's feet. The `CrewAvatarPopout` does not have this bug because it mounts `OrbitControls target={[0, 1.42, 0]}` (face height); the non-interactive gallery slots have no controls, so nothing aimed the camera.

**Fix (frontend only, `MeetingView.tsx`).** A tiny in-Canvas `FaceFraming` helper (`useThree((s) => s.camera)` → `camera.lookAt(0, 1.42, 0)` + `updateProjectionMatrix()` once on mount, renders `null`), mounted as the first child of the gallery Canvas. Face height `1.42` matches the popout's `OrbitControls` target. `CrewAvatarPopout` and `CrewVRM` are untouched. The three MeetingView test mocks of `@react-three/fiber` gain a `useThree` stub (the mock replaces the whole module). Full UI suite **1373 passed / 1 skipped** (the 3 MeetingView files green with the new mock; net +0 tests — the R3F Canvas is mocked so the lookAt is a code-level + live-verified guard); `npm run build` clean. No backend/REST/pytest. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-948: Group-chat hygiene — strip the internal `<intent …>` self-tag from fan-out replies (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#884)

**Bug.** In a group chat, agent replies leaked the AD-722a divergence self-tag (e.g. `<intent emotion="warm">`) into the visible transcript (Captain's screenshot). The AD-722a tag is parsed + **unconditionally stripped** only on the 1:1 path (`apply_divergence_check` at `routers/agents.py:agent_chat`); the group fan-out (`routers/thread_fanout.py` `_send_one`) took the raw LLM reply and persisted/returned it **without** that strip. Internal markup reaching the human is an instant "this is AI" tell.

**Fix (backend only, `thread_fanout.py`).** `_send_one` now calls the single-source `strip_intent_self_tag` (from `avatars/divergence_detector.py`, BF-603 hardened — leading/inline/trailing, optional-quote tolerant, prose-safe) on the resolved reply text **before** the NO_RESPONSE decline check / persist / return. The strip is **unconditional** (even when divergence detection is OFF — defense-in-depth, the tag must never reach the Captain), and placed before the decline check so a decline trailing a tag is still detected. Reuse only — the regex / 1:1 call site / `apply_divergence_check` are untouched. +2 pytest (`tests/test_ad948_group_intent_tag_strip.py`, BF-287 real `ChatThreadStore`+`IntentBus`+fan-out): a quoted + unquoted tag-bearing reply is stripped in BOTH `per_agent_replies` and the persisted message rows; prose containing the word "intent" is preserved verbatim. Blast-radius `-k "thread or chat or fanout or divergence"` **607 passed**, zero regressions. No UI change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### BF-614: Group chat — crew replied all-at-once and never to each other; an added member showed a "?" avatar

**Context.** A Captain-reported cluster of group-chat problems from an Ezri+Yeo room: (a) both agents replied to EVERY Captain message at the same time (an unnatural wall of simultaneous replies), (b) the agents never responded to EACH OTHER — only when the Captain sent, and (c) Yeo (added to the room after it was created) rendered a grey "?" avatar instead of his badge/initial.

**Root cause — (a) and (b) are ONE linked bug.** The AD-915 facilitator's `max_speakers_per_turn` defaults to `0` (= OFF, the AD-914 "all crew reply at once" behavior) and `config/system.yaml` never set it. So round 0 fanned to BOTH agents (the simultaneous wall, (a)). And the AD-935 reactivity cascade excludes a round's OWN speakers from the next round (an agent never reacts to itself) — so in a 2-agent room where BOTH spoke in round 0, round 1 had NOBODY left to react, and the cascade terminated immediately ((b)). The two symptoms share the single cause: an uncapped round 0 consumes every speaker. **(c)** is independent: the group fan-out's `_send_one` returns an empty `callsign` string when it can't resolve the added participant, and the frontend `ChatMessageRow` used `msg.callsign ?? hostCallsign` — `??` does NOT catch `''` (only null/undefined), so the badge received an empty string and `AgentAvatarBadge` rendered its `'?'` fallback initial.

**Decision.** (1) Set `group_chat.max_speakers_per_turn: 1` in `config/system.yaml` (the Pydantic default stays `0` for zero-config boot). One cap fixes BOTH (a) and (b): round 0 now picks the single most-relevant agent (an @-mentioned agent is still always included — the facilitator's hard-include is preserved), and because only one agent speaks per round the OTHER is free to react in the next round, so the cascade actually runs: Ezri → Yeo → Ezri turn-taking that references each other, bounded by `max_agent_rounds` + the convergence gate as before. (2) `ChatMessageRow` resolves the author callsign as `(msg.callsign && trim) || agents.get(authorId)?.callsign || (msg.authorId != null ? '' : hostCallsign)` — a blank reply callsign now resolves from the agents map by the real `authorId`; a genuinely unresolvable explicit author keeps the honest `'?'` (never a wrong host attribution), and a legacy/1:1 message with no author still falls back to the host. The avatar department color resolves from the same `authorAgent`.

**Not addressed here (reported, triaged):** voice ("can't hear each agent") — meeting voice gates on `meetingActive && voiceEnabled`; the voice-output toggle moved into the Engineering Bridge station (AD-945) and was most likely off (a settings state, not a code defect — verify in the station's Environment config). The "no separate meeting window" is current AD-937/938 design (add-people transitions the profile card in place). The "LLM proxy returned no response" is the BF-612/BF-289 empty-content-after-uptime surface a proxy restart clears.

**Verification.** +4 Vitest (`ChatMessageRow.test.tsx` — blank-callsign→agents-map, explicit callsign, legacy host fallback, unresolved-author→'?'); full UI suite **1373 passed / 1 skipped** (+4, zero regressions); `npm run build` clean. Focused pytest `-k "group_chat or facilitat or config or fanout or thread"` **940 passed** (the `max_speakers_per_turn: 1` yaml loads cleanly; no facilitator/fanout regression). No new backend code — the facilitator already honored the cap; only the operator config value changed. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### BF-613: Meeting-view crew avatar was always the badge (the VRM was read off the never-hydrated base Agent), and the Captain had no in-meeting camera control

**Context.** In a meeting (`MeetingView`), each crew member rendered only their `AgentAvatarBadge` (the "E" glyph) instead of their VRM avatar — yet the SAME agent's VRM rendered fine in the separate `CrewAvatarPopout` window. Root cause: `AvatarSlot` read `appearance` (which carries `vrm_url`) off a **narrow cast of the store's base `Agent`** — but the base `Agent` never carries `appearance`; it is a per-agent `AgentProfileData` field hydrated on demand from `GET /api/agent/{id}/profile` (the source `AgentProfilePanel` feeds into `CrewAvatarPopout`). So `vrmUrl` was ALWAYS `undefined` in production and every slot fell to the badge. This is the BF-287 mocked-contract class: `MeetingView.test.tsx` seeded `appearance.vrm_url` **directly on the mock Agent** (`base.appearance = …`), so the test was green on a contract production never satisfies. Separately, `CaptainSlot` (AD-939) showed the Captain's camera only when it was *already* active and offered no way to start it from the meeting — the Captain asked to "turn my camera on from here to share with the meeting."

**Decision.** Two frontend-only fixes in `MeetingView.tsx`. (1) **Hydrate the crew VRM from the profile**, exactly as the popout does: `AvatarSlot` now fetches `GET /api/agent/{agentId}/profile` in a `useEffect` (cancellable, `typeof fetch` guard, `.catch` honest-degrade) and reads `vrm_url` / `expression_overrides` / `dsl.expression_resting` from the fetched `appearance` instead of the base-Agent cast; absent/failed fetch → badge (the CI/dev default with zero `.vrm` assets, and the no-backend case). Department (badge color) still comes off the store Agent. (2) **Add an in-meeting camera toggle** to `CaptainSlot`: a stroke-SVG camera button (`data-testid="captain-camera-toggle"`, `aria-pressed`, amber when on, NO emoji — HXI #3) that drives the SAME global camera the rest of the HXI uses — `startCameraStream()` when off, `stopCameraStream()` when on (both idempotent); the existing slot reflects the live stream once active.

**Verification.** The mocked tests are rewritten to the PRODUCTION contract: `MeetingView.test.tsx` no longer seeds `appearance` on the Agent — it drives a `fetch` stub keyed by agent id, and the VRM cases `await screen.findByTestId('crew-vrm-…')` (the fetch is async). +3 new `MeetingView.captain.test.tsx` cases for the toggle (present + labelled, off→`startCameraStream`, on→`stopCameraStream`). Full UI suite **1369 passed / 1 skipped** (+3 over the 1366 BF-612-era baseline, zero regressions); `npm run build` clean. **Live-verified** on the dev server (real store + components + routing): seeding a meeting fired `GET /api/agent/counselor_0/profile` (the fetch that NEVER fired before), `CrewVRM` mounted and attempted the load (`[AD-721 VRM load failed]` for the dev-only missing `.vrm` → badge, as designed), and the `captain-camera-toggle` rendered with `aria-label="Turn camera on"`. On the real backend (where the `.vrm` is the binary already shown in the popout) the identical path renders the avatar. No backend/REST/pytest change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-946b: A bare `>` in the command palette lists every station launch (Bridge as Ship's Computer — polish, #873) — AD-946 opened the palette on a leading `>`, but `matchPaletteCommands('', …)` returned `[]`, so a bare `>` (before the Captain types a search term) rendered the CommandPalette empty-state "No matching command." instead of the full launch list — a discoverability gap: the Captain could not SEE what commands exist without already knowing a term to search. **Decision:** an empty/whitespace query now returns ALL commands — `commands.slice()`, a fresh array so a caller can never mutate the registry-derived source — so a bare `>` lists every launch (Ward Room, Chats, Crew, Personnel, Metrics, Notebooks, Records, Explorer, Work Board, System, Settings) and typing narrows it; "No matching command." now shows ONLY for a genuinely non-matching query (e.g. `>xyzzy`). This is standard fuzzy-finder semantics (an empty filter = everything) and the literal VS-Code `>`-then-nothing model (the first item is highlighted, Enter runs it). **Why it is safe (the NL guarantee holds):** the change is one line in the pure helper `matchPaletteCommands`, and BOTH call sites — `handleSubmit` (the Enter path) and the live `paletteMatches` (the render path) in `IntentSurface.tsx` — are already gated on command-mode (the leading `>`), so an empty query only ever reaches the helper once the Captain has typed `>`; a plain natural-language question (no `>`) still never calls the helper and submits byte-for-byte via `/api/chat`. The `>` trigger, the registry-as-single-source-of-truth (`buildBridgeStations`→`buildPaletteCommands`), and the presentational `CommandPalette` empty-state (unchanged — it still renders "No matching command." when handed an empty list, which now happens only on a real miss) are all untouched. Frontend only, no net test delta: the AD-946 `paletteCommands.test.ts` "empty query → `[]`" case is rewritten to "empty/whitespace query → ALL commands" + a `not.toBe(cmds)` fresh-array guard. Full UI suite **1366 passed / 1 skipped** (unchanged), `npm run build` clean. Forward marker AD-946a (voice command of stations) inherits this behavior — it consumes the same helper. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-943: Command-Station model + registry (Bridge as Ship's Computer, foundation) — generalize the Bridge's ad-hoc `BridgeSection` composition into a typed, reusable COMMAND-STATION taxonomy + registry, and migrate the 3 existing sections through it. The Bridge is the single modern "Ship's Computer" control surface, deliberately distinct from the bioluminescent agent mesh (the Ship's Computer is NOT an agent — AD-398); today its sections are hand-written one-offs, and the AD-944/945/946 wave each need a typed slot to drop a launch/config item into. **Decision:** a new `ui/src/components/bridge/stations.tsx` defines `CommandStation = {id, title, accent, defaultOpen, count?, onExpand?, body?, actions: StationAction[], config: StationConfig[]}` (a *station* = a menu group for one area of the ship; `StationAction = {id, label, onInvoke, count?}` = a discrete launch, `StationConfig = {id, label, render}` = an inline settings surface), plus the canonical 6-station taxonomy `STATION_META`/`STATION_ORDER` (`communications, personnel, science, operations, engineering, command`), a `buildBridgeStations(ctx)` factory, and `isPopulated(st)`. **The mapping (the decision):** Communications → `communications` (`#b080d0`); **Work Board → `operations`** (`#d0a030` — the mission/task pipeline is running the ship's work); **System → `engineering`** (`#70a0d0` — ship subsystems / is-the-machinery-online); `personnel` (`#50b0a0`), `science` (`#5090d0`), `command` (`#f0b060`) are modelled placeholders. ### AD-940: Draggable CHATS panel (`chatsPanelPos`, GamePanel pattern) — the floating CHATS panel can now be moved by its header, so it never traps an open chat window underneath it. **Frontend only — no change to the AD-938 CHATS list/filter/open logic, no resize (forward marker AD-940a), no backend/pytest.**

**The problem (Captain-reported).** The CHATS panel was a fixed floating panel (`top:60` / `left:60` / `bottom:60`); when a chat window opened under it the Captain couldn't drag it out of the way.

**The fix.** `useStore` gains `chatsPanelPos: {x,y}` + `setChatsPanelPos` mirroring `profilePanelPos`/`setProfilePanelPos` (interface, init, action), initialised to `{x:60, y:60}` — the panel's prior on-screen origin, so enabling drag moves nothing on first render. `ChatsPanel`'s root reads the pos (`left`/`top`), and the CHATS header is a `cursor:move` drag handle (`data-testid="chats-drag-handle"`) wired with the `GamePanel.startDrag` pattern — capture the offset on mousedown, track `window` mousemove, tear the listeners down on mouseup; the New-chat / Close controls `stopPropagation` on mousedown so a click never starts a drag. The old `bottom:60` vertical pin (which would fight a free drag) becomes `maxHeight: calc(100vh - 120px)`, keeping the list bounded-scroll while the panel moves freely.

**Deviation (documented).** The build prompt said `position:'absolute'`; I kept `position:'fixed'` — it is the value of both precedents the prompt cites (`GamePanel`, `AgentProfilePanel`) and of the current code, and the mirrored drag math is viewport-coordinate (`clientX - offset`), which only positions correctly under `fixed`. `absolute` would have regressed (scroll-with-content + a coordinate-space mismatch). The init pos is the real on-screen origin `{60,60}` rather than the prompt-summary's illustrative `{24,96}`, to honor its stated "match the current on-screen position so nothing visually jumps".

**Tests & gates.** +5 Vitest (`ChatsPanel.drag.test.tsx` — the `setChatsPanelPos` action, the root rendering at a seeded pos, the header `cursor:move` + a mousedown→`window`-mousemove→mouseup sequence moving the panel, New-chat/Close NOT dragging, the HXI no-emoji guard; mocked `threadApi`, REAL store via `setState`, BF-287). Full UI suite **1328 passed / 1 skipped** (224 files; +11 over the 1317 baseline, zero regressions); `npm run build` clean. No backend → no pytest. **COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.** Forward marker: **AD-940a** (resize the CHATS panel from a corner handle, the AgentProfilePanel pattern).
