### AD-938: Group chat shows the real thread transcript (hydrate-on-open + thread-keyed messages) — opening a group from CHATS now renders the `GroupChatHeader` (participants + meeting toggle) AND the group's actual message transcript with per-author avatars + `HH:MM` timestamps, instead of an empty 1:1-looking view. **Frontend only — no backend / REST / pytest (the `GET /messages` endpoint already exists), no WebSocket/poll, no AD-933/934/935 pipeline / facilitator / Ward Room / `IntentMessage` change.**

**The problem (Captain-reported, live-repro).** Opening a group (e.g. "Ezri, Yeo") from the CHATS list opened the host agent's profile with an EMPTY transcript and NO group header (no participant chips, no meeting toggle); adding people to a 1:1 then opening the new group showed the same broken 1:1-looking view.

**The mechanism (TWO root causes, verified vs HEAD).** **(1) The opened group thread was never hydrated into `chatThreads`.** `ChatsPanel.handleOpen` (`ui/.../chats/ChatsPanel.tsx:98`) called `openGroupChatThread(host, thread.id)` but never `setChatThread(thread)` — even though it HAD the `thread` object — so `chatThreads.get(groupId)` was `undefined` and everything that reads it broke: `GroupChatHeader` (`if (!thread) return null`, mounted at `ProfileChatTab.tsx:859`), the `meetingActive` selector (`chatThreads.get(activeThreadId)?.metadata.meeting_active`), and `MeetingView`'s participant list. **(2) The transcript rendered the per-AGENT buffer, not the thread's messages.** `ProfileChatTab` set `messages = agentConversations.get(agentId)?.messages` and the only history load was `GET /api/agent/{id}/chat/history` (the agent's 1:1 history); the group thread's messages were never fetched, so a group always showed the HOST agent's 1:1 buffer. `activeThreadId` (AD-937) was correct for the send target + meeting flag, but the DISPLAYED transcript ignored it.

**The fix (frontend, two parts).** **Part 1 (hydrate-on-open):** `ChatsPanel.handleOpen` and `NewChatModal`'s 2+ create branch now call `setChatThread(thread)` (already in the store, `useStore.ts:1311`) before `openGroupChatThread`, so the header/participants/meeting flag/transcript resolve the moment the host opens. (`handleJoin` already routes through `handleOpen`.) **Part 2 (thread-keyed transcript):** (a) `threadApi.listMessages(threadId, limit=200)` wraps `GET /api/threads/{id}/messages` → `{thread_id, messages:[…]}` (verified `routers/threads.py:302`; each `{id, thread_id, author_id, role, body, created_at, metadata}`), Tier-2 `[]` on failure. (b) `useStore` gains a `threadMessages: Map<string, AgentProfileMessage[]>` display slice + `setThreadMessages` (load-on-open) / `appendThreadMessage` (send-reconcile, capped to the last 200). (c) `ProfileChatTab` adds a load-on-open `useEffect([activeThreadId])` that maps the DTOs via a new pure `threadDtoToMessage` (captain→`role:'user'`/no avatar, agent→`role:'agent'`+`authorId`+`callsign` resolved from the agents map, else→`system`) into the slice; switches the displayed source via a pure `selectTranscriptMessages(activeThreadId, threadMsgs, conversation?.messages)` (thread context → the thread's real messages; cold 1:1 with no thread → the per-agent buffer, unchanged AD-406 UX); and reconciles the send path — the optimistic Captain message + each group `per_agent_reply` (with `authorId`/`callsign`, NO `callsign:` text prefix — the AD-936 `ChatMessageRow` header shows the author) + the 1:1 reply (`authorId: agentId`) are ALSO `appendThreadMessage`'d when a thread is active (the existing `addAgentMessage` calls stay for the no-thread path + cross-session seed). The three pure/data-path helpers (`threadDtoToMessage`, `selectTranscriptMessages`, `loadThreadMessages`) live in a NEW audio-dep-free `profileTranscript.ts` (the AD-936 `ChatMessageRow` extraction precedent) so they're unit-testable without rendering the audio/screen-dep-laden `ProfileChatTab`. **Net:** a thread (group or warm 1:1) renders its real persisted transcript with per-author avatars + `HH:MM`; a cold 1:1 (no thread yet) renders the per-agent buffer exactly as before; `agentConversations`/`addAgentMessage` are untouched.

**Tests & gates.** +28 Vitest across 5 new files (BF-287 real store via `useStore.setState`/`getState`, mocked `threadApi`): `threadApi.listMessages` (map / `[]` `!ok` / `[]` throw / endpoint+limit/encode); `store/threadMessages` (set / overwrite / isolation / append / 200-cap); `ProfileChatTab.threadTranscript` (`threadDtoToMessage` role mapping; `selectTranscriptMessages` switch; two-author distinct avatars via `ChatMessageRow`; `loadThreadMessages` load+map+`[]`-degrade; the group send-reconcile data path — Captain + per-author replies, no `callsign:` prefix; HXI no-emoji guard on the 5 changed sources); `ChatsPanel.hydrate` (a group-row click hydrates `chatThreads` AND opens via the override); `NewChatModal.hydrate` (the 2+ create branch hydrates the new group + null-degrade). Full UI suite **1317 passed / 1 skipped** (222 files; +28 over the 1289 baseline, zero regressions); `npm run build` clean (tsc -b + vite). No backend change → no pytest. **COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.** Forward markers: **AD-935a** (live WebSocket/poll push so a peer's messages stream into an open thread without a reopen — this AD loads on open + reconciles on send, enough for the synchronous-cascade model), **AD-938a** (paginate/scrollback for long threads; `listMessages` currently loads the last 200).

### AD-937: Non-destructive 1:1→group transition (fixes the unreachable-1:1 regression) — adding a person to a 1:1 chat no longer destroys it; the add-people flow branches on thread shape (1:1 → a SEPARATE new group via `createThread`; group → `addParticipant`), and a dedicated `activeProfileThreadId` override addresses groups without clobbering the host's single `threadIdByAgent` 1:1 slot. **Frontend only — no backend / `add_participant` / pytest, no AD-933/934/935 pipeline / facilitator / Ward Room / `IntentMessage` / `Glyphs.tsx` change.**

**The problem (Captain-reported).** Adding a person to a 1:1 chat destroyed the 1:1 and made it unreachable: reopening the agent's profile showed the group, not the 1:1.

**The mechanism (TWO layers, verified vs HEAD).** **Layer 1 — destructive backend mutation:** AD-917 `GroupChatHeader.handleAdd` (`ui/.../profile/GroupChatHeader.tsx:59`) called `addParticipant(threadId, agentId)` → `ChatThreadStore.add_participant` (`src/probos/threads/__init__.py:435`), an in-place read-modify-write that rewrote the SAME row's `participants ["a"]→["a","b"]` — repurposing the 1:1 INTO the group (AD-932 `EmptyChatAddPeople` materialized the 1:1 then handed off to the same picker). **Layer 2 — addressing collision:** `threadIdByAgent` (`useStore.ts:336`) is a SINGLE slot per agent; group-open bound the group into it (`ChatsPanel.handleOpen` + `NewChatModal` 2+ both did `setThreadForAgent(host, groupId)`), so `ProfileChatTab`'s `props.threadId ?? threadIdByAgent.get(agentId)` resolved a roster-open to the GROUP — the group hijacked the agent's 1:1 slot.

**The fix (frontend, two parts).** **Part A (non-destructive create):** `NewChatModal` gains optional `seedParticipantId?` — pre-populates `selected=[seed]` and renders the host as a LOCKED, non-removable chip (`new-chat-seed-<id>`; `removeSelected` no-ops on the seed). The 1:1 add control — `GroupChatHeader`'s ≤1-crew branch and the rewired AD-932 `EmptyChatAddPeople` (which now opens the seeded modal instead of `createThread([id])`+`setChatThread`+`setThreadForAgent`) — opens the seeded modal, so confirming with 2+ runs the existing `createThread({title, participants})` and mints a SEPARATE group; the 1:1 row is NEVER mutated. The ≥2-crew group path keeps the inline `AddParticipantPopover`→`addParticipant` mutate flow (correct — matches Teams). **Part B (stop groups hijacking the 1:1 slot):** `useStore` gains `activeProfileThreadId: string|null` (default null) + `openGroupChatThread(hostId, threadId)` (sets the override + `activeProfileAgent` + dismisses the tooltip, but NOT `threadIdByAgent`); `openAgentProfile` ALSO sets `activeProfileThreadId: null`. A NEW pure `resolveProfileThreadId(prop, activeProfileThreadId, threadIdByAgent, agentId)` (its own audio-dep-free module so the priority is unit-testable without rendering `ProfileChatTab`) resolves `prop > override > per-agent 1:1` at ALL THREE `ProfileChatTab` sites (the reactive `activeThreadId` selector + the group-fanout send path + the 1:1 send path, so a send while viewing a group routes to the group); `ChatsPanel.handleOpen` and the `NewChatModal` 2+ branch open via `openGroupChatThread`. **Net rule:** a group is addressed by `activeProfileThreadId`; the agent's `threadIdByAgent` slot is reserved for its 1:1; reopening from the roster clears the override → the (un-mutated, Part A) 1:1 resolves. Both Captain requirements satisfied.

**Tests & gates.** +11 Vitest: new `ui/src/components/profile/__tests__/ad937ThreadResolution.test.ts` (`openGroupChatThread` sets the override not the slot; `openAgentProfile` clears it; resolver priority; the HEADLINE Captain repro — seed `threadIdByAgent[ezri]=oneToOneId`, `openGroupChatThread(ezri, groupId)`, then `openAgentProfile(ezri)` resolves to `oneToOneId` NOT `groupId`), plus seeded-modal/override cases across `NewChatModal`/`EmptyChatAddPeople`/`GroupChatHeader`/`ChatsPanel`. Obsolete-contract updates (the AD-923 sibling-break pattern): the AD-931 `NewChatModal` 2+ test and the AD-919 `ChatsPanel` row-open tests now assert `openGroupChatThread` (override set, `threadIdByAgent` untouched); the AD-917 `GroupChatHeader` add-participant test moved to a ≥2-crew thread (1-crew now opens the modal); the AD-932 `EmptyChatAddPeople` materialize-then-mutate suite rewritten to the seeded-modal contract. Full UI suite **1289 passed / 1 skipped** (217 files; +11 over the 1278 baseline, zero regressions); `npm run build` clean (tsc -b + vite). No backend change → no pytest. **COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.** Forward markers: **AD-937a** (backend is-default `add_participant` guard — defense-in-depth; 1:1 detection by `is_default` is imperfect since client `createThread([id])` omits it), **AD-937b** (explicit custom group-name input; NewChatModal currently auto-titles from callsigns).

### AD-936: Per-message chat metadata — author avatar + `HH:MM` timestamp (Teams/Slack/Discord-style) — the profile chat transcript now renders, above each bubble, the author's `AgentAvatarBadge` + callsign name label (agent messages) and a dim local `HH:MM` timestamp (every message); group replies thread the real author's `agent_id`/`callsign` so each shows its OWN avatar instead of a shared host badge + a `callsign:` text prefix. **Frontend only, additive/backward-compatible — no backend/REST/pytest, no WebSocket/poll (AD-935a), no `Glyphs.tsx` / `AgentAvatarBadge` API change, no date-separator headers (AD-936a).**

**The problem (Captain-reported).** The group-chat transcript showed neither who said what (every agent reply used the HOST agent's badge with the author's callsign jammed into the text as a `callsign:` prefix) nor when (no timestamp rendered). The Captain asked for the Teams/Slack/Discord treatment: a profile icon next to each reply + a date/time stamp.

**The mechanism (verified vs HEAD).** Part B (timestamp) was **pure render** — `AgentProfileMessage` already carried `timestamp: number` (`ui/src/store/types.ts:320`, set to `Date.now()/1000` in `useStore.addAgentMessage`). Part A (avatar) needed author identity the model lacked: the AD-914 group fan-out added every reply via `addAgentMessage(hostAgentId, 'agent', `${callsign}: ${text}`)` — the HOST id for ALL replies. **Three additive changes:** (1) `AgentProfileMessage` gains optional `authorId?` / `callsign?`; (2) `useStore.addAgentMessage` gains an optional 4th `opts?: { authorId?: string; callsign?: string }` param (interface decl + impl; **conditional-spread** so omitted keys keep legacy/1:1 messages byte-identical; existing ~10 call sites unchanged); (3) `ProfileChatTab` group-reply add threads `{ authorId: r.agent_id, callsign: r.callsign }` and DROPS the inline `callsign:` text prefix (the avatar + name label replace it). The heavy bubble JSX + a pure `formatChatTime(tsSeconds) -> HH:MM` helper are extracted into a NEW presentational `ChatMessageRow({ msg, hostAgentId, hostCallsign, body? })` (the `groupsend`/`bf294b` precedent — ProfileChatTab's audio/screen deps make a full render impractical under jsdom, so the testable piece lives in its own light module importing only `useStore` + `AgentAvatarBadge`). The row resolves the avatar `department` via the established `ChatsPanel.deptOf` runtime cast (`Agent` has no formal `department` field) with a `''` Tier-2 fallback (badge degrades to the default-colored initial), falls back to the HOST agent for `authorId`-less (1:1 / legacy) messages, and shows NO avatar for `user`/`system` (dim timestamp only; the existing dim-italic system style preserved). The body is passed in pre-rendered (`renderMessageBodyWithArtifacts(msg.text, threadId)`), so `ChatMessageRow` stays decoupled from the AD-797 artifact renderer. **+8 Vitest** (`ui/src/components/profile/__tests__/ProfileChatTab.metadata.test.tsx`, BF-287 real store via `useStore.setState`): agent avatar+callsign+`HH:MM`, two DISTINCT per-author avatars, host-avatar fallback, `user`=timestamp/no-avatar, `system` unchanged, `formatChatTime` shape (locale-agnostic `/\d{1,2}:\d{2}/`), `addAgentMessage` back-compat (no opts) + opts land, no-emoji guard (`?raw` source + rendered DOM). Full UI suite **1278 passed / 1 skipped** (216 files; +8 over the ~1270 baseline, zero regressions); `npm run build` clean (tsc -b + vite). No backend change → no pytest. **COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.** Forward marker: **AD-936a** (date-separator / "Today" headers).

### AD-935: Agent-to-agent group-chat reactivity (bounded synchronous cascade) — after the Captain round, an agent reply fans to the OTHER crew for up to `max_agent_rounds` extra rounds, gated by the AD-915 convergence gate + `[NO_RESPONSE]` + exclude-prior-speakers + the round cap, so agents react to each other in real time; **synchronous (awaited) within the Captain POST**, NOT async — every reply returns in the existing `per_agent_replies`. Default OFF in Pydantic, ON in system.yaml. **No async/fire-and-forget cascade (AD-935a), no chat WebSocket/poll, no reply-shape / `direct_message` / `DmReplyPipeline` / AD-934-step / AD-933b-ref / `IntentMessage` / Ward Room change, no agent-initiated cascade (AD-935b), no trust/Hebbian from a2a (AD-935c).**

**The problem (Captain-reported, verified vs HEAD).** In a group chat agents only respond when the **Captain** posts — if an agent asks a *peer* a question there is no reply until the Captain sends another message. Root cause: the group fan-out fires ONLY on `role=="captain"` (`routers/threads.py` `append_message`), and AD-914 deliberately bounded it to "fan once and STOP" (no agent-to-agent) to avoid loops. AD-935 adds **bounded** agent-to-agent reactivity.

**Why synchronous-bounded over async.** The chat transcript has **no live-refresh** — there is no polling loop and no `chat_message`/`thread_message` WebSocket case in `ui/src/store/useStore.ts` `handleEvent`; `ProfileChatTab` renders only what the send POST returns in `per_agent_replies`. A fire-and-forget async cascade would therefore create messages the UI never shows until a manual refresh, AND is harder to bound. So AD-935 runs the cascade **synchronously within the Captain's POST** and returns ALL cascade replies (across rounds) in the existing `per_agent_replies` list, which the UI already renders in order. True streaming/async reactivity is forward marker **AD-935a** (unlocked once a live-refresh exists). This mirrors the Ward Room's round-capped a2a reactivity but on `ChatThreadStore` and synchronous.

**The mechanism (five changes, verified vs HEAD).** (1) `config.GroupChatConfig` gains `agent_reactivity_enabled: bool = False` + `max_agent_rounds: int = 2` (transitional flag #14 — ships OFF; zero-config boot byte-identical). (2) `config/system.yaml` `group_chat:` flips both ON for the operator (AD-925's default-False-Pydantic / true-yaml precedent). (3) `routers/thread_fanout.py` extracts `group_chat_fanout`'s single-round core (facilitate → `gather(_send_one)` → AD-933a episode write) into `_fan_one_round(runtime, store, thread_id, *, trigger_body, candidate_ids, exclude_ids, vision_messages, sanity_gate, t_start, before=None)`, and rewrites `group_chat_fanout` as round 0 (Captain, `before=captain_msg.created_at`) + a bounded loop: each round fans the PREVIOUS round's agent messages to the OTHER crew (`exclude_ids` = that round's speakers), stopping on empty `speaking_order` / convergence / all-decline / the round cap. `_fan_one_round` rebuilds the prior window from the store each call (cascade rounds pass `before=None` so the window INCLUDES the just-persisted replies — each speaker sees the full transcript); `vision_messages` is round-0 only. The threaded `before` arg is what keeps round 0 **byte-identical** to AD-914 (the existing `test_captain_turn_passed_as_text_not_history` asserts the Captain turn is excluded from history). The cascade is **awaited** (synchronous), Tier-2 honest-degrade (a round failure logs and returns the replies gathered so far). (4) `_send_one` honors `[NO_RESPONSE]`: after the AD-933 escalation, a decline (case-insensitive, after strip + bracket removal == `NO_RESPONSE`) or an empty reply returns `{..., "text": "", "_declined": True}` — an early return BEFORE the persist — and `_fan_one_round` filters `_declined` entries before the episode write and the returned `per_agent_replies`, so a decline never reaches `append_message`, the episode, or the cascade trigger (this also fixes round 0, where a literal `[NO_RESPONSE]` would previously have been persisted + shown). (5) `cognitive_agent` passes `params["is_group_chat"] = True` from the fan-out (reaches `observation["params"]`, the same dict `vision_messages` flows through) and adds the overridable `_conversational_group_chat_protocol(observation)` hook (next to `_conversational_deliberate_protocol`, invoked next to `_delib_proto`) returning the group decline-teaching string when `params.get("is_group_chat")` — **gap-regex-safe** (no `can't`/`cannot`/`don't have`/`unable to`/`not able to`, verified against `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE`; `[NO_RESPONSE]` itself does not match — no space after `no`, `RESPONSE` is not a gap word). The decline mechanism is load-bearing: with the default `max_speakers_per_turn=0` every agent replies in round 0, so the cascade only produces extra rounds when agents DECLINE (leaving the asker's message to fan to the others) or under a speaker cap / @-mention asymmetry — exactly the "is a response required?" judgment the Captain asked for.

**The full guard set.** round cap (`max_agent_rounds`, hard backstop) · AD-915 `ChatFacilitator` convergence gate (empty `speaking_order` once the recent agent exchange converges — the semantic terminator) · `[NO_RESPONSE]` declines · exclude-prior-round-speakers (an agent never reacts to its own message) · @-mention bypass (a peer-addressed agent is hard-included even under a speaker cap). **+13 pytest** (`tests/test_ad935_group_reactivity.py`, BF-287 — real `ChatThreadStore` on `tmp_path`, real `IntentBus(SignalManager(reap_interval=1.0))`, real-but-fake registry/agents whose subscribed `direct_message` handlers return scripted replies keyed by per-agent call index (NOT `MagicMock`), a real `GroupChatConfig` toggled per test, a recording `episodic_memory` stub): all 12 spec cases (flag-OFF AD-914 parity, 2-round converse, round-cap stop, convergence stop, `[NO_RESPONSE]` not persisted/propagated, `[NO_RESPONSE]` round-0 fix, exclude-author, all-decline stop, @-mention bypass under cap, AD-933a episode per cascade reply, gap-safe teaching hook split into off/on, Tier-2 degrade). The existing AD-914/915/916/933/933a/933b fan-out tests stay green (**72 passed**, byte-identical — no obsolete-contract updates needed). Focused gate **13 passed**; blast-radius `-k "thread or chat or fanout or facilitat or convergence or reply or pipeline or group or cognitive_agent"` **1025 passed / 1 skipped** (the 4 `test_skill_agent.py::TestSkillPipeline` fails are the pre-existing serial full-suite isolation flakes — green **26/26 in isolation**, unrelated). No UI change → no Vitest. **COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.** Forward markers: **AD-935a** (async/streaming reactivity once a live-refresh exists), **AD-935b** (cascade on agent-initiated group posts, AD-918/AD-924), **AD-935c** (trust/Hebbian learning from a2a chat exchanges).

### AD-934: In-chat `[THINK]`/`[DELIBERATE]` deep-tier re-roll (Option C) — a flag-gated post-LLM pipeline step that, on a `[THINK]`/`[DELIBERATE]` marker in an agent's draft reply, makes ONE deep-tier LLM pass to reconsider + improve the draft, replacing the reply text; default OFF → zero behavior change — **no Option A/B AD-632 chain, no `DmSanityGateConfig` / existing-17-step / `DmReplyContext` / `build_response` / AD-933a-episodic / AD-933b-ref / facilitator / `IntentMessage` / Ward Room change**

**Why Option C over A/B.** The design doc ([prompts/ad-934-in-chat-deliberate.md](../../prompts/ad-934-in-chat-deliberate.md)) framed three options: (A) wire `[THINK]` into the dormant AD-632 sub-task chain via the DM escape hatch, (B) DM-specific chain templates + two-turn re-dispatch, or (C) redefine `[THINK]` as a contained deep-tier re-roll of the agent's own draft. The Captain chose **C**: the agentic loop already serves deep tool-work (chains exist for tool decomposition), so the missing capability in chat is *inline deliberation* — an agent thinking harder about its own answer — not chain re-dispatch. C is tool-free, single-pass, and fully reversible (flag default OFF). Options A/B remain a hard-stop fork in the design doc and are explicitly **not** built here.

**The mechanism (four additive changes, verified vs HEAD).** (1) `config.DmDeliberateConfig(BaseModel)` — `enabled: bool = False`, `tier: str = "deep"`, `max_tokens: int = 800` — mounted on `SystemConfig` right after `dm_targeted_lookup` (convention #14: opt-in transitional flag, default OFF; zero-config boot byte-identical). (2) `dm_sanity_gate` `_DELIBERATE_RE = r"\[(?:THINK|DELIBERATE)\b[^\]\n]*\]"` (well-formed; an optional focus hint like `[THINK be rigorous]` is reserved for AD-934a) + `_DELIBERATE_STRIP_RE` (lax, `\]?`) and `extract_deliberate(text)->bool` / `strip_deliberate(text)->str`, mirroring the AD-845 `[CREATE_TASK]` parse/strip contract (lax strip removes well-formed AND malformed markers so none leak). (3) `reply_pipeline.step_4j_deliberate_parse` — early-returns on no text / no sanity gate; reads `config.dm_deliberate`; **always strips the marker first** (even disabled) so it never reaches the Captain; then, only when `enabled` AND a marker is present, makes ONE deep-tier `llm_client.complete(LLMRequest(prompt, system_prompt, tier, max_tokens))` pass and adopts `resp.content` (re-stripped) or **honest-degrades to the draft** on a missing client / empty / raised response — **NEVER raises** (Tier-2). It is registered in `_full_steps()` BETWEEN `step_4g_create_task_parse` and `step_5_episodic_store` (so the re-rolled reply is what the episodic / divergence / emit steps see → `run()` is now **18** steps) and APPENDED to `_escalation_steps()` after 4g (the channel-agnostic group subset is now **7**), so the 1:1 path AND the AD-933 group fan-out both gain the capability behind the one flag. (4) `cognitive_agent._conversational_deliberate_protocol(observation)` — an overridable (Open/Closed) hook that returns the `[THINK]` teaching string only when `config.dm_deliberate.enabled` (else `""`), invoked in the conversational branch next to `_task_proto`/`_nb_proto`. The teaching string is **gap-regex-safe** (no `can't`/`cannot`/`don't have`/`unable to`/`not able to`) — the `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE` lesson — verified by a test asserting `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE.search(...) is None`.

**Scope fence.** Default OFF means zero behavior change out of the box. NO Option A/B (no AD-632 chain wiring, no `_pending_sub_task_chain`, no `_build_chain_for_intent` DM branch, no chain templates, no two-turn re-dispatch); NO change to the duplicated-cluster `DmSanityGateConfig`, the existing 17 steps' order/bodies, `DmReplyContext`, `build_response`, the AD-933a episodic write, the AD-933b ref surfacing, the facilitator, `IntentMessage`, or the Ward Room; the hook returns `""` when the flag is OFF. **+14 pytest** (`tests/test_ad934_deliberate.py`, BF-287 — real `DmSanityGate` + real `DmDeliberateConfig` + `DmReplyContext` built directly + a real-but-fake `_FakeLLMClient` (NOT `MagicMock`) whose `complete(request, *, priority=…)` records the request and returns an object with `.content`). **Two obsolete-contract step-membership tests updated** (the direct, necessary consequence of inserting 4j — the same pattern AD-933a/933b used, NOT scope creep): AD-933's `_ALL_STEPS` 17→18 + `_ESCALATION_SUBSET` 6→7 (and `test_run_invokes_all_eighteen_steps_in_order`), AD-933b's `_ALL_STEPS`/`_ESCALATION_STEPS` likewise (and `test_run_still_eighteen_steps_in_order`, `len==18`); the `test_bf296` `inspect.getsource(_full_steps)` guard greps for 4b, which 4j does not move → stays green. Focused gate **14 passed**; blast-radius `-k "dm or reply or pipeline or sanity or deliberate or escalat or cognitive_agent or config"` **1376 passed / 1 skipped**, zero regressions. No UI change → no Vitest. **COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.** Forward markers: **AD-934a** (per-agent opt-in / richer teaching + thread the `[THINK reason]` focus hint into the re-roll prompt), **AD-934b** (surface a subtle "deliberated" indicator in the HXI).

### AD-933b: Group-chat image generation — add `step_4c_image_gen_parse` (AD-730-3 `[GEN_IMAGE]`) to the AD-933 channel-agnostic escalation subset so a crew agent can generate an image in a room, and surface the generated SHA refs onto the persisted group message metadata — **no `build_response` / 1:1-path / `DmReplyContext` / `IntentMessage` / facilitator / AD-933a-episodic-write / Ward Room / return-shape change**

**The verified invisible-image gap.** `reply_pipeline.step_4c_image_gen_parse` is already channel-agnostic and 1:1-safe: it reads `ctx.sanity_gate` + `ctx.runtime.config.avatars.image_gen_*`, calls `dispatch_image_gen(runtime, agent_id=…, prompt=…)`, appends the returned SHA to `ctx.generated_attachment_ids`, and honest-degrades (marker stripped, operator message appended) when the tier is disabled/unconfigured — nothing in it is 1:1- or avatar-scoped. But AD-933's `_escalation_steps()` deliberately omitted 4c, and the group fan-out (`thread_fanout.group_chat_fanout._send_one`) returns `{agent_id, callsign, text}` and never calls `build_response()` — the 1:1 method that exposes `generated_attachment_ids` on the response. Net: a group-generated image would be created and persisted to `AttachmentStore` (AD-731 SHA refs) yet **invisible** — no path carried the ref to anywhere the room could render it.

**The two additive changes.** (1) `_escalation_steps()` adds `self.step_4c_image_gen_parse` in **run()-order** (4c precedes 4e in `_full_steps`), so the subset tuple becomes `(4c, 4e, 4i, 4h, 4f, 4g)` and `run_escalation_only()` runs **6** steps. `run()` and `_full_steps()` are **byte-identical** — 4c was already in `_full_steps`, so the 1:1 path is untouched; only the docstring's Included/Excluded lists and the relative-order parenthetical were corrected (4c moved from Excluded → Included; the stale `Forward markers: AD-933a/AD-933b` line replaced by the live `AD-933b-2` `step_4d_follow_up` deferral). (2) `_send_one` initializes `generated_ids: list[str] = []` before the AD-933 escalation block, then — inside the same Tier-2 try, after `reply_text = pipeline.ctx.response_text or reply_text` — captures `generated_ids = list(pipeline.ctx.generated_attachment_ids or [])` from the **SAME** `pipeline.ctx` the AD-933 block already built (no second pipeline), and in the persist block extends the existing `append_message` metadata `{"intent_id": intent.id, "fanout": "ad914"}` with `"generated_attachment_ids": generated_ids` **only when non-empty** (AD-916 established `metadata`-carried attachment refs on chat messages). Tier-2: a skipped (no reply / no agent) or raised escalation leaves `generated_ids == []` and the persisted metadata **byte-identical** to the AD-914 baseline; the `{agent_id, callsign, text}` return shape is unchanged.

**Why `step_4d_follow_up` stays out (the subset grows by exactly one).** `step_4d_follow_up_parse` schedules a synthesized user-turn via the runtime's `conversation_pacing_scheduler` — in a 1:1 the target is unambiguous, but in a multi-agent room "who is the follow-up addressed to / who re-speaks" is undefined, so it is deferred as forward marker **AD-933b-2** (and UI rendering of group-generated images, which AD-916's `metadata` ref carriage now makes possible, is **AD-933b-3**). The right answer is the minimal subset extension, not a follow-up redesign. **One obsolete-contract test was updated** — the AD-933 `test_run_escalation_only_invokes_only_the_subset` asserted the OLD 5-step `_ESCALATION_SUBSET`; that constant was re-pointed to the 6-step subset (4c first), preserving its named intent (escalation runs ONLY the subset; the other 11 steps never fire) — the same obsolete-contract-test pattern as AD-933a's `test_group_path_writes_no_1to1_episode` re-point, not scope creep. +5 pytest (`tests/test_ad933b_group_image_gen.py`, BF-287 real `ChatThreadStore`+`IntentBus`+`DmSanityGate`; `dispatch_image_gen` monkeypatched at its source module `probos.cognitive.image_gen_dispatch` because step_4c imports it function-locally): spy-level `run_escalation_only()` runs exactly `{4c,4e,4i,4h,4f,4g}` (other 11 not) + `run()` still 17 byte-identical; fan-out-level group `[GEN_IMAGE a cat]` surfaces `metadata.generated_attachment_ids == ["sha-xyz"]` (marker stripped), disabled tier honest-degrades (operator message appended, no ref key, no crash), and a plain reply leaves metadata exactly `{"intent_id","fanout"}`. Focused gate **5 passed**; blast-radius `-k "thread or chat or fanout or reply or pipeline or image or escalat"` **860 passed / 4 failed / 1 skipped** (the 4 fails are the pre-existing `test_skill_agent.py::TestSkillPipeline` serial full-suite isolation flakes — `Event loop is closed` cross-test pollution — **green 7/7 in isolation**, about skill-pool spawning, zero connection to AD-933b). No UI change → no Vitest. **COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.** Forward markers: **AD-933b-2** (in-chat `[FOLLOW_UP]`), **AD-933b-3** (UI render of group-generated images), **AD-934** (in-chat `[THINK]`/`[DELIBERATE]`).

### AD-933a: Group-anchored episodic write for the fan-out — add a Tier-2 episodic-write loop at the END of `group_chat_fanout` so every group-chat reply persists ONE `channel="chat"` / `session_type:"group"` episode tagged with the thread id, mirroring the AD-719 @-mention fan-out but group-anchored; closes the learning-loop hole AD-933 left open — **no `_send_one` / `DmReplyPipeline` / `_store_action_episode` / `step_5` / 1:1-path / facilitator / `IntentMessage` / Ward Room change**

**The verified no-episode gap.** A group-chat fan-out reply wrote **no episode at all** — a learning-loop integrity hole. Two paths both decline the write: (1) the fan-out sends `direct_message` with `params["from"]="hxi_profile"` (`thread_fanout._send_one`), and the agent's universal episodic safety-net `_store_action_episode` (`cognitive_agent.py:8034`) **skips exactly that case** (`if intent.intent == "direct_message" and source in ("hxi_profile","captain"): return`), deferring to the pipeline's `step_5_episodic_store`; (2) AD-933 deliberately **excluded** `step_5` from the group escalation subset because `step_5` hardcodes `session_type:"1:1"`/`channel:"dm"`/`participants:["captain", callsign]`, which would **mislabel** a multi-agent turn. So neither path fired — agents could not remember what they said in a room (no episodic recall, no dreaming consolidation, no wellness/divergence analysis), violating the standing invariant "every execution path stores an episode or the learning loop breaks."

**The mirror-AD-719 fix.** The AD-719 @-mention fan-out (`routers/chat.py` ~L215–256) already solves the identical problem on the 1:1-chat substrate: per resolved reply it writes one group-shaped episode (`dream_adapter.build_episode(...)` when a `dream_adapter` is present, else a direct `Episode(...)` with `AnchorFrame(channel="chat", trigger_type="at_mention_fanout")`), inside a Tier-2 `try/except` that logs and continues. AD-933a mirrors this exactly at the END of `group_chat_fanout` (after `replies = await asyncio.gather(...)`), but group-anchored: `episodic_memory = getattr(runtime, "episodic_memory", None)` (skip entirely if `None`); participants resolved **once** as `["captain"] + [callsign-or-agent_id per crew speaker]`; then for each reply — **skipping** the sentinel set `{"(no response)", "(delivery failed)", ""}` and any reply with no `agent_id` — build the episode (prefer `runtime.dream_adapter.build_episode(episode_input, {"response":…, "agent_ids":[…]}, t_start, t_end)` when a `dream_adapter` exists; else a direct `Episode(timestamp=time.time(), user_input="[group chat] Captain: …", dag_summary={}, outcomes=[{"intent":"direct_message","success":True,"response":reply["text"][:500],"session_type":"group","callsign":…,"source":"group_chat_fanout"}], agent_ids=[reply["agent_id"]], duration_ms=…, source="group_chat_fanout", anchors=AnchorFrame(channel="chat", trigger_type="group_fanout", participants=…, chat_thread_id=thread_id))`), then `await episodic_memory.store(episode)` inside a `try/except Exception` that logs `AD-933a: group episode store failed …; continuing` and **NEVER raises** — the fan-out always returns all replies even if a store fails. `t_start = time.monotonic()` is captured at the TOP of the function (new module-level `import time`); `t_end` right after the gather. `source="group_chat_fanout"` is a distinct memory tag, parallel to AD-719's `"multi_agent_chat"`, so group episodes are trivially filterable for recall/dreaming.

**Why `step_5` stays excluded (the fix is additive, not a `step_5` generalization).** The right answer is **not** to teach `step_5_episodic_store` to write group episodes: `step_5` is the 1:1-pipeline's episodic writer, hardcoded to `session_type:"1:1"`/`channel:"dm"` and `participants:["captain", callsign]`, and it runs inside `DmReplyPipeline.run()` (the 1:1 `/chat` path). Reusing it for group would require a context-conditional that mutates the 1:1 contract — a Defense-in-Depth and Single-Responsibility violation — and AD-933 already established that the group fan-out runs only the **channel-agnostic** escalation subset (`step_5` is deliberately out). AD-933a instead writes a **dedicated, group-shaped** episode at the fan-out call site, where the thread id, participants, and group semantics are all in scope, leaving the 1:1 pipeline and `step_5` byte-identical. The preferred `dream_adapter.build_episode` branch mirrors AD-719 for DRY/consistency (and runs in production, where a `dream_adapter` exists); the direct `Episode(...)` fallback carries the explicit group anchors and is the branch exercised by the BF-287 tests (their runtime has no `dream_adapter`). **One obsolete-contract test was updated** — the AD-933 `test_group_path_writes_no_1to1_episode` asserted `recorder.stored == []` (the pre-AD-933a "no episode at all" behavior that AD-933a's entire purpose overturns); it was re-pointed to "group episodes ARE written now, and NONE are 1:1-labelled" (`session_type != "1:1"`, `channel != "dm"`), preserving its named intent (step_5/the 1:1 writer never fires on the group path). This is the direct, necessary consequence of the spec'd behavior change — the same obsolete-contract-test pattern as AD-933's own `test_bf296` re-point, not scope creep. +6 pytest (`tests/test_ad933a_group_episode.py`, BF-287 real `ChatThreadStore`+`IntentBus`+a real-but-fake recording `episodic_memory`, no `dream_adapter`); focused gate **6 passed**, blast-radius `-k "thread or chat or fanout or episod or dream"` **1285 passed / 1 skipped**. Forward markers: **AD-933b** richer escalation subset, **AD-934** in-chat `[THINK]`/`[DELIBERATE]`.

### AD-933: Wire the AD-726 one-shot escalation ladder into the AD-914 group-chat fan-out — refactor `DmReplyPipeline.run()`'s 17-step tuple into `_full_steps()` + `_run_steps(steps)` (run() **byte-identical**) and add a public `run_escalation_only()` that runs only the **channel-agnostic escalation subset** (`[ACTION]` / notebook / mesh-read / artifacts / `[CREATE_TASK]`); `thread_fanout._send_one` runs that subset on the raw reply so a group turn can escalate, not just ship a Tier-1 reply — **no `run()` behavior change, no step-body change, no `DmReplyContext` change, no facilitator / `IntentMessage` / vision / Ward Room change**

**The Tier-1-only group seam, closed.** The 1:1 chat path (`routers/agents.py:agent_chat`) and the group fan-out (`routers/thread_fanout.py:group_chat_fanout._send_one`) are structurally identical up through `result = await runtime.intent_bus.send(intent)` — both build `IntentMessage(intent="direct_message", …)` and read `result.result`. But the 1:1 path then constructs a `DmReplyContext` + `DmReplyPipeline` and runs the **post-LLM escalation + cleanup ladder** (AD-726: inline mesh reads AD-869, `[ACTION]` dispatch AD-745, `[CREATE_TASK]` AD-845, artifact extraction AD-797, notebook AD-911, plus 1:1-specific steps), whereas `_send_one` took `reply_text = str(result.result)` **RAW** and persisted it — it **never constructed the pipeline**. So group chat was **Tier-1 only**: an agent in a room could not resolve an inline mesh read, dispatch a browser `[ACTION]`, or open a task via `[CREATE_TASK]`. `DmReplyPipeline` was already **extracted** from the endpoint (AD-726) precisely so it could be reused; the fan-out simply never got wired to it. AD-933 is that wiring.

**Three execution modes, one source of truth.** The post-LLM ladder now has three callers, mapped explicitly: (1) **1:1 `/chat`** → `run()` (the full 17 steps); (2) **group fan-out** → `run_escalation_only()` (the 5-step subset); (3) **proactive `[GROUP_CHAT]`/`[STATUS]`/`[ARTIFACT]` tags** → the AD-924/927/928 proactive extractors (unchanged). To keep them DRY, `run()`'s hardcoded 17-step tuple is extracted into `def _full_steps(self) -> tuple[Callable, ...]` and the `for step in (…)` loop body into `async def _run_steps(self, steps)` (the verbatim AD-726 per-step `try/except … logger.warning("AD-726: pipeline step %s raised …")` guard); `run()` becomes `await self._run_steps(self._full_steps())` — **byte-identical** (same 17 steps, same order, same guard; a regression-guard test asserts `run()` still invokes all 17 in order). `_escalation_steps()` returns the subset in run()-order — `step_4e_action_dispatch`, `step_4i_notebook_parse`, `step_4h_mesh_read_parse`, `step_4f_extract_artifacts`, `step_4g_create_task_parse` — and `run_escalation_only()` runs exactly that under the same guard. In `_send_one`, `sanity_gate = getattr(runtime, "dm_sanity_gate", None)` is resolved **once** before the `asyncio.gather` (DRY; `step_4g` needs it), and **only when** a real `result.result` came back **AND** `agent is not None`, it builds `DmReplyPipeline(DmReplyContext(…, sampling_state=None, avatar_event_bus=None, chat_thread_id=thread_id))`, `await pipeline.run_escalation_only()`, and adopts `reply_text = pipeline.ctx.response_text or reply_text` (now tag-stripped + may carry the `(Task opened: <id>)` suffix) before the existing `store.append_message(…)`. The whole block is **Tier-2 honest-degrade** (an inner `try/except` plus the per-step guards inside the pipeline) so any failure ships the raw `reply_text` rather than silencing a reply.

**Why the *subset*, not the full `run()`.** Running the full pipeline verbatim on group replies is **wrong** because several steps carry 1:1 semantics — the decisive one is `step_5_episodic_store`, which hardcodes `session_type:"1:1"`, `channel:"dm"`, `participants:["captain", callsign]`; firing it on a multi-agent group reply writes **mislabeled** episodes — a learning-loop integrity regression. `step_6` (working memory) similarly records `"Captain DM"`, and `step_1` (sanity retry), `step_2/3` (games), `step_4b` (outbound DM), `step_4c` (image-gen), `step_4d` (follow-up), `step_7` (divergence), `step_8` (mark-emitted/avatar), `step_9` (emotion) are all 1:1/avatar-scoped. So AD-933 runs only the **channel-agnostic** steps: each is a strict no-op for any reply lacking its marker, and the markers are emitted only by specifically-taught agents (e.g. Yeo for `[CREATE_TASK]`), so the subset is inherently bounded and safe outside the 1:1 path. None of the module's ordering invariants (sanity-before-games, self-check-before-episodic, divergence-before-emit) involve these five, so the subset is internally order-independent; run()-order is kept for clarity.

**Non-goals / forward markers.** **`DmReplyPipeline.run()` behavior byte-identical** (all 17 steps, same order, same guard); the 1:1 `/api/agent/{id}/chat` path **unchanged** (still calls `run()`); **no step-method body change**, no `DmReplyContext` field change, no `build_response()` change. **NO** facilitator / who-speaks-order / `IntentMessage` / vision-pipeline / persist-call change. **NO** AD-632 chain touch (`_CHAIN_ELIGIBLE_INTENTS`, `_should_activate_chain`, `_execute_chain_with_intent_routing`, `_pending_sub_task_chain`) — in-chat `[THINK]`/`[DELIBERATE]` via the dormant escape hatch is the deferred **AD-934**. **NO** AD-925 task-room logic (it fires downstream automatically when a created task fans to ≥2 crew); **NO** Ward Room. A correct **group-anchored** episodic write is forward marker **AD-933a**; an optional richer subset is **AD-933b**. **Tests: +8 pytest** (`tests/test_ad933_group_chat_escalation.py`, BF-287 — real `WorkItemStore` (in-memory SQLite, started), real `ChatThreadStore` on `tmp_path`, real `IntentBus(SignalManager(reap_interval=1.0))` with subscribed `direct_message` handlers, real `DmSanityGate` on `runtime.dm_sanity_gate`, real-but-fake registry/callsign stubs — no MagicMock at the substrate boundary): group `[CREATE_TASK]` opens a dispatchable `yeo-delegated` work item + persists the reply tag-stripped with `(Task opened: <id>)`; plain reply is a no-op (zero work items); `dm_sanity_gate=None` honest-degrades; the group path writes NO 1:1-labelled episode (recording `episodic_memory` proves `step_5` excluded); an AD-869 mesh marker runs/strips without hanging (empty pool → `step_4h` fast-degrades, no bus TTL wait); `run_escalation_only()` invokes ONLY the 5-step subset and `run()` still invokes all 17 in order (spy guards); the fan-out return shape `{agent_id, callsign, text}` is preserved with the mutated `text`. The `test_bf296` `inspect.getsource(run)` structural guard was re-pointed at `_full_steps` (the tuple's new home — its intent, step_4b present + ordered, is preserved). Focused gate **8 passed**; blast-radius `-k "thread or chat or fanout or dm or reply or pipeline or create_task or escalat"` **1164 passed | 1 skipped**, zero regressions. No UI change → no Vitest. **COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed** (the Captain decides the push). Forward markers: **AD-933a** (group-anchored episodic write), **AD-933b** (richer subset), **AD-934** (in-chat `[THINK]`/`[DELIBERATE]`).

### AD-932: Discoverable "+ Add people" on an empty/fresh 1:1 chat — a small `EmptyChatAddPeople` affordance, mounted by `ProfileChatTab` only when `!activeThreadId`, that **materializes** the 1:1 thread (`createThread([agentId])`) so the existing AD-917 `GroupChatHeader` (+ its `AddParticipantPopover`) takes over — a materialize-then-hand-off, frontend-only, **no `GroupChatHeader` contract change, no backend, no Ward Room**

**The undiscoverable-add gap on a fresh 1:1, closed.** The AD-917 in-chat group controls mount in `ProfileChatTab` only as `{activeThreadId && <GroupChatHeader threadId={activeThreadId} />}`, and `GroupChatHeader` early-returns `if (!thread) return null`. A brand-new 1:1 has **no thread until the first message is sent** (`get_or_create_default_for_agent` creates the row server-side on the first `agent_chat` turn), so on an empty 1:1 `activeThreadId` is `undefined` → the header never mounts → there is **no add-participant control at all**. The only pre-AD-932 path to "add someone" was send-a-message-first-then-find-the-thin-header-bar — exactly the Captain's "undiscoverable" observation.

**Materialize, then hand off (don't duplicate the picker).** AD-932 adds a focused `ui/src/components/profile/EmptyChatAddPeople.tsx` mounted via one sibling line `{!activeThreadId && <EmptyChatAddPeople agentId={agentId} />}`. On click it creates the 1:1 thread, writes it into the store, and points the agent at it — `setChatThread(t)` + `setThreadForAgent(agentId, t.id)` — which makes `activeThreadId` resolve, so the **existing** `GroupChatHeader` (and its `AddParticipantPopover`) mounts on the next render and the Captain uses *that* picker to add the second crew member. AD-932 only carries the empty state from "no thread" → "thread exists, header visible"; it does **not** re-implement the picker. Auto-opening the picker on materialize would need a new `GroupChatHeader` prop (`defaultPickerOpen`); to keep the header's contract unchanged that is deferred as forward marker **AD-932a**.

**Why `createThread`, not a hidden default.** There is no client-callable "get-or-create my 1:1 thread" endpoint — `get_or_create_default_for_agent` is invoked only server-side by the `agent_chat` path. When `ProfileChatTab` shows the empty state the client genuinely has **no** thread for the agent (`threadId` prop undefined AND `threadIdByAgent.get(agentId)` empty — the exact gate for rendering the button), so `createThread({ title: callsign, participants: [agentId] })` is the correct client-side materialization; the row it mints (`participants=[agentId]`, `project_id=NULL`) is also what the server's default lookup matches. The known minor edge (a second `participants=[agentId]` row if a server default existed but was never hydrated) is Tier-2 acceptable — the Captain's intent is a group, so the next `addParticipant` turns it into `[agentId, X]`; no backend de-dup is added here.

**Disjoint by construction; self-gated.** The mount is mutually exclusive with `GroupChatHeader` (one iff `activeThreadId`, the other iff `!activeThreadId`) and disjoint from the AD-929 Files rail (`showWorkspaceFiles = !!activeThreadId && isWorkspaceRoom(...)` is `false` when `!activeThreadId`), so it never co-renders with the rail, `MeetingView`, or the meeting gates (all `activeThreadId`-gated). The component self-gates on `agent?.isCrew` (only a crew 1:1 can become a group; non-crew / unknown host → renders nothing). `createThread` honest-degrades to `null` → keep the button, no store write. HXI #3 — inline-SVG `UserPlus` (reused; **no `Glyphs.tsx` exports**, the export-count test stays green), amber `#f0b060` / dim, glow-on-hover, no emoji.

**Non-goals / forward markers.** **Independent of AD-931** (builds on AD-917/threadApi; touches only `profile/`, imports nothing from `chats/`). **NO `GroupChatHeader` change** (forward marker **AD-932a** = auto-open picker). No full-`ProfileChatTab` render test (the `groupsend`/`bf294b` precedent: "too heavy to render" → component-isolation tests only). **NO Ward Room DM convergence**, chain-pipeline, `ward_room/*`, or AD-574c-i. No backend / REST / pytest / new endpoint / `get_or_create_default_for_agent` exposure. No AD-929 Files-rail / AD-925 task-room change. No `LeftRail.tsx` wire. No eager thread creation on profile open (materialized only on the explicit click). **Tests: +8 Vitest** (`profile/__tests__/EmptyChatAddPeople.test.tsx`, BF-287 real store + mocked `threadApi.createThread`): renders for crew; nothing for non-crew / unknown agentId; click → `createThread` once with `{title, participants:[agentId]}`; success writes `setChatThread` + `setThreadForAgent`; honest-degrade on `null`; clickable; no-emoji. Full Vitest **1270 passed | 1 skipped** (215 files; baseline 1262 + 8, zero regressions); `npm run build` clean (`tsc -b`). **COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed** (the Captain decides the push). ### AD-931: Unified CHATS surface — one Teams/Slack-style home listing BOTH 1:1 and group conversations with a prominent "+ New chat" picker; **repurposes** (moves + renames) the AD-919 `GroupChatListPanel` into `ChatsPanel`, widens the filter to `isChat` (1:1 + group, **excluding** AD-925 task rooms), and branches the create flow on selection count — frontend-only, no backend, **NO Ward Room DM convergence** (the two DM systems stay a deliberate pipeline A/B test)

**The "no way to start a chat" gap, closed — and the two-mental-models seam removed.** The Captain's observations (verified against HEAD): (1) `GroupChatListPanel` (AD-919) was **visibility + Join only** — it listed group chats but had **no create affordance** anywhere in the HXI; (2) the TopNav exposed "GROUP CHATS" as a thing apart from 1:1 DMs, whereas Teams/Slack present **one Chats list** holding both — a 1:1 lived only inside an agent's profile chat tab and never appeared in a list. AD-931 is the single unified entry point: one **CHATS** panel that lists 1:1 + group with a **"+ New chat"** picker.

**Repurpose + rename, not a sibling.** A second panel would violate "one chats home," so AD-931 **moves** `groupchat/GroupChatListPanel.tsx` → `chats/ChatsPanel.tsx`, extracts the five pure helpers (`crewParticipantIds`/`isAgentCreated`/`isGroupChat`/`captainJoined`/`hostAgentId`) + constants verbatim into `chats/chatFilters.ts`, and renames the store flag `groupChatListOpen` → `chatsOpen` (+ `openGroupChatList`/`closeGroupChatList` → `openChats`/`closeChats`) and the TopNav `GROUP CHATS` (testId `group-chats-toggle`) → `CHATS` (`chats-toggle`). The internal rename (not just the label) is because once the panel lists 1:1s the old name is actively misleading; grep confirmed the blast radius is **only** `useStore.ts`, `App.tsx`, the panel, and its test (no App-level test references the flag). `LeftRail.tsx` stays the forward marker AD-719b-parent-wire (untouched).

**The unified `isChat` filter — admits 1:1s, excludes task rooms.** A new pure `isChat(thread, agents)` widens AD-919's `isGroupChat`: `!thread.task_id && (isAgentCreated(thread) || crewParticipantIds(thread, agents).length >= 1)`. 1:1s appear because `get_or_create_default_for_agent` (`threads/__init__.py:636`) inserts a real listed `chat_threads` row (`participants=[agentId]`, `metadata.is_default=true`, `task_id=NULL`), and `GET /api/threads` (`list_threads`) returns ALL non-archived rows with **no participant filter** — so this is frontend-only, no backend change. The `!task_id` gate **excludes AD-925 task rooms** (`crew_executor.py:319` sets `task_id`), so the list reads like Teams' *Chat* list, not its *Teams/Channels* list. Within a row, `isGroupChat` still distinguishes: a **group** keeps the AD-919 treatment (multi-avatar strip, agent-created badge, **Join** when `!captainJoined`); a **1:1** shows a single avatar + callsign and **no Join** (Join would `add_participant('captain')`, meaningless for a 1:1).

**"+ New chat" branches on selection count (avoids the duplicate-1:1 trap).** `NewChatModal` **reuses** the AD-917 `AddParticipantPopover` as its selection surface — each `onAdd` accumulates into `selected[]`, the running selection is fed back as `existingParticipantIds` so picked agents drop out, removable chips above the popover, a **"Start chat"** CTA disabled until `selected.length >= 1`. On confirm: **1 agent → `openAgentProfile(agentId)`** (do NOT `createThread` — the server-side `get_or_create_default_for_agent` owns the 1:1 default; minting a second `participants=[agentId]` row would diverge from the `agent_chat` default lookup); **2+ agents → `createThread({ title, participants })`** (`title` = selected callsigns joined, fallback `"New group chat"`) then `setThreadForAgent(selected[0], thread.id)` + `openAgentProfile(selected[0])` (verbatim AD-919 host pattern); `createThread` honest-degrades to `null` → keep the modal open (Tier-2), no throw.

**Non-goals / forward markers.** **NO Ward Room DM convergence** — Ward Room DMs (`channel_type=='dm'`, `DmActivityLog`, the **chain pipeline**, `ward_room/*`, **AD-574c-i**) are untouched: the two DM systems are a **deliberate A/B test** (Ward Room = chain pipeline, 1:1 Chats = one-shot pipeline), so convergence is **gated on a pipeline decision**, not folded in here. No backend / REST / pytest (every endpoint already exists). No `LeftRail.tsx` wire. No `Glyphs.tsx` exports (reuse `UserPlus`/`Close` + local inline SVGs — the export-count test stays green). No `createThread` for the 1-agent path. No `GroupChatHeader`/`ProfileChatTab` change. The discoverable in-chat add-people on an empty 1:1 is the sibling **AD-932** (intentionally split out). **Tests (Vitest, UI hard rule): +25 across three new files** — `chats/__tests__/chatFilters.test.ts` (8 — `isChat` admits 1:1 / group / agent-created, excludes task room + captain-only; `isGroupChat`/`hostAgentId`/`captainJoined` parity), `chats/__tests__/ChatsPanel.test.tsx` (11 — migrated from the 10 AD-919 panel tests with test #1 FLIPPED to "lists BOTH 1:1 and group; excludes task room", + a 1:1-row-no-Join + 1:1-click-opens-host case), `chats/__tests__/NewChatModal.test.tsx` (6 — button opens modal + popover; Start gate ≥1; 1→`openAgentProfile` no `createThread`; 2+→`createThread` + open host; chip remove; no-emoji), **superseding** the deleted 10-test `groupchat/__tests__/GroupChatListPanel.test.tsx` (net suite ≈ +15). Full Vitest **1262 passed | 1 skipped** (214 files; baseline 1247 + 25 − 10 superseded, zero regressions); `npm run build` clean (`tsc -b`). **COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed** (the Captain decides the push).  — `POST /api/work-items/{work_item_id}/inputs` populates the AD-926 `WorkItem.metadata["input_attachments"]` convention via the SHARED chat uploader and a single read-merge-write (the WRITE half of the Task Workspace Rooms Inputs folder; the AD-926 read endpoint + the AD-929 Files rail already work)

**The population path AD-926 deferred.** AD-926 shipped the READ (`GET /api/threads/{id}/inputs`) and AD-929 the display (the Files rail), but the authoritative `WorkItem.metadata["input_attachments"]` source was a **defined-but-dormant seam** — nothing WROTE it (`git grep AD-926a` returned only two forward-marker comments). The Captain asked: "attach multiple files as context inputs for a task." AD-926a is the missing WRITE half — a new `POST /api/work-items/{work_item_id}/inputs` (multipart `files: list[UploadFile]`) on the **existing** `/api` workforce router (NOT under `threads.py`: inputs are owned by the work item, and a thread learns about them through its `task_id`).

**Reuse the uploader, never a parallel one.** Each file routes through the SHARED `chat._validate_and_store_attachment` — the same AD-720a defense-in-depth chain the chat multipart endpoint uses: feature gate → MIME allowlist → size cap → sha256 → magic-byte `validate_attachment_bytes` → idempotent content-addressable `AttachmentStore.write` — with the DEFAULT `origin="chat_attachment"` (operator intent, never age-reaped, last to LRU-evict; a new `task_input` origin would coerce to `chat_attachment` anyway per the `_normalize_origin` allowlist, so none is added). On success a ref `{content_hash, mime, filename}` (the exact shape `_collect_task_inputs` reads, `source="task"`) is appended; `filename` comes from the `UploadFile` (the uploader's success dict has none).

**Single read-merge-write (the `update_work_item` REPLACE crux).** `WorkItemStore.update_work_item(id, metadata=…)` writes the `metadata` column as a WHOLE-COLUMN REPLACE (`json.dumps`), with no native merge and no `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` / optimistic concurrency. So the merge MUST happen at the call site: validate+store ALL N files FIRST, accumulate the refs, then ONE `get_work_item` → `dict(metadata)` → append the new refs (DEDUPE by `content_hash`, so an idempotent re-upload is a no-op) → `update_work_item(metadata=merged)`, preserving every other metadata key plus any existing `input_attachments`. Storing all files before the single write eliminates the intra-request race; the cross-request last-writer-wins is a documented bounded seam (an operator-driven manual action, rare concurrency) → a store-level atomic `append_input_attachments` (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, mirroring `ChatThreadStore.set_title`) is the forward marker **AD-926a-2**. `update_work_item` is deliberately NOT refactored here.

**Honest-degrade per file; operator authority.** A rejected file (oversize / mime mismatch / disallowed) is collected into `skipped` rather than 500-ing the whole request — good files still attach. 503 when `work_item_store` is None, 404 when the work item is missing (mirroring the sibling work-item routes). Authority is operator/Captain-facing and mirrors the other work-item mutations (PATCH / transition / assign / delete have no per-caller authority check): attaching a file is additive, reversible, low-risk → **no consensus gate** (Safety Budget axiom), stated in the docstring.

**UI — the "+ Attach" affordance.** `WorkspaceFilesRail` gains a `taskId?` prop (`ProfileChatTab` passes `workspaceThread?.task_id`); the Inputs section shows a multi-file "+ Attach" button (a hidden `<input type="file" multiple>` + inline stroke-SVG, HXI #3 no-emoji, amber `#f0b060`) ONLY when `taskId` is set — a ≥2-crew room without a bound work item has no place to hold inputs (a forward-marker constraint, stated). A new `inputsApi.attachTaskInputs(workItemId, files)` posts ONE multipart `files[]` request (mirroring `ProfileChatTab.uploadAttachment`) and refreshes the rail's local `inputs` from the returned list.

**Non-goals / forward markers.** No input edit / versioning (inputs are immutable context; the editable side is artifacts/outputs, AD-797/AD-927). No delete-input in v1 (**AD-926a-1**). No store-level atomic merge — `update_work_item` is not refactored (**AD-926a-2**). No new attachment origin. No kanban / `WorkBoard` card attach button. No change to the `AttachmentStore` Protocol, the `WorkItem` schema/dataclass, the AD-926 read endpoint / `_collect_task_inputs`, the AD-925 create path, or the message-attachment (`source="message"`) path. No consensus gate / quorum, no new `EventType`, no new config field, no new REST router (extend the workforce router). **Tests:** `tests/test_ad926a_task_file_upload.py` (+10, BF-287 — real `WorkItemStore` + real `FilesystemAttachmentStore` + real `ChatThreadStore` + real `SystemConfig`, `UploadFile` built from `io.BytesIO`, the chat uploader store cache seeded so the write lands in the test store: two-file append + read-back, bytes land by sha256, second-upload append preserving a sentinel metadata key, within-request dedupe, mixed good/bad per-file skip, disallowed-mime skip, 404, 503, empty-files no-op, integration via `GET /api/threads/{id}/inputs` `source="task"`) + `ui/src/components/inputs/__tests__/inputsApi.attach.test.ts` (+5) + `ui/src/components/workspace/__tests__/WorkspaceFilesRail.attach.test.tsx` (+5). Focused pytest **28** (10 AD-926a + 10 AD-926 + 8 AD-925); blast-radius `-k "workforce or work_item or thread or chat or attachment or input"` **797 passed**; full Vitest **1247 passed | 1 skipped** (212 files; baseline 1237 + 10, zero regressions); `npm run build` clean. **COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed** (Task Workspace Rooms epic held for Captain review/push). Forward markers: **AD-926a-1** (delete-input), **AD-926a-2** (atomic store-level append).

### AD-930: Crew presence layer — a Microsoft-Teams-style per-crew presence dot (`offline | online | working | in_meeting`) computed by a read-only polled `GET /api/crew/presence` that **aggregates three verified-existing signals (liveness, `meeting_active` thread membership, recent `last_active`) and invents no telemetry**; the last Teams-signature gap after group chat (AD-913→919), meetings (AD-920→923), and the Task Workspace Rooms epic (AD-925→929)

**The presence dot the Captain asked for.** The request: "a good indicator to see if the agent is actively working or in a meeting." Every signal a presence layer needs already exists, so AD-930 is **aggregation, not new instrumentation**. `online`/liveness = `BaseAgent.is_alive` (`AgentState` ∈ {ACTIVE, DEGRADED}, `agent.py:101`) over `registry.all()` filtered by `is_crew_agent`; `in_meeting` = the agent is a participant of a non-archived chat thread whose `metadata.meeting_active` is set (AD-920); `working` = `AgentMeta.last_active` (`types.py:40`, bumped in `update_confidence()` after each completed op) within a new `CommunicationsConfig.presence_working_window_seconds` (default 90.0).

**Decision 1 — the 4-state model + precedence.** `PresenceState = offline | online | working | in_meeting`. **Liveness is the floor:** a not-alive agent is `offline` regardless of thread membership (SPAWNING/RECYCLING/absent). Among alive agents the precedence is the Captain's stated order `in_meeting > working > online` — an agent both recently-active *and* in a meeting reads as `in_meeting` (matching Teams' "In a meeting" busy variant). Keyed by `agent_id` (the registry instance id, which is also what thread `participants` and `meta` are keyed on).

**Decision 2 — `working` is an HONEST recent-activity proxy, not an in-flight flag.** There is **no canonical per-agent "currently executing right now" backend source at HEAD** — `avatars/telemetry.py:24` states it verbatim (the avatar `load` is a TTS-speaking approximation, not task work). The real signal that *does* exist is `AgentMeta.last_active`, bumped after each completed operation (tool dispatch, `CognitiveAgent.handle_intent`, the proactive loop) and already consumed as a recency signal at `introspective_telemetry.py:111`. So v1 `working` = "completed an operation within `presence_working_window_seconds`" — a last-completed-op proxy, explicitly NOT a fabricated in-flight flag. A true in-flight signal is the forward marker **AD-930a**. The window field ships ON by default (read-only/computed, not a transitional behavioral flag).

**Decision 3 — one read-only POLLED endpoint on the existing router, not a stream.** `GET /api/crew/presence` is appended to the **existing** `/api/crew` router (`crew.py:32`, no new router) → `{"presence": {agent_id: state}, "count": N}` for crew only. A polled GET is the v1 path (simplest, least-invasive, exactly-once computed server-side) over a new WebSocket channel or riding the fleet avatar-telemetry stream. Tier-2 honest-degrade throughout: `registry None` → `{}`,`0`; `chat_thread_store None` or a meeting-scan failure → no `in_meeting` (agents fall through to `working`/`online`); config-missing → the 90s default.

**Decision 4 — UI: a pure `PresenceDot` + a roster-scoped poll + an optional badge overlay.** A pure no-emoji `PresenceDot` (green `#60c070` / amber-pulse `#f0b060` / blue `#5090d0` / dim `#666680`; `data-presence` + `data-pulse` test hooks; HXI #3 stroke/SVG, HXI #4 motion=state — the amber pulse encodes "working"). A `presence: CrewPresenceMap` store slice + `fetchPresence` (mirrors the `openCrewManifest` fetch+set idiom, minus open/close — presence is ambient data, not a panel) polled every 10s **while `CrewRosterPanel` is open**, a dot beside each `CrewRow` callsign, and an **optional** `presence?` prop on the reusable `AgentAvatarBadge` (omitted = byte-identical original badge, backward-compatible — no existing call site/test changes). v1 only the roster feeds presence; wiring it into every badge surface app-wide needs a global poll → forward marker **AD-930b**.

**Non-goals / forward markers.** No true in-flight "working" signal / new telemetry infrastructure (**AD-930a**). No activity feed / status messages (that is AD-928's `[STATUS]`). No global app-wide presence poll wiring every badge surface (**AD-930b**). No new WebSocket channel, no riding the fleet avatar-telemetry stream. No `degraded`/`away` states (DEGRADED agents are `is_alive`, so they read `online`/`working`). No change to `AgentState`/`LifecycleState`, `BaseAgent`, `AgentMeta`, `ChatThreadStore`, the `/api/crew/roster` or `/api/ontology/crew-manifest` endpoints, `MeetingView`, `ParametricAvatar`/`CrewVRM`, consensus/trust, `IntentMessage`, or `Glyphs.tsx`. No new `EventType`, no new REST router (extend `crew.py`), no new config class (extend `CommunicationsConfig`), no new store method beyond `fetchPresence`. (Verify-first correction: the spec assumed `CommunicationsConfig` used `field_validator`s for the status caps — it does not; the new `presence_working_window_seconds` is a plain field with a sensible default, matching the existing class style, so no invented validator.)

**Tests:** `tests/test_ad930_presence.py` (+9, BF-287 — a real `ChatThreadStore` on `tmp_path` + a real-but-fake `_FakeRegistry` of `_FakeAgent` duck-stubs with controllable `is_alive`/`meta.last_active` + a real `CommunicationsConfig`, direct-`await` of `crew_presence` over a `SimpleNamespace` runtime, no MagicMock at the store/config boundary): `in_meeting`; `working` (just inside 90s); `online` (just outside 90s); `offline` (not alive); non-crew excluded; precedence (`in_meeting` beats `working`); `registry None`; `store None` degrade; count integrity. **+12 Vitest** across three new files — `PresenceDot.test.tsx` (6), `CrewRosterPanel.presence.test.tsx` (3), `AgentAvatarBadge.presence.test.tsx` (3). Backend focused gate 20 (9 AD-930 + 11 AD-924); full Vitest **1237 passed | 1 skipped** (210 files; baseline 1225 + 12, zero regressions); `npm run build` clean. **COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed** (held for Captain review/push alongside AD-926a). ### AD-928: Show-your-work status protocol — one `[STATUS]…[/STATUS]` tag family with an optional `final` flag posts a `metadata.kind="status"` message into the agent's task room (reusing the AD-927 participation resolver unchanged), giving a task room the Microsoft-Teams "activity feed" feel; message-only v1 (the AD-928 row of the Task Workspace Rooms epic AD-925 → AD-929, filled after Captain deferral)

**The activity feed of the workspace room.** AD-925 auto-creates the task room, AD-926/927 give it Input + Output folders, AD-929 assembles them into a Teams-channel surface. AD-928 adds the **narration**: as the crew work a task they post meaningful progress into the room and a clear final result, so a human watching sees the work happen and a crisp completion — the Teams activity-feed feel. The mechanism mirrors AD-924/AD-927 exactly: a rank-gated, anti-flooded proactive action tag that posts into the agent's bound task room, plus a `federation.md` standing order that teaches the norm. It is assembly over existing primitives (`ChatThreadStore.append_message`, the AD-927 resolver), not new substrate.

**Decision 1 — ONE `[STATUS]` tag with an optional `final` flag, NOT two tags.** A single paired tag carries both progress narration and the final result: `[STATUS]body[/STATUS]` → `metadata={"kind":"status"}`; `[STATUS final]body[/STATUS]` → `metadata={"kind":"status","status_final":true}`. A new module-level `_STATUS_PATTERN` (`r'\[STATUS(\s+final)?\s*\](.*?)\[/STATUS\]'`, `DOTALL|IGNORECASE`; `bool(m.group(1))` is the final flag, g2 is the body) mirrors `_ARTIFACT_PATTERN`. **Why one tag, not `[STATUS]` + `[RESULT]`:** DRY — a second tag doubles the regex / extractor / rank-gate / cap surface for a semantic that is just a boolean on the same message kind. The activity-feed feel = a stream of `kind="status"` messages plus one distinctly-marked completion (`status_final`); a flag on the same kind gives a UI consumer (AD-928b) exactly what it needs without a second code path. Mirrors AD-923's deterministic `metadata.meeting_end` marker.

**Decision 2 — binding: REUSE `_resolve_agent_task_room(agent.id)` identically.** The proactive turn carries no inherent thread. Bind the status post to the agent's task room with the **existing AD-927 participation resolver, unchanged**: the most-recently-active non-archived thread that has a `task_id` and lists the agent as a participant. No room → honest-degrade (suppress, strip the tag, no post, no crash). This builds on AD-925 (the agent IS a participant of its auto-created room). The resolver takes the agent **id string** (`_resolve_agent_task_room(agent.id)`), mirroring the artifact extractor call exactly.

**Decision 3 — post via `ChatThreadStore.append_message` (message-only).** Post the status as a normal thread message authored by the agent (`role="agent"`). `append_message` is SYNC, returns `ChatThreadMessage | None` (`None` if the thread is missing — built-in honest-degrade), and its `to_dict()` carries `metadata`, so the existing `GET /api/threads/{id}/messages` already surfaces the marker for any future UI consumer (AD-928b). No new store method, no new endpoint.

**Decision 4 — rank gate Lieutenant+, caps `status_max_per_turn=3` + `status_max_bytes=4096`.** Three NEW `CommunicationsConfig` fields after `artifact_max_bytes`: `status_min_rank="lieutenant"` (status narration and artifact output are the two task-room work-output channels — same tier reads cleanly; the whole proactive-action surface is already Lieutenant+, so Lieutenant is the floor of "can take proactive actions at all", and dropping to Ensign would make status the *only* action an Ensign can take), `status_max_per_turn=3` (status is frequent by design — narrate *milestones* — so 3 allows "started / progress / done"; the 4th+ suppressed `rate_limited`), `status_max_bytes=4096` (4 KiB — status lines are short prose, smaller than the artifact 256 KiB; oversize → suppressed `too_large`). The gate is wired INLINE in `_extract_and_execute_actions` immediately after the AD-927 artifact gate, reusing the in-scope `_RANK_ORDER_DM`. The bare opening tag of a rank-gated-out status is later removed by the pre-existing BF-203 hallucinated-tag cleanup — correct, the status path simply never ran (so the gated-out test asserts no-post + no-action, NOT tag survival).

**Decision 5 — UI status-chip render is DEFERRED to forward marker AD-928b.** Rendering `metadata.kind="status"` distinctly in the transcript is not cheap at HEAD: `ChatMessage` has no `metadata`/`kind` field; the thread-message load path renames `body → text` and does not carry `metadata` into the conversation; the render is a heavy inline `messages.map` loop in `ProfileChatTab`; and there is an open live-refresh question (does the room transcript poll for agent-posted messages between Captain turns?). Because the backend persists the marker and the existing `GET messages` endpoint already surfaces it, **AD-928b is a pure presentational follow-up with no backend dependency** (mirrors the epic's backend-first discipline: AD-927 shipped off the existing `ArtifactDrawer`, AD-926 shipped the `InputsList` unmounted).

**Decision 6 — message-only v1; lifecycle transition is forward marker AD-928a.** The roadmap row aspires to tie the final result to the work-item lifecycle (`in_progress → done`). **v1 is MESSAGE-ONLY: no work item is transitioned.** Verified: `grep work_item|current_task|task_id|transition_work_item` over `proactive.py` returns ONLY the two `task_id` references inside the AD-927 resolver — there is no clean current-work-item handle in the proactive context (the same gap AD-925/AD-927 documented). A lifecycle transition is a validated state-machine write (`transition_work_item`, AD-498/BF-72/AD-861) that needs the work-item id, which is not available here; it stays with `CrewTaskExecutor` / a richer binding → **AD-928a** (shares the AD-927a gap).

**Non-goals / forward markers.** No work-item lifecycle transition (**AD-928a**). No UI — no status-chip render, no `ChatMessage` type change, no `ProfileChatTab` edit, no store-slice / live-refresh change (**AD-928b**). No presence layer online/working/in-meeting (**AD-930**). No second tag (`[RESULT]`) — one `[STATUS]` family with a `final` flag. No change to `_resolve_agent_task_room`, `ChatThreadStore.append_message`, the `[ARTIFACT]`/`[GROUP_CHAT]` extractors, `AgentGroupChatService`, the intent bus, `CrewTaskExecutor`, `CrewOrchestrator`, any consensus/trust path, `BaseAgent`, or `IntentMessage`. No new REST route, no new `EventType`, no new store method, no new config class (extend `CommunicationsConfig` only). No binary/attachment status — short text only. **Dormancy:** unlike AD-925's auto-create wiring, `[STATUS]` is NOT gated by `agentic_dispatch.orchestrator_enabled` and does NOT depend on `CrewTaskExecutor` — it fires whenever any Lieutenant+ agent that participates in a task room emits the tag (participation-based binding), so the capability is live the moment a task room with participants exists. **Tests:** `tests/test_ad928_show_your_work.py` (+13, BF-287 — a real `ChatThreadStore` on `tmp_path` behind a `MagicMock(spec=ProbOSRuntime)` shell, `_FakeAgent`/`_Clock` duck stubs, rank driven by injected trust). Focused gate 35 (13 AD-928 + 11 AD-927 + 11 AD-924); blast-radius `-k "proactive or status or thread or chat or group or artifact or standing or manual"` green. **COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed** (the whole epic AD-925 → AD-929 is held for Captain review; HEAD now 6 ahead of origin/main = AD-924).

### AD-929: Unified workspace view — a collapsible right-hand "Files" rail inside `ProfileChatTab` (Inputs + Outputs), gated to workspace rooms, so a task room reads like a Microsoft Teams channel (Conversation + Files); the surface that completes the Task Workspace Rooms epic (AD-925 → AD-929)

**The assembly AD: bind Conversation + Files into one surface.** AD-925/926/927 delivered the substrate (auto task room) and both file folders (Inputs, Outputs), but the pieces were never assembled — `InputsList` was mounted nowhere, and the artifact Outputs (`ArtifactDrawer`, AD-797) lived only in the `CompactApp` tray, absent from the full HXI where task/group rooms actually open (AD-919 routes a room to `AgentProfilePanel` → `ProfileChatTab`). The Captain's refined goal: "an experience like HR collaborating in Microsoft Teams." Teams maps a project channel to Conversation (the transcript) + Files (shared inputs + produced outputs) + Meet (already built, AD-920 `MeetingView`). AD-929 is frontend-only — every endpoint already exists (`/api/threads/{id}/inputs` AD-926, `/api/artifacts/thread/{id}` + `/content` AD-797) — so **no backend, no pytest, no new REST route, no new EventType, no new store slice**.

**Decision A — layout = a collapsible right-hand "Files" rail inside `ProfileChatTab` (chosen over a tab bar).** `ProfileChatTab` is the **only mount common to both hosts** — `CompactApp` (Yeo tray) *and* `AgentProfilePanel` (full HXI) — so putting the Files surface inside it means the rail travels with the conversation into both hosts with one component and no host-specific layout surgery. The rail keeps the **conversation as the primary column** (Teams defaults a channel to its Conversation) and adds a right rail with two stacked sections — INPUTS (top) over OUTPUTS (bottom) — reusing the HXI right-rail idiom already established by `ArtifactDrawer`. **A tab bar atop the room was rejected:** it hides the conversation when viewing Files (a live collaboration room wants Files co-visible with the transcript), and `AgentProfilePanel` already has a **per-agent** tab bar (Chat | Work | Memory | Profile | Health | Self-image) — a per-thread "Files" tab there is a category error (those tabs describe the *agent*, not the *room*) and it does nothing for `CompactApp`, which has no tab bar.

**Decision B — gate = workspace room only (no rail on a 1:1 DM).** A new **pure** `isWorkspaceRoom(thread, agents)` (`ui/src/components/workspace/isWorkspaceRoom.ts`) returns `true` when `thread.task_id` is set (an AD-925 auto task room — authoritative) **OR** it has **≥2 crew participants** (a group room; AD-917 turns a 1:1 into a group at the 2nd crew participant). The crew-count idiom is the **verbatim `GroupChatHeader:36-40` filter** (exclude the `"captain"` sentinel, resolve each id to its agent via `agents.get`, keep only `isCrew`). Both `task_id` and `participants` are on the client store view `AD791aChatThreadView`, so the gate is a pure function over store data (no fetch). A 1:1 DM (one crew participant, no `task_id`) shows **no rail**.

**Decision C — Outputs = the lighter `ArtifactList`, NOT the full `ArtifactDrawer` (the drawer is never double-mounted).** The new `WorkspaceFilesRail.tsx` composes the **presentational** AD-797 `ArtifactList` fed by a self-contained `fetchThreadArtifacts(threadId)` call, so the full `ArtifactDrawer` stays exactly where it is in `CompactApp` (untouched) and the rail uses a *different, lighter* component. The rail owns its own fetch + local state (exactly like AD-926's `InputsList` + `inputsApi` pattern), with **no coupling** to the global `selectedArtifactId` / `artifactsByThread` slice the standalone drawer owns. Outputs rows are read-only "open" actions — selecting an artifact opens `/api/artifacts/{id}/content` in a new tab (parity with `InputsList`'s open-the-bytes model); rich inline `ArtifactViewer` preview stays the standalone drawer's job (forward marker **AD-929a**). INPUTS composes the AD-926 `InputsList` fed by `fetchThreadInputs(threadId)`. Both fetches are Tier-2 honest-degrade to `[]`.

**Decision D — collapse persisted, default-collapsed on first run.** Collapse state persists under `localStorage probos.workspaceFiles.collapsed` (the `ArtifactDrawer` `'1'`/`'0'`/`null` load/persist idiom with a new key), but **defaults to collapsed on first run** (a thin 28px "FILES" rail with a count badge) — a deliberate divergence from `ArtifactDrawer`'s default-expanded, justified by the primary host (`AgentProfilePanel`) being a 420px floating panel where an expanded 300px rail would crowd the chat; the Captain expands on demand (the panel is resizable). HXI #3: **local inline stroke-SVG glyphs** (`strokeWidth 1.5`, amber `#f0b060` / dim `#666680`, no emoji); `Glyphs.tsx`/`Glyphs.test.tsx` are untouched (the AD-917/919 export-count gotcha). `ProfileChatTab` mounts the rail behind the gate via three small edits (import + 3 selectors + wrap the outer return's column in a row with the rail as a `showWorkspaceFiles && activeThreadId` sibling); the chat column is byte-identical for 1:1 DMs.

**Non-goals / forward markers.** No backend / no pytest (all endpoints exist). No `ArtifactDrawer` change, no `CompactApp` edit (the benign cosmetic double-Outputs in the tray — rail + standalone drawer for a workspace room — is resolved by gating the standalone `<ArtifactDrawer />` to non-workspace threads = forward marker **AD-929b**, not this AD). No inline `ArtifactViewer` in the rail (**AD-929a**). No per-room "Files" tab in the full-HXI panel (**AD-929c**, Teams-truer for the full HXI only). No show-your-work status protocol (**AD-928**, deferred for Captain review). No presence layer (**AD-930**). No task-level upload (**AD-926a**).
