### AD-744 — Interactive share-to-agent (Wave 178)

**Context.** AD-733-2 ships ambient screen sensing; the most common
operator request is the one-shot "look at THIS" — Captain wants to share
a single frame with a named agent without standing up an ambient stream.
Existing infrastructure (AD-720 AttachmentStore, AD-742c `bound_agent_ids`,
AD-733a BF-302 `force=True` bypass) covers the plumbing; AD-744 composes
them into a single Captain-facing surface.

**Decision.** Reuse the existing `/api/perception/camera/frame` endpoint
(no new server endpoint). The combination `(force=true AND non-empty
agent_ids)` is the explicit-share signal. New
`PerceptionConfig.explicit_share_enabled` (default True — the underlying
`getDisplayMedia` browser prompt provides the per-click consent so
default-on is safe; the toggle is for kiosk operators) gates the
explicit-share path independently of ambient streams. The shared frame
flows through AttachmentStore (AD-731 invariant) and rides on the next
DM turn's `attachment_ids` via existing AD-720/730 plumbing — no new
multimodal wire format.

Browser side: new `useScreenShare` hook (one-shot; `track.stop()` on
EVERY track in `finally` — distinct from AD-733-2's long-lived stream);
stroke-SVG monitor + up-arrow glyph next to the existing paperclip on
the WardRoomThreadDetail DM composer (HXI #3); Tier-2 honest-degrade
returns `null` from the hook on any failure (user cancel, network blip,
server 5xx) — the DM composer text is never clobbered.

admits, operator-preview-still-admits, force-flag propagation, distinct
anchor trigger_type, AD-731 source-scan rerun, camera-source share
parity); +6 vitest (getDisplayMedia called once, track stopped after
grab, multipart contents, success payload, getDisplayMedia reject

(button hidden in non-DM view, visible in DM view, click appends to

### AD-745 — Conversation → action handoff; browser scope v1 (Wave 178)

**Context.** After AD-744 ships, the Captain can share a screen frame
with an agent. The natural next sentence is "click that button for me."
Today the agent honest-degrades — it can describe what it sees, but has
no path to act. AD-706 already ships the BrowserTool substrate (Playwright
sessions per Captain, AD-706e action vocabulary, AD-706e classifier,
AD-541b anchor episodes per action); AD-745 ships the dispatch layer
that connects a CognitiveAgent's DM reply to BrowserTool.

**Decision (GATE 1 — Captain ruling).** Per-action Captain ACK is the
canonical consent posture. Tier-1 (observation-only: screenshot, state,
scroll, mouse_move) dispatches inline; tier-2 (click, type, drag,
non-destructive key_combo, mouse_button) waits for in-thread Captain
ACK; tier-3 (compute_use_click, eval_js, upload_file, download,
destructive key_combo, ANY verb on URL matching `destructive_url_patterns`)
waits for explicit destructive-confirmation modal. NO autopilot in v1.

Surface: `[ACTION: {"verb":"click","args":{"selector":"#submit"},"intent":"..."}]`
bracket marker on agent DM replies; new `DmReplyPipeline.step_4e_action_dispatch`
between AD-743 4d and BF-296 4b; new `ActionDispatcher` in-memory registry;
new `routers/agent_actions.py` mounted at `/api/browser`:

- `POST /actions/{id}/ack` — tier-2 Captain ACK; calls BrowserTool.invoke
- `POST /actions/{id}/abort` — Captain abort; sets `BrowserSession.aborted=True`
- `GET  /actions/by-thread/{thread_id}` — per-thread action list

Browser side: `ui/src/components/chat/AgentActionLog.tsx` — collapsed by
default per HXI #5; per-entry tier glyph (stroke-density encoded,
a11y-safe — no color reliance); pulse animation on `ack_pending` (1.2s)
and `confirm_pending` (0.6s) per HXI #4; per-action ABORT button.

**AD-731 invariant.** Frame refs (SHA-256 from AttachmentStore) only on
outcomes; before/after_frame_ref slots reserved for the
screenshot-before / screenshot-after audit trail. Source-scan asserts
`b64encode` absent from `action_parser.py`, `action_dispatcher.py`,
`routers/agent_actions.py`.

**AD-541b integration.** Every dispatched action writes an Episode with
`anchors=AnchorFrame(channel="action", trigger_type="agent_action_executed",
trigger_agent=<agent_id>)`. Outcomes carry `verb`, `args_hash` (sha256),
`tier_classified`, `before_frame_ref`, `after_frame_ref`, `result`.

**Scope.** Default-OFF (`action_dispatch_enabled=False`). Per-DM-turn
cap = 1 (AD-745-6 forward marker for multi-step plans). Consecutive-
autonomous cap = 5 (AD-706c-2 Guard #10 generalized across all verbs).
Destructive URL allow-list = 10 fnmatch patterns by default. NO browser
binaries committed — `playwright install chromium` is operator-run.
BrowserSession ALWAYS uses an isolated `user_data_dir`, NEVER Captain's
default profile (AD-745-5 forward marker tracks the consensual
profile-clone exception).

**Test coverage.** +23 pytest (7 parser + 8 pipeline + 3 episode-anchor
+ 5 endpoints); +6 vitest (AgentActionLog component).

**Forward markers** (filed in roadmap, no GH issues per AD-722c-3):

- AD-745-1 — `DesktopActionTool` OS-pointer scope. Absorbs AD-721j
  Blender Connector per Wave 178 Captain ruling. Trigger: Captain shares

- AD-745-2 — **Autopilot mode** (opt-in quorum substitution for Captain
  ACK). Modeled on GitHub Copilot CLI autopilot
  (https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/autopilot).

Bytes never committed (gitignored under `data/*`). New `ui/src/audio/whisperLoader.ts` lazy-injects the UMD glue via `<script>` tag (NOT ESM `await import()` — whisper.cpp ships UMD per upstream `examples/whisper.wasm/main.js`). New `CognitiveConfig.whisper_model_path` field (default `whisper/ggml-tiny.en.bin`; restart-required per BF-308). FieldDescriptor registered in the AD-741 LLM Tiers section. NO STT functionality exposed — AD-705a is the consumer. 0-line diff on `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md` (entries land at AD-705a ship). +6 pytest, +5 vitest (3 required + 2 helper-seam checks). Closes #561.

## AD-790 (drafted, 2026-05-21) — Yeo Desktop first-run setup experience (Claude-Desktop-grade onboarding)

**Status:** drafted. **Parent:** AD-759 (Electron host, SHIPPED Wave 186). **Sibling forward markers:** AD-759a..e (autostart / installer / auto-update / signed installer / CI). **Issue:** #714.

**Problem.** AD-759 shipped the Yeo Electron tray host that wraps the browser HXI. There is no first-run setup experience — opening the packaged app drops the operator into the raw HXI with no orientation, no runtime-connection check UX, no branded welcome, no "you are signed in as X, Yeo will help you with Y" framing. Captain reference benchmark is the Claude for Windows installer→splash→`Get started`→home flow: branded installer with progress, dark welcome splash with product mark + one-line value prop + single primary CTA, then a minimal account/connect step, then the chat home. ProbOS needs equivalent polish for Yeo to feel like a daily-driver app and not a dev tool.

**Decision.** Add a first-run onboarding surface inside the existing `desktop/` Electron workspace (NEW renderer route `#/onboarding`) that runs before the HXI loads on first launch, persists a `firstRunComplete` flag in Electron `app.getPath('userData')/yeo-state.json`, and is re-triggerable via tray-menu `Reset Setup…`. The surface is a 4-step linear flow rendered by the same Vite/React/TypeScript stack the rest of the desktop renderer uses (no new framework):

1. **Welcome** — full-window dark canvas, ProbOS/Yeo wordmark, one-line value prop ("Your crew, ready when you are"), single `Get started` primary button. Matches Claude Desktop welcome shape; ProbOS visual language (amber accent, stroke-SVG mark — HXI Design Principle #3 no emoji).
2. **Runtime connect** — auto-probes `PROBOS_RUNTIME_URL` (default `http://127.0.0.1:8765`); on success shows green "Connected to your local crew"; on failure shows three remediation options (Start runtime / Change URL / Run later). Honest-degrade per AD-732 pattern. No silent retry loops.
3. **Captain Card** — minimal prompt for display name + optional voice/avatar pick (deferred to AD-757 surface if not present yet). Writes to existing Captain-Card store; does NOT introduce a new identity primitive.
4. **Ready** — three suggested first prompts ("Brief me on today", "Read my unread mail", "What's on my calendar") rendered as click-to-send tiles. Tapping any tile completes onboarding, sets `firstRunComplete=true`, and routes to the main HXI with the tile's text pre-populated into the intent surface.

**What this AD is NOT.** Not a re-skin of the HXI. Not a new design system. Not a separate splash window (the splash is a renderer route inside the existing `BrowserWindow`, so single-instance lock + deep-link + Electron lifecycle from AD-759 still hold). Not installer-level branding (that lives at AD-759b/d). Not auto-update onboarding (AD-759c). Not telemetry-consent UX (separate AD, file as forward marker AD-790a if needed). Does NOT call out to the network beyond the local runtime probe.

**Prior-art absorption (pattern only, no code copy).**
- Claude for Windows (product pattern) — installer→splash→`Get started`→home flow; one-line value prop; primary-only CTA; minimal account step. License: proprietary. Absorb the SHAPE only.
- VS Code Welcome page (MIT) — multi-step walkthrough renderer pattern, "complete step" persistence, re-runnable via command palette. Architecture reference only.
- Linear desktop (proprietary) — runtime-connection retry UX with three explicit remediations. Pattern only.

**License posture.** Renderer-only React + existing dependencies. No new npm deps. No new Python deps. No model-weight or font additions. Apache-2.0 / MIT compatible across the board.

**Test plan.** +6 vitest in `desktop/src/renderer/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.test.tsx` (welcome→connect happy, connect failure→remediation, connect failure→change-URL flow, Captain-Card name validation, suggested-prompt tile click pre-populates intent, `firstRunComplete` persists and skips on next launch). +2 vitest in `desktop/src/main/firstRunGate.test.ts` (reads/writes `yeo-state.json`, tray-menu `Reset Setup…` clears flag). No pytest changes (Python runtime unchanged).

**Forward markers.**
- **AD-790a** — Telemetry-consent step inside onboarding (opt-in only; trigger: when any telemetry capability ships).
- **AD-790b** — Installer-side branded progress UI (trigger: AD-759b NSIS installer ships).
- **AD-790c** — Cloud-runtime mode toggle in step 2 (trigger: commercial overlay ships hosted runtime).
- **AD-790d** — Localized onboarding strings (trigger: i18n framework lands).

**Acceptance.** First launch of packaged Yeo presents the 4-step flow. Second launch goes straight to HXI. Tray menu has `Reset Setup…` that clears the flag. All 8 vitest tests green. Manual smoke: package the app, install, run on a clean Windows profile, complete the flow, restart, confirm no re-prompt; trigger Reset, confirm re-prompt. Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

## AD-825 (Wave 192, 2026-05-22) — Drain-before-cancel shutdown semantics

Closes #760. Inserts a drain phase BEFORE the AD-824 cancel sweep in `startup/shutdown.py` so write-holding background loops (episodic backup, anything that opens a Chroma/SQLite/tar transaction) can finish the current atomic operation cleanly instead of being cancelled mid-write (which is the same pathology AD-819 / AD-822 have to repair on the next boot). New `ProbOSRuntime._drain_tasks: set[asyncio.Task]` registry + `_shutdown_event: asyncio.Event` + `_signal_drain_stop()` helper; `_spawn_background(...)` grows kw-only `drain_on_shutdown: bool = False` parameter that routes the task to `_drain_tasks` instead of the AD-824 `_background_tasks` set. New `MemoryConfig.shutdown_drain_timeout_s` (default 30s, range 1.0..300.0). Drain phase signals the event, awaits `asyncio.wait(_drain_tasks, timeout=shutdown_drain_timeout_s)`, logs WARNING for any task that doesn't drain in time. The AD-824 cancel sweep that runs immediately after now also reaps any drain task that didn't exit cleanly — drain is best-effort, cancel is the fallback. `_episodic_backup_task` migrated to `drain_on_shutdown=True`; its loop body replaces bare `asyncio.sleep(N)` with `asyncio.wait_for(self._shutdown_event.wait(), timeout=N)` + early-exit checks before/after each tar so an in-flight snapshot finishes cleanly. New `DreamScheduler.stop_gracefully(timeout)` (uses `asyncio.shield` so the timeout doesn't cancel the in-flight cycle) called from shutdown Phase 1 BEFORE the explicit `dream_cycle()` so the monitor loop's own cycle cannot collide with the explicit one (concurrent-writer hazard on the same Chroma collection was the suspected cause of today's `consolidation_result=failed` events). `ReconsolidationScheduler` and `FailureDistiller` are passive (no `start()`/`stop()`, no task ownership) and are covered transitively when the in-flight cycle finishes. +7 pytest in `tests/test_ad825_drain_shutdown.py` (drain routing, default routing regression, clean-exit semantics, drain-timeout-falls-through-to-cancel, in-flight-atomic-write-completes, drain-exception-does-not-block-marker, AD-824 sweep regression). Zero new deps.

## AD-826 (2026-05-22) — Whisper-first STT priority

Closes #767. The browser Web Speech API is reliable in Chrome but flaky in Edge / Firefox / Safari (silent session death, empty results, no errors). The AD-705a whisper.cpp WASM path works in every browser that ships WebAssembly + SharedArrayBuffer. Inverting the default — whisper primary, browser SR fallback after 2 empty whisper transcripts — eliminates the cross-browser reliability gap without changing the underlying privacy invariant (audio still stays in the browser). Operators on a single-browser deployment can revert with `cognitive.primary_stt: browser`. New `cognitive.primary_stt: Literal["whisper", "browser"]` (default `whisper`) + `cognitive.fallback_stt_enabled: bool` (default True) in `src/probos/config.py`; both registered in the `llm_tiers` SectionDescriptor for hot-reload. New `GET /api/voice/health` in `src/probos/routers/voice.py` returns `{primary_stt, engine, backend_available, healthy}` — filesystem-only probe via `resolve_whisper_model_path(...)` checking `cognitive.offline_stt_enabled` + on-disk GGML file presence; NO subprocess is created because whisper inference runs in the browser, not the runtime. `ProfileChatTab.tsx` PTT click handler now branches on `voiceHealth.primary_stt`: whisper-primary + healthy arms `whisperStt` first; new `emptyWhisperCountRef` falls through to browser SR after 2 empty whisper transcripts (mirror of AD-760). Whisper-primary + unhealthy honest-degrades to browser SR for the press without consuming any counter (operator asked for whisper but artifacts are missing). Browser-primary preserves the AD-760 path verbatim. Mic button `title` exposes the active engine (`Voice input (whisper)` / `Voice input (browser)`) — text only, no emoji per HXI #3. +8 pytest in `tests/test_ad826_voice_config.py`; +5 vitest in `ui/src/__tests__/ProfileChatTab.ad826.test.tsx`. UI `npm run build` green per BF-279 gate.


## AD-822b (2026-05-23) — Boot-time HNSW file validation (pre-open structural probe)

Closes #755. Adds a read-only structural validation layer that runs in the AD-822 subprocess probe BEFORE `chromadb.PersistentClient(...)` opens the collection. Where AD-822 catches torn-HNSW segfaults by isolating them in a child process, AD-822b prevents the segfault by detecting truncation / header-vs-file inconsistency through cheap file I/O on `header.bin`. Together with AD-820 (unclean-shutdown gating) this forms a three-layer defense: AD-820 detects the bad shutdown last run, AD-822 catches latent corruption that survives gating, AD-822b stops the cases that would otherwise produce SIGSEGV before chroma's native mmap path touches them. New `validate_hnsw_files(data_dir)` in `src/probos/episodic_health.py` walks every UUID-named subdir that contains a `header.bin`, parses the 100-byte chroma-hnswlib header via `struct.unpack("<IQQQQQQiIQQQdQ", ...)` (4-byte u32 version prefix + 13 upstream hnswlib fields in `saveIndex` order — layout verified 2026-05-23 against the preserved corrupted dir at `C:\Users\seang\AppData\Local\ProbOS\data\chroma-corrupted-2026-05-22-150712\`; size_data_per_element=1676 / mult=1/ln(16) / M=16 / maxM0=32 / ef_construction=100 all decoded cleanly), and checks: `cur_element_count <= max_elements`, `size_data_per_element` in `[64, 65536]`, `data_level0.bin` size equals `size_data_per_element * max_elements`, `length.bin` entry count equals `max_elements`, `link_lists.bin` exists (sparse format; size not gated). Each problem accumulates one error string prefixed with the relative path; first-boot data dirs (data_dir missing or no header.bin subdirs) return ok=True since absence is healthy. Wired into `src/probos/_episodic_probe.py` between the `chroma.sqlite3` marker check and `chromadb.PersistentClient` open; on failure the probe writes `hnsw-validation: <error>` lines to stderr and exits 5 (new code reserved alongside AD-822's 0/1/2). `EpisodicHealthResult` gains `file_validation_failed: bool` (default False) and `check_episodic_health` branches on `exit_code == 5` to set it. `EpisodicCorruptionDetected` gains kw-only `file_validation_failed` parameter whose True branch shapes a distinct operator message leading with "HNSW index appears truncated or corrupted (structural validation failed)" and naming `probos rebuild-episodic` / backup restore / skip-envvar options. `_serve` in `__main__.py` threads `_health.file_validation_failed` into the exception. Read-only: never opens `data_level0.bin` (could be hundreds of MB), only the 100-byte `header.bin`; wall time <2ms per dir on warm cache (measured), <50ms gate enforced by the healthy-dir test via `time.perf_counter()`. No new dependencies; no `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` (uses the existing AD-822 Popen path). +7 pytest in `tests/test_ad822b_hnsw_validation.py` (healthy dir + perf gate, truncated data_level0, missing-header skip, cur>max sanity, missing-data-dir first-boot, end-to-end subprocess exit-5, propagation through `check_episodic_health`). AD-820..826 regression suite (69 tests) remains green.

## AD-812 (2026-05-23) — Natural-language scheduled actions

## BF-301 (2026-05-23) — Migrate browser STT from whisper.cpp WASM to transformers.js

Closes #775. The AD-826 architecture (local-first STT, browser-side inference, browser SR as fallback) ships intact; only the local engine swaps. whisper.cpp's WASM example bundle has been abandoned upstream (https://huggingface.co/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/resolve/v1.5.4/... returns "Invalid rev id", the whisper.ggerganov.com GitHub Pages CDN 404s, 
pm i whisper.cpp ships only JS glue with no stable WASM mirror). The industry has converged on `@huggingface/transformers` v3 (Apache 2.0, ~3M weekly npm downloads) which ships the `Xenova/whisper-tiny.en` ONNX model directly from the HF CDN with browser Cache API persistence — zero operator setup, identical behavior across Chrome / Edge / Firefox / Safari / Chromium-Electron. New `ui/src/audio/transformersStt.ts` mirrors the AD-705a `whisperStt.ts` public surface (`armTransformersStt` / `disarm` / `onTransformersTranscript` / `onTransformersTranscribing`) and adds a new `onTransformersProgress(handler)` channel so the UI can render a first-load model download bar (`data-testid="bf301-progress"`, amber `#f0b060` per HXI #3). New `ui/src/audio/transformersWorker.ts` owns the `pipeline('automatic-speech-recognition', 'Xenova/whisper-tiny.en')` lifecycle in a dedicated Web Worker (`new Worker(new URL('./transformersWorker.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })`; postMessage init/transcribe/shutdown protocol with transferred Float32 ArrayBuffer to avoid a copy on every utterance). All three production call sites migrated via import-name swap so the BF-290/292/293/294/294b/300 mic UX gating logic remains untouched: `ProfileChatTab.tsx`, `IntentSurface.tsx`, `conversationController.ts`. Backend `cognitive.primary_stt` Literal extended to `"transformers" | "whisper" | "browser"` (default flipped from `whisper` to `transformers`); `whisper` retained as a deprecated alias that resolves to `engine: "transformers"` in `/api/voice/health` so saved operator configs do not break. New `cognitive.transformers_model` field (default `Xenova/whisper-tiny.en`; operators can pin `Xenova/whisper-base.en`). `/api/voice/health` adds a `model` field and no longer probes the GGML filesystem path (browser owns the fetch via HF CDN + Cache API); `backend_available` semantics become `resolved_engine == 'transformers' AND offline_stt_enabled`, `healthy` becomes `backend_available OR resolved_engine == 'browser'`. `ProfileChatTab.tsx` PTT branching updated to accept both `primary_stt='transformers'` (new default) AND `primary_stt='whisper'` (deprecated alias) as the local-first engine. `whisper_model_path`, `whisperStt.ts`, `whisperLoader.ts`, `scripts/whisper-tiny-en-fetch.ps1`: retained with deprecation banners for one release cycle; follow-up hygiene PR will delete them. `onnxruntime-web` removed from `optionalDependencies` (v3 bundles it internally). New Vite `stt-vendor` `manualChunks` branch keeps the ~1MB transformers.js + onnxruntime runtime out of the main bundle (lazy on PTT arm). Privacy invariant preserved: audio bytes never leave the browser; the only HF-CDN traffic is ONNX weight shards in / transcript text out. Honest-degrade: worker emits `{status: 'error'}` progress event on model-fetch failure; existing AD-826 empty-counter fallback to browser SR continues to work. Bundle delta: main `index` chunk unchanged at 48.8 kB (gzip 15.4 kB); new `stt-vendor` chunk at 13.43 kB (gzip 5.34 kB) for the main-thread shim + lazy `transformersWorker` chunk at 877 kB + `ort-wasm-simd-threaded` at 21.6 MB (gzip 5.1 MB) loaded only when STT arms. +9 backend pytest (`tests/test_bf301_voice_health.py`) + 3 AD-826 backend tests migrated (default flipped, `whisper`-alias path, `model` field). +9 worker-boundary vitest (`ui/src/__tests__/transformersStt.bf301.test.tsx`) + 9 integration vitest (`ui/src/__tests__/ProfileChatTab.bf301.test.tsx`) + 5 AD-826 frontend tests migrated + 7 BF-290/292/293/294/300 + conversationController + conversationWiring tests re-pointed at the new module-mock target. Vitest 924 → 957 (+33). Backend AD-820..AD-826 + BF-291/295/296/297/298/300 regression suite green (112/116 pass; 4 pre-existing AD-822/AD-823 chromadb HNSW fixture failures on HEAD are unrelated to BF-301). UI `npm run build` green per BF-279 gate.

relative → under `_probos_root()`; NEVER the CWD) in `piper_backend.py`; `_resolve_binary_path` rewritten to anchor via `_anchor_path`; `_resolve_voice_model(voice_model, voices_base)` now takes an already-anchored base instead of hardcoding `Path("tools/piper/voices").resolve()`. **DD-2:** new `TTSConfig.voices_dir` (default `"tools/piper/voices"`) makes the voices dir configurable, threaded `select_backend(config.voices_dir)` → `PiperBackend.__init__(voices_dir=...)` → both `_resolve_voice_model` call sites (configured voice + the BF-291 `voice_override` path); default preserves the historical location byte-for-byte. **DD-3 (BF-628 class):** `startup/finalize.py._wire_relationship_inference` now reads the absolute `runtime.data_dir` (AD-468 public property) instead of the relative `getattr(config, "data_dir", "data")` fallback, so `rejection_cache.sqlite` opens regardless of launch CWD; honest-degrade try/except unchanged. **DD-4:** the two `synthesize` degrade WARNINGs (binary-missing, voice-missing) now log the RESOLVED candidate path (what/why/what-next) instead of only the configured string. **DD-5 (report-only, NOT fixed here):** other CWD-relative `Path("tools/…"|"data/…")` of the same class — `routers/avatars.py:131` (sibling hardcoded `tools/piper/voices`), `agents/code_search.py:254` (`tools/rg`), `config.py` defaults `data/captains_log` `data/plan_of_day` `data/agent_probes.db`, `proactive.py:275` (`data/briefing_state.json`), `routers/security.py:43` (relative `data` + private `_data_dir`), `cognitive/session_manager.py:20` (`data/sessions`) — left for follow-up; an unbounded sweep was explicitly out of scope. ## AD-1026 (2026-06-17) — Quiet, phased boot output with a `--verbose` flag

Closes #970. Presentation-only — the default `probos serve` console boot is short and issue-focused; a new `--verbose`/`-v` restores the historical full detail. **No boot LOGIC changed** (`runtime.start()`, the wirers, `_ensure_ollama`/`_create_llm_client`/`_check_nats`, the banner version, and the per-logger `setLevel(WARNING)` block are all untouched); the entire diff is `src/probos/__main__.py` + `tests/test_ad1026_boot_verbosity.py`. **DD-1 (console level):** new pure `_console_log_level(log_level, verbose) -> int` (`logging.WARNING` when not verbose, else `getattr(logging, log_level.upper(), logging.INFO)`) + a `verbose: bool = False` param on `_setup_logging`; the **console** `StreamHandler` level is set via the helper while the rotating **file** handler stays at INFO+ in both modes (full diagnostics always on disk) and the root logger stays at the configured level (so the file handler still receives INFO+). Net: the default console shows only WARNING/ERROR; `--verbose` restores today's INFO/DEBUG console stream. Intentional default-behavior change (console INFO→WARNING) — the file log preserves everything. **DD-2 (collapse pools):** new pure `_render_boot_summary(status: dict, verbose: bool) -> list[str]` replaces the inline per-pool loop in `_boot_runtime`. Collapsed default = a single `✓ {total_agents} agents across {N} pools` line + the existing red-team line, NO per-pool lines; `verbose=True` = the byte-identical per-pool `✓ Pool {name}: {n} {type} agents` lines + red-team + a labelled Total line. A pool below its target size (`current_size < target_size`) surfaces its own line even collapsed (issue-on-detail), so a degraded boot is never hidden. The banner, `Data dir:`, ollama/LLM/NATS status, and `ProbOS ready.` lines print in both modes. **DD-3 (flag + threading):** `serve_parser` gains `--verbose`/`-v` (`store_true`); `args.verbose` threads → `_serve` → `_boot_runtime(..., verbose=...)` → `_setup_logging(..., verbose=...)` + the `_render_boot_summary` call, and into `_boot_and_run` (the `--interactive` path), with `verbose=False` explicit for the bare-`probos` default-shell dispatch. ## BF-633 (2026-06-21) — Missing `await` in the episode-decay sweep silently killed AD-873 decay

Found in the live boot log (`RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'ActivationTracker.get_activations_batch' was never awaited`). **Root cause.** `EpisodicMemory.sweep_episode_decay` (the AD-873 Ebbinghaus decay sweep, run each dream cycle) called the activation tracker WITHOUT `await`: `activations = activation_tracker.get_activations_batch(list(ids)) or {}`. The real `ActivationTracker.get_activations_batch` is `async def`, so the call returned a coroutine (truthy ⇒ `or {}` never fired); every episode then raised `AttributeError` on `activations.get(ep_id, …)`, was caught by the per-episode try/except, and skipped — so the whole decay/reinforcement sweep silently no-op'd, leaked an un-awaited coroutine per cycle, and emitted the RuntimeWarning. The other three call sites (`activation_tracker.py:235/271`, `routers/memory_graph.py:111`) await it correctly; this one dropped it. **Why tests didn't catch it (BF-287 contract-divergence class).** `test_ad873`'s `_FakeActivationTracker.get_activations_batch` was **sync** (`def`), so the fake's contract DIVERGED from the real async method — no-await returned a dict and the test stayed green while production was broken. **Fix.** (1) `episodic.py`: add `await`. (2) `test_ad873`: make `_FakeActivationTracker` AND `_BrokenTracker` `async def` to match the real signature — the regression guard (a future dropped await now makes the reinforcement tests fail because the un-awaited-coroutine path skips every episode → `reinforced==0`). (3) New `test_sweep_awaits_async_tracker`: asserts `inspect.iscoroutinefunction(ActivationTracker.get_activations_batch)` (locks the contract), uses an async fake that records it was awaited, and asserts reinforcement is applied. **Gates.** `test_ad873_episode_decay.py` + `test_sif.py` 43 passed with `-W error::RuntimeWarning` (no un-awaited-coroutine warning leaks); full suite green. Activates on next reboot. Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

## BF-635 (2026-06-22) — Hand-off detection missed an address opening the final paragraph (Natural Conversation epic #882)

The Captain's live 5+ crew room: Wesley closed his turn addressing a peer at the START of his penultimate sentence ("Anvil, you're in Engineering ... Does the stasis gap hit you the same way ...?"), with the actual question running one sentence PAST the address — and Anvil was never pulled into the cascade. **Root cause.** `crew_profile.extract_handoff_callsign` (BF-619) inspected only (1) the LEADING address of the whole message and (2)/(3) the LAST sentence (opening vocative / trailing comma-vocative). Wesley's "Anvil," opened the PENULTIMATE sentence, so it matched none of the three → `addressed` empty → the AD-951 next-speaker selection never hard-included Anvil. Confirmed live against his exact text (returns `None`). **Fix.** Add case 4: scan a bounded window back from the last sentence (`_HANDOFF_WINDOW=2`, the 2 sentences before the last), MOST-RECENT first, for a sentence-opening vocative `@?(\w+)\s*[,:]`. The leading comma/colon preserves the BF #467 ABOUT-vs-TO discipline (only a sentence ADDRESSED to a peer matches, never one about them); the last-sentence checks (cases 2-3) still run first so the most-recent address wins; the window bound keeps a referential name far up-message from being read as a closing hand-off. **Tests.** NEW `test_bf635_handoff_window.py` (13: the Wesley penultimate-sentence shape; Anvil→Ezri reply shape; last-sentence-trailing beats the window; leading still wins; address-beyond-window→None; referential/mid-sentence mentions in-window→None; BF-619 cases preserved; lowercase; empty). BF-619 + AD-951 regression green (36 together). Gate: full suite **17585 passed**. Activates on next reboot. Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

## BF-636 (2026-06-22) — A transient empty LLM result was persisted as a fake "(no response)" reply (Natural Conversation epic #882)

The Captain's live 5+ crew room during an LLM-proxy restart: several agents showed "(no response)" entries that looked like the crew ignoring a direct question. **Root cause.** `routers/thread_fanout._send_one` converted an EMPTY intent result (proxy timeout / overload / the BF-622 echo-degradation case) into the literal string `"(no response)"` (and a delivery exception into `"(delivery failed)"`). Neither string is `[NO_RESPONSE]` nor empty-after-strip, so both slipped PAST the `_declined` thinning gate and were PERSISTED (`append_message`) + shown as if the agent had posted them — polluting the transcript and feeding future context. A deliberate silence (`[NO_RESPONSE]`) is correctly thinned; only a transient FAILURE leaked. **Fix.** A new nested `_dispatch_intent()` returns `text=""` on empty/None/exception (NOT a visible placeholder), so the existing `_declined` check thins it exactly like a decline — no fake reply is ever persisted. PLUS an explicitly ADDRESSED (hard-included) agent — the peer a prior speaker or the Captain named (AD-951) — gets ONE retry before being thinned, so a transient failure on the named peer auto-recovers; un-addressed agents are thinned immediately (no whole-room retry-amplification when the proxy is already struggling). The BF-622 echo strip moves inside the dispatcher (an only-echo reply degrades to "" → thinned). **Tests.** NEW `test_bf636_empty_result_thinning.py` (6, BF-287 real bus/store/registry: empty→thinned-not-shown; un-addressed empty→single dispatch no retry; delivery exception→thinned; addressed empty-then-real→retry recovers with 2 dispatches; addressed empty-twice→thinned, bounded to one retry). THREE obsolete-contract tests updated to the new thinning contract (`test_ad914_group_chat_fanout.py` ×2 — no-subscriber + raising now thinned not sentinel; `test_ad933a_group_episode.py` ×1 — empty result thinned from replies + episodes). Gate: full suite **17585 passed** (the only failures were the 3 obsolete-contract tests, now updated; 6 unrelated skill_agent/task_scheduler parallel-contention flakes pass in serial). Activates on next reboot. Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

## AD-905 (2026-06-21) — Counselor-gated Clinical view (HXI), frontend-only

Closes #868. The UI half of the clinical-confidential trio (#866/AD-903 read surface + #867/AD-904 notes store, both committed at HEAD 99223db8): a new "Clinical" tab in the Crew Personnel Console that visualizes an agent's longitudinal cognitive health and lets the Counselor/Captain append confidential notes. **Frontend-only** — consumes the committed AD-903/904 endpoints read-only; NO backend/router/config/Python change, NO new npm dependency, NO chart library (hand-rolled inline SVG only). **Two reusable primitives** (NEW `ui/src/components/clinical/`) that MIRROR the BehavioralMetricsPanel inline Sparkline rather than importing/refactoring it: `Sparkline.tsx` (pure-SVG 0-100 viewBox, <2 pts → dashed baseline, ≥2 → strokeWidth-1.5 polyline Y-inverted; adds an optional fixed `[min,max]` window so a bounded series like self-similarity 0..1 reads as high-but-flat instead of auto-scaling, + `role=img`/aria-label/`<title>`) and `ZoneStrip.tsx` (categorical green/amber/red rect band + exported `zoneColor` single-source for the readout pill; empty → one dim baseline rect). **`ClinicalPanel.tsx`** (deps-injectable `fetchImpl`, mirror SkillRequestPanel) owns its OWN agent picker (does NOT reuse the roster master-detail or the store), parallel-fetches `GET /api/counselor/clinical/{id}` + `GET /api/counselor/notes/{id}` on select, and renders **one viz per stream SHAPE, not five identical lines (HXI #4):** trust→Sparkline + Beta-mean readout, zones→ZoneStrip, self-similarity→bounded Sparkline, hebbian-drift→a single directional stroke-glyph scalar (NOT a sparkline), duty→a success-rate bar. **The server `require_crew_scope` gate is the REAL boundary; the `authorized` prop is presentation:** HXI calls OMIT `as_agent_id` (= Captain authority = allowed, byte-identical to the committed AD-903 gate); a server **403 on either endpoint swaps the whole panel to `clinical-unauthorized`**, while the `authorized={false}` client placeholder renders WITHOUT any fetch. Notes are CONFIDENTIAL-headed (stroke lock glyph), newest-first, with an optimistic-prepend write box (`created_at` → `new Date(created_at*1000).toLocaleString()` — the store stamps epoch SECONDS); a failed POST keeps the typed text. **DD (trust.raw defensive):** the trust readout prefers the Beta mean `alpha/(alpha+beta)` when `raw` is a well-formed 2-tuple (the true stored value) and honest-degrades to the latest `new_score` otherwise — readout-only, guarded against non-finite/zero-sum, never throws. Honest-degrade throughout (`!ok`/503 → `clinical-error` banner over an empty shell; partial server payload coerced to defaults via `mergeStreams`). HXI #3: stroke-only SVG glyphs (strokeWidth 1.5, amber `#f0b060` active / dim `#666680`), no emoji; data-testid on every surface; keyboard-activatable picker rows (`role=button`, `tabIndex=0`, Enter/Space) + aria-labels. **4 surgical edits** to `CrewPersonnelConsole.tsx` (import, `ConsoleView` += `'clinical'`, tabs += `['clinical','Clinical']`, a standalone branch before the final `) : (` — zero touch to the roster master-detail or the store). **roadmap.md left untouched — no clean unique anchor for the #868 clinical-view-UI item (only unrelated forward markers AD-729c-1 / AD-740-2).** Pre-reserved sub-number under #868 — highest landed top-level = AD-1052, NO new top-level. **Gates:** focused `vitest run src/components/clinical` 15 passed (3 files); full UI baseline 1735 passed / 1 skipped (270 files, 0 regressions); `npm run build` (tsc -b + vite) clean. ### AD-708e: LAN mDNS advertisement for PADD discovery (#484)

**Problem.** A handheld PADD on the same LAN as the runtime has no stable way to reach the HXI: the server binds `127.0.0.1` by default, and even bound to `0.0.0.0` a phone needs the host's DHCP-assigned IPv4 (which churns). The Captain wants "type `probos.local` and you're in" — a stable, memorable LAN address.

**Decision.** A default-OFF, opt-in mDNS service advertiser behind a `ServiceAdvertiser` Protocol (DIP). `DiscoveryConfig` (default `enabled=False`) is mounted on `SystemConfig` via `Field(default_factory=...)` — NO `config/system.yaml` edit, so a default install is byte-identical. `build_advertiser(cfg, host, port)` returns a `NoOpAdvertiser` (advertises nothing, `start()→False`) when discovery is off, the config is absent, or the optional `zeroconf` lib is missing; otherwise a `ZeroconfAdvertiser` that publishes `_probos._tcp.local.` + a `<hostname>.local` A record + the live server port. Wired in `__main__._serve` (NOT `startup/finalize` — host/port live only in `_serve`, and finalize can't see a `--host` override): build + `start()` after the listening banner, `stop()` guarded in the cleanup `finally`. The `zeroconf` import is LAZY (inside `start()`), so the server boots fine with the lib absent. Host semantics are explicit: a specific non-loopback host advertises as-is; bind-all (`0.0.0.0`/`""`) resolves the LAN IPv4 (no-packet UDP-connect trick; warn+skip if unresolved); loopback (`127.0.0.1`/`localhost`/`::1`) warns + skips (advertising an unreachable loopback A record is worse than nothing — the operator must `probos serve --host 0.0.0.0`). A mDNS failure is Tier-2 honest-degrade (log + stop + return `False`) and NEVER blocks the server; `stop()` is idempotent and never raises.

**License disposition.** `python-zeroconf` is **LGPL-2.1-or-later**. The Apache-2.0 core must stay LGPL-free, so `zeroconf` is an **OPTIONAL extra** — `[project.optional-dependencies] discovery = ["zeroconf>=0.130"]`, installed via `pip install probos[discovery]`. It is a normally-imported, unmodified, pip-installed library — **NEVER vendored or modified**. The core install pulls in nothing LGPL; the advertiser is a `NoOp` when the extra is absent.

**Security.** Default-OFF (opt-in). The advertised `ServiceInfo` carries ONLY non-sensitive fields: the service type, the human-readable instance name, the LAN IPv4, the port, and a static TXT `path` hint. NEVER a token, identity, filesystem path, or username (test-enforced — `test_service_info_excludes_secrets`). CAVEAT: auth is OFF by default (`auth.crew_scope_token=""`), so advertising a default install makes ProbOS LAN-discoverable AND LAN-accessible. Advertising ≠ granting, but the exposure is real — the `DiscoveryConfig` docstring states "set a token and bind `--host 0.0.0.0` deliberately before enabling this." Loopback binds are skipped, so no unreachable record is ever published.

**Browser reality (honest scope).** mDNS delivers a stable `.local` HOSTNAME (OS-resolved: Bonjour/iOS, Win10-1703+ DNS client, systemd-resolved/Avahi) so the user can type `http://probos.local:<port>` — NOT zero-input service discovery. Browsers have no DNS-SD / Network-Service-Discovery API (the WICG spec was abandoned for security), so a web PADD CANNOT browse `_probos._tcp`. Zero-input discovery is native-app-only — the deferred AD-708-1. The win here is a memorable, stable address, not auto-connect.

**Tests + gates.** NEW `tests/test_ad708e_mdns_discovery.py` (10, BF-287 real `_FakeAsyncZeroconf` with ASYNC register/unregister/close recorders — a sync fake would hide a missing `await`): factory flag-off / lib-absent → `NoOp`; flag-on + lib → `Zeroconf`; `NoOp` idempotent; register + unregister + close exactly-once; loopback → skip + warn (caplog); bind-all → resolved LAN IP packed into the `ServiceInfo` address; secrets excluded; a register error → honest-degrade `False` (no propagation); `inspect.getsource(_serve)` contains `build_advertiser(` + `.stop()`. `tests/test_config.py` +3 (DiscoveryConfig default-off on both the leaf and the root model; service_type + hostname validators reject bad values). Gate (PROBOS_DATA_DIR-isolated, the live instance is running): `pytest tests/test_ad708e_mdns_discovery.py tests/test_config.py -q -n 0` → **16 passed**. Import smoke: `SystemConfig().discovery.enabled is False` AND `zeroconf` NOT in `sys.modules` after `import probos.discovery` (LAZY import proven — server boots without the lib). `get_errors` clean; `config/system.yaml` untouched; default install byte-identical. AD-708e is a PADD-discovery sub-number under #484 (top-level stays AD-1052). UNCOMMITTED. Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

### AD-1053 — Actionable accept→dispatch affordance on the notification surface (OSS plumbing)

**Context.** Current highest landed top-level AD = **AD-1052** (verified in `DECISIONS.md` + `PROGRESS.md`; the only `AD-1053+` strings were tentative reservations inside an epic decomposition — none landed). AD-1053 is the next sequential top-level. It is a thin, generally-useful extension of the AD-323 Bridge notification surface: a notification can carry an optional producer-authored `suggested_action`, the HXI renders an **Accept** button for it, and accepting it broadcasts the carried intent into the mesh then acknowledges the notification. Any agent/producer can use it — it is generic OSS infrastructure (it enables a commercial overlay consumer, which is out of scope here). Additive + default `None` → byte-identical when unused.

**Decision (additive — 2 Python, 2 UI, 0 config).** **(1)** `notifications.py` — `AgentNotification.suggested_action: dict[str, Any] | None = None` (next to `action_url`), serialized in `to_dict()`; `NotificationQueue.notify(...)` gains a trailing `suggested_action` param (default `None`, so every existing call site is byte-identical); NEW public `NotificationQueue.get(id) -> AgentNotification | None` accessor (the accept route needs to read one notification — there was only the private `_notifications` + `snapshot()`). The action shape is `{label, intent, params, target_agent_id?}` — all keys optional except a non-empty `intent` is required to dispatch. **(2)** `routers/system.py` — NEW `POST /api/notifications/{id}/accept` (placed after `ack-all`; imports `IntentMessage`). It reads the PRODUCER-authored `suggested_action` off the notification, builds `IntentMessage(intent=action["intent"], params=action["params"], target_agent_id=action.get("target_agent_id"))`, `await runtime.intent_bus.broadcast(...)` (which delegates to `send()` when targeted and passes the AD-698 pre-intent-authorization seam + consensus gating), then `acknowledge`s the notification. Honest-degrade, always HTTP 200 (never a 500): not-found → `{"dispatched": False, "reason": "not_found"}`; no `suggested_action`/no intent → ack-only `{"dispatched": False, "reason": "no_action"}`; no `intent_bus` → `{"dispatched": False, "reason": "no_bus"}`; a dispatch exception → `{"dispatched": False, "reason": "dispatch_error"}` (left UNACKED for retry). Success → ack + `{"dispatched": True, "intent": ..., "responders": len(results)}`. **(3)** `store/types.ts` — `NotificationView.suggested_action?: {label?; intent?; params?; target_agent_id?}`. **(4)** `bridge/BridgeNotifications.tsx` — when `suggested_action?.label` is truthy, `NotificationCard` renders ONE **Accept** button (stroke-SVG check glyph, `strokeWidth 1.5`, amber `#f0b060`, NO emoji — HXI #3/#10) that `stopPropagation()`s (so the card's `ack` onClick does not also fire) and POSTs `/api/notifications/{id}/accept`. No `suggested_action` → the card is byte-identical to pre-AD-1053.

**Security (defense-in-depth).** The client supplies ONLY the notification `id`; the intent + params come from the PRODUCER-authored `suggested_action` already on the notification — the client cannot inject an arbitrary intent. The dispatch still passes the normal AD-698 pre-intent-authorization seam + consensus gating (if the carried intent `requires_consensus`). The route mirrors the existing `ack`/`ack-all` scope surface (`Depends(get_runtime)` only); a deployment exposing the API beyond the Captain can gate it with `require_crew_scope` as a hardening step (deployment note only — no new auth middleware in this AD).

**Default-OFF / byte-identical-when-unused.** A notification created without `suggested_action` serializes with `suggested_action=None` and every pre-AD-1053 key unchanged (test-asserted); the `ack`/`ack-all`/snapshot/event flows are untouched; the card renders no Accept button. `config/system.yaml` UNTOUCHED.

**Tests + gates.** Backend `tests/test_ad1053_actionable_notifications.py` (**8**, BF-287 real fixtures — real `NotificationQueue`, a real `IntentBus(SignalManager())` with a capturing subscriber, the real `IntentMessage`, FastAPI `TestClient` via `dependency_overrides[get_runtime]`): field default-None + `to_dict`; `notify(...)` round-trip via `snapshot()`; `get` hit + miss; accept happy path (the real bus captures `IntentMessage(intent="direct_message", target_agent_id="a1")`, the notification is acked, `{"dispatched": True, "responders": 1}`); accept no-action → ack-only; accept not-found; accept no-bus honest-degrade; default-None serializes byte-identical. UI `bridge/__tests__/BridgeNotifications.test.tsx` (**3** Vitest): Accept button renders + POSTs to the accept endpoint on click (stopPropagation → only `/accept`, not `/ack`); no Accept button without `suggested_action`; no-emoji scan (source + DOM). **Gates:** backend isolated `pytest tests/test_ad1053_actionable_notifications.py -q -n 0` → **8 passed**; focused notification/system-router regression (telemetry/intent-bus/ontology/decision-queue/alert-feedback/mcp-app-routes/selective-disclosure) → **89 passed, 0 regressions**; focused vitest **3 passed**; full UI suite **288 files, 1918 passed / 1 skipped** (was 1915/1 — +3, 0 regressions); `npm run build` (tsc -b + vite) **clean**; `get_errors` clean on all 6 touched files. AD-1053 enables a commercial overlay consumer (out of scope here). UNCOMMITTED. Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

### AD-1054 — OS-activity sensor (desktop foreground-window watcher → `os.activity` event) (OSS plumbing)

**Context.** Current highest landed top-level AD = **AD-1053** (verified in `DECISIONS.md` + `PROGRESS.md`; zero `AD-1054+` strings landed). AD-1054 is the next sequential top-level. A `grep` for `os_activity|OS_ACTIVITY|active_window|foreground_window` across `src/probos` returned ZERO OS-activity-detection hits — there was no foundation for surfacing "what app/window is the Captain in" as a runtime signal. This AD adds ONLY the raw sensor plumbing (a desktop watcher, a consent flag, a runtime ingestion endpoint, a runtime event), like heartbeat or the AD-708e mDNS advertiser. **Pure sensor — no intelligence, no suggestions.** Nothing in OSS consumes the event; it gates a commercial overlay consumer, out of scope here. **Default-OFF, local-only, active-window metadata ONLY — NO keystroke/screen/clipboard capture. Additive → byte-identical when off.**

**Decision (additive — 3 Python, 2 desktop TS, 1 desktop dep, 0 config-yaml).** **(1)** `config.py` — NEW `OSActivityConfig(BaseModel)` (`enabled: bool = False`; `poll_interval_seconds: int = Field(default=5, ge=1, le=60)`) mounted on `SystemConfig` after `device` via `Field(default_factory=OSActivityConfig)` — the consent gate; default OFF; no `config/system.yaml` edit (model default, so a default install boots byte-identical). **(2)** `events.py` — `EventType.OS_ACTIVITY = "os_activity"` + NEW `@dataclass OSActivityEvent(BaseEvent)` (`active_app`, `window_title`, `app_path`, `url`, `ts`); serializes per the `BaseEvent.to_dict()` contract `{type, data, timestamp}`; metadata only — no keystroke/screen/clipboard field exists; `ts` is the client capture time, `BaseEvent.timestamp` the server emit time. **(3)** `routers/system.py` — `import time` + `from probos.events import OSActivityEvent`; NEW `OSActivityIngest(BaseModel)` (`active_app` min_len 1/max_len 256; `window_title`/`app_path`/`url` bounded; optional `ts`); NEW `POST /api/os-activity` (consent-gated: `cfg is None or not cfg.enabled` → `{"ingested": False, "reason": "disabled"}` + emit NOTHING; else `runtime.emit_event(OSActivityEvent(...))` with a server-`time.time()` fallback when `ts` omitted; emit raises → honest-degrade `{"ingested": False, "reason": "emit_error"}` HTTP-200, never 500; a malformed body → FastAPI 422) + NEW `GET /api/os-activity` (the watcher's public self-gate read returning ONLY `{enabled, poll_interval_seconds}` — no secrets — so the watcher decides whether to poll WITHOUT crew-scope auth; the crew-scoped `routers/config.py:GET /api/config` is deliberately NOT used). The consent flag is server-authoritative — the client cannot enable capture. **(4)** `desktop/package.json` — `get-windows` `^9.2.0` (MIT, sindresorhus, the successor to `active-win`) added to a NEW `dependencies` block (the desktop had only `devDependencies`); NOT vendored — `externalizeDepsPlugin()` keeps it (and its MIT FFI dep `koffi`) out of the electron-vite main bundle. **(5)** NEW `desktop/src/main/osActivityWatcher.ts` — pure `mapActiveWindowToPayload(Result, now)→payload|null` (honest-degrade null on a no-owner/unfocused shape) + pure `shouldEmit(prev, next)` change-detector (true on first sample / app-or-title change) + `startOsActivityWatcher(deps)→stop()`: a heartbeat that ALWAYS re-reads consent first (`GET /api/os-activity`), and only when `enabled` polls `activeWindow()` every `poll_interval_seconds` and POSTs to `/api/os-activity` ONLY when the window CHANGED. `get-windows` is a LAZY dynamic `import("get-windows")` inside the default source (Vitest / a lib-absent host never loads the native/FFI helper); `fetch` + `activeWindow` are injectable (DI) for tests; honest-degrade (probe undefined / Wayland / permission-denied → `logWarn` + skip; a failed POST drops one sample, no throw); the `setTimeout` handle is HELD and cleared in `stop()`. **(6)** `desktop/src/main/index.ts` — imports `startOsActivityWatcher`; a module-scope `stopOsActivityWatcher` handle; armed (gated) in `app.whenReady()` right after `createMainWindow()` (`startOsActivityWatcher({ getRuntimeUrl })`); stopped on a NEW `app.on("before-quit", ...)` handler.

**Two privacy gates (defense in depth).** The runtime `POST /api/os-activity` endpoint is the authoritative boundary (refuses + emits nothing when off); the desktop watcher INDEPENDENTLY self-gates on `GET /api/os-activity` (does not call `activeWindow()` when off — the sensor does not even run without consent). Neither alone is trusted.

**Privacy guarantees (explicit).** (1) Default-OFF (two gates). (2) Consent required to start (no capture without the Captain enabling the flag). (3) Local-only — the `OS_ACTIVITY` event is emitted in-process to runtime listeners; this AD does NOT persist, export, or transmit it off-host. (4) Active-window metadata only (app name + title + optional app path / url) — explicitly NO keystrokes, NO screen content, NO clipboard. (5) Change-detection — a sample POSTs only on a window CHANGE (heartbeat + diff), not a continuous stream. (6) Additive / byte-identical when off. **ActivityWatch (MPL-2.0) is pattern-absorbed only** (heartbeat poll-on-interval + local-only + opt-in consent) — NO MPL code copied.

**What this does NOT change.** No consumer of `OS_ACTIVITY` in OSS (nothing subscribes; inert until a separate overlay consumer subscribes — no intelligence/suggestion layer added here); no `config/system.yaml` edit; no file read/write; no `file_path` field (forward-only; `get-windows` does not provide the edited-document path); no packaging/installer (the deferred AD-759b must `asar`-unpack `get-windows`/`koffi` for a packaged app — flagged forward, no artifact produced today); no new router registration; no `/api/config` change.

**Tests + gates.** Backend `tests/test_ad1054_os_activity_sensor.py` (**13**, BF-287 real fixtures — real `SystemConfig` (flip the consent flag), the real `OSActivityEvent` (real `BaseEvent.to_dict`), a thin recording `emit_event` sink, FastAPI `TestClient` via `dependency_overrides[get_runtime]`): config default-OFF + bounds (ge=1/le=60); mounted on `SystemConfig`; `EventType.OS_ACTIVITY.value`; `OSActivityEvent.to_dict()` shape + no keystroke/screen/clipboard field; `GET` OFF/ON; `POST` OFF → `{ingested:False, reason:disabled}` AND no event captured; `POST` ON → `{ingested:True}` + exactly one `OSActivityEvent` with mapped fields; `ts`-omitted → server fallback `ts > 0`; bad payload (missing/empty/over-length/wrong-type) → 422 + no event; emit-raises → honest-degrade `{ingested:False, reason:emit_error}` HTTP-200; default round-trips OFF. Desktop `desktop/src/main/osActivityWatcher.test.ts` (**9**, vitest DI + `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.runOnlyPendingTimersAsync()`): `mapActiveWindowToPayload` well-formed/minimal/bad-shape; `shouldEmit`; consent OFF → no probe + no POST; consent ON → probe + POST the mapped JSON; change-detection (same window → one POST, changed → a 2nd); honest-degrade (probe throws / returns undefined → no POST, no throw); and the lazy-import gate — a hoisted `vi.mock("get-windows")` import spy proves `get-windows` is NEVER imported when consent is off. **Gates:** backend isolated `pytest tests/test_ad1054_os_activity_sensor.py -q -n 0` → **13 passed**; backend regression `test_config.py` + `test_events.py` + `test_ad1053_actionable_notifications.py` + `test_ad637d_system_events_nats.py` → **56 passed, 0 regressions**; desktop focused watcher vitest **9 passed**; full desktop vitest **85 passed** (was 76, +9, 0 regressions); `npm install` succeeded (resolved `get-windows`/`koffi`); `npm run build` (electron-vite) **clean** (main bundle 41.22 kB; `get-windows` externalized); `get_errors` clean on all 8 touched files. AD-1054 gates a commercial overlay consumer (out of scope here). `config/system.yaml` UNTOUCHED. UNCOMMITTED. Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
